title: Prenatal exposure to maternal depression and antidepressants and neurodevelopmental outcomes: A population cohort study
abstract: by Saraid McIlvride, Neha Rao, Sarjit Singh, Scott M. Nelson, Jill P. Pell, Michael Fleming Background The long-term effects of antidepressant use in pregnancy on child neurodevelopment are unclear; meanwhile antidepressant use in pregnancy is increasing. We aimed to clarify associations between prenatal maternal depression and/or antidepressant exposure and neurodevelopmental outcomes in school-age children. Methods and findings This population-wide cohort study included 167,447 children born in Wales, UK between 2009 and 2016, followed until 2022 (mean age 5.68 years) using linked primary care, maternity and education records. Exposures were one or more antidepressant prescriptions during pregnancy or up to one month before conception, and/or maternal depression diagnosis recorded in the two years before delivery. Outcomes were all-cause and cause-specific special educational need (SEN), including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), sensory impairment, communication difficulties, learning difficulties, physical and medical difficulties, and behavioral-emotional-social difficulties, as well as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Generalized estimating equation models with an interaction term between maternal depression and antidepressant exposure were used to investigate SEN and causes of SEN. Predicted probabilities and marginal effects were derived to quantify absolute risk. Separate models were fitted for individual antidepressant classes and combinations. Cox proportional hazards regression and flexible parametric survival models were used for time to ADHD diagnosis. Covariates included child sex, area-level deprivation quintile, ethnicity, age, maternal age, smoking, parity, multiple birth and epilepsy.In total, 12,630 children (7.6%) were exposed to untreated depression during pregnancy; 7,005 (4.2%) to treated depression; and 5,996 (3.6%) to antidepressant medication without a recorded depression diagnosis. SEN was associated with both maternal depression (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.25 (95% CI [1.20,1.31])) and antidepressant medication exposure (aOR 1.46 (95% CI [1.38,1.56])). Predicted probabilities of all-cause SEN were highest among children exposed to both maternal depression and antidepressants (26.5 per 100 children (95% CI [25.5,27.5])) and lowest among unexposed children (20.0 per 100 (95% CI [19.8,20.2])). Depression alone was associated with an increase to 23.6 per 100 children (95% CI [22.9,24.3]), while antidepressant exposure without depression was associated with an increase to 26.3 per 100 (95% CI [25.3,27.4]). Antidepressant exposure was associated with a 6.3% absolute increase in SEN risk (95% CI [5.2,7.4]) among children of mothers without depression and 2.9% absolute increase (95% CI [1.7,4.1]) among children of mothers with depression. Associations with antidepressant exposure were observed across multiple outcomes including ASD (aOR 1.59 (95% CI [1.31,1.92])) and ADHD (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.89 (95% CI [1.57,2.27])). No antidepressant class showed a markedly different association with SEN risk, although tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) and serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) had significant differences in absolute risk of SEN when comparing treated and untreated depression (TCAs 8.8% (95% CI [3.2,14.4]); SNRIs 8.8% (95% CI [2.6,15.0])). Key limitations include potential confounding by indication and depression severity, as women prescribed antidepressants likely represent a more severely depressed group. Conclusions Offspring of mothers with depression have a higher risk of SEN that cannot be attributed solely to antidepressant exposure. Prenatal exposure to antidepressants may confer a small additional absolute risk, but findings may partly represent confounding by depression severity. Further research is needed.

title: From wrist to research: Harnessing smartwatch data for equitable cardiovascular research
abstract: by Manpreet Kaur, on behalf of the PLOS Medicine Staff Editors Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of death, and progress in reducing mortality has stalled, calling for more research. An opportunity lies in harnessing cardiovascular data from smartwatches. However, ethical and logistical barriers need to be overcome to ensure smartwatch-derived data is utilised to inform equitable and actionable cardiovascular research. title: The inverted pyramid of care in modern-day obstetrics
abstract: by Laura A. Magee, Peter von Dadelszen, Kypros H. Nicolaides Summary points Traditional antenatal care consists of an accelerating frequency of visits with advancing gestational age, as the bulk of pregnancy complications occur in late pregnancy. The ‘inverted pyramid of care’ concept describes a focus on structured risk assessment in early pregnancy, to facilitate prevention and enhanced surveillance of those at increased risk of maternal, intrinsic fetal, and uteroplacental problems. Since publication of this concept in 2011, it has become clear that early pregnancy screening may be contingent, with a sub-population identified for re-screening in mid- or late pregnancy. Maternal conditions (such as pre-eclampsia), intrinsic fetal conditions (such as chromosomal abnormalities) and uteroplacental problems (such as placenta accreta spectrum) can now be predicted or identified at earlier stages. This Policy Forum advocates for building risk-stratified care pathways around early prediction, prevention, and personalised surveillance. We provide updated guidance for ‘inverted’ antenatal care, including optimal screening timepoints and the most accurate methods of screening. We also highlight recent advances in diagnostics and treatment that we anticipate will further improve antenatal care in the future, including development and integration of artificial intelligence-assisted technologies.

title: Encampment sweeps and persistent homelessness among unhoused people who use drugs in Vancouver, Canada: A prospective cohort study
abstract: by Kanna Hayashi, Eric C. Sayre, Jennifer McDermid, Samona Marsh, Caitlin Shane, Michael-John Sheridan Milloy, P.O.W.E.R. , Thomas Kerr Background Housing is a key determinant of health. In response to increasingly visible homelessness amid a growing housing crisis, many jurisdictions in North America forcibly displace unhoused people from public spaces, routinely confiscating their personal belongings. While prior research demonstrated various health-related harms associated with these “encampment sweeps,” the impact on housing placements among otherwise unhoused people remains unclear. We sought to estimate the relationship between experiencing encampment sweeps and transitioning from homelessness among unhoused people who use drugs in Vancouver, Canada. Methods and findings Data were derived from two harmonized prospective cohort studies of people who use drugs in Vancouver, followed through semi-annual interviews between December 1, 2021 and May 31, 2025. We used proportional hazard marginal structural modeling (MSM) to examine if experiencing municipal government-enforced confiscation of personal belongings was associated with no longer reporting homelessness in the past 6 months during follow-up among unhoused participants after adjusting for a range of potential time-varying confounders including demographic characteristics, drug use patterns, health status and other social/structural exposures. A secondary analysis replaced confiscation of belongings with municipal government-enforced forced displacement that may have not involved confiscation of belongings between June 1, 2023 and May 31, 2025. Among 235 participants, 59 (25.1%) reported confiscation of their belongings at baseline. During follow-up, 128 (54.5%) stopped reporting homelessness, corresponding to an incidence rate of 55.6 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 46.4, 66.1) cases per 100 person-years. In the secondary analysis, 50 (32.5%) of 154 participants reported forced displacement at baseline and 62 (40.3%) stopped reporting homelessness during follow-up. In the proportional hazard MSM, confiscation of belongings (adjusted hazard ratio [AHR]: 0.35; 95% CI [0.13, 0.94]; p = 0.036) and forced displacement (AHR: 0.07; 95% CI [0.02, 0.20]; p Conclusions The confiscation of personal belongings and forced displacement might undermine pathways to housing. Our findings underscore the need for policy approaches that prioritize access to dignified and affordable housing rather than practices that perpetuate homelessness. Future research should assess the quality of housing that unhoused people are placed in and examine how it relates to returning to homelessness.

title: Evaluation of the tuberculosis notification impact from an intermediary-facilitated public–private mix intervention in Viet Nam: A population-level quasi-experimental study
abstract: by Luan Nguyen Quang Vo, Thuy Thi Thu Dong, Huy Ba Huynh, Binh Anh Luong, Huong Thi Lan Mo, Andrew James Codlin, Rachel Forse, Thuy Doan To Mai, Lan Phuong Nguyen, Jacob Creswell, Luong Van Dinh, Hoa Binh Nguyen, Phu Xuan Vu, Tuan Dinh Nguyen, Lan Huu Nguyen, Thi Minh Ha Dang, Son Van Luu, Nam Hoang Do, Huyen Thanh Truong, Phan Do Nguyen, Tushar Garg, Jad Shedrawy, Kristi Sidney Annerstedt, Minh Huy Pham, Jamie Tonsing, Tom Wingfield, Mohammed Ahmed Yassin, Nhung Viet Nguyen, Knut Lönnroth Background Treatment coverage gaps remain a major barrier to ending tuberculosis (TB). Public–private mix (PPM) entails the engagement of healthcare providers outside of national TB programs (NTP). PPM strategies are promoted to improve TB notification, particularly in high-burden settings with fragmented care systems, and intermediary agencies are recognized as effective mechanisms to operationalize PPM by bridging NTPs and out-of-network healthcare providers. However, population-level evidence is rare, as most evaluations have been limited to pilot studies, small geographic areas, or uncontrolled designs. This study documents the population-level association of a PPM intervention with TB notifications through the use of unbiased analytical methods to account for heterogeneity from the intervention’s staggered deployment and dynamic intensity. Methods and findings We present a non-randomized, quasi-experimental evaluation of a large-scale intermediary-facilitated PPM intervention conducted between 2020 and 2023 in 15 provinces of Viet Nam, covering 40.6 million people equivalent to 40% of the population. The intervention engaged 3,154 non-NTP providers in TB care, linking them to the NTP through systematic screening, referral, and reporting mechanisms. The model emphasized active case finding, provider incentives, patient support and integrated data systems to raise notifications as the primary outcome. We analyzed quarterly province-level TB notification data from 2016 to 2025 using a heterogeneity-robust extended two-way fixed-effects framework to estimate the average treatment effect on the treated. The analysis adjusted for province and calendar-quarter fixed effects, and for COVID-19 disruptions. Using Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood fixed-effects models, we estimated dose–response effects and post-intervention patterns and triangulated effects with an interrupted time-series analysis of national notifications and repeated all analyses using the intermediate outcome of PPM notifications. Lastly, we calculated marginal cost per additional notification from a funder perspective. The intervention was associated with 316.8 additional notifications per province-quarter (95% confidence interval [CI] [23.4, 610.2]; p = 0.034). Regarding dose–response effects, we observed a 1.4% increase in notifications per 100 verbal assessments per 100,000 population (incidence rate ratio [IRR]=1.00014; 95% CI [1.00002, 1.00025]; p = 0.018). National models suggested 3,206 (95% CI [1,658, 4,763]; p p Conclusions This study furnishes robust, policy-relevant evidence that intermediary-facilitated PPM implemented at scale in Viet Nam was associated with significant, dose–responsive increases in PPM and TB notifications at provincial and national levels. These findings promote intermediary agency models as an effective mechanism to operationalize PPM at scale and to generate public health benefits in closing TB treatment coverage gaps. In an era of constrained global health financing, leveraging existing provider networks through intermediary-facilitated PPM offers an affordable and scalable strategy to sustain momentum towards ending TB.

title: The effect of lifestyle interventions in women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: by Oladipupo Olalere, Min-Dee Koh, Katie Crabb, Olanike Ajijola, Saba Tariq, Chau Thien Tay, Aya Mousa, Soha Sobhy, Lynne Robinson, Rima Dhillon-Smith, Kathy Hoeger, Lisa Moran, Helena Teede, Shakila Thangaratinam Background Lifestyle interventions are recommended as first-line treatment in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), but their effectiveness across various outcomes remains unclear. In this systematic review, we evaluate the effectiveness of lifestyle interventions on reproductive, anthropometric, and metabolic outcomes. Methods and findings We searched Medline, EMBASE, All EBM, PsycInfo, and CINAHL to June 2026 for studies examining lifestyle intervention compared with minimal or no treatment (usual care) in PMOS. Meta-analyses were conducted using random-effects model to estimate pooled odd ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). We conducted subgroup analyses to evaluate differences by intervention type and duration, and by baseline body mass index (BMI).A total of 34 studies (1,871 participants) were included from the retrieved 1,798 publications. Women who participated in lifestyle interventions were more likely to achieve regular menstrual cycles OR 4.03 (95% CI [1.16, 14.05] I 2 = 73%, 5 studies, 237 women), and have reduced waist circumference mean difference (MD) −2.38 (95% CI [−4.68, −0.08] I 2 = 90%, 18 studies, 915 women), fasting glucose MD −0.13 (95% CI [−0.25, −0.02] I 2 = 86%, 22 studies, 1,045 women) and fasting insulin MD −6.08 (95% CI [−9.86, −2.30] I 2 = 71%, 18 studies, 824 women) compared to women who had minimal or no treatment. Subgroup analyses showed that diet interventions had greater effect on reducing fasting glucose levels while exercise was most effective at reducing waist circumference and fasting insulin. In women with PMOS who were overweight or obese, lifestyle interventions led to greater reduction in weight, waist/hip ratio, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, total testosterone, total cholesterol, and low-density lipoprotein. The main limitation of this review is the high between-study heterogeneity in pooled estimates across many of the outcomes. Conclusion Our review found that lifestyle interventions were associated with improved menstrual regularity and metabolic outcomes in women with PMOS, suggesting complementary benefits as no single intervention showed overall superiority. These findings support international recommendations, which endorse lifestyle interventions as first-line treatment, tailored to individual needs.

title: A multi-attention mechanism-improved ResNet18 approach for lithology identification and classification
abstract: by Yan Zhang, Fan Zhang, Jiaming Li, Lantao Huang, Ruifeng Li Lithology identification is vital for improving geological exploration accuracy, optimizing petroleum exploration schemes, and ensuring construction engineering safety. Traditional identification methods suffer from low efficiency, high cost, and heavy dependence on domain expertise. This study proposes a lithology identification approach based on the ResNet18 backbone, in which five lightweight attention mechanisms, namely CBAM, channel-only attention, ECA, SE, and spatial-only attention, are systematically compared, and the best-performing CBAM module is embedded to strengthen feature extraction and discrimination capacity. The Open-Source Computer Vision (OpenCV) library is adopted for dataset preprocessing, where raw images are converted to grayscale to suppress interference from irrelevant information. Comparative experiments demonstrate that CBAM outperforms the other evaluated attention modules and is therefore incorporated into the final network architecture. A hyperparameter sensitivity analysis of the CBAM-based model demonstrates that the model performance varies with different combinations of learning rate and batch size. When trained with a learning rate of 0.0001 and a batch size of 16, the model achieves a lithology identification accuracy of 86.36%, substantially improving overall recognition performance. By integrating CBAM into ResNet18, the proposed method enables accurate recognition to support multi-field engineering applications, reduce risks, and promote intelligent precision.

title: A qualitative exploration of variations in social prescribing in primary care for people living with dementia in England: Barriers and enablers to positive service experiences
abstract: by Jenny Corser, Amy Rathbone, Anne Martin, Hannah Barker, Kritika Samsi, Marie Polley, Lucy Clark, Euan Sadler, Emma Wolverson, George Rook, Louise Robinson, Esme Moniz-Cook, Louise Allan, Chris Fox, Jane Cross, Katherine Bradbury The number of people living with dementia and related costs continue to grow worldwide. Although generally associated with memory difficulties, non-cognitive symptoms of dementia are common and usually stem from unmet needs. Evidence emerging suggests that social prescribing improves the wellbeing of people living with dementia. This study explored adaptations to key elements of social prescribing for people living with dementia, as well as barriers to and enablers of positive experiences among people living with dementia and service providers. The qualitative study engaged people living with dementia (n = 8), carers (n = 9) and service providers (n = 17) involved in social prescribing through primary care. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, and the essential ingredients of social prescribing schemes comprised the initial organising categories for template analysis. The final template included four integrative themes: unique challenges of dementia; interpretations of the social prescribing role; integration of social prescribing into dementia care; and evaluation, improvement and sustainability. Positive workplace cultures and skills in dementia care and support enabled multidisciplinary collaborations and the successful adaptations of the generic social prescribing model to improve the experiences among people living with dementia and service providers. Resistance to and confusion about the social prescribing link workers’ role, and inappropriate referrals were barriers to positive experiences and bottom-up feedback. Primary care networks’ agreements on core outcomes within proactive systems of dementia care and support may promote meaningful bottom-up feedback on the effectiveness of social prescribing for people living with dementia, guiding service improvements.

title: Disparities in screening participation and stage at diagnosis for breast and bowel cancers among individuals with pre-existing mental health disorders: A population-based study
abstract: by Yueh-Hsin Wang, Ajay Aggarwal, Elizabeth A. Davies People with pre-existing mental health disorders (PMHD) often have lower cancer screening uptake and later-stage diagnoses. It remains unclear whether these disparities persist within highly accessible universal healthcare systems without strict gatekeeping. We simultaneously investigated the associations between PMHD and both screening participation and stage at diagnosis of breast and bowel cancers within the Taiwan health service. Using nationwide National Health Insurance and Cancer Registry data covering over 99% of the population, we compared outcomes between individuals with and without PMHD. Propensity score matching was applied for the screening cohort. Adjusted odds ratios were estimated using logistic regression, with subgroup analyses for severe PMHD. Overall, PMHD was associated with higher screening participation (adjusted odds ratios [aOR]: breast = 1.04, bowel = 1.12) and reduced odds of metastatic disease at diagnosis (breast = 0.72, bowel = 0.93), although the magnitude of these associations was modest, particularly for bowel cancer. Conversely, individuals with severe PMHD had significantly lower odds of screening (breast = 0.81, bowel = 0.88) despite high outpatient use. Furthermore, while the severe group retained reduced odds of metastatic breast cancer at diagnosis (aOR = 0.79), they showed no staging advantage for bowel cancer. While Taiwan’s highly accessible universal healthcare system may contribute to a surveillance effect benefiting the general PMHD population, significant disparities persist for individuals with severe illnesses. Targeted interventions, procedural simplifications for self-administered tests, and multidisciplinary person-centred care models, may be needed to ensure health equity.

title: Linking academic stress to loneliness, anxiety, and depression: The association of problematic micro-drama use among Chinese university students
abstract: by Haoyuan Yu, Zhibiao Yang Objective Problematic micro-drama use (PMDU) has received increasing attention as micro-dramas have become widely consumed among young adults in China. This study examined the associations between academic stress and PMDU among Chinese university students, explored which dimensions of academic stress were uniquely associated with PMDU, and examined the associations between PMDU and loneliness, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 510 Chinese university students. Participants completed measures of academic stress, PMDU, loneliness, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms. Multiple linear regression analyses were conducted while controlling for gender and age. The Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure was applied to relevant families of multiple tests. Results Higher academic stress was associated with greater PMDU (β = .447, p Conclusions Academic stress, particularly stress related to perceived learning effectiveness, was associated with greater problematic micro-drama use among Chinese university students. Higher PMDU was also associated with greater loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. These findings identify PMDU as a media-use behavior relevant to both academic stress and psychological well-being, although the cross-sectional design does not establish the direction of these associations.

title: Microbial community structure of Penaeus vannamei post-larvae naturally infected with multiple viruses in hatchery tanks
abstract: by Betsy Andrade, Mery Ramírez, Guillermo Reyes Background This study offers an observational evaluation of how viral and bacterial infections co-occur with alterations in the microbiome and survival of Penaeus vannamei post-larvae, one of the most economically important species in global aquaculture. Methods Eleven commercial larval production tanks were classified into three distinct infection scenarios using histology and PCR: Baculovirus penaei (BP) monoinfection, mixed infections (BP, white spot syndrome virus [WSSV], and acute hepatopancreatic necrosis disease [AHPND]-causing bacteria), and non-infected controls. High-molecular-weight DNA was subjected to shotgun metagenomic sequencing on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform, followed by evaluation of microbial diversity, community structure, and infection-associated microbial signatures. Results Although BP was the most abundant viral genus across infected groups, severe mortality was observed only under mixed-infection conditions, which were closely associated with AHPND-causing bacteria presence and microbiome disruption rather than with BP alone. Deep metagenomic sequencing revealed reduced, distinct microbiome structures in shrimp infected with BP and in those with mixed infections, compared to non-infected individuals. Non-infected post-larvae maintained complex and well-balanced bacterial communities, predominantly composed of Donghicola and Muricauda . Nudiviridae and Oscillospiraceae showed comparable relative abundances in BP-only and mixed-infection groups. In contrast, mixed infections were characterized by a relative increase in Vibrio , together with the PCR-detection of PirAB toxin genes, whereas WSSV remained detectable in the metagenomic dataset despite its comparatively low relative abundance, while the infection remained thermally suppressed and asymptomatic in the larvae. Functionally, infected larval microbiomes were enriched for transposases, retrotransposons, and virulence-factor genes. The near-complete BP-GR25 genome (119,245 bp) was assembled and annotated from larval metagenomes. Conclusion These results highlight the value of high-throughput sequencing in the early detection of pathogens in aquaculture, where subtle microbial shifts during postlarval stages can be valuable indicators of health status for production.

title: Comparative genomics of seven Tenacibaculum maritimum isolates from farmed Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ), Atlantic halibut ( Hippoglossus hippoglossus ), and lumpfish ( Cyclopterus lumpus ) in Canada and Norway reveals conserved features
abstract: by Erwan Lagadec, Snorre Gulla, Sverre Bang Småge, Enrique Pino-Martinez, Kjetil Solheim, Sigurd O. Handeland, Are Nylund Tenacibaculum maritimum is a major bacterial pathogen of marine fish responsible for ulcerative disease outbreaks and high mortality in numerous fish species and represents an important challenge in aquaculture worldwide. In this study, we characterized seven newly sequenced T. maritimum isolates recovered from farmed Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ), Atlantic halibut ( Hippoglossus hippoglossus ), and lumpfish ( Cyclopterus lumpus ) in British Columbia (Canada) and Norway, including the first complete genome of T. maritimum isolated from Atlantic salmon in Norway. Comparative genomic analysis revealed the presence of a complete Type IX secretion system (T9SS) and the canonical gliding-associated machinery. We also identified a largely conserved repertoire of candidate T9SS substrates and several major host-interaction proteins. Phylogenetic analysis placed the isolates in several well-supported clades comprising strains from different geographic origins and host species. Characterization of the O-antigen gene clusters identified three different types (1−0, 2−1, and 4−0), whose distribution was not congruent with the phylogenetic relationships among isolates. Colony development of the four Norwegian isolates on agar was strongly influenced by incubation temperature, with rapid growth at 20–24°C, slower growth at 12–16°C, and only limited growth at 8°C. This study expands the available genomic resources for T. maritimum and highlights the importance of integrating genomic and environmental surveillance to improve tenacibaculosis management in aquaculture systems.

title: Reduced cognitive empathy and differences in EEG activity in low-achieving adolescents
abstract: by Samuel Hernández-González, María Ángeles Gómez-Climent, Albert Clemente-Soriano, Jose Luis Alba Robles, Carlos Caurín-Alonso, Jordi Solbes Students with low academic achievement tend to display more maladaptive behaviours in interactions with peers and teachers. Empathy plays a key mediating role in these interactions and is also linked to academic performance. In particular, facial emotion recognition is one component of socioemotional processing that may contribute to empathic responding. To explore the relationship between empathy, emotion recognition, and academic achievement, a comparative study was conducted with 40 students aged 14–17, divided into two groups: one with low academic achievement enrolled in a school support programme, and a control group with adequate academic performance. A multimethod approach was applied, including the Basic Empathy Scale, a facial expression recognition test, and electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings. Results showed significantly lower cognitive empathy in the low-achieving group in the primary between-group analysis. The overall between-group difference in facial emotion recognition accuracy was not statistically significant. EEG analyses identified exploratory between-group differences in source-level oscillatory activity estimates during facial-expression processing. These electrophysiological findings provide complementary information about task-related activity patterns but should not be interpreted as specific neural markers of empathy or as confirmation of a behavioural facial emotion recognition deficit. Overall, the multimethod approach offers complementary perspectives on socioemotional functioning in low-achieving adolescents, although the exploratory EEG findings require cautious interpretation and replication in larger, independent samples.

title: Sound and music in video games: A systematic review of player engagement and a meta-analysis of positively valenced player experience
abstract: by Enja Heikkilä, Andrew Danso, Geoff Luck Video game sound and music have previously been found to influence player engagement and affective responses during gameplay. However, a systematic investigation into the full extent of these effects has not been conducted. This review examined the influence of music and sound on players’ affective responses and engagement during video game play, with a meta-analysis of positively valenced experience (enjoyment, fun or positive affect). Fourteen studies met the inclusion criteria, six of which provided data for the meta-analysis. Game audio was associated with more positively valenced experience than silence ( g = 0.48, 95% CI [0.22, 0.74]; small-sample adjusted 95% CI [0.14, 0.82]). Heterogeneity ( I ² = 58%) was accounted for by one self-selected music condition; without it, the effect was smaller and homogeneous ( g = 0.34, 95% CI [0.18, 0.50]; I ² = 0%). In exploratory subgroup analyses, sound effects showed a consistent benefit ( g = 0.46), whereas the added effect of music over game sound was uncertain ( g = 0.31, adjusted 95% CI [−0.07, 0.68]). In the narrative synthesis, music and sound were often associated with higher immersion, flow and motivation. Thirteen of the 14 studies were rated at low risk of bias. Evidence that game audio improves players’ affective experience is promising but preliminary; its effect on engagement has not yet been tested quantitatively, and further research and standardisation of methods are needed.

title: A qualitative study of the barriers and facilitators to adopting a sustainable diet among adolescents in Ireland
abstract: by Connor Dupuits, Amanda McCloat, Elaine Mooney An increasing body of evidence indicates that systemic changes to the food system are necessary to mitigate ongoing environmental degradation. The adoption of sustainable dietary practices is an actionable individual-level strategy that may benefit both human health and environmental sustainability. This paper aimed to explore the barriers and facilitators to adopting a sustainable diet among adolescents in Ireland. The data from this research seeks to clarify the steps needed to support this dietary transition. Data were collected from four sites, involving 48 participants aged 15–17 years in seven semi-structured focus groups. Non-probability convenience sampling was employed. Transcripts were audio-recorded, transcribed, and inductively coded to identify barriers and facilitators, which were then deductively mapped onto the Theoretical Domains Framework and presented on the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation – Behaviour model. Barriers ( n = 33) were more frequent than facilitators ( n = 8) in the adoption of a sustainable diet. Prominent barriers to adopting a sustainable diet included a lack of knowledge about the characteristics of a sustainable diet, a current diet that does not align with a sustainable diet, a lack of practical skills for preparing a sustainable diet, unaccommodating school canteens, and cultural influences such as a strong attachment to meat. Facilitators to the adoption of a sustainable diet were the view that this diet promotes human health, and the acknowledgement of the changes required to make their diet more sustainable. However, although participants could identify changes to make their diets more sustainable, most were unwilling to transition at present. This research is important because it provides insights into the design of future interventions using the Behaviour Change Wheel intervention framework to facilitate behaviour change to support adolescents’ transition to a sustainable diet.

title: From public digital discourse to sustained engagement: Digital cultural translation of the Twenty-Four Solar Terms
abstract: by Jiafeng Jiang, Yuchen Song Digital media can increase the visibility of living heritage without securing understanding or sustained engagement. We examined how public digital discourse about the Twenty-Four Solar Terms can be translated into an interpretive stimulus and how users evaluate it. We collected 3,433 publicly visible online text units and retained 1,101 after cleaning and anonymisation. The retained corpus informed collaborative thematic reading; 1,089 texts met the token threshold for keyword extraction and auxiliary topic-model inspection. Thematic analysis identified six cultural theme categories. They covered seasonal diet and bodily care; temporal order and heritage knowledge; and natural phenology and seasonal perception. They also covered folk customs and ritual life; aesthetic imagery and digital creative expression; and agricultural production and everyday practice. These categories informed a five-page storyboard through theme-design mapping and expert-assisted review. Survey data from 350 valid respondents were analysed with covariance-based structural equation modelling (CB-SEM) and supplementary fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). Information clarity, visual aesthetics, perceived explorability and perceived authenticity were positively associated with perceived cultural value. Perceived explorability had the largest standardised path estimate for cultural value, and perceived authenticity was also associated with cultural identity. Perceived cultural value and cultural identity were associated with sustained cultural engagement intention. Configurational analysis identified four sufficient configurations for high engagement and four for low engagement. The two solution sets were asymmetric rather than mirror images. These findings link perceived interpretive qualities, cultural value and cultural identity with sustained cultural engagement intention.

title: Factors associated with mortality among critically ill pediatric patients referred to a tertiary hospital in Indonesia
abstract: by Desy Rusmawatiningtyas, Indah Kartika Murni, Dwi Astuti Dharma Putri, Antonius H. Pudjiadi, Hennie Knoester, Job B.M. van Woensel Background An efficient referral system is an important but often under-recognized determinant of survival in critically ill children. Previous studies have reported high mortality rates among pediatric patients transferred to tertiary care facilities. This study aimed to identify factors associated with Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) mortality among critically ill children transferred and admitted to a tertiary-level referral hospital in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Material and methods This prospective cohort study was conducted over a 12-month period (July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024) and included all critically ill children admitted to the PICU following interhospital referral. Demographic, clinical, referral, and transport data were prospectively collected. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with PICU mortality. Results A total of 334 children were included, with a median age of 6 years. PICU mortality was 25.4%. The most common referral indication based on the Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) was central nervous system dysfunction. Pre-referral management most commonly included oxygen therapy, antibiotic administration, and fluid resuscitation. Compared with survivors, non-survivors had higher PELOD-2 scores and were more likely to require intubation, mechanical ventilation, and vasoactive support before referral. In the multivariable analysis, pre-referral vasoactive support (adjusted OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.20–4.15; P = 0.011) and higher PELOD-2 scores within the first 24 hours after PICU admission (adjusted OR 1.32 per 1-point increase, 95% CI 1.20–1.45; P Conclusion PICU mortality among critically ill children transferred and admitted to a tertiary-care hospital in Indonesia remains high. Pre-referral vasoactive support and higher PELOD-2 scores at PICU admission were independently associated with PICU mortality. These findings generate the hypothesis that improvements in early stabilization and communication may improve outcomes, warranting prospective evaluation.

title: Comparison of IOL power calculation formulas in short eyes using ESCRS calculator and eyetemis: Influence of anterior segment biometry
abstract: by Chung Young Kim, Joo Youn Oh, Hyuk Jin Choi, Mee Kum Kim, Chang Ho Yoon This study compared the refractive prediction accuracy of seven contemporary intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation formulas in eyes with short axial length and assessed the influence of anterior chamber depth (ACD) and lens thickness (LT) on prediction error (PE). A total of 124 eyes with an axial length ≤22.0 mm that underwent uncomplicated phacoemulsification with implantation of a Tecnis ZCB00 IOL were included. Predicted postoperative refractions were obtained using the ESCRS calculator for Barrett Universal II, Cooke K6, EVO 2.0, Hill-RBF 3.0, Hoffer QST, Kane, and Pearl-DGS. Formula performance was evaluated using robust trimmed-mean analyses of trueness, precision, and accuracy implemented in the Eyetemis platform, along with conventional PE metrics and the proportions of eyes within predefined error thresholds. The mean axial length was 21.67 ± 0.31 mm, and the mean implanted IOL power was 25.2 ± 1.6 D. Kane showed a lower trimmed-mean absolute PE than Hoffer QST (0.376 vs. 0.445 D; p = 0.014). No significant inter-formula differences were observed at clinically relevant error thresholds. ACD and LT showed weak, formula-specific associations with PE; however, these findings were exploratory and not clinically actionable. Overall, contemporary formulas provided broadly comparable refractive accuracy in short eyes, although small formula-specific differences were observed.

title: Beyond mid-thigh: Ultrasound assessment of hamstring muscle architecture at multiple muscle lengths in relation to strength
abstract: by Gulsah Karaca Yilmaz, Ali Cihan Dagli, Omer Batin Gozubuyuk, Nazif Ekin Akalan, Sergen Devran, Meryem Merve Oren Celik, Bulent Bayraktar Objectives To investigate the relationship between ultrasound-based muscle architecture parameters and isometric knee flexor muscle strength in healthy individuals, and to evaluate whether distal (25%) and proximal (75%) measurement sites differ in their ability to reflect muscle strength compare to the commonly used mid-thigh (50%) region. Methods Isometric muscle strength was measured in 20 healthy (22.15 ± 2.41 y; 8 females, 12 males) participants using a hand-held dynamometer. Ultrasound parameters (cross-sectional area, muscle thickness, pennation angle) of the biceps femoris-long head, semitendinosus, and semimembranosus were measured at 25%, 50%, and 75% of thigh length. Associations between strength and ultrasound-based parameters were examined using multiple linear regression analysis. Results Moderate-to-high correlations (r = 0.615–0.815) were observed between muscle strength and cross-sectional area for all muscles at 50%. The regression model explained 89% of the variance in muscle strength ( p Conclusions The cross-sectional area of the semimembranosus at 50% of muscle length showed the strongest ultrasound-based predictor of isometric muscle strength. However, measurement at the distal site demonstrated robust associations, suggesting this region may serve as a practical alternative. In contrast, proximal measurements were limited and showed non-significant associations with strength. These findings can help expand the clinical and research applications of ultrasound imaging for assessing hamstring strength. Given the exploratory nature of this study, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Experiences and challenges of healthcare professionals in oncological surgery during the COVID-19 pandemic: A qualitative study
abstract: by Antonia L. Stengler, Elke Mattern, Ulrich Ronellenfitsch, Anke Steckelberg Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic posed significant challenges not only to healthcare systems but also to healthcare professionals. This study explores the experiences, perceptions, and perceived burdens of healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients undergoing oncological surgery during the pandemic, with a particular focus on clinical staff working in hospital-based care in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Methods A qualitative, interpretive-hermeneutic approach was employed using one focus group and one individual semi-structured interview. Participants were healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients undergoing oncological surgery. The focus group included 12 participants, and one additional participant took part in an individual interview. The transcripts were independently coded and analytically annotated by two researchers and systematically analyzed in an iterative process using MAXQDA. The analysis combined deductively informed codes derived from the interview guide with inductively developed codes emerging from the data. The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) reporting statement. Results In September 2024, one focus group and one individual interview were conducted with a total of 13 participants, predominantly nurses and nursing assistants. Nine categories were identified. Participants described substantial emotional, professional, and organizational burdens during the COVID-19 pandemic, including stress, anxiety, increased demands, uncertainty, and difficulties in maintaining usual standards of patient care. Participants also reported challenges related to postponed or adapted oncological treatments, communication with patients under infection-control measures, postoperative care under capacity constraints, team collaboration, and the availability and use of personal protective equipment. Political measures, changing regulations, and the occupational vaccination mandate were perceived by participants as sources of uncertainty, frustration, and reduced autonomy. Despite these challenges, participants also described experiences of team cohesion and professional commitment. Participants expressed a need for clearer guidance, accessible contact persons, psychosocial support, supervision, and greater involvement in decision-making. Conclusion The findings suggest that healthcare professionals involved in hospital-based oncological surgical care experienced substantial emotional, ethical, and organizational challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants’ accounts indicate that pandemic preparedness should extend beyond infection control and include clear communication, consistent guidance, psychosocial support, supervision, and adequate organizational resources. Given the small, convenience-based, and predominantly nursing sample, these findings should be interpreted as context-specific accounts rather than as representative of healthcare professionals in oncological surgery as a whole.

title: The lived experience of intimate partner violence among first-generation latino immigrants in Southern New Mexico
abstract: by Jochebed Ade-Oshifogun, Jodi Patterson, Kwabena Adu Agyemang, Angelica Carabajal Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a significant public health concern that disproportionately affects immigrant populations. First-generation Latino immigrants in the United States experience IPV within complex cultural, relational, and structural contexts that remain underexplored. This study aimed to explore and describe how first-generation Latino immigrants in Southern New Mexico experience and make meaning of IPV and to examine the cultural and relational influences shaping these experiences. A qualitative phenomenological design was used, and reporting followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guidelines. Twenty-four first-generation Latino immigrants were interviewed; two who described observing rather than personally experiencing IPV were excluded, yielding an analytic sample of 22 who participated in in-depth, semi-structured interviews conducted in English or Spanish using a trauma-informed and culturally responsive approach. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and translated where necessary. Data was analyzed using thematic analysis informed by phenomenological principles, supported by Intellectus® Qualitative software and manual coding to ensure rigor and depth. Data saturation was reached during data collection. Six major themes emerged: cultural factors, abuse, culture of silence, control, universal factors, and systemic barriers to legal and support resources. Participants described IPV as shaped by cultural norms, normalization of violence, fear, dependency, and limited access to resources. A pervasive culture of silence, reinforced by stigma, immigration-related fears, and social isolation, constrained help-seeking behaviors. Structural barriers further limited access to legal protections and support systems, exacerbating vulnerability. Findings highlight the need for culturally responsive, multilevel interventions that address the social, cultural, and structural determinants of IPV among Latino immigrant populations. Efforts to improve access to support services and reduce systemic barriers are critical to enhancing safety and positive health outcomes.

title: From accounting systems to business performance: A serial mediation model with IPMA evidence from Vietnamese SMEs
abstract: by Van Tung Tran, Ngo Ngoc Thu Le, Ngoc Nguyen Thao Ngo, Thi Nhung Nguyen, Kha Vy Pham This study examines how organisational and technological antecedents shape management accounting information quality and adoption level among Vietnamese small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and how these characteristics influence decision quality and business performance, with business environment uncertainty as a moderator. Using a cross-sectional survey of 503 Vietnamese SME managers, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and importance-performance map analysis to test a five-antecedent serial mediation model grounded in contingency theory and information processing theory. All ten hypotheses were supported. Information technology capability was the strongest driver of accounting information quality (β = 0.508), and market competition intensity was the strongest driver of adoption level (β = 0.385). Decision quality was the strongest direct driver of business performance (β = 0.558), and business environment uncertainty positively moderated this relationship (β = 0.238). All five serial indirect paths to business performance were statistically significant. The importance-performance analysis identified information technology capability as the highest-priority investment area, combining high importance with low realised performance (52.01 out of 100). To our knowledge, this study offers one of the first comprehensive tests of a serial mediation model linking these antecedents to business performance through accounting characteristics and decision quality in Vietnamese SMEs, one of the first importance-performance prioritisation maps for managers in this context, and extends contingency theory by identifying business environment uncertainty as a pure moderator rather than a direct antecedent. Findings suggest Vietnamese SME managers should prioritise digital accounting infrastructure investment ahead of expanding accounting tool adoption, and that government support for digital accounting tools may be warranted. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, partly addressed through theoretically grounded antecedent ordering, predictive validity testing, and multi-method bias assessment; the single-country scope reflects Vietnam's structural representativeness of wider ASEAN transition economies.

title: Research on strengthening of T-shaped reinforced concrete simply supported beams with U-shaped jackets to enlarge the cross-section: Theoretical analysis, experiments, and finite element analysis
abstract: by Jian-fa Wang, En-he Bao, Ming-su Zhou, Yong-song Wu, Chang-jian Xiao To promote the reuse of existing beams, an experimental investigation was conducted on T-shaped reinforced concrete (RC) beams strengthened with U-shaped RC jackets. Three specimens were tested: one unstrengthened T-shaped control beam and two strengthened beams. Each jacket comprised additional reinforcing bars and higher-strength concrete cast along both sides of the web and the beam soffit, transforming the original T-shaped cross-section into a rectangular section. All three specimens were subjected to cyclic loading, and corresponding finite element simulations were performed to investigate their hysteretic response, skeleton response, flexural deformation, and failure modes. The strengthened beams exhibited load-carrying capacities more than twice that of the unstrengthened beam, and the finite element simulations generally reproduced the experimental responses. Based on truss–arch synergy, an analytical model was developed to predict the load-carrying capacity of RC beams. The predictions agreed well with the experimental results, supporting the reliability of the proposed model.

title: Erector spinae plane block added to intercostal nerve block versus intercostal nerve block alone for postoperative analgesia in video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: A randomized controlled trial
abstract: by Hyerim Kim, Dongwook Won, Jee-Eun Chang, Jin-Young Hwang, Jung-Man Lee, Tae Kyong Kim Objective The aim of the study was to investigate whether the addition of an erector spinae plane block (ESPB) to surgical intercostal nerve block (INB) provides additional postoperative analgesic benefits in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). Methods This prospective, randomized controlled trial included 60 adult patients undergoing elective three-port VATS. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either combined ESPB plus INB (EI) or INB alone. Patients, surgeons, ward nurses, postoperative outcome assessors, and data analysts were blinded to group assignment, whereas the anesthesiologists performing the intervention were unblinded. The primary outcome was pain intensity at 1 hour postoperatively, assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS). Prespecified secondary outcomes included repeated postoperative NRS pain assessments through 48 hours and cumulative opioid consumption at 24 hours. Results The NRS pain score at 1 hour postoperatively was 5.83 ± 2.86 in the EI group and 5.52 ± 3.10 in the INB group (mean difference 0.31, 95% confidence interval [CI], −1.25 to 1.87, p = 0.691). In a post hoc exploratory longitudinal analysis, a linear mixed-effects model demonstrated no significant group-by-time interaction in postoperative NRS pain scores (F[7, 401.2] = 0.81, p = 0.581). Cumulative opioid consumption at 24 hours, expressed as intravenous morphine equivalents, was 41.0 mg (interquartile range [IQR], 31.0–58.5) in the EI group and 40.0 mg (IQR, 29.1–48.3) in the INB group (between-group difference, 3.0 mg; 95% CI, −6.2 to 12.0; p = 0.501). Conclusions Adding single-injection ESPB to surgical INB did not significantly reduce 1-hour postoperative pain scores or 24-hour opioid consumption following VATS. Larger adequately powered studies are required to determine whether smaller clinically relevant incremental benefits exist. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03949790

title: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi and mycorrhizal helper bacteria co-inoculation alters drought-associated physiological traits and leaf abscisic acid concentration in citrus rootstocks
abstract: by Prananath Barman, Sanjay Kumar Singh, Raj Kumar, Daya Shankar Mishra, Anil Shukla, Avnish Kumar Pandey, Ali Khadivi, Yazgan Tunç Plants rely heavily on root-associated microflora to mitigate various environmental stresses such as drought and the use of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) as a biological instrument to enhance plant drought tolerance, through the formation of mutualistic associations, seems like a novel strategy for sustainable agriculture. Thus, a glasshouse study was undertaken with two citrus rootstocks (Troyer citrange and Cleopatra mandarin) under 20 days of differential moisture regimes (well-watered and water-stress condition), after 270 days of inoculation with two AMF strains ( Glomus intraradices and mixed strains of Gigaspora decipiens + Glomus mosseae ) alone or in combination with mycorrhizal helper bacteria (MHB), i.e., phosphate solubilising bacteria (PSB), Azospirillum or Providencia , with an objective of testing the hypothesis that AMF and MHB might influence ABA accumulation in citrus leaves, thereby altering physio-biochemical response to declining soil water status. The seedlings dually inoculated with AMF and MHB exhibited significantly higher relative water content of leaf as well as rhizospheric soil. Glomus intraradices in association with PSB or Azospirillum accumulated higher concentrations of osmolytes (phenols, proline and total soluble sugars) and antioxidant metabolites (glutathione and carotenoids) in leaves under WS condition. Significantly altered leaf tissue ABA accumulation was noticed in dual inoculated treatment of Glomus intraradices and Azospirillum for Troyer citrange (3.517 µg g-1 F.W.) and G . intraradices and PSB for Cleopatra mandarin seedlings (3.079 µg g-1 F.W.), under water-stress condition, as compared to other microbial inoculants including control. Thus, water deficit stress induced physiological and biochemical response pathways could be modified by AMF and MHB. Under these experimental conditions, Troyer citrange exhibited higher relative water content, photosynthetic activity, and stomatal conductance under drought conditions than Cleopatra mandarin seedlings, offering a potential microbial intervention strategy for mitigating osmotic stress in semi-arid environments.

title: Atrial fibrillation is independently associated with impaired myocardial perfusion
abstract: by Niklas Vartiainen, Suvi Hartikainen, Antti-Pekka E. Rissanen, Elina Kariniemi, Aleksi J. Leikas, Eero Strengell, Svantte Halttunen, Paavo-Ilari Kuikka, Juha E. K. Hartikainen, Tomi P. Laitinen A characteristic feature of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) is impaired myocardial blood flow (MBF). Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) is also associated with reduced hyperemic MBF. However, it is unknown whether an independent association exists between AF and MBF in symptomatic patients with suspected obstructive CAD. We studied 874 patients at Kuopio University Hospital (Finland) who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and [ 15 O]H 2 O myocardial perfusion positron emission tomography due to suspected obstructive CAD in 2017–2023. The final cohort comprised 31 AF patients and 120 propensity score-matched sinus rhythm (SR) patients. The matching criteria were age, sex, body mass index, number of traditional risk factors for CAD (0–5), calcium score, and total CCTA status (i.e., the overall severity of CCTA findings). Global hyperemic MBF was lower in AF patients than in SR patients (median 1.9 mL/g/min [IQR 1.4–2.6 mL/g/min] vs. 3.0 mL/g/min [IQR 2.4–3.6 mL/g/min], p < 0.001). Impaired hyperemic MBF (< 2.3 mL/g/min in ≥ 1 segment) was more frequent in AF patients (n = 25/31, 81%) than in SR patients (n = 50/120, 42%, p < 0.001). Furthermore, the presence of AF was independently associated with reduced hyperemic MBF in three multivariate general linear models (p < 0.001 in each model). To summarize, AF was independently associated with impaired hyperemic MBF in patients with suspected obstructive CAD. This association should be considered in clinical practice when interpreting the results of myocardial perfusion imaging in patients with AF.

title: Paradoxical hepcidin–iron dysregulation in primary sclerosing cholangitis
abstract: by Petr Kordac, Milan Hajek, Monika Cahova, Mojmir Hlavaty, Petr Sedivy, Monika Dezortova, Dita Pajuelo, Kamila Balusikova, Jan Brezina, Pavel Drastich Background Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic, progressive liver disease characterised by biliary inflammation. Its exact aetiology remains unclear. This study aimed to use a combination of diagnostic methods and blood analysis to better understand the metabolic changes accompanying PSC. Methods PSC patients (n = 60) and healthy controls (n = 60) were evaluated by magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy (hepatic fat and iron content), ultrasonography, standard blood analysis expanded with markers of iron metabolism, and colonoscopy. Results PSC patients exhibited significant liver fibrosis and elevated liver enzymes. Serum hepcidin was increased ( p p p p Conclusion PSC patients demonstrated an atypical pattern of iron metabolism: elevated circulating iron and depleted liver iron stores despite increased hepcidin levels. This paradox suggests a disruption of hepcidin-mediated iron regulation, potentially sustaining a proinflammatory environment. Further investigation is warranted to clarify underlying mechanisms and therapeutic implications. Trial Registration Clinical Trials I.D.: NCT06026449

title: Fluid-layer-assisted mold temperature control for injection-molded bridge-type compliant mechanisms: Experimental thermal validation and simulation-based benchmarking against conventional cooling channels
abstract: by Pham Son Minh, Thanh Trung Do, Pham Ngoc Chuong, Hung-Son Dang The injection molding of bridge-type compliant mechanisms is sensitive to non-uniform mold temperature because the thin flexure hinges are prone to premature solidification and incomplete filling. This study evaluates a fluid-layer-assisted mold temperature-control architecture using experimental thermography, transient thermo-fluid simulation, a representative straight-channel thermal baseline, melt-filling analysis, and displacement testing of molded HDPE mechanisms. The fluid-layer thermo-fluid model was validated against infrared measurements, yielding a mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.01 °C and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 6.44 °C across six validation points. Under the numerical benchmark condition of an 80 °C inlet temperature, a mass flow rate of 59.5 g/s, and 40 s heating, the fluid-layer architecture was predicted to increase the average cavity-surface temperature by approximately 4.0 °C and reduce the maximum longitudinal temperature difference by 28.6% relative to the straight-channel model. Independent thermography of a representative steel straight-channel insert under the same inlet-temperature and flow-rate conditions showed a lower and more non-uniform surface-temperature field than the steel fluid-layer configuration, confirming the direction of the predicted thermal advantage. Melt-filling simulations subsequently predicted incomplete filling at the thin flexure region for the straight-channel configuration and complete filling for the fluid-layer configuration; this filling comparison remains simulation-based. For HDPE blends containing 0–25 wt% recycled material, the molded mechanisms retained an approximately linear input–output displacement response over the investigated range. At an input displacement of approximately 175 µm, the mean output displacement decreased from 857 µm for virgin HDPE to 745 µm at 25 wt% recycled HDPE. The results support the fluid-layer architecture as a conventionally machinable approach for improving mold-surface thermal control, while polymer morphology, fatigue durability, and experimental straight-channel filling remain subjects for future work.

title: Heart rate and blood pressure variability, and baroreflex sensitivity, during heat exposure in persons with type 2 diabetes and hypertension
abstract: by Mojdeh Rafieian, Erlend Hoftun Farbu, Anje Christina Höper, Rasmus Valtonen, Mika Kallio, Henna Hyrkäs-Palmu, Craig Crandall, Tiina Maria Ikäheimo The autonomic nervous system regulates cardiovascular homeostasis during stressors such as heat, but the effects of type 2 diabetes (T2D) with hypertension on such responses are unclear. Twenty male participants (10 with type 2 diabetes and hypertension and 10 age-matched healthy controls; mean ages 64 ± 4.14 and 63 ± 5.42 years) underwent a 90-minute whole-body heat exposure at 40 °C and 50% relative humidity. Heart rate variability (HRV), baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), and blood pressure variability (BPV) were assessed before, during and after the heat exposure. Heat exposure increased heart rate in both groups but this response was less in T2D (5.43 bpm; ~ 7% increase) versus controls (13.96 bpm; ~ 22% increase; p = 0.014). Similarly, reductions in HRV indices to heat stress were generally smaller in magnitude among participants with T2D. For example, high-frequency power (HF RR) decreased by 31.21 ms² (~54.5% reduction) in T2D because of heat exposure, compared with a reduction of 179.35 ms² (~74% reduction) in controls (p = 0.038). Further, LF BRS decreased by 1.07 ms/mmHg (~25% reduction) vs. 3.96 ms/mmHg (~51% reduction) (p = 0.021), HF BRS by 1.58 ms/mmHg (~35% reduction) vs. 4.15 ms/mmHg (~62% reduction) (p = 0.034), and mean BRS by 1.18 ms/mmHg (~26% reduction) vs. 4.16 ms/mmHg (~58% reduction) (p = 0.010) in those with T2D versus controls, respectively. Low-frequency power (LF RR), LF/HF ratio and BPV parameters also showed smaller (though nonsignificant) changes in T2D. Overall, combined T2D and hypertension produced blunted autonomic responses to short-term heat exposure, potentially increasing vulnerability to temperature extremes.

title: SIRT5 deficiency exacerbates sepsis acute renal injury by activating ACSL4/FTH1 axis dependent ferroptosis
abstract: by Liliang Jiang, Xi Yu, Guang Shan, Ziqi He, Yongbo Liu, Wenlong Lin, Lingling Song, Zhongyuan Xia Sepsis‑associated acute kidney injury (S‑AKI) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients, yet effective targeted therapies remain lacking due to an incomplete understanding of its pathogenesis. Ferroptosis, an iron‑dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has recently been implicated in AKI, but the upstream regulators of this process in sepsis remain undefined. Here, we identify SIRT5, a mitochondrial NAD ⁺ ‑dependent desuccinylase, as a critical endogenous suppressor of ferroptosis in S‑AKI. Using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) murine model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)‑stimulated HK‑2 proximal tubular cells, we show that SIRT5 expression is significantly downregulated in septic kidney injury. Renal tubular‑specific ablation of Sirt5 exacerbated CLP‑induced renal dysfunction, structural damage, and tubular cell death, whereas AAV9‑mediated SIRT5 overexpression attenuated these pathological changes. Mechanistically, SIRT5 deficiency tipped the balance of the ACSL4/FTH1 axis toward ferroptosis: it increased ACSL4‑dependent membrane lipid remodeling and reduced FTH1‑mediated iron sequestration, accompanied by suppression of the antioxidant enzyme GPX4. Consequently, lipid peroxidation, iron overload, and mitochondrial damage were markedly amplified. Notably, knockdown of ACSL4 in SIRT5‑deficient HK‑2 cells effectively reversed lipid peroxidation, iron accumulation, and cell death, establishing ACSL4 as a key downstream effector of SIRT5‑mediated ferroptosis suppression. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized SIRT5–ACSL4/FTH1 regulatory axis that governs ferroptotic susceptibility in renal tubular cells during sepsis, and suggest that pharmacological restoration of SIRT5 activity or blockade of ACSL4‑driven ferroptosis may offer novel therapeutic avenues for S‑AKI.

title: Airway management and anaesthetic interventions for children with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis

Several airway-management and anaesthetic techniques have been evaluated to facilitate tracheal intubation and reduce perioperative airway complications, but the comparative evidence from randomised controlled trials has not been systematically evaluated. title: Pathways to the emergence of online group polarization in sports events
abstract: by Jianshan Bai, Deping Hu, Tao Wang Online group polarization surrounding sports events has emerged as a significant challenge for digital public opinion governance. Drawing on social combustion theory, the study identifies seven explanatory conditions: political triggers, news narrative frames, opinion leaders, capital intervention, first media, event attributes, and stakeholder participation. Using a sample of 24 recent high-profile sporting events, the study employs crisp-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (cs QCA) to investigate the configurational pathways leading to online group polarization and to generate insights for its mitigation. The findings identify five distinct pathways through which online group polarization in sports events emerges, revealing two underlying generative mechanisms. The first is the “sensitive issues–emotional narrative” mechanism, while the second is the “non-sensitive issues–capital involvement” mechanism.

title: Practice-dependent changes in body representation but not in reaching distance following virtual tool-use
abstract: by Amir Jahanian Najafabadi, Christoph Kayser Previous research has shown that tool-use can modify neural representations of our body and the space surrounding us. Furthermore, virtual tools can become incorporated into the user’s body representation after training. However, the extent to which such changes depend on the amount of sensorimotor experience remains unclear. In the present study, we investigated whether different amounts of virtual tool-use training (30, 60, 90 and 120 trials) influence body and action-oriented spatial representations. Participants completed a tactile distance judgment (TDJ) task, indexing body representation; and a reaching distance estimation (RDE) task, indexing perceived actionable space, before and after virtual tool-use training. Virtual tool-use produced an overall decrease in TDJ responses, indicating plastic changes in the forearm tactile distance perception. Although the magnitude of change varied across training conditions, the strongest and most reliable evidence for TDJ change emerged following 120 trials of practice, suggesting that extended sensorimotor experience may be required for stable modifications of body representations. In contrast, RDE changed modestly from pre-test to post-test but did not vary systematically with training duration, suggesting that perceived reaching distance may adapt more rapidly and with less dependence on additional practice. Arm length was a significant predictor of RDE error, indicating that stable anatomical constraints continue to influence reachability judgments despite tool-use experience. Together, these findings suggest a dissociation between body representation and perceived reaching distance, with each exhibiting distinct temporal dynamics following tool-use training. More broadly, the results demonstrate that virtual tool-use can induce changes that transfer to subsequent physical assessment, highlighting virtual environments as a valuable framework for investigating body representation plasticity and tool embodiment.

title: Long-range actin-driven endosymbiont mobility in an animal-algal symbiosis
abstract: Hundreds to thousands of dinoflagellate symbionts (Amphidinium sp., 10–20 μm in size) move up to hundreds of micrometers inside the tissue of their acoel worm hosts (Waminoa sp., millimeters in size). Host actin machinery is primarily responsible for driving symbiont mobility at speeds around 1 μm/s, and symbionts move inside ribbon-like host cells (∼200 nm thin), which stretch to accommodate symbionts moving through them.

title: Somatic DNA-repeat expansions initiate distinct yet analogous changes in Huntington’s disease cortical and striatal neurons
abstract: Single-cell-resolution analysis of brain tissue in Huntington's disease (HD) reveals that cortical and striatal neurons pass through analogous biological changes, each initiated by a neuron's own expanding DNA repeat. In cortical neurons, as in striatal neurons, the DNA repeat expands somatically over decades (phases A and B) and becomes toxic at about 150 CAGs, initiating cell-identity erosion (phase C), the formation of nuclear inclusions of aggregated HTT protein, a derepression crisis (phase D), and then death of the neuron.

title: Multimodal spatial transcriptomics redefines cortical pathology in Huntington’s disease
abstract: By using multimodal spatial transcriptomics to measure somatic repeat expansion, huntingtin pathology, and transcriptional profile in every cell of intact tissue sections, we identify in the Huntington’s disease cortex that large somatic CAG repeat expansions are linked to the selective loss of L5–6 NP and L6b deep-layer excitatory neurons. Intranuclear inclusions of huntingtin were most prevalent at intermediate somatic repeat expansions and were associated with broader transcriptional changes than somatic repeat expansion alone.

title: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial
abstract: A single-dose AAV-CRISPR therapy restores dystrophin in humanized DMD mice and achieves durable editing with manageable safety in non-human primates. title: Perforin triggers iron-induced mitochondrial damage to drive ferroptosis and anti-tumor immunity
abstract: Perforin is best known for delivering granzymes into tumor cells, but this study shows it has a second, independent killing function: it drives iron uptake and mitochondrial iron overload that trigger ferroptosis. This granzyme-independent pathway links cytotoxic immunity to iron metabolism, predicts patient response to checkpoint blockade, and points to iron supplementation as a possible lever for boosting anti-tumor immunity.

abstract: The orphan transporter MCT6 is the route by which the meal- and exercise-associated metabolite Lac-Phe exits intestinal cells and enters the blood. title: In-cell discovery and characterization of a non-canonical bacterial protein translocation-folding complex
abstract: In-cell cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) combined with proteomics, integrative structural modeling, and bioinformatics enables discovery and functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins. In the minimal bacterium Mycoplasma pneumoniae, this reveals a complex that links Sec-based protein translocation and extracellular folding, capable of supporting both co- and post-translational pathways.
authors: ["Rasmus K. Jensen, Liang Xue, Federico Marotta, Joseph C. Somody, Joel Selkrig, Swantje Lenz, Juri Rappsilber, Mikhail M. Savitski, Jan Kosinski, Athanasios Typas, Maria Zimmermann-Kogadeeva, Peer Bork, Julia Mahamid"]

abstract: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) resolves and quantifies an almost complete view of bacterial translation, revealing how gene expression machineries coordinate across the processes of transcription, translation, and membrane engagement directly within a minimal bacterium.
authors: ["Joseph M. Dobbs, Rasmus K. Jensen, Julia Mahamid"]

title: A pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition links APOE4 to cerebrovascular degeneration
abstract: APOE4 causes a pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition that promotes cerebrovascular fibrosis and perivascular amyloid accumulation. TGF-β inhibition reverses this pathological remodeling and thus presents a therapeutic strategy to restore cerebrovascular homeostasis in these high-risk individuals.
authors: ["Braxton R. Schuldt, Dominic Haworth-Staines, Andrea Perez-Arevalo, Diede W.M. Broekaart, Ashley Harlock, Leon Wang, Anna Bright, Georgia Gallagher, Grace Rabinowitz, Alison M. Goate, Towfique Raj, Ana C. Pereira, Joel W. Blanchard"]

title: Shifts in embryonic oxygen levels cue heterochrony in limb initiation
abstract: Mammalian embryos see a substantial increase in available oxygen once the placenta forms. This increase in oxygen exposure serves as a trigger for initiating the development of the hindlimb, thus controlling developmental timing and, more broadly, linking the maternal environment to evolutionary changes in body plan.
authors: ["Meng Zhu, ChangHee Lee, Rinaldo Catta-Preta, Clifford J. Tabin"]

title: Microbial signaling coordinates group oviposition and predator defense in migratory locusts
abstract: This study reveals an egg-associated bacterial signaling mechanism that couples reproductive synchronization with offspring defense in the locust L. migratoria, expanding the functional landscape of insect-microbe-predator interactions and demonstrating how microbial signals can shape complex ecological behaviors.
authors: ["Jinxi Yuan, Liping Nie, Lei Shang, Zhongqiang Jia, Shuang Shan, Xiaoqing Zhang, Lingzhi Shi, Yuxiao Zeng, Benke Hong, Xu Cheng, Liwei Zhang, Guirong Wang, Bill S. Hansson, Hetan Chang"]

title: Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons
abstract: Retrotransposons can infect neighboring cells using a mechanism that relies on a small fusogen-like protein rather than on the envelope protein that is typically required for infection.

title: Projection-defined modules reveal mouse motor cortex architecture
abstract: The mouse motor cortex divides into 16 spatially organized modules based on distinct subcortical projections. This specificity covaries with cortical connectivity patterns and cell-type composition along two spatial axes, thereby defining the rules by which motor cortex modules integrate with granularity into brainwide and precisely wired neuronal networks to influence movement.

abstract: An AI-designed IL-21 mimetic converts transient KRAS inhibitor responses into durable pancreatic cancer remissions through CD4 T cells, independent of CD8 T cells and tumor MHC class I expression.

title: Chloroplasts balance energy production and stress resilience via a cold-induced signaling pathway
abstract: Cold-stress signals are transmitted to chloroplasts and subsequently trigger cold responses through an RAF-like bi-kinase module where cytoplasmic RAF3 and plasma membrane RAF6 translocate to chloroplasts, where they inhibit photosynthetic activity but activate nuclear cold-responsive gene expression.

abstract: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle-encoded CD19×CD3 T cell engager depletes B cells with attenuated cytokine release in preclinical models. In three patients with treatment-refractory immune thrombocytopenia, treatment with this T cell engager achieved sustained platelet recovery over 6 months, suggesting that mRNA-encoded T cell engagers represent a promising therapeutic approach for resetting autoreactive immunity in B cell-driven autoimmune disease.

abstract: Copper binding drives MYH9 polymerization, triggering cytoskeletal collapse and cuproptosis. HThPA releases intracellular copper through glutathione depletion, exposing a therapeutic vulnerability in drug-resistant tumors.

title: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes
abstract: Metax is a cross-domain metagenomic profiler that uses genome-wide coverage evidence to improve species-level microbial profiling and distinguish supported taxa from artifacts. Across diverse datasets, Metax enables robust taxonomic profiling, pathogen detection, contamination assessment, and discovery of disease-associated bacterial and viral signatures.
authors: ["Zhi-Luo Deng, Nasim Safaei, Alice Carolyn McHardy"]

title: Mitochondrial ATP promotes T cell differentiation through chromatin accessibility
abstract: Cell-mediated immunity requires cytotoxic CD8+ T cells that adopt and maintain an effector phenotype. Here, D-α-hydroxybutyrate (DAHB) is shown to act as a metabolic adjuvant, driving the conversion of proliferating CD8+ T cells into cytotoxic effector cells by linking mitochondrial ATP production to chromatin remodeling and gene expression.

abstract: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-based therapy holds promise for reversal of bone loss in osteoporosis. This phase 1 study establishes the safety and feasibility of intravenous administration of glycocalyx-engineered human MSCs and provides evidence that MSCs derived from the bone marrow of older individuals with osteoporosis retain clinically meaningful osteoregenerative capacity.

title: Architecture of the serotonergic projectome in the mouse brain
abstract: Serotonin neurons innervate nearly the entire mammalian brain, yet how their projections are organized has remained unclear. Systematic whole-brain serotonergic axon collateralization mapping reveals five projectomic groups that preferentially target functionally related regions, with each projectomic group connecting to specific spatial transcriptomic and behavioral profiles.

title: Caloric restriction modulates genome-wide somatic mutation in mice
abstract: Mutations accumulate in cells with age, while caloric restriction extends lifespan across diverse animals. Grońska-Pęski et al. study the effect of caloric restriction on mutations genome-wide in mice, finding reduced mutation burdens across several tissues and cell types, thereby establishing that diet can alter mutation accumulation genome-wide during aging.

title: Structural basis of a SWI/SNF-associated transcription pre-initiation complex
abstract: Cryo-EM and genetic analyses reveal that the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeler is an integral component of the transcription pre-initiation complex.
