abstract: An expanded atlas of human cells maps the expression of nearly all human transcription factors across 701 cell-type/tissue combinations and uncovers the heterogeneous nature of senescence across tissues and cell types.
authors: ["The Tabula Sapiens Consortium"]

title: Oxygen-responsive bacterial glycosphingolipid links symbiont fitness and immune development in neonatal host
abstract: How do maternal gut bacteria seed the rapidly developing neonatal gut? Heo et al. show that Bacteroides fragilis produces a distinct membrane lipid that enables this strict anaerobe to tolerate a microaerobic environment. This finding highlights divergent evolutionary strategies among related species, most of which rely on lipids conferring broader fitness.
authors: ["Kyoo Heo, Da-Jung Jung, Ji-Sun Yoo, Byoungsook Goh, Dennis L. Kasper, Sungwhan F. Oh"]

title: De novo pan-rhodamine binders for fluorescence microscopy from mammalian cells to extremophiles
abstract: We developed an AI-based and principled computational strategy for de novo design of Rhobins, compact pan-rhodamine binders with high brightness, reversible binding, and extreme stability. It enables superior live-/fixed-cell, super-resolution, and single-molecule imaging with properties surpassing existing tags. It also supports extremophile imaging at 75°C, inaccessible with current tools.

abstract: A dynamic atlas of gene regulation was generated by perturbing every expressed gene across 22 million primary human CD4+ T cells under resting conditions and following re-stimulation. The resulting map reveals context-specific regulators of immune programs and links regulatory pathways to naturally occurring T cell states and autoimmune disease risk.

title: Gut microbiota generate dinitrosyl iron complexes with cardiometabolic benefits
abstract: Gut bacteria convert inorganic nitrate and non-heme iron into bioactive dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) that distribute systemically and signal independently of free nitric oxide. These microbe-derived DNICs protect against cardiometabolic disease and fatty liver by restoring compromised metabolic signaling pathways.

title: RNA structures regulate norovirus life cycle and enable rational attenuation in vivo
abstract: Genome-wide mapping of RNA structure in murine norovirus reveals structural elements whose disruption impairs viral replication in cells and in vivo. title: Multimodal brain cell atlas across the adult macaque lifespan
abstract: A multimodal single-nucleus atlas of 2,955,873 nuclei spanning eight macaque brain regions across the adult lifespan, including exceptionally old individuals, reveals region-specific and shared patterns of cellular vulnerability during aging. This framework provides a basis for dissecting shared and divergent molecular programs underlying primate brain aging, longevity, and neurodegeneration.

abstract: Functional profiling of ∼200,000 genomic segments from vertebrate-infecting viruses uncovers RNA elements that boost gene expression by stabilizing mRNAs and enhancing translation, revealing the diversity of TENT4-dependent mixed tailing and identifying canonical poly(A) polymerase-mediated cytoplasmic polyadenylation, together expanding our understanding of post-transcriptional regulation and RNA therapeutic design.

title: Charge control enables bright and stable deep-red colloidal quantum well LEDs
abstract: Liao et al. present a layer assembly strategy based on a cascade hole-transport layer (HTL) for deep-red colloidal quantum-well light-emitting diodes (CQW-LEDs). Compared with single-HTL devices, cascade-HTL (TCTA/NPB) devices show improved luminance, external quantum efficiency, and operational lifetime. The cascade-HTL structure balances electron and hole injection, reduces recombination losses, and optimizes the recombination zone.

abstract: Lee et al. report a redox-balanced (Ti,Mo)N electrode that couples Ti oxygen scavenging with Mo oxygen buffering to minimize interfacial oxygen exchange in 5-nm Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 ferroelectrics. title: Long-term ultrasound-enhanced convective injection device for neural drug delivery
abstract: Delivering drugs directly into the brain can bypass the blood-brain barrier, but their spread through tissue remains limited. LUCID combines a miniature ultrasound array, an injection channel, and wireless control to improve local distribution. The device increased dye spread during a 20-h phantom experiment and enlarged contrast-agent distribution in mouse brain. These findings support further development toward sustained neural drug delivery, while long-term performance in living tissue remains to be tested.

title: From actuation to autonomy: Physical and artificial intelligence in magnetic robots
abstract: Yang et al. discuss the complementary roles of physical intelligence (PI) and artificial intelligence (AI) in magnetic robot autonomy. PI encodes adaptive physical responses through material properties, structural organization, robot design, and collective interactions. AI provides perception, planning, and adaptive control. The integration of PI and AI supports autonomous task execution with reduced human intervention. This perspective further highlights applications of autonomous magnetic robots in biomedicine, bio-interaction, surface processing, object manipulation, and environmental remediation.

title: Bending-driven elastocaloric cooling enables efficient high-performance solid-state refrigeration
abstract: Solid-state cooling offers a potential route to reducing reliance on gaseous refrigerants, but practical devices require effective material deformation and heat transfer. Maruf et al. demonstrate a device that bends commercially available nickel titanium wire between separate hot and cold roller heat exchangers to move heat without vapor-compression refrigerants. Measurements show how cooling output and efficiency vary with operating conditions, including cooling across a temperature difference, while single-module experiments provide a basis for exploring future multi-stage systems in practical applications.

title: An implantable optoelectronic platform for untethered, automated, and shock-free optogenetic termination of ventricular tachycardia in rodents
abstract: Den Ouden et al. develop a lightweight, fully wireless, closed-loop optoelectronic platform that continuously monitors heart rhythm and uses light instead of electrical shocks to correct dangerous arrhythmias in rodents. This shock-free platform lays the groundwork toward ambulatory studies and offers a promising foundation for pain-free bioelectronic cardiac therapies.
authors: ["Bram L. den Ouden, Shanliang Deng, Cindy I. Bart, Wilhelmina H. Bax, Bastiaan J. Boukens, René H. Poelma, Willem D. van Driel, GuoQi Zhang, Antoine A.F. de Vries, Vincent Portero, Daniël A. Pijnappels"]

title: Smart contact lens for personalized glucose level sensing and forecasting
abstract: Paek et al. present a smart contact lens for tear glucose sensing and personalized glucose analysis. Tear glucose profiles acquired during oral glucose tolerance tests enable glucose tolerance classification, while individualized computational models forecast glucose responses to meal and exercise scenarios. A conversational user interface was developed to present personalized glucose assessment and forecasting.
authors: ["Joonho Paek, Wonjung Park, Hunkyu Seo, Hayoung Song, Dayeon Kim, Won Gi Chung, Seung Hyun An, Yeon-Mi Hong, Jayoung Kim, Yong-ho Lee, Jang-Ung Park"]

title: Implantable neural chip with electrochemical sensing and optogenetic stimulation for monitoring of cholinergic pharmacological responses
abstract: Son et al. present an implantable neural chip that combines wireless electrochemical acetylcholine (ACh) sensing with optogenetic stimulation. Paired enzyme and non-enzyme electrodes reject electroactive interferents through differential subtraction, while a chitosan porous structure with Ag@Pt NWs supports sensitive detection. The system monitors optogenetically evoked ACh changes in mice and pharmacologically induced ACh changes in minipigs.
authors: ["Jieun Son, Saehyuck Oh, Jeongdae Ha, Hyunjae Lee, Janghwan Jekal, Nayoung Park, Yaeeun Kim, Soon Moon Jeong, In Sun Choi, Jong-Cheol Rah, Jinyoung Won, Kyung Seob Lim, Kyung-In Jang"]

title: Large-stroke thin haptic interface for restoring pressure and friction in virtual reality
abstract: Wang et al. present a haptic interface based on a skeleton network with orthogonal continuous beams. The 0.8-mm-thick display achieves a 12-mm stroke; generates normal force, shear force, vibration, and combined stimuli; and scales to an 8 × 8 array with a 15-mm pixel pitch. SNAH is also used to mimic the sensations of touching hard, soft, negative-stiffness, viscoelastic, and brittle materials.
authors: ["Xinyuan Wang, Yiqi Li, Zhiqiang Meng, Chang Qing Chen"]

title: Dual-mode energy harvester for capturing low-frequency oscillation and multidirectional air flow
abstract: Jia et al. present an energy harvester that couples low-frequency oscillation and multidirectional wind energy through a dual-rotor electromagnetic transduction pathway. Oppositely driven magnets and coils enhance relative electromagnetic motion, enabling dual-mode power generation in stochastic outdoor conditions.
authors: ["Shangxian Jia, Liangdong Wei, Jinlong Ke, Miao Chen, Shitong Fang, Mingjing Cai"]

title: Dual-fiber photometry and multielectrode electrophysiology system for functional measurements in engineered 3D neural microtissues
abstract: Kundu et al. present a dual-fiber photometry and microelectrode array system (DF-PHOTOMES), a multimodal acquisition device that combines fiber-optic fluorescence detection of genetically encoded biosensors and microelectrode array recordings, to measure 3D optical and electrophysiological activity, respectively, from intact neural 3D tissues. The DF-PHOTOMES enables spatially resolved functional measurements independent of tissue size, geometry, or culture format.
authors: ["Srikanya Kundu, Vijay Veerisetty, Ramakrishnan Balasubramanian, Ty Voss, Pranav Bende, Savannah Wood, Anthony Garrison, Shayne Frebert, Cristina Antich, Sarah Tori Ellison, Sam Michael, Meghav Verma, Min Jae Song, Marc Ferrer"]

title: Microneedle-micropump phytoinjector platform for tunable and localized delivery in living plants
abstract: Localized delivery tools can help researchers perturb defined regions of living plant tissue without treating the whole plant. Li et al. develop a phytoinjector combining open-side microneedles with a speaker-driven micropump for tunable fluid delivery and active Agrobacterium transport into tobacco leaves. The platform supports externally controlled plant intervention and provides a foundation for future sensor-triggered delivery.
authors: ["Leyang Li, Abdullah Bukhamsin, Mufeeda Mundummal, Kareem S. Hamdan, Ikram Blilou, Khaled Nabil Salama"]

title: Temperature-compensated silicon nanomembrane gauges for monitoring lithium-ion battery swelling
abstract: Kim et al. present a silicon nanomembrane strain gauge for battery swelling monitoring. Utilizing a temperature-compensated Wheatstone half-bridge circuit, these externally attachable gauges track reversible and irreversible expansion of lithium-ion pouch cells. The integrated wireless in situ system provides real-time data for battery safety management.
authors: ["Taemin Kim, Kyubeen Kim, In Sik Min, Ankan Dutta, Young Soo Kim, Giyoung Kim, Jongchan Han, Jongwoon Shin, Jeong Eun Ju, Doohyun J. Lee, Heekyeong Choi, Hokeon Lee, Myeongki Cho, Jaejin Park, Kyowon Kang, Mingyu Sang, Huanyu Cheng, Ju Young Lee, Ki Jun Yu"]

title: Risk-informed framework for in silico regulatory evaluation of medical devices
abstract: Xue et al. present a risk-informed framework for integrating in silico clinical trial evidence into regulatory evaluation of medical devices. Using a transcatheter aortic valve implantation device exemplar, the review links harm prioritization, context-of-use definition, model influence, decision consequence, and credibility evidence to support risk-informed, regulatory-ready computational modeling and simulation.
authors: ["Yidan Xue, Ali Sarrami-Foroushani, Steven Kreuzer, Cahal McVeigh, Mark Grumbridge, René Bombien, Alexander McLaren, Pawan Kumar Pandey, Adesola Samson Ademiloye, Parker Tyler, Michael MacRaild, Arezoo Zakeri, Alistair Revell, Geoffrey Banda, Daniel Hill, Perumal Nithiarasu, Andrea Manfrin, Martha De Cunha Maluf-Burgman, Alejandro F. Frangi"]

title: Magnetically actuated brush-structured capsule for intestinal surface sampling
abstract: This study presents a magnetically actuated capsule with an internal flexible brush for targeted intestinal surface sampling. External permanent magnets control capsule locomotion and immobilization, whereas magnetic actuation drives the brush to collect biological material from the intestinal surface. Experiments conducted using porcine intestine show that the collected samples are suitable for subsequent intestinal microbiome analysis.
authors: ["Yuguo Dai, Shuzhang Liang, Hao Mo, Huaiyi Zhang, Kenta Yamamoto, Hiroki Kawashima, Fumihito Arai"]

title: A fluidic-shear device for minimally disruptive, site-selective collection of viable cells from excised fallopian-tube tissue
abstract: Accessing viable cells from defined tissue sites is difficult without disrupting the surrounding specimen. Avalle et al. present a handheld fluidic-shear device that rapidly collects growth-competent cells from millimeter-scale regions of excised tissue, supporting spatial tissue sampling and patient-derived model generation.
authors: ["Domitille Avalle, Bert J.C. Vandereydt, Sean M. Parks, Huaiyao Peng, Rebecca Stone, Angela M. Belcher, Kripa K. Varanasi"]

title: Low-power polarization-sensitive DUV optoelectronic synapses based on PEA2PbCl4 nanowire array/organic-semiconductor heterojunctions
abstract: A polarization-sensitive deep-ultraviolet optoelectronic synapse can adeptly mimic biological synaptic functions with an exceptionally low power consumption of 0.45 fJ per synaptic event and a polarization ratio of 1.71 at 266 nm polarized light. The device applications in polarized light-enhanced DUV fingerprint identification with an accuracy as high as 98.4% and in high-pass filtering with the ability to process polarization-related information in polarimetric images are demonstrated.
authors: ["Youneng Tang, Hao Zheng, Shunzi Li, Can Fu, Wenhua Yang, Liangpan Yang, Zhixiang Huang, Chao Xie"]

title: A perovskite-electrolyte dual-iontronic synapse for near-sensor tactile computing, sliding recognition, and adaptive interaction
abstract: Gong et al. develop a perovskite-electrolyte dual-iontronic synapse and construct a full-iontronic afferent nerve system, enabling near-sensor tactile computing, 100% accurate sliding-pattern recognition, and adaptive closed-loop sensorimotor interaction for intelligent robotic manipulation.
authors: ["Jiangdong Gong, Feng Gong, Xiangyang Wang, Mengkang Deng, Yao Ni, Haihang Ye, Huanhuan Wei, Su-Ting Han, Wentao Xu"]

title: Multiplex ovarian hormone monitoring in sweat using a dual-aptamer wearable sensor
abstract: Hormone testing typically relies on intermittent blood sampling, limiting access to longitudinal endocrine dynamics. Lee et al. develop a wearable sweat sensor that measures estradiol and progesterone together using two orthogonal aptamer-redox systems on a single printed electrode. Integrated passive microfluidic buffering normalizes variations in sweat pH and ionic strength before measurement, enabling consistent sensing across different sweat conditions. Serial single-use measurements demonstrate the feasibility of longitudinal ovarian hormone tracking and motivate larger studies of wearable endocrine monitoring.
authors: ["Yerim Lee, Cui Ye, Jeonghee Yeom, Yonglin Chen, Jiahong Li, Jihong Min, Minqiang Wang, Wei Gao"]

title: Achieving long retention in area-dependent resistive memory with phase-separated amorphous tantalum oxide
abstract: Nonfilamentary nonvolatile memory devices have been constrained by limited data retention performance. In this work, we demonstrate a Ta2O5 memory device that is not only both nonfilamentary and nonvolatile but also retains information for over 22 h at 190°C. We demonstrate both bulk compositional changes during switching as well as area-dependent switching behavior.
authors: ["Sangyong Lee, Anton V. Ievlev, Dongjae Shin, Jingxian Li, Yiyang Li"]

title: Octopus-inspired flexible optical tactile sensor for multimodal mechanical and color perception
abstract: Li et al. develop a camera-free, octopus-inspired flexible optical tactile sensor capable of simultaneously perceiving contact force, surface roughness, material stiffness, and full-spectral color. By physically decoupling mechanical deformation from spectral reflection, this compact device enables highly accurate multimodal object recognition for intelligent robotic manipulation.
authors: ["Jiahui Li, Jianlong Hong, Xinkai Xie, Huiyun Zhang, Qing Hao, Qiongfeng Shi, Jun Wu"]

title: In situ process monitoring of extrusion-based bioprinting via physics-informed thermal video imaging
abstract: Monitoring print quality in bioprinting is challenging because most biomaterials are transparent, making optical imaging ineffective. This work introduces a monitoring framework based on infrared thermography, which detects the geometry of the extruded filament through its thermal signature rather than its appearance. By synchronizing the thermal signal with the printer’s programmed toolpath, the framework extracts spatially resolved geometric measurements and feeds them into a statistical process monitoring scheme that reliably detects deposition defects without annotated training data.
authors: ["Egon Prioglio, Bianca Maria Colosimo"]

title: From screening to mechanism-informed analysis: A standardized high-throughput electrochemistry platform for redox species discovery
abstract: Finding useful redox molecules for energy devices is slow because measurements are often manual and hard to compare. Li et al. introduce HT-EChem, a microliter-scale, 96-well electrochemistry workflow that standardizes cyclic voltammetry across many chemical conditions. The platform maps how pH and molecular structure shape redox behavior, turning screening data into interpretable guides for electrolyte discovery.
authors: ["Chuyue Li, Xinyue Liu, Mousumi Dey, Eduardo Martínez González, Lilian Moumaneix, Ayesha Kousar, Pekka Peljo"]

title: Self-powered full-lifecycle tribological in situ monitoring via tribovoltaic topological dynamics and physics-informed neural network
abstract: This study presents a self-powered intelligent perception system that uses the tribovoltaic effect to monitor dynamic friction interfaces. By combining topological dynamics with a physics-informed neural network, the methodology successfully extracts early warning signals of microscopic wear and accurately predicts friction evolution across the full lifecycle.
authors: ["Song Wang, Likun Gong, Zhi Zhang, Xiantao Zhang, Hongjie Zhang, Fei Guo, Chi Zhang, Qinkai Han, Shaoze Yan, Yuming Wang"]

title: On-shaft gearbox sensing powered by torsional vibration
abstract: Torsional vibration generated in gear-rotor systems contains both mechanical energy and information about system dynamics, but accessing these signals remains challenging. Qin et al. develop a torsional self-powered sensing system that converts torsional vibration into transverse vibration and uses acoustic black hole structures to enhance energy harvesting. The self-powered system supports wireless data transmission and on-shaft monitoring for fault diagnosis.
authors: ["Lichang Qin, Yue Yu, Jigang Feng, Baoyu Wang, Nanyi Li, Junrui Liang, Zhaoye Qin, Fulei Chu"]

title: Adaptive conductance optimization for suppressing wire-resistance-induced errors in crossbar arrays
abstract: Compute-in-memory hardware offers high energy efficiency for AI, yet parasitic wire resistance induces severe computational errors as arrays scale up. Here, we introduce an adaptive conductance optimization (ACO) method that iteratively remaps device conductance to suppress the error due to parasitic IR drops. By aligning the practical behavior of the crossbar array with the target computation, the ACO reduces computational errors to below 1% on large arrays, paving the way for accurate analogue VMM operations at scale.
authors: ["Yichen Zhao, Cong Wang, Zhiping Wu, Dehe Kong, Wei Wei, Shuo Ding, Xing-Jian Yangdong, Yu Shen, Yu Wang, Jun Zhang, Wenbin Li, Shi-Jun Liang, Feng Miao"]

title: Piezoelectric microjet cooler with high volumetric flow rates via pumping vortex coupling
abstract: Peng et al. present a compact piezoelectric microjet for providing cooling airflow in space-limited electronics. By optimizing rectification stability, which governs the repeatability and consistency of airflow from inlet to outlet, the authors designed coordinating chamber pumping with tip-vortex momentum to achieve reliable cooling.
authors: ["Boyang Peng, Xingyu Wei, Zhiran Yi, Xiuxuan Li, Yu Fan, Wenming Zhang"]

title: Biodegradable architected stents for endoscopic internal drainage
abstract: Phowarasoontorn et al. present BRIDGE, a TPMS-integrated drainage stent designed for postoperative gastric leaks. Architected lattices improve flexibility, kink resistance, and fluid transport, while an SLA-printable biodegradable resin enables fabrication of degradable prototypes. This design framework offers a path toward gastric leak-specific devices and may inform temporary stents for other endoluminal drainage applications.
authors: ["Parima Phowarasoontorn, Yongbin Ko, Zhansaya Makhambetova, Abdel-Hameed Dabbour, Sungyun Sohn, Wegood M. Awad, Heba Tageldeen Naser, Irina Sinenko, Oraib Al-Ketan, Mohamed Ali, Juan S. Barajas-Gamboa, Juan P. Pantoja, Ahmed AlZubaidi, Carlos Abril Vega, Panče Naumov, Nader Masmoudi, John Rodriguez, Matthew Kroh, Khalil B. Ramadi"]

title: Ultraviolet-induced degradation mechanisms and mitigation strategies for silicon solar cells
abstract: Zhou et al. review ultraviolet-induced degradation in crystalline silicon solar cells, from bulk and interfacial mechanisms to their impacts on passivated emitter and rear contact, tunnel oxide passivated contact, heterojunction technology, and back contact structures. Mitigation strategies are discussed, including UV-resistant passivation, doping, and optical management, and opportunities for back contact, tandem, and space applications are proposed.
authors: ["Yihao Zhou, Muhammad Umair Khan, Shuo Deng, Yalun Cai, Zichen Wang, Martin A. Green, Ning Song"]

title: Opto-electro-mechanical copackaging tactile sensing based on single-contact μLED and CMOS array grayscale imaging
abstract: Zhang et al. present an opto-electro-mechanical copackaged tactile sensor. SC-LED self-emissive tactile units convert contact into light signals, fiber bundles transmit parallel optical signals, and CMOS imaging maps 3D force data to 2D grayscale, lessening circuit complexity for high-density robotic tactile perception.
authors: ["Shuqian Zhang, Shixiong Lin, Wenhao Li, Xiongtu Zhou, Yongai Zhang, Chaoxing Wu"]

title: Biohybrid navigation through real-time terrain recognition and natural climbing in cyborg insects
abstract: Ariyanto et al. present a terrain-adaptive navigation framework for a cyborg insect to traverse complex terrain by combining real-time MLP-based terrain recognition with innate climbing behavior. The navigation identifies surface, climb, descend, and hole terrains and adaptively adjusts electrical stimulation to match terrain conditions. By aligning the navigation control with natural locomotion, the system reduces navigation time, travel distance, and unnecessary stimulation while improving traversal efficiency.
authors: ["Mochammad Ariyanto, Xiaofeng Zheng, Ryo Tanaka, Chowdhury Mohammad Masum Refat, Keisuke Morishima"]

title: Eyeglass-type continuous monitoring of respiration and cardiovascular trends using ultrahigh-sensitivity strain sensors
abstract: Lee et al. present a non-adhesive eyeglass-based platform for continuous respiration and cardiovascular trend monitoring during daily activities. Ultrahigh-sensitivity carbon/LIG-LIG strain sensors integrated into the nose pads and frame hinge detect subtle nasal and oral-breathing-related deformations. Respiratory features extracted from the system are used to estimate time-series trends in R–R interval and blood pressure using a lightweight regression model.
authors: ["Do Hoon Lee, Naruhito Seimiya, Kuniharu Takei"]

title: Surpassing 20% efficiency in droplet-based electricity generator via resonance-enhanced total current collection
abstract: Zhao et al. report a resonance-enhanced total-current droplet energy harvester that couples displacement-current generation at the solid-liquid interface with conduction-current generation from cantilever-vibration-driven electromagnetic induction. By matching droplet impacts with cantilever resonance, the device achieves 20.4% energy conversion efficiency.
authors: ["Dongyang Zhao, Xingbao Huang, Leiyang Wang, Hongxin Hong, Hao Wu"]

title: Laser-scribed graphene textile electrodes for dual-mode and high-linearity iontronic pressure sensors
abstract: Flexible pressure sensors are critical for wearable electronics but often suffer from limited sensing ranges and single-function architectures. Here, we develop a laser-enabled iontronic device integrating O/N/S-doped graphene textile electrodes and microstructured ionic gels. The device achieves broad-range quasi-linear pressure sensing while retaining electrochemical charge-storage capability. This work provides a scalable strategy toward multifunctional wearable systems that combine sensing and energy-related functions within a single platform.
authors: ["Xuan Yang, Yan Zhang, Heping Cui, Dongfang Dai, Jincheng Li, Jiabing Yu, Xianping Chen, Kai Zheng"]

title: Unifying consent standards for implantable brain-computer interfaces
abstract: Young et al. examine key considerations in the consent process for iBCIs, frontier devices that may restore function for people with disabling neurological conditions, including severe speech and motor impairments. The authors propose unifying consent standards and a corresponding iBCI consent checklist to advance patient-centered clinical translation across a life cycle process spanning pre-implantation, peri-implantation, and long-term use.
authors: ["Michael J. Young, Julian D. Sandbrink, Laura Y. Cabrera, Komal Kampasi, Philip Kennedy, Maryam Masood, Daniel B. Rubin, Lynn Brielmaier, Paul J. Ford, iBCI-CC Ethics, Neural Data Security, and Data Privacy Workgroup"]

title: Robotic birds that can walk, take off, fly, and land autonomously
abstract: Flapping-wing robots have better agility at small scale over fixed-wing or rotary-wing robots. In order to create robotic birds that can walk, take off, perch, fly, and land autonomously, the integration of high-energy-density power modules, optimized wing and body designs, large power-to-weight ratio actuators, and low-power and lightweight sensors and processors is required.
authors: ["Jianglong Guo, Yunru Mu, Zheng Zhong, Wenfu Xu, Bing Li"]

title: Fall-resistant and trajectory-adaptive self-rolling robot driven by liquid crystal elastomer cables
abstract: Liu et al. present an untethered, electrically driven robot consisting of electrothermal liquid crystal elastomers, controllers, and batteries. The robot can navigate and adapt its rolling trajectory via wireless control, demonstrating enhanced rolling performance on diverse terrains, impact resistance, and repeatable operation.
authors: ["Changyue Liu, Hanzhi Ma, Junwen Zhang, Lingqi Tang, Qiguang He, Tianyu Li, Lingxin Yuan, Zixuan Wang, Pengqi Fu, Xiang Guo, Jiping Yang, Kai Li, Zhijian Wang"]

title: Maximizing dynamic range and performance of anatase TiO2 ECRAM through structure and programming
abstract: As artificial intelligence pushes the limits of traditional computing, electrochemical random-access memory (ECRAM) offers a revolutionary pathway toward ultra-efficient, brain-inspired hardware. In this study, we unveil critical design rules for ECRAM by directly comparing symmetric and asymmetric anatase LixTiO2 architectures. Through systematic exploration of programming parameters, we unlocked an extraordinary dynamic range (>6,000) and hundreds of highly linear and symmetric memory states. Neural network simulations validate this new understanding, demonstrating ∼2% MNIST classification error and outperforming existing analog memory models.
authors: ["Ana I. Alvarez, Stefan A. Theodoru, Travis P. Pollard, Jonathan Boltersdorf, Wendy L. Sarney, John M. Hoerauf, Alexander C. Kozen, Kyle N. Grew, Gary W. Rubloff, A. Alec Talin, Marshall A. Schroeder"]

title: Interface design and material strategies for high-fidelity electrotactile haptic displays
abstract: Abdal et al. examine how the combination of soft electronics, electrode design, stimulation strategies, and psychophysical evaluation is reshaping electrotactile interfaces toward more realistic and comfortable digital touch. In this review, we discuss the key engineering and biological barriers that limit widespread adoption, including unstable skin-electrode interactions and inconsistent perception, while highlighting emerging strategies to improve fidelity and wearability. These developments are expanding electrotactile technologies toward applications in prosthetics, wearable interfaces, gaming, and extended reality.
authors: ["Abdulhameed Abdal, Tarek Rafeedi, Ritwik Vatsyayan, Shadi A. Dayeh, Yon Visell, Darren J. Lipomi"]

title: Defect-modulated self-powered perovskite neuromorphic photodetector array for dynamic trajectory prediction
abstract: Wang et al. present an active-matrix, photovoltaic-type, perovskite neuromorphic photodetector array based on monolithic integration of blade-coated organic-inorganic hybrid perovskite materials on thin-film transistor active-matrix backplanes. The 256 × 256 array of 65,536 pixels enhances static image contrast and captures trajectories. Leveraging spatiotemporal information with historical memory, it improves neuromorphic processing of trajectory prediction for obstacle-avoidance decision-making.
authors: ["Saisai Wang, Jiazhe Xu, Qi Huang, Rui Wang, Lin Zhou, Yingjie Tang, Guanlei Zhao, Shuo Yang, Siyu Zhang, Fanfan Li, Shuhui Ren, Kaixin Ge, Lixiang Xing, Rui Wang, Bowen Zhu"]

title: Untethered robotic fish for interactive exploration in centimeter-scale underwater confined space
abstract: Yu et al. present an untethered soft robot that can navigate through centimeter-scale confined spaces underwater. Through biomimetic research on the compound actuation of a type of jellyfish, the robot is supported by flexible batteries and electroactive polymer (EAP) materials. By regulating the actuation waveform, the robot can be controlled and can navigate through tight underwater spaces for 15 min.
authors: ["Zhenping Yu, Jiaxin Chen, Guangming Cui, Yining Xu, Fangming Li, Ziqiang Wang, Juntian Qu"]

title: Electromagnetic Modeling of Bundle Branch Block and Application in Magnetocardiographic Diagnosis
abstract: Bundle branch block (BBB) causes delayed and asynchronous ventricular activation. This study proposes an integrated framework that links biophysically interpretable magnetocardiography (MCG) features to ventricular electrophysiology using both simulations and clinical recordings. We performed whole-heart electrophysiological simulations to examine how conduction block alters ventricular depolarization and shapes QRS morphology in MCG. We then collected 32-channel OPM-MCG data from 416 subjects (203 BBB, 213 controls) and extracted two time-domain features—QRS width and QRS complexity—followed by logistic-regression classification.
authors: ["Ziyuan Huang, Guiyu Bai, Yangyang Cui, Haitao Niu, Rui Shang, Qinghai Ren, Yuguo Chen"]

title: Design strategies and anti-tumor applications of nanorobots
abstract: Malignant tumors remain a major global health challenge due to their heterogeneity, poor therapeutic specificity, and frequent development of multidrug resistance. Conventional treatment strategies are often hindered by limited tumor penetration, systemic toxicity, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In recent years, nanorobots—engineered nanoscale devices with autonomous or guided navigation capabilities—have emerged as a transformative platform in precision oncology. These intelligent systems integrate active targeting, stimuli-responsive drug release, and multifunctional therapeutic modules, enabling dynamic interactions with the tumor milieu.
authors: ["Dong Niu, Yi Fang, Zengpeng Dong, Xiao Liu, Tong Guan, Wenbin Fu, Yanli Zhang"]

title: Study on the Adsorption of Rose Anthocyanins by Rose Residue Activated Carbon
abstract: The extraction technology for rose anthocyanins is becoming increasingly sophisticated, and the activated carbon prepared from biological materials has abundant pores and strong chemical stability, low production cost, and can be recycled. Therefore, activated carbon was prepared from rose pomace to adsorb rose anthocyanins. The results show that the best static adsorption process parameters are RP-AC at 1.1 g, the crude extract concentration of anthocyanin at 30 mg/L, adsorption time of 20 h, pH=2; the best dynamic adsorption parameters are 1 mL/min and the sample concentration of 50 mg/L.
authors: ["Deye Qu, Jiangpan Zhu, Yali Yu, Chunni Lei, Bo Wang, Weiqiang Dong, Jixiong Xu"]

title: Synthesis of domestic and international studies on the layout of synchrotron light source installations
abstract: This study analyzes global trends in synchrotron light source (SLS) facility development, showcasing their essential function in materials, biology, and chemistry research. By mapping current and planned installations, we identify key growth areas and their implications for scientific and industrial innovation, and many other scientific and technological fields. The paper evaluates core design principles, layout optimization approaches, and technical specifications of prominent SLS facilities, contrasting domestic and foreign advancements.
authors: ["Zhenkun Sun, Zhi Wu, Yifang Wu, Hao Shi, He Zhou, Hailong Wang"]

title: Ancient Ecuadorian genomes reveal millennia of genetic continuity on the Pacific Coast of South America
abstract: Abstract The demographic history of pre-Columbian South American populations remains poorly understood, particularly along the Pacific coast where ancient genomic data are scarce. Here, we present the first whole genomes from ancient individuals buried at Salango, Ecuador, spanning ∼2,300 to ∼740 years before present and representing 3 distinct cultural phases. Despite major environmental disruption following the Pululahua volcanic eruption and substantial sociopolitical change, these individuals exhibit remarkable genetic continuity across nearly 2 millennia. Population genetic analyses consistently support long-term continuity at Salango, while demographic modeling suggests that the Ecuadorian coastal lineage diverged from other Southern Native American (SNA) lineages approximately 9,800 years ago (95% CI: 9.6–10.1 ka). Together, these findings are consistent with coastal Ecuador representing a long-standing component of early South American population structure while maintaining connections with neighboring Andean populations through time. In addition, we recovered authentic Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) DNA from an infant dated to ∼2,300 BP with skeletal lesions consistent with tuberculosis, providing molecular evidence for one of the earliest documented cases of MTBC infection in pre-contact South America. Although the moderate pathogen genome coverage precludes detailed phylogenetic interpretation, the combined osteological and molecular evidence expands the record of tuberculosis in ancient South America. Overall, our study provides the first ancient genomic data from Ecuador, establishing an important geographic reference for investigating the demographic and biological history of the Pacific coast of South America.

title: Beyond Alzheimer’s story: How an engineered molecule gained an endogenous essence
abstract: Abstract A hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is extra-neuronal protein aggregates formed mainly by the amyloid-β peptide (Aβ), that are deposited inside the brain as amyloid plaques. The formation of amyloid plaques requires participation of zinc ions. The 11-Glu-Val-His-His-14 region of Aβ is critical for interaction between Aβ and zinc ions. The engineered peptide Ac-His-Ala-Glu-Glu-NH 2 (HAEE) acts as competitive inhibitor of such interactions and suppresses formation of Aβ aggregates in animal models of AD. We sought to develop a reliable method for studying the behavior of the synthetic HAEE peptide in the human blood in preparation for clinical trials of this peptide as a potential anti-amyloid drug for AD. The analytical method to monitor HAEE concentration in blood plasma combines separation by high-performance liquid chromatography and registration on a mass detector of the parent quasi-molecular ion and fragment ions. We discover that HAEE peptide represents a normal endogenous component of human blood plasma. Moreover, the HAEE level has been significantly reduced in patients with a clinical diagnosis of AD ( n = 200) as compared with the control participants with no clinical diagnosis of cognitive impairment ( n = 150). Deficiency of endogenous HAEE may be considered as a potential blood-based biomarker in the diagnosis of AD, while exogenous synthetic HAEE may serve as a drug in AD-modifying therapy.

title: Devaluation underlies gendered US faculty departures across disciplines and institutions
abstract: Abstract Women faculty experience academia differently from men in many ways, which can lead them to consider leaving their positions. Using a large-scale survey of both current and former tenure-line faculty across nearly all US PhD-granting institutions and 29 disciplines, we investigate which aspects of the academic workplace are (i) most gendered and (ii) most relevant to faculty retention patterns among respondents. Analyzing 6,615 free-text responses reveals that feeling devalued at work, both in formal evaluations and informal interactions, is the topic where women and men’s reported experiences diverge the most when given the opportunity to discuss anything that needed to be different about their jobs—a pattern that holds for nearly 300 institutions and across both STEM and non-STEM fields, and was particularly strong for women of color and tenured women in our sample. This is in contrast to most existing gender-based interventions in academia that target work–life balance. Further, devaluation is the topic most strongly associated with gendered departures among respondents, accounting for the majority of the gender gap in both considering leaving (current faculty) and leaving (former faculty). Finally, illustrative quotations contextualize gender-based devaluation in academia. These results provide new evidence for the long-known gender gap in faculty retention, illuminating how gendered dynamics in the workplace cross disciplines and institutions and relate to gendered decisions to leave academia.

title: Gender differences in attitudes toward academic effort and boys’ underachievement: A large-scale international study
abstract: Abstract In most developed countries, boys underperform academically compared with girls. One possible explanation lies in boys’ more negative attitudes toward school and learning. Using data from 750,000 15-year olds across 61 countries, we investigate gender gaps in attitudes toward academic effort, including students’ beliefs about the importance of trying hard in school. Boys consistently report less positive attitudes than girls, regardless of socioeconomic status, family structure, or grade repetition. These gender gaps are observed in nearly all countries and are larger in more developed societies. At the individual level, attitudes toward effort are linked to academic achievement, particularly in reading. At the national level, countries with larger gender gaps in effort-related attitudes tend to have more boys among low performers and fewer boys in tertiary education, especially in the arts and humanities, but not in STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) fields. Finally, across countries, these gaps are associated with gender differences in ability beliefs and parental support and with the strength of gender stereotypes, pointing to the role of gender norms in shaping educational attitudes. These findings suggest that cultural and psychological factors may play a key role in shaping gender disparities in education.

title: Discovery as public infrastructure: Renewing the social contract for science
abstract: Abstract Scientific capacity built over generations is being weakened by abrupt political disruption just as discovery is becoming faster, more convergent, globally networked, and more socially consequential. Restoring funding and protecting scientific institutions are urgent, but not sufficient: the postwar compact that sustained discovery before its uses were known must be renewed for 21st-century conditions and made resilient to arbitrary disruption. We propose the Discovery Compact, a renewed social contract among government, science, industry, and the public that treats discovery as shared public infrastructure—capacity a plural society builds, tends, and holds in common across generations. It is organized around five criteria: (i) sustaining discovery as national infrastructure; (ii) enabling institutions to move at speed without sacrificing rigor; (iii) building scientific capacity through people, openness, and mobility; (iv) translating discovery without depleting its source; and (v) securing democratic legitimacy and institutional resilience. Together, these criteria direct policy toward durable scientific capacity and insulate against indiscriminate deregulation, compulsory commercialization, arbitrary institutional disruption, and political control of scientific judgment. This Perspective is not a legislative template but an invitation to a national and international process of protecting and renewing the institutions and infrastructure through which societies discover, generate, protect, and prepare.

title: Perceived political bias in large language models reduces persuasive abilities
abstract: Abstract Conversational AI has been proposed as a scalable way to correct public misconceptions, yet its effectiveness may depend on perceptions of political neutrality. As large language models become objects of partisan conflict, political elites increasingly portray them as ideologically aligned. We test whether such credibility attacks reduce persuasion by conversational AI. In a preregistered US survey experiment ( N = 2,144), participants completed a three-round conversation with ChatGPT (GPT-4.1) about an economic policy misconception they personally held. The conversation corrected misconceptions across all conditions, but a short message indicating that the model was biased against the respondent's political party attenuated this correction by 28% relative to a neutral control and reduced trust in and willingness to use AI. Even under this adversarial framing, the majority of the persuasion effect survived. Pairwise transcript comparisons suggest a behavioral mechanism: treated respondents pushed back more and engaged less receptively rather than disengaging. These findings identify perceived partisan alignment as a user-side lever that conditions, but does not eliminate, the persuasive power of conversational AI.

title: Viral capsid-membrane interactions propel non-Brownian movements of nonenveloped reoviruses during entry
abstract: Abstract Understanding how nonenveloped viruses breach host cell membranes is critical for developing strategies to block viral entry, a key step in infection. Despite extensive study, how viral capsids and host lipid membranes dynamically cooperate during membrane penetration remains poorly defined. Here, using reovirus as a model nonenveloped virus and planar model membranes, we identify previously unrecognized non-Brownian membrane motions of infectious subvirion particles (ISVPs) by single-virus tracking. We then integrate experiments with computational modeling to dissect the stepwise, processive capsid–membrane interactions encoded in these distinct dynamics. We show that ISVP motion transitions from an initial phase of directed translocation to progressively confined diffusion. This behavior is consistent with a multistep entry mechanism in which initial capsid–membrane contact triggers release of the membrane-active μ1N peptide. Together, our data and simulations support a model in which membrane-inserted μ1N may accumulate locally to create retention sites that promote further virus adsorption and progressively restrict particle mobility. By directly visualizing these motion signatures, we resolve transient and cooperative capsid–membrane interactions that are difficult to capture using conventional biochemical approaches. Together, these findings provide new insight into early membrane penetration events of nonenveloped viruses.

title: Correction to: Sequence-encoded conformational biases correlate with self-assembly modes of intrinsically disordered proteins
abstract: This is a correction to: Ryoga Kobayashi, Norio Yoshida, Yohei Miyanoiri, Hideki Nakamura, Miu Ekari, Emi Sakamoto, Misato Tsutsumi, Kayo Imamura, Takashi S Kodama, Hidehito Tochio, Naotaka Sekiyama, Sequence-encoded conformational biases correlate with self-assembly modes of intrinsically disordered proteins, PNAS Nexus , Volume 5, Issue 7, July 2026, pgag189, https://doi.org/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgag189

title: A multiscale signaling–biophysical framework reveals mechanisms of macrophage-mediated RBC clearance in sickle cell and Gaucher disease
abstract: Abstract Red blood cell (RBC) clearance by macrophages maintains blood homeostasis and is dysregulated in the hemolytic disorder sickle cell disease (SCD) and the lysosomal storage disorder Gaucher disease (GD), where biophysical and biochemical alterations promote premature phagocytosis. We develop a multiscale hybrid modeling framework integrating signaling dynamics, biophysical simulations, and machine learning to investigate the mechanisms governing RBC phagocytosis in these diseases. Our approach couples a systems biology model of macrophage–RBC signaling with dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) simulations of molecular diffusion and membrane interactions, and leverages Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for simultaneous parameter inference, hidden-state reconstruction, and integration of multiscale mechanistic constraints. The DPD framework provides mechanistic insight into antibody diffusion, receptor engagement, and membrane-level interactions during macrophage–RBC contact, generating spatially resolved trajectories of CD47–SIRP α signaling and antibody–receptor binding that serve as intermediate observables constraining the signaling model. The model accurately captures differential phagocytic responses between healthy and altered RBCs, revealing diminished inhibitory signaling and changes in SHP1-mediated pathways in both SCD and GD. Identifiability analysis combining Fisher Information Matrix diagnostics and profile likelihood confirms that parameters governing the CD47–SIRP α –SHP1 axis are among the most robustly recoverable, and simulations of therapeutic perturbations with anti-SIRP α antibodies demonstrate modulation of engulfment outcomes. We further employ Physics-Informed Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (PIKANs) as an alternative to standard PINNs, demonstrating improved robustness under noise and sampling variability. More broadly, our multiscale platform linking biophysical simulation with systems-level inference is generalizable, offering mechanistic insights and computational tools for therapeutic exploration in diseases involving dysregulated phagocytosis.

title: Spatial patterning and selection: How the environment shapes molecular complexity
abstract: Abstract Assembly theory predicts that a distinguishing signature of life is its ability to produce complex molecules in abundance, opening new possibilities for life detection. Experimental validation of this approach has so far relied on abiotic controls like meteoritic material, or simple, well-mixed chemical systems. However, decades of research in self-organization have shown that spatial patterning can foster dynamical complexity. This raises the possibility that systems with spatial patterns might promote abiotic formation of molecules with higher-than-expected assembly indices—a measure defined within assembly theory to assess structural complexity—potentially leading to false positives in life detection approaches based on this framework. To probe this possibility, we compare how assembly indices in a simplified in silico chemistry scale relative to those in molecular space, and then ask how spatial organization shapes their distribution in our model. Our findings reveal that transport factors, such as diffusion, significantly affect the distribution of chemical species within a system. Additionally, spatial topology markedly shapes the distribution of assembly indices: while it does not enable arbitrary complexity, ordered lattices in particular can shift the assembly indices of abiotic chemistry upward. Moreover, we demonstrate that diffusion can impede the formation and detectable upper limit of these high assembly index molecules, bearing important implications for life detection experiments and astrobiological missions.

title: Conversational AI increases political knowledge as effectively as self-directed internet search
abstract: Abstract Conversational AI systems are increasingly being used in place of traditional search engines to help users complete information-seeking tasks. This has raised concerns in the political domain, where biased or hallucinated outputs could misinform voters or distort public opinion. However, in spite of these concerns, the extent to which conversational AI is used for political information-seeking, as well as the potential impact of this use on users’ political knowledge, remains uncertain. Here, we address these questions: First, in a representative national survey of the UK public ( n = 2,499), we find that in the week before the 2024 election, as many as 32% of chatbot users—and 13% of eligible UK voters—have used conversational AI to seek political information relevant to their electoral choice. Second, in a series of randomized controlled trials ( n = 2,858 total), we find that across issues, models, and prompting strategies, task-directed conversations with AI to research-specific political topics increase political knowledge (increase belief in true information and decrease belief in misinformation) to the same extent as self-directed Google search. Taken together, our results suggest that people in the United Kingdom are increasingly turning to conversational AI for information about politics. These findings substantially extend prior work by demonstrating that conversational AI's effects on political knowledge generalize across multiple topics, political perspectives, and model families, suggesting that the shift toward AI-assisted political information-seeking may not lead to increased public belief in political misinformation.

title: A versatile fluorescent reporter for Usutu virus drug screening and infection tracking
abstract: Abstract Usutu virus (USUV) is an emerging mosquito-borne orthoflavivirus closely related to West Nile and Japanese encephalitis viruses. Despite its increasing prevalence in Europe and reports of neuroinvasive disease in humans, the molecular and immunological determinants of USUV infection remain poorly understood, largely due to the absence of tractable experimental tools. Here, we report the generation and characterization of the first full-length fluorescent reporter USUV. Using a previously established infectious clone of the Vienna 2001 strain, we inserted the mScarlet-I gene into a permissive region of the viral genome, generating a stable and replication-competent reporter virus. In human hepatoma cells, USUV-mScarlet exhibited replication kinetics comparable to wild-type virus and maintained fluorescence over at least 10 serial passages. Application of this system identified remdesivir and interferon-alpha 2a (IFN-α2a) as potent USUV inhibitors and revealed robust induction of the type I IFN response in infected mouse fibroblasts, despite overall attenuation in this cell type. In IFN signaling deficient mice, which are permissive for viral replication, USUV-mScarlet infection resulted in transient disease and reporter expression in multiple peripheral tissues. Among splenocytes, specific myeloid cell subsets were highly enriched in reporter expression, suggesting their role as targets of viral infection. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that USUV-mScarlet recapitulates wild-type infection dynamics in human hepatoma cells while enabling single-cell/quantitative visualization and sorting of infected cells to assess viral spread and host responses. This reporter platform provides a versatile tool for studying USUV biology and will facilitate the development of targeted antivirals and vaccines against this emerging orthoflavivirus.

title: Building adaptive capacity of US Gulf Coast city practitioners to extreme weather events
abstract: Abstract Building city practitioners’ capacity to prepare for and respond to climate change-driven events can increase coastal cities’ resilience. We conducted a first-of-its-kind mixed methods research project from 2021 to 2023 with 46 US Gulf Coast small and midsize cities to measure the effectiveness of an adaptive capacity-building intervention: a stormwater planning tool called FloodWise Communities (FWC) deployed through the engagement between researchers and practitioners in each city. City practitioners were surveyed preintervention and postintervention between September 2021 and December 2022. Interviews were then conducted through July 2023. We found (i) FWC positively relates to perceptions of actionable knowledge and a change in adaptation intentions; (ii) city practitioners’ adaptation-relevant roles and responsibilities positively related to their perceptions of actionable knowledge and adaptation intentions, with implications for their agency to build adaptive capacity; and (iii) anticipated and unanticipated uses of the FWC tool influenced city practitioners’ perceptions of their adaptive capacity.

title: Ancient and animal-specific regulatory modes of EWS::FLI1 revealed by a minimal yeast model
abstract: Abstract Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is an aggressive, human-exclusive tumor typically driven by the EWS::friend leukemia integration 1 (FLI1) fusion protein. To assess whether EWS::FLI1's neomorphic functions depend on evolutionarily recent cofactors, we expressed EWS::FLI1 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae , a minimal system in which the BAF complex is strongly diverged and ETS transcription factors (ETS-TFs), polycomb group (PcG) proteins, and CBP/p300 are absent. We used co-IP/mass spectrometry to map the yeast interactome, ChIP-seq to identify gDNA binding sequences, RNA-seq for gene expression, and engineered reporters to test conversion of GGAA tandem repeats (GGAAμSat) into neoenhancers. We found that the yeast EWS::FLI1 interactome was limited and distinct from its human counterpart, sharing core machinery (RNA polymerase II, FACT) but lacking BAF/SWI–SNF and spliceosome complexes, and showing enrichment for SAGA. EWS::FLI1 binds to hundreds of yeast genomic sites with preference for putative ETS-TF consensus sequences and CA dinucleotide repeats, and redirects RNA polymerase II to EWS::FLI1-bound loci. Yet, EWS::FLI1-expressing cells presented only minimal transcriptional dysregulation, in contrast to the extensive changes observed in human and Drosophila cells. Finally, EWS::FLI1 successfully converted silent GGAAμSat sequences into active enhancers in yeast. This remarkable result occurs despite the absence of homologs for key human activators, such as CBP/p300, suggesting that EWS::FLI1 can mobilize functionally related, nonhomologous pathways to establish neoenhancers at GGAAμSat sites. Altogether, our results indicate that EWS::FLI1's core ability to drive GGAAμSat-dependent gene expression is a conserved, ancient property, while GGAAμSat-independent extensive transcriptome reprogramming depends on animal-specific cofactors and pathways.

title: Identifying common G protein–coupled receptor interacting proteins independent of heterotrimeric G proteins and β-arrestins
abstract: Abstract The canonical paradigm of G protein–coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling recognizes G proteins, β-arrestins, and GPCR kinases as the primary transducers that shape GPCR signaling. However, multiple studies have demonstrated that other interacting proteins regulate GPCR function in addition to these pathways, termed GPCR-interacting proteins (GIPs). The atypical chemokine receptor 3 (ACKR3) does not couple to G proteins, and β-arrestins have been shown to be dispensable for many of its functions. Here, we employed proximity labeling to identify proteins that interact with ACKR3 in cells devoid of β-arrestins. Among conserved proteins from our and several similar GPCR-based proximity labeling experiments, we discovered components of the endocytic machinery and other putative interacting proteins that can interact with GPCRs independent of G proteins and β-arrestins. Notably, we discovered that the bone morphogenetic protein 2–inducible kinase (BMP2K) interacts with ACKR3 in a phosphorylation-dependent manner that is distinct from its interaction with β-arrestin. We demonstrate BMP2K's ability to interact with many different GPCRs with varying dependency on β-arrestin. Using molecular dynamic simulations, we discovered an asparagine-proline-phenylephrine (NPF)-binding motif in BMP2K critical for its interaction with GPCRs and determined that this motif is conserved across many other GIPs. These findings reveal an expanded network of GIPs that interact with GPCRs independent of G proteins and β-arrestins, highlighting alternative mechanisms by which GPCR signaling may be transduced beyond canonical paradigms.

title: Salient air pollution mobilizes bottom-up green engagement: Evidence from the world's largest green mobile program
abstract: Abstract Air pollution imposes large health and economic costs worldwide, yet most mitigation efforts still rely primarily on top-down regulation of major emitters. We examine whether salient deterioration in local air quality mobilizes bottom-up engagement with a green digital program. Using user-month panel data on 200,000 users of Ant Forest—the world's largest green mobile program—across 331 Chinese cities from 2019 to 2020, we show that the same individuals respond to severe local pollution by generating more green energy through eligible low-carbon activities, engaging more intensively and more frequently with the program to collect the resulting credits, and redeeming more credits for collaborative tree planting in the following month. The responses are dose-responsive—larger under “Hazardous” (AQI ≥ 300) than “Very Unhealthy” (AQI ≥ 200) conditions—and representative survey data show that pollution exposure raises stated environmental concern. Our findings indicate that digital green programs can help translate heightened environmental concern into measurable green engagement and downstream environmental contributions, complementing top-down regulation.

title: Deep learning without weight symmetry
abstract: Abstract Backpropagation (BP), a foundational algorithm for training artificial neural networks, predominates in contemporary deep learning. Although highly successful, it is widely considered biologically implausible, because it relies on precise symmetry between feedforward and feedback weights to accurately propagate gradient signals that assign credit. The so-called weight transport problem concerns how biological brains learn to align feedforward and feedback paths while avoiding the nonbiological transport of feedforward weights into feedback weights. To address this, several credit assignment algorithms, such as feedback alignment and the Kolen–Pollack rule, have been proposed. While they can achieve the desired weight alignment, these algorithms imply that if a neuron sends a feedforward synapse to another neuron, it should also receive an identical or at least partially correlated feedback synapse from the latter neuron, thereby forming a bidirectional symmetric connection. However, experimental studies of cortical connectivity do not support the widespread prevalence of such symmetric connections, and in fact report many unidirectional connections, thus imposing a biological constraint on credit assignment. We refer to the failure of existing algorithms to satisfy this constraint as the weight symmetry problem. To address this challenge of biological constraints on connectivity, we introduce the product feedback alignment (PFA) algorithm. We demonstrate that PFA can eliminate explicit weight symmetry entirely while closely approximating BP and achieving comparable performance in deep convolutional networks. Our results offer an approach to solve the longstanding problem of credit assignment in the brain, leading to more biologically plausible learning in deep networks compared to previous methods.

title: Cultural proximity reveals a local premium in collective memory
abstract: Abstract Collective memory—shared information about the past that shapes a group's identity—is often examined through constructs such as familiarity or salience, conflating its local and global components. Here, we untangle these components using multilingual online attention traces for over 50,000 Wikipedia biographies spanning 137 billion pageviews and a large-scale behavioral recognition experiment in which more than 41,000 participants answered factual questions about famous biographies. Our experiment reveals a robust local memory premium, with people being around 10% points more likely to answer correctly questions about someone from their country and about five points more likely to answer correctly questions about biographies with whom they share a language. Finally, we study the impact of three major life events: Nobel Prizes, Oscars, and deaths in local and global online attention, finding these events produce brief but strong surges in local attention and slower but sustained increases in global attention. These findings add important spatial and temporal nuances to our understanding of collective memory.

title: Edge seismic phase picking: Model distillation for multimodal early-warning systems
abstract: Abstract Seismic monitoring is entering a high data volume, multimodal sensing regime driven by dense sensor deployments, including micro-electro-mechanical systems arrays, large-N (100s–1000s) Nodal arrays, distributed acoustic sensing, and other geophysical instruments. Machine learning models, with appropriate tuning and calibration, are capable of achieving close to expert-level performance in seismic detection and phase picking. The emerging operational challenge is how to scale that machine intelligence across future multimodal sensing networks. Effective incorporation of these capabilities remains constrained by telemetry bandwidth, centralized computation architectures, and communication latency. Here, we present XiaoNet, a proof-of-concept edge machine learning architecture for seismicity monitoring based on a simple system principle: perform first-pass inference near the sensor and transmit concise metadata rather than continuous streams. Using knowledge distillation, we compress a state-of-the-art PhaseNet model by over 93% into XiaoNet, a 240 KB model designed for edge deployment, while preserving strong phase-picking performance across datasets. Deployment on a Raspberry Pi 5 shows sub-millisecond inference latency for 30-s 3-channel waveform windows. By shifting inference to the edge and transmitting concise event metadata payloads, the framework demonstrated the potential for edge inference to reduce communication latency. Substituting an event metadata message payload for continuous raw waveform stream largely mitigates the dominant source of variable telemetry delay under moderate to heavy load. This result supports a feasible architecture in which edge inference devices complements centralized observatories, potentially improving resilience and response speed for seismic monitoring and may extend to future multimodal subsurface and infrastructure sensing systems.

title: Stable sentiment and persistent dynamics in US economic news over 45 years
abstract: Abstract Collective emotion is often inferred from the tone of mass media, but such emotion is not directly observed. One approximation is to extract sentiment from text and use sentiment indexes as proxies to study the temporal organization of news sentiment. Using a daily index of US economic news sentiment from 24 newspapers (1980–2025), we examine whether the response time of this sentiment process has changed. Although the average balance of positive and negative coverage has remained broadly stable, the persistence of news sentiment states has increased substantially. In dynamical terms, this implies longer residence times in optimistic or pessimistic regimes and weaker short-run correction of sentiment shocks. Complementary statistics show declining sentiment volatility, fewer reversals, and increasing bimodality, i.e. a stronger separation between positive and negative sentiment states. We also find an asymmetry between bursts of negative and positive sentiment, with negative bursts tending to last longer. These patterns are consistent with a minimal endogenous-memory model in which a slowly evolving latent sentiment component becomes more persistent while short-range corrective feedback weakens. The findings indicate a change in the temporal response of the US economic newspaper sentiment index over the last 45 years, with sentiment shocks leaving longer traces than expected under short-memory exponential decay. News-based sentiment is thus better modeled as persistent episodes rather than as daily reactions that reset after each event.

title: CatRange enables robust prediction of enzyme variant kinetic regimes
abstract: Abstract Predicting enzyme kinetics directly from sequence remains a central challenge in computational biology, particularly for mutations at catalytically essential residues. Existing models often default to wild-type predictions even when mutations cause substantial activity loss. This limits their utility for enzyme design and mechanistic inference. Here, we introduce CatRange, a machine learning framework trained on CatLog-27k, a human-in-the-loop, AI-agent curated dataset of 27,176 in vitro enzyme–substrate kinetic records. CatLog-27k was created through systematic audit and correction of BRENDA and SABIO-RK, with mutant entries manually reconciled against 2,158 source articles. CatRange reframes kinetic prediction as classification into log 10 -spaced bins for catalytic turnover ( k cat ) and substrate affinity ( KM ), rather than exact-value regression. This formulation reflects the order-of-magnitude scale at which enzyme kinetics are commonly interpreted. It reduces sensitivity to assay variability while preserving distinctions among functional catalytic and binding states. Using joint enzyme–substrate representations and gradient-boosted classifiers, CatRange predicts kinetic ranges for wild-type and mutant enzymes across held-out, out-of-distribution, and few-shot mutation settings. The model achieves robust order-of-magnitude recovery and class-balanced discrimination. Moreover, it captures mutation-induced transitions across kinetic regimes, including activity losses caused by perturbations of annotated catalytic residues. CatRange also identifies nonenzyme sequence inputs. Together, CatLog and CatRange provide an interpretable, mutation-sensitive framework for enzyme engineering and kinetic metabolic modeling.

title: Broadcast ritual dynamics among US Catholics during the 2025 papal conclave
abstract: Abstract The 2025 papal conclave offered a natural experiment to trace how shared emotion and group identity evolve on the timescale of hours to days after a global broadcast ritual. Smartphone prompts delivered four surveys per day to 117 US Catholics from 2 days before the first ballot until 12 days after the inaugural blessing, yielding over 5,900 observations. Continuous-time models estimated that collective enthusiasm showed a small, instantaneous surge (0.25 SD) at the “Habemus Papam” announcement and then decayed by half within 16 hours. Religious identity changed more slowly, with a half-life of 42 h, and exhibited a comparable jump (0.20 SD) at the announcement, both jumps measured relative to the prevailing balloting-phase level. Dynamic cross-effects showed that elevated enthusiasm predicted modest gains in identity (cross-drift = 0.18 SD day −1 ), whereas higher identity predicted reduced enthusiasm (cross-drift = −0.39 SD day −1 ), suggesting regulatory feedback. Ritual phases also shifted trajectories: during secret balloting, constant inputs for enthusiasm (+0.13 SD) and identity (+0.12 SD) were modestly elevated relative to preballoting, whereas postannouncement phases slightly undershot preritual baselines. Finally, participants with above-average combined engagement showed little to no decline in self-rated religiosity, whereas those below average declined by 0.41 SD. These findings demonstrate a two-step process—an immediate wave of collective affective alignment followed by a slower, lasting identity build—and show that mediated rituals can align dispersed audiences and prolong the salience of group identity.

title: Full dynamic similarity experiments and predictive modeling of wind turbine aerodynamics across control strategies
abstract: Abstract Wind turbines operate in turbulent atmospheric flow that constantly changes. In field tests, the full impacts of turbine design and operation are difficult to measure because confounding effects from atmospheric flow cannot be controlled. We address the gap in controlled experiments of wind turbines across control settings at dynamic similarity using a unique experimental framework that enables representative study of full-scale wind turbines in a laboratory-sized wind tunnel by pressurizing up to 220 atmospheres. This pressurization enables high-throughput experiments of a scaled wind turbine, at high Reynolds numbers and across yaw-misalignments and tip speed ratios relevant to commercial wind turbines. The results confirm that control strategies currently in use that were designed for turbines operating in ideal conditions without yaw misalignment should be modified, as the tip speed ratio that maximizes power depends on the yaw angle. Critically, the changes in forces and power with misalignment angle strongly depend on the tip speed ratio. We present a Unified Wind Turbine (UWT) model, which accurately predicts the behavior observed in these controlled experiments. The reliability of the UWT model to predict the synergistic effects of yaw misalignment and tip speed ratio enables its use in wind turbine design and wind farm flow control optimization to maximize the energy production and value of wind power systems. The cost-efficient experimental testbed in a pressurized wind tunnel presented herein offers a unique opportunity to study aerodynamics at dynamic similarity with large-scale, commercial turbines without many confounding effects and challenges faced in performing field tests.

title: Sequential ejaculated- and testicular-sperm ICSI cycles in couples with prior ICSI failure: a within-pair analysis of embryo quality, euploidy, and live birth
abstract: IntroductionPersistent poor outcomes after intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) occur in a clinically significant subset of couples despite reassuring conventional semen analysis. In such couples, testicular sperm aspiration (TESA) may be undertaken in a subsequent cycle on clinical and embryological grounds. We assessed whether TESA-ICSI improves embryo-quality indicators and live birth rates compared with EJAC-ICSI in couples whose initial EJAC-ICSI cycle did not result in a live birth.MethodsThis retrospective paired cohort study included 58 sequential ICSI cycle pairs at a single tertiary IVF center. Each pair comprised an initial ICSI cycle with ejaculated sperm (EJAC-ICSI) that had not resulted in a live birth, followed by a subsequent TESA-ICSI cycle in the same couple; the cycle pair was the unit of analysis. The primary outcome was live birth rate per cycle; secondary outcomes included fertilization, blastulation, Grade A blastocyst formation, PGT-A, clinical pregnancy, miscarriage, and live birth per embryo transfer. Paired comparisons used McNemar exact and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.ResultsTotal oocyte, mature oocyte, 2PN, and blastocyst counts were similar between paired cycles (all p > 0.05), while the fertilization rate was lower in TESA-ICSI cycles at the oocyte level (71.3% vs. 79.7%; p = 0.001). By contrast, the blastulation rate per 2PN was higher in TESA-ICSI cycles (p = 0.008), as was the Grade A blastocyst rate both at the per-embryo level (EJAC: 2.4% vs. TESA: 8.9%; p = 0.0006) and at the per-patient level (p = 0.0032). PGT-A euploidy increased from 27.9% to 65.0% (p = 0.0009), the clinical pregnancy rate from 6.9% to 31.0% (p = 0.0026), and the live birth rate from 0% to 29.3% (absolute risk difference 29.3%; number needed to treat 3.4) (p = 1.5 × 10−5), while the miscarriage rate per clinical pregnancy fell from 4/4 to 1/18 (p = 0.0007).ConclusionsIn couples whose prior EJAC-ICSI cycle had not resulted in a live birth, a subsequent TESA-ICSI cycle in the same couple was associated with significant improvements in embryo quality, euploidy, and live birth without change in embryo numbers. These findings support TESA-ICSI as a reasonable therapeutic option in this clinical scenario.

title: Stroke in Saudi Arabia: epidemiology, prevention, clinical management, and emerging innovations—a narrative review
abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of disability and mortality worldwide and poses an increasing public health challenge in Saudi Arabia. This review summarizes national and regional data from Saudi Arabia on epidemiology, risk factors, clinical practices, and future directions of stroke management. The annual incidence of stroke is approximately 57 cases per 100,000 population, with higher rates among older adults and men. The overall number of stroke cases continues to increase, driven by population aging, demographic growth, and lifestyle-related risk factors. Hypertension, diabetes, obesity, dyslipidemia, and smoking are the principal modifiable risk factors, whereas age, sex, and genetics remain key non-modifiable contributors. Current challenges include weak primary prevention, limited public awareness, and insufficient emergency response systems. Although significant advances in acute stroke treatments, such as thrombolysis and thrombectomy, are widely available in tertiary centers, national access remains uneven, and disparities persist in secondary prevention and rehabilitation. Emerging innovations, including AI-based diagnostics, personalized treatment strategies, and integrated stroke care networks, are increasingly shaping clinical practice. Comprehensive national strategies are needed to strengthen prevention, optimize acute and long-term management, and inform policy development to reduce Saudi Arabia’s growing stroke burden.

title: PV-WTConv: a parallel network for abnormal white blood cell classification based on wavelet transform convolution
abstract: In the field of cell detection research, the detection of abnormal white blood cells is not only central to the early diagnosis of malignant haematological diseases such as leukaemia and myelodysplastic syndromes, but also serves as a key indicator for assessing infectious diseases, immunodeficiencies and the efficacy of chemotherapy. The use of computer-aided techniques to accurately classify white blood cells in microscopic images can assist clinicians in diagnosing and detecting various blood-related diseases more promptly and accurately. However, the accurate identification and classification of white blood cells remains challenging due to the blurred boundaries between abnormal white blood cells and normal white blood cells—or even those exhibiting physiological variations—the lack of uniform and fixed morphological criteria for different types of abnormal cells (such as leukaemic cells and hyperplastic cells), and interference from factors such as the complexity of cell imaging and staining techniques. Therefore, this paper proposes a parallel classification network for abnormal white blood cells based on wavelet transform convolution, designed to enhance the accuracy of recognising and classifying different categories of abnormal white blood cells. This study utilised the AWBC-LZWH dataset of abnormal white blood cell images, provided by the Department of Clinical Laboratory Medicine at Liuzhou Workers’ Hospital, for the main training, validation and testing phases, and conducted supplementary experiments using the PBC_dataset of peripheral blood cell images, which was collected and publicly released by the Hospital Clínic de Barcelona. PV-WTConv achieved an accuracy of 94.4% on AWBC-LZWH, compared with 56.9% for the convolutional baseline and 91.4% for ResNet50, corresponding to absolute differences of 37.5 and 3.0 percentage points, respectively. The results of this study indicate that PV-WTConv demonstrates good classification performance on the evaluated white blood cell image datasets; however, its clinical diagnostic value still requires further validation through prospective, multicentre studies.

title: Sex differences in testosterone and obesity
abstract: Androgens, particularly testosterone, play a central role in the regulation of energy metabolism and adipose tissue distribution; however, their physiological effects exhibit marked sexual dimorphism. In males, testosterone, primarily secreted by the testes, has been reported to inhibit adipogenesis and limit the accumulation of visceral fat. Conversely, obesity itself may suppress testosterone production, creating a deleterious feedback loop between the two. In females, testosterone is derived from the ovaries, adrenal glands, and peripheral conversion of androgen precursors, and obesity may be associated with relative androgen excess. Excess androgen signaling is implicated in the promotion of further fat accumulation and is a characteristic feature of metabolic disorders such as polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS, formerly known as PCOS). This review summarizes the bidirectional relationship between testosterone and obesity in both sexes and discusses future research directions.
