title: Integrated Energy-Efficient Scheduling of Distributed Flow Shop and Distribution Using a Q-Learning-Based Multi-Objective Cooperation Evolutionary Algorithm
abstract: Production and distribution are indispensable in a supply chain. Practically, finding an overall optimization of the two processes has become an urgent problem. This article addresses an integrated energy-efficient scheduling problem of distributed flow shop and distribution in the context of economic globalization and environment sustainability. First, a mixed integer programing model is formulized to achieve minimal maximum completion time, minimal total energy consumption and minimal maximum workload of factories. Second, a Q-learning-based multi-objective cooperation evolutionary algorithm with problem-specific knowledge is specially developed. A cooperation strategy is devised to search a solution space using three populations. Three heuristic rules are proposed to initialize the populations. A knowledge-based local search is devised to refine better individuals. A Q-learning-based approach is designed to adaptively choose premium search strategies at each iteration. Finally, the designed method is compared with three meta-heuristics in prior research and a mathematical programming solver CPLEX. The comparison experiments are conducted by using a group of benchmark instances and a real-world case. The outcomes confirm outstanding capacities of the developed model and algorithm for dealing with the considered problems.
authors: ["Zhengpei Zhang;Yaoguang Hu;Lixiang Zhang;Yanzi Zhang;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Adaptive Convergence Indicator and Neighborhood Fuzzy Crowding Distance for Multimodal Multi-Objective Optimization
abstract: Multimodal multi-objective optimization is a popular research direction characterized by different points on different Pareto optimal solution sets (PSs) in the decision space, corresponding to the same point on the Pareto front in the objective space. In addition, there may exist some multimodal multi-objective optimization problems (MMOPs) with local PSs. Finding all the equivalent global PSs and local PSs is the key to solving MMOPs. To solve these problems, this paper proposes a multimodal multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MMOEA) based on the adaptive convergence indicator and neighborhood fuzzy crowding distance (ACEA-NFCD). The adaptive convergence indicator is able to calculate the local convergence indicator and global convergence indicator through the adaptive selection of neighborhood knowledge, which can effectively preserve all global PSs and local PSs and exclude the interference of isolated solutions. Moreover, in order to increase the diversity of the population, neighborhood crowding distances in the decision space and the objective space are integrated via fuzzy set theory, improving the truncation and selection process. The superior performance of ACEA-NFCD is demonstrated by experimentally comparing it with nine of the most advanced MMOEAs on four benchmark suites and one practical application of map-based distance minimization.
authors: ["Qianlong Dang;Xiaochuan Gao;Baosheng Li;Tao Zhan;Maoguo Gong;Xiaoyu He;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Concentration-Guided Attention-Residual Feature Excitation Diffusion Model for High Dynamic Range Image Restoration in Magnetic Particle Imaging
abstract: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is a cutting-edge tomographic technique used to map the distribution of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles. In biomedical applications of high sensitivity imaging, the image quality is often compromised due to the high dynamic range in sample concentrations. The signals from low concentration samples may be overshadowed by those from high concentration samples particularly when the sample spacing is small. The impact of noise is also more pronounced. Hardware improvements are relatively complex, whereas the traditional methods lack robustness to different levels of interference, which makes it challenging to recover the information from different concentration distributions. Therefore, this study proposed a concentration-guided attention-residual feature excitation diffusion model for recovering distributions of different concentration samples interfered by the high dynamic range. The method demonstrated an enhanced focus on the estimation of noise features in low concentration sample locations by employing a strategy of feature excitation and fusion. Furthermore, the proposed greyscale preservation block is capable of more accurately estimating noise at different greyscale levels. Our method was evaluated on simulated and collected MPI image data. The experimental results indicated that our method, under simulated conditions with a sample spacing of 5 mm and a concentration ratio of 90 exhibits an enhanced capacity for restoring image information compared to existing image restoration methods. Specifically, when applied to real-world data, the proposed method can also achieve image restoration with a dynamic range of 10-fold, even when the imaging range of the MPI scanner is limited.
authors: ["Yuanduo Liu;Zechen Wei;Bingye Wang;Xin Yang;Jie Tian;Hui Hui;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Crystal Quotient Graph and Periodic Message Passing Enhancing Material Property Prediction
abstract: Crystal structures exhibit unique structural features: 1) periodicity, which produces the infinite repetition of atomic arrangements in three-dimensional space, and 2) symmetry, the set of isometries defined by a space group that maps a crystal structure to itself. Linking structural information to material properties requires an efficient representation and a complex mapping model. Current graph representation methods inadequately consider the symmetry and periodicity of crystal structures, resulting in structural redundancy with multiple nodes serving the same topological roles. In this paper, we propose a crystal quotient graph representation to remove the structural redundancy from the crystal graph, which can speed up the material property prediction model. We also introduce periodic message passing, including periodic message encoding and adaptive aggregation function mechanisms to improve the learning capabilities of graph neural network. By implementing periodic message encoding, we integrate the crystal's periodicity into the computational processes of the neural network. The adaptive aggregation function mechanism automatically determines the suitable aggregators using multi-objective Bayesian optimization with max-value entropy search. Extensive experiments show that our model outperforms state-of-the-art models in accuracy across various material properties. The quotient graph representation also shows superiority in terms of both prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Moreover, we provide highly accurate performance in three specific end-user scenarios.
authors: ["Weiwei Zhang;Lixin Tang;Meiling Xu;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Security Quasi-Synchronization Control of Fractional-Order Fuzzy Multiplex Networks With Short Memory Windows
abstract: In this article, the quasi-synchronization problem of fractional-order fuzzy multiplex networks is investigated using event-triggered control approach. To tackle the issue of control channel blockage caused by the DoS attacks, an improved model of fractional-order fuzzy multiplex networks with short memory windows is established. A fuzzy logic-based security control scheme is designed to ensure the quasi-synchronization of fractional-order fuzzy multiplex networks with short memory windows under DoS attacks, which is event-triggered and effectively avoids the occurrence of the Zeno behavior. Compared with conventional results of event-triggered control for fractional-order networks, under the consideration of DoS attacks, the exponential quasi-synchronization is achieved instead of Mittag-Leffler synchronization and asymptotic synchronization, which improves the convergence speed. Furthermore, the upper bound of the radius of the convergence ball of synchronization errors is also estimated. Some numerical simulations of fractional-order power systems are finally provided to illustrate the effectiveness of proposed results.
authors: ["Yao Xu;Shipeng Zhen;Xiangpeng Xie;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Multi-Contrast Multi-Slice Triple-Pathway Fusion Framework for Missing MRI Synthesis
abstract: Multi-contrast Magnetic Resonance Images (MRI) are widely used in disease diagnosis and clinical treatment. However, the limitation of the imaging principle results in both time-consuming and economically costly acquisitions of multi-contrast MRI images. Current synthesis methods primarily focus on mono-contrast and single slice data, overlooking the inherent structural and textural similarities among MRI contrasts, as well as the anatomical continuity across consecutive slices. To address these issues, we propose a Multi-contrast Multi-slice Triple-pathway fusion framework for missing MRI Synthesis (MMTS). Our framework consists of two core components. First, a triple-pathway module based on a Swin Transformer architecture enhanced with convolutional layers and residual connections. This module is designed to concurrently extract and fuse features from multiple contrasts and adjacent slices. Second, a synthesis module built with stacked dense blocks integrates these features into the target contrast by combining shallow and deep cross-contrast representations. Extensive evaluations on the SIMON and BraTS datasets demonstrate that MMTS effectively utilizes complementary information, outperforming both single-input variants and state-of-the-art methods. For instance, in T$_{2}$ -weighted image synthesis, MMTS achieves a 0.48 dB PSNR gain over the best baseline by fusing PD, FLAIR, and T$_{2}$$^{*}$ inputs, leading to superior quantitative and visual performance.
authors: ["Xuebin Sun;Yanwei Pang;Hang Qu;Zhenchang Wang;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Crystal Materials Design via Physics-Guided Evolutionary Multi-Objective Optimization With Knowledge Transfer
abstract: The design of new crystal materials holds significant scientific value for societal advancement. Recent advancements in machine learning-based approaches have demonstrated considerable promise in the realm of crystal material design. However, their effectiveness relies heavily on the availability of high-quality and extensive training datasets, which are often challenging to collect in practice. To this end, we propose a novel physics-informed evolutionary transfer optimization framework that can design new crystal materials without necessitating extensive data. Specifically, we introduce a physics-informed encoding for materials, enabling the use of multi-objective evolutionary optimization to simultaneously optimize multiple physical objectives that are critical to the effective design of crystal materials, including the validity, properties, and energy of crystal materials. Additionally, to mitigate the slow optimization speed of evolutionary computation, we propose a physics-informed evolutionary transfer optimization technique to enhance the design speed of optimized materials. We conducted comprehensive experiments to analyze the designed crystals from the perspectives of validity, density functional theory (DFT) validation, formation energy, and energy above hull. The experimental results validate the immense potential of the proposed physics-informed multi-objective evolutionary optimization framework in crystal material design.
authors: ["Cheng Chen;Haokai Hong;Wanyu Lin;Kay Chen Tan;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: OPM-Miner: One-Off Sequential Pattern Mining for Multivariate Time Series Analysis
abstract: A time series is a common form of data that contains a wealth of valuable information. Sequential pattern mining (SPM) methods can be used to analyze this type of series; however, traditional SPM methods mainly focus on analyzing one-dimensional time series, and it is difficult to analyze multivariate time series. More importantly, multivariate time series may interact with each other. To address these issues, this paper explores one-off SPM for multivariate time series analysis (OPM) and presents an OPM-Miner algorithm. At data preprocessing stage, the original multivariate time series is converted to binary inverted dictionaries to avoid the need to scan the original database. At support calculation stage, we introduce strategies for pruning infrequent items and bit index sliding, and develop strategies called Over and Under to further improve the efficiency of support calculation. This paper selected 10 competitive algorithms and 16 real-life multivariate databases to verify the performance of OPM-Miner. The experimental results show that OPM-Miner outperforms other competitive algorithms. More importantly, OPM-Miner can be used for air pollution detection, as it reveals the interactive relationships between various air pollutants, and can predict future trends in air pollutants.
authors: ["Youxi Wu;Yaqi Liu;Yan Li;Jing Liu;Cong Shen;Yazhou Zhang;Xindong Wu;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Finite-Horizon Distributed Optimal Consensus Control of Discrete-Time Homogeneous Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This paper addresses a critical gap in multi-agent systems control by introducing a model-free approach for finite-horizon distributed optimal consensus control of discrete-time homogeneous leader-following systems. While existing model-free optimal consensus methods focus exclusively on infinite-horizon scenarios with asymptotic convergence, they prove inadequate for time-sensitive applications requiring consensus within predetermined time frames. We propose a time-varying Q-function (TVQfn) framework that uniquely addresses the time-varying nature of finite-horizon optimal control without requiring system dynamics knowledge. Through local consensus error formulation, we transform the finite-horizon optimal consensus problem into a global consensus error-based regulation problem and demonstrate that its solution is equivalent to solving time-varying Riccati equations via distributed control protocols. Our key theoretical contribution establishes that global optimal consensus performance can be achieved through purely local control actions with appropriately designed coupling gain. The proposed TVQfn methodology enables direct estimation of time-varying Riccati equation solutions using linear algebraic computations, eliminating iterative updates and function approximation errors common in existing learning approaches. Simulation results demonstrate superior finite-horizon consensus performance compared to established infinite-horizon methods.
authors: ["Wei Wang;Ke Wang;Chaoxu Mu;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: SAT-GCN: Spatial-Aware Transformer-Enhanced Graph Convolutional Network for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
abstract: In the domain of skeleton-based action recognition, Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) approaches have achieved remarkable progress, substantially advancing the field. Although recent GCN-based approaches have introduced dynamic topology modeling and the learning of multi-scale or long-range dependencies, the capture of distant joint interactions and non-physical semantic relationships remains fundamentally constrained by the inherent limitations of skeletal connectivity. As a consequence, the recognition accuracy of actions requiring global motion coordination or involving fine-grained movements is adversely affected. To address this challenge, we propose a novel Spatial-Aware Transformer Graph Convolution (SAT-GC) module. This module effectively integrates the global attention mechanism of Transformers with the local relational modeling capabilities of GCNs. Building upon this module, a powerful graph convolutional network, termed SAT-GCN, is further developed using a progressive modeling strategy. The proposed network retains the inherent local skeletal topology and simultaneously strengthens the ability to model dynamic and long-range dependencies among joints. This design enables more comprehensive spatial feature extraction from complex action sequences. The proposed SAT-GCN has been evaluated on four benchmark datasets: NTU RGB+D, NTU RGB+D 120, NW-UCLA, and Kinetics-Skeleton 400. Extensive experimental results have demonstrated that SAT-GCN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across evaluation settings.
authors: ["Ying Zhang;Shurong Yang;Qiao Zhang;Yongcheng Cui;Cui-Hua Zhang;Weili Ding;Changchun Hua;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Learnable Time-Frequency Transform With Application to EEG Signal Analysis
abstract: Time-frequency transforms play a crucial role in the analysis of time series such as Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. However, traditional time-frequency transforms, including the Short-Time Fourier Transform and Wavelet Transform, generally rely on manually pre-defined window functions or wavelet bases, making it challenging to achieve optimal time-frequency analysis. To address this limitation, we propose a data-driven Learnable Time-Frequency Transform (LTFT), which is capable of updating its complex-valued window during training through backpropagation. The LTFT spectrogram can be jointly optimized with other gradient-based neural networks, such as long short-term memory and convolutional neural networks, to achieve better classification and analysis performance. This approach eliminates the need for manual design and selection of window functions or mother wavelets, as required by traditional methods. Extensive experiments over a synthetic time series dataset, a motor imagery EEG dataset, multi-class epileptic EEG datasets, and an affective EEG dataset demonstrate that LTFT-based networks can achieve both higher classification accuracy and improved time-frequency resolution when compared to other time-frequency transforms. Overall, LTFT provides a general neural network architecture for time-frequency analysis, serving as a frontend for an end-to-end neural network model to obtain task-related, optimized time-frequency representations for EEG signals.
authors: ["Guoyang Liu;Lan Tian;Weidong Zhou;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Boundary Constraint and Dynamic Graph Feature Decoupling for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
abstract: The weakly supervised semantic segmentation tasks have progressed through pseudo-labels derived from class activation maps. Most methods perform poorly in complex scenes, capturing local foreground features and relying on simple context. To address these challenges, we propose the boundary constraint and dynamic graph feature decoupling(BC-GFD) approach, which is designed to enhance foreground features representations through three key components: the Moment-Constrained Fusion strategy (MCFS), the Dynamic Graph Relational Mapping(DGRM) strategy, and the semantic difference measurement(SDM) strategy. Specifically, MCFS is designed to emphasize and constrain non-discriminative regions, while DGRM manages long-range dependencies between global contextual semantics to extract global fine-grained features. Meanwhile, SDM focuses on quantifying foreground-background disparity, enhancing the ability to decouple local fine-grained features. BC-GFD effectively focuses on constraining boundary features and integrating global-local complementary foreground features to enhance adaptability to complex contexts. Extensive experiments on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 demonstrate the effectiveness of our method and achieve the state-of-the-art performance.
authors: ["Zhoufeng Liu;Bingrui Li;Chunlei Li;Shumin Ding;Miao Yu;Di Huang;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: SageIQ: Scene-Graph-Guided Blind Image Quality Assessment
abstract: Conventional Blind Image Quality Assessment (BIQA) methods typically assess the entire image quality, which is suboptimal for tasks like autonomous driving that concern specific Task-Aligned Region (TAR). Moreover, we observe that advanced Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM)-based BIQA models exhibit bias when evaluating small regions, leading to inaccurate perceptual judgments. To address these issues, we propose SageIQ (Scene-graph-guided Evaluation for Image Quality), a pipeline SageIQ-P for TAR localization, an approach consisting of an MLLM-based BIQA model SageIQ-M, and a dataset SageIQ-D. SageIQ-P is designed to automatically identify and evaluate TARs, with the advantages of being training-free and allowing plug-in integration of off-the-shelf BIQA models without retraining. It operates in three stages: scenegraphbased triplet construction, LLMdriven triplet analysis, and integration of weighted BIQA scores into a final assessment. Since SageIQ-P can produce small-sized TAR crops that may encounter small-region scoring bias in existing BIQA models, we propose SageIQ-M to alleviate this bias by injecting scale information through scale-aware images and size-prompted cues, achieving size awareness across both visual and textual modalities. In addition, we develop a fully automated approach to construct a region-level test set SageIQ-D, significantly reducing the human effort needed. Experimental results demonstrate that our methods achieve superior BIQA performance.
authors: ["Renwei Yang;Zhengjie Yang;Yun Wang;Dapeng Oliver Wu;Shiqi Wang;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Small Traffic Object Detection on Drone Views: A Lightweight Network Based on Neural Architecture Search and Multi-Scale Feature Enhancement
abstract: In the field of intelligent transportation, the integration of drones with object detection algorithms enables the flexible collection of traffic information. To address the challenges posed by limited computational resources on drone platforms and the small object sizes observed from aerial views, this study proposes a lightweight detection network for small traffic objects. Specifically, a new neural architecture search (NAS) method based on the principle of maximum entropy is introduced. By considering actual latency as a constraint, we employ a coarse-to-fine evolutionary search strategy to develop a lightweight and high-performance backbone network. Meanwhile, the model’s accuracy and real-time performance are further enhanced by incorporating a dual-branch anchor-free decoupled head that effectively separates the tasks of classification and localization. To tackle the issue of detecting small objects in aerial images, a cascade receptive field aggregation module (CRAM) is proposed, which embeds receptive field paths of different sizes into the feature pyramid, thereby enhancing the model’s multi-scale feature learning capability. Furthermore, a new Wise-IoU loss with distance attention is employed to more accurately regress ground truth boxes of small traffic objects and improves detection accuracy. Extensive experiments on the VisDrone2019-DET dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The proposed method shows great potential for enabling the implementation of traffic object detection algorithms on resource-constrained devices such as drones.
authors: ["Wei Sun;Xuancheng Liu;Xiaorui Zhang;Tiantian Peng;Quanbo Ge;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: MARTA: Multi-Person Activity Recognition With mmWave Based on Temporal Attention
abstract: Radar technology has been widely applied in human activity recognition (HAR), however, most existing algorithms are primarily relying on micro-Doppler signature for classification to achieve action recognition. While such methods, combined with the advancement of deep neural networks, perform well in single-target scenarios, increasing model complexity is leading to higher computational costs and greater hardware requirements. Moreover, in complex multi-target environments, micro-Doppler-based approaches are often facing recognition failures. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a multi-person action recognition system based on mmWave radar point cloud data. The system employs a specifically designed person identification algorithm that effectively separates point clouds corresponding to multiple targets. Each frame of point cloud data is then subjected to dimensionality reduction, followed by feature extraction using a 2D convolutional neural network (2D-CNN). These features are subsequently fed into a temporal attention long short-term memory (TA-LSTM) network for action classification and recognition. The proposed method utilizes multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar to collect three datasets, which are used to evaluate the performance of person identification, single-person action recognition, and multi-person action recognition. Experimental results demonstrate that the system can accurately distinguish between multiple targets in close proximity. The action recognition accuracy for single-person and multi-person scenarios reaches 96.5% and 92.3%, respectively, significantly outperforming existing point cloud-based human recognition algorithms.
authors: ["Haoming Feng;Huaqing Li;Wenwen Zhu;Denghao Li;Yukun Huang;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: CROP: Conservative Reward for Model-Based Offline Policy Optimization
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) aims to optimize a policy using collected data without online interactions. Model-based approaches are particularly appealing for addressing offline RL challenges because of their capability to mitigate the limitations of data coverage through data generation using models. Nonetheless, a prevalent issue in offline RL is the overestimation caused by distribution shift. This study proposes a novel model-based offline RL algorithm named Conservative Reward for model-based Offline Policy optimization (CROP). CROP introduces a streamlined objective that concurrently minimizes estimation error and the rewards of random actions, thereby yielding a robustly conservative reward estimator. Theoretical analysis shows that the designed conservative reward mechanism leads to a conservative policy evaluation and mitigates distribution shift. Experiments showcase that with the simple modification to reward estimation, CROP can conservatively estimate the reward and achieve competitive performance with existing methods. The source code will be available after acceptance.
authors: ["Hao Li;Xiao-Hu Zhou;Shu-Hai Li;Mei-Jiang Gui;Xiao-Liang Xie;Shi-Qi Liu;Shuang-Yi Wang;Zhen-Qiu Feng;Zeng-Guang Hou;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Feature Smoothing for Generating Transferable Adversarial Examples
abstract: Transfer-based adversarial attacks generate transferable adversarial examples from a surrogate model to deceive unknown target models. Input diversity is an effective technique to enhance the adversarial transferability by shifting the attention regions of inputs. However, current existing input-diversity-based attacks primarily focus on the input space, neglecting the impact of high-frequency components in the feature space. This limits the adversarial transferability because adversarial perturbations primarily concentrate on high-frequency components. In this paper, we propose a feature orchestration (FO) layer to smooth the extracted embeddings via trained low-pass filters. FO filters out the high-frequency components in the feature space, alleviating the overfitting of adversarial noise to the surrogate model. Based on the proposed FO, we propose a novel feature orchestration attack (FOA). Specifically, FOA apply various transformations and mixups to generate diverse variants in the input space, and smooths the extracted embeddings by FO in the feature space. Evaluations on ImageNet and Caltech101 underscore the superior attack performance of the proposed FOA, compared to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines. In particular, the targeted success rates of FOA outperform the SOTA baselines by about 7%$\sim$65% on ImageNet and about 3%$\sim$33% on Caltech101. Even against defended models, FOA achieves an average targeted success rate of over 53%, exceeding baselines by more than 40%.
authors: ["Junlin Liu;Xinchen Lyu;Chenshan Ren;Ni Wei;Jingfeng Zhang;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Box Embedding With Probabilistic Reasoning for FOL Queries Over Knowledge Graph
abstract: The limitations of existing approaches for modeling first-order logic (FOL) queries over knowledge graphs (KGs) have motivated the development of probabilistic reasoning methods. While box embedding techniques provide a flexible geometric framework for complex query answering, they primarily rely on local operator-level transformations. As a result, it becomes difficult to strictly preserve logical constraints, particularly for negation and compositional reasoning under complex query structures. Moreover, approximation strategies such as simple averaging or neural merging operations may introduce accumulated errors during multi-step inference. To address these challenges, we propose an MLN-enhanced box embedding framework that integrates probabilistic logical reasoning into geometric query modeling. Specifically, we construct logical expressions from relations in KG and predicates in FOL queries, and develop corresponding Markov Logic Network (MLN) structures to capture global dependencies among entities and relations. These MLN-derived dependencies are then leveraged to guide the execution of projection, intersection, union, and negation operators in the box embedding space. To ensure scalability on large knowledge graphs with numerous entities, we further introduce a variational expectation–maximization (VEM) based MLN learning strategy, enabling efficient parameter estimation and inference. By jointly modeling the correlations between input boxes and newly generated boxes through MLN parameters, our approach aligns local geometric operations with global relational semantics. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing approaches across multiple benchmark datasets.
authors: ["Zhongbin Li;Kun Yue;Jianyu Li;Lixing Yu;Zhiwen Tang;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Generation and Evaluation of Privacy-Preserving Tabular Synthetic Data Using Self-Attention Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: The rapid advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have led to the generation of synthetic data using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The generation of high-fidelity synthetic data has become increasingly important in various fields, including healthcare, finance, and social sciences, where data privacy and scarcity pose significant challenges for training ML models. In healthcare and finance, where data privacy is paramount, synthetic data provides a valuable alternative to real data, facilitating research and model development. This paper presents a Self-Attention GAN. This GAN significantly improves the performance of tabular data by incorporating a Self-Attention mechanism in the Discriminator compared to other existing GANs. We evaluated our model using various tabular data, comparing its performance with existing GAN-based approaches. Our results demonstrate that the inclusion of Self-Attention improves the ability of the model to capture complex dependencies within the input data, leading to synthetic datasets that closely mirror the statistical properties of the original data. The improved synthetic data ensures privacy while retaining high utility for machine learning tasks.
authors: ["Qaiser Razi;Amit Chougule;GSS Chalapathi;Vikas Hassija;Biplab Sikdar;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Fine-Grained Hierarchical Perception Siamese Network for Battery Surface Defect Detection
abstract: Battery surface defect detection is an essential part of maintaining quality standards in battery production. However, challenges persist when addressing defects with complex and variable shapes, particularly when there is low separability between the defects and the background. To tackle these issues, this paper introduces the Fine-Grained Hierarchical Perception Siamese Network for Battery Surface Defect Detection (FHS-Net), which detects defects by leveraging the differences between the inspected image and a reference image. The framework comprises a weight-sharing visual encoder, a Fine-Grained Enhancement Module (FGEM), and a Hierarchical Perception Decoder (HPD). Specifically, FGEM fuses adjacent stage feature maps from the backbone to capture fine-grained details at shallow levels and semantics at deeper levels, improving defect feature extraction. HPD calculates loss at each decoding layer, forming a hierarchical perception that enhances defect awareness from intermediate layers, progressively improving recognition accuracy. Furthermore, to enrich defect detection datasets, we collected a battery surface defect dataset named BSD, which consists of 2,183 images obtained from actual production lines using an automated optical inspection (AOI) camera. Comprehensive experiments performed on the BSD, NEU-SEG, and Magnetic-Tile-Defect datasets highlight the outstanding performance of the proposed framework.
authors: ["Ying Xu;Yingwen Chen;Yikui Zhai;Wenfeng Pan;Hufei Zhu;Jianhong Zhou;Tianlei Wang;Pasquale Coscia;Angelo Genovese;C. L. Philip Chen;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning via Fractional-Order Gradient Descent With Adaptive Momentum Under Non-IID Data
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralized data sharing, yet its practical deployment is often hindered by slow convergence and excessive communication overhead, particularly under non-Independent and non-Identically Distributed (non-IID) data distributions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes Federated Fractional Order Gradient Descent with Adaptive Momentum (FedFOGDAM), a novel client-side optimization framework that integrates fractional-order gradients with adaptive momentum and bias correction to accelerate convergence and reduce the number of communication rounds (CRs) required for model convergence. By leveraging the memory effect of fractional-order calculus, FedFOGDAM stabilizes local updates and mitigates client drift, while adaptive momentum enhances update consistency across heterogeneous clients. We provide a rigorous convergence analysis under non-convex objectives, demonstrating improved convergence behavior compared to conventional integer-order optimizers. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets under both IID and non-IID settings show that FedFOGDAM consistently achieves communication-efficient convergence and competitive accuracy.
authors: ["Mahmudul Hasan;Yong Xiang;Md Palash Uddin;Jine Tang;John Yearwood;Longxiang Gao;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: Fuzzy-Logic-Based Coevolutionary Neural Dynamics for Nonconvex Optimization With Application
abstract: Solving nonconvex optimization problems is crucial in scientific research and industrial applications. However, many real-world applications often encounter challenges in parameter selections and limited robustness. To address these issues, this paper proposes a fuzzy-logic-based coevolutionary neural dynamics (FLCND) algorithm for nonconvex optimization problems. Specifically, the proposed FLCND algorithm incorporates a coevolutionary mechanism and a fuzzy neural dynamics (FND) model. The constructed FND model employs a convergence parameter that can be adaptively adjusted to enhance the search efficiency and convergence of the proposed FLCND algorithm. Furthermore, the FND model exhibits noise tolerance, which enables the proposed FLCND algorithm to efficiently search the global optimum under constant and bounded random noises. Theoretical analyses are provided to prove the FLCND algorithm's noise tolerance and global convergence characteristics. In addition, the effectiveness of the FLCND algorithm is assessed through a series of numerical experiments. Finally, the FLCND algorithm is applied to two engineering optimization problems, including the design optimization of an I-beam and the manipulability optimization of a multi-manipulator system, demonstrating its practical applicability.
authors: ["Yun Liao;Jiazheng Zhang;Liangming Chen;Juntao Liu;Long Jin;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: LGIEA: A Local-Global Information Guided Evolutionary Algorithm for Influence Maximization
abstract: The influence maximization (IM) problem has attracted the attention of many researchers. However, most of the existing algorithms do not fully use the comprehensive information (local and global information) of the network, which causes the performance of these algorithms to decrease on some networks. To this end, this paper proposes a local-global information guided evolutionary algorithm (LGIEA) for IM problem in social networks. In LGIEA, the local-global information of the network is fully utilized to find the nodes with high potential influence during the evolutionary optimization. Specifically, local information pertains to the neighborhood surrounding the node, whereas global information is associated with the shell value of the node. By leveraging the aforementioned local-global information, we propose an evolutionary algorithm that constructs a novel local-global metric and employs a search space reduction strategy to guide population evolution. Additionally, we design strategies for initialization, crossover and mutation to improve the evolutionary process. Experimental results on 12 real-world networks and four simulated networks verify the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed LGIEA in comparison with nine representative baseline algorithms and four variants of LGIEA.
authors: ["Haipeng Yang;Chuang Liu;Xinxiang Xu;Yuanyuan Ge;Yao Lu;Lei Zhang;"]
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: SleepXNet: DeepSeek-Guided Hybrid Transformer Model for Clinically Interpretable EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification
abstract: Sleep-stage classification using EEG signals is crucial for understanding brain activity during sleep; however, the black-box nature of most deep learning models limits their clinical adoption and practical use. This study presents a novel hybrid framework that enhances both classification accuracy and interpretability. The pipeline begins with Spectrum Attention-Based Bandpass Filtering (SABF), which denoises EEG signals and preserves important spectral features. A conditional GAN is used to address class imbalance and missing data by generating synthetic segments. The feature extraction process uses a dual-path strategy: (i) the Fourier-Temporal Fusion Network (FTFNet) captures time-frequency and inter-channel relationships by utilizing TKABNet and FTLNet, and (ii) parallel CNN streams extract spatially complementary features from both raw and wavelet-transformed EEG. These outputs are fused to form a unified representation that supports rich abstraction. The fused features are passed through a Transformer encoder to model long-range dependencies, a bidirectional GRU (Bi-GRU) for local temporal continuity, and a Graph Attention Network (GAT) to capture physiological transitions. The model feeds the combined output into a fully connected layer that uses softmax to predict the final sleep stage. For interpretability, the DeepSeek module integrates SHAP-based attribution, attention map visualization, and neuro-symbolic reasoning (e.g., spindle $\rightarrow$ N2). DeepSeek also generates clinician-style reports with visual and textual justifications. Evaluations on the SleepEDF-20, CAP, and MASS-SS3 datasets show that the model achieves the highest Accuracy on SleepEDF-20 (88.1%) and CAP (82.0%), while maintaining competitive Accuracy on MASS-SS3 (87.5%), demonstrating strong generalization, transparency, and readiness for clinical deployment.

title: KPViT: Kronecker-Patch Vision Transformer for Musculoskeletal Abnormality Detection
abstract: Musculoskeletal abnormality detection is of great significance to diagnosing musculoskeletal system diseases. However, it is challenging to detect musculoskeletal abnormality from X-rays because of these problems: 1) Lesion imaging findings are often indistinguishable in musculoskeletal radiographs; 2) The imaging findings of abnormal bones are similar to those of normal ones. To solve such issues, a Kronecker-Patch Vision Transformer (KPViT) is proposed for musculoskeletal abnormality detection from radiographs, where the Local Selective Region Aware (LSRA) module is developed to locate small lesions from musculoskeletal radiographs by focusing on local lesion areas in the image, and the Global Fine-Grained Feature Aware (GFFA) module is devised to distinguish similar lesion imaging findings from normal ones by mining fine-grained differences in global view feature maps. Experiments conducted on the MURA dataset show that the proposed KPViT outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, achieving the Cohen’s Kappa of 84.75% and an accuracy of 85.66%, further assisting radiologists in musculoskeletal abnormality diagnosis.

title: Three-Dimensional Geometric Information Based Grasping Points Computation and Trajectory Planning for Human-Mimic Robotic Arm
abstract: The computation of grasping points and trajectory planning are crucial phases for autonomous grasping of unknown real-time objects using robotic arms, particularly for multi-fingered human-like manipulators. These operations should be accurate and fast enough to match the real-time requirements. Although deep learning techniques yield satisfactory grasping performance but they are often limited to trained object classes and require heavy on-board computation. Existing geometric grasp planning approaches typically rely on simplified grippers or object symmetry assumptions, which limit their applicability to low degree-of-freedom (DOF) hands. In this paper, we present a fast and accurate geometry-based novel method to compute grasping points for a human like five-fingers robotic arm to grasp any random object. The proposed method explicitly computes thumb and finger grasping points using visible surface geometry extracted from RGB-D data without assuming object symmetry or object-specific models. A subdivision-based trajectory planning and smoothing approach is adapted and integrated into the framework to guide the fingertips smoothly toward the computed grasping points for stable grasping. A deep learning–based instance segmentation module is used only for object detection and masking, whereas grasp synthesis and trajectory planning are entirely geometry-driven. The proposed method is implemented and experimentally validated on a 20-DOF in-house developed robotic arm using a Kinect RGB-D camera. Experimental results demonstrate approximately 12% reduction in cumulative grasping point error and 17% improvement in grasp execution time compared with state-of-the-art methods. title: Distributed Online Learning for Constrained Nonseparable Problems With Privacy Preservation
abstract: In large-scale distributed systems, data is stored across multiple locations and must be processed in real time to ensure rapid responses to consumer demands. However, this distributed nature introduces significant privacy challenges, as the data often contains sensitive information such as salaries, medical records, or personal identifiers. Considering these factors, this work centers on developing differentially private distributed online algorithms. The goal is to tackle the constrained online convex nonseparable problems over unbalanced directed networks. To this end, we first design an algorithmic framework by leveraging Nesterov’s dual averaging technique, where every node (learner) is only responsible for training a part of the model parameter. Under this framework, we develop a differentially private distributed online dual averaging learning algorithm, termed DP-DARE, by incorporating the stochastic subgradient rescaling technique. We demonstrate that DP-DARE achieves sublinear expected dynamic regret under various Laplacian noise scale parameters (increasing, constant, and decreasing) while ensuring $\epsilon$-differential privacy across all scenarios. Moreover, the robustness of DP-DARE to arbitrary, fixed, but bounded communication delays is briefly discussed. Experimental evaluations ultimately confirm the validity of the analytical findings.

title: MMA-UNet: A Multi-Modal Asymmetric UNet Architecture for Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
abstract: Multi-modal image fusion (MMIF) aims to map useful information from various modal into the same representation space, thereby producing informative fused images. However, existing fusion algorithms often overlook the alignment of multi-modal feature space and tend to symmetrically fuse multi-modal images, leading to unreasonable bias towards a single modal in certain regions of the fusion results. In this work, we first revealed the distribution difference between feature space of different modal. To overcome the fusion performance degradation caused by the difference in the fusion process, we designed a guidance mechanism to accelerate the feature extraction speed of infrared images by the network, thereby reducing the feature-space distribution gap between multi-modal feature. Unlike conventional symmetric fusion schemes that rely on layer-wise correspondence between encoders, we propose a Multi-Modal Asymmetric UNet (MMA-UNet), adopting an asymmetric fusion strategy that enables cross-level feature fusion. This design allows modality-specific representations at different semantic depths to be selectively integrated through cross-level feature pairing, thereby ensuring that features from different modalities are fused within a compatible feature space. Extensive multi-modal image fusion on public datasets, as well as the experiments on downstream tasks, consistently demonstrated the proposed MMA-UNet outperforms competitive state-of-the-art methods in both qualitative and quantitative evaluations.

title: GraphGS: Mitigating Pseudo-Label Shift in Imbalanced Node Classification via Balanced Feature Propagation and Minority Node Selection
abstract: Graph-structured data in real-world applications often grapple with class imbalance, where underrepresented minority nodes result in biased predictions and diminished learning performance. Although pseudo-labeling methods offer a promising solution for addressing class imbalance, they remain susceptible to pseudo-label shift. This phenomenon occurs when class biases in pseudo-labels propagate during data augmentation, further compromising model effectiveness. To overcome these challenges, we present GraphGS, an innovative framework designed to alleviate pseudo-label shift in class-imbalanced graph datasets. GraphGS integrates two pivotal components: a feature balancer that curtails excessive information transfer from majority to minority nodes, safeguarding the unique characteristics of minority classes, and a node selector that identifies high-confidence minority nodes through similarity metrics. Together, these components enhance minority class representations without introducing noise, enabling more equitable and reliable training of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). Comprehensive experiments on diverse real-world datasets underscore the robustness and adaptability of GraphGS. Notably, on the CiteSeer dataset, GraphGS achieves an outstanding 2.60% improvement in accuracy over state-of-the-art methods, marking a significant advance in minority class classification.

title: Robust and Equitable Skin Lesion Classification via Adaptive Feature Alignment and Structured Sparse Interleaved Learning
abstract: Automated dermoscopic image classification remains challenging because of substantial interdataset distribution shifts, severe class imbalance, and high intra-class variability. This study introduces a computationally efficient and diagnostically reliable framework that integrates two novel components: an Adaptive Feature Alignment Module (AFAM) for prototype-guided refinement of pretrained feature embeddings, and a Sparse Interleaved Feature Module (SIFM) that applies structured sparsity within fully connected transformations to yield compact and discriminative representations. Comprehensive evaluations on six public benchmarks, including comprehensive external validation, demonstrated strong generalizability and consistently superior performance relative to diverse baseline and state-of-the-art models while incurring only negligible computational overhead. Quantitative Grad-CAM analysis confirms high spatial correspondence between activation maps and clinically relevant lesion regions, and fairness assessments reveal minimal subgroup-level performance disparities. Ablation studies further substantiate the complementary contributions of AFAM, SIFM, and imbalance-aware optimization. Overall, the proposed alignment–sparsity paradigm provides a robust, generalizable, and interpretable framework for dermoscopic image classification with strong potential for equitable point-of-care clinical deployment.

title: Securing Medical AI: Adversarial Attack Detection and Mitigation in CAD Systems
abstract: Frequency-constrained adversarial attacks introduce imperceptible, high-frequency distortions that undermine the reliability and safety of AI-assisted medical diagnostics, posing a serious challenge to trust and resilience in socially-interactive, human-AI healthcare systems. To address this, we introduce Sentinel, a pioneering framework that detects, classifies, and mitigates adversarial attacks in medical image analysis without requiring training or model specificity. Sentinel integrates a lightweight detection module that uses a confidence scorer to analyze predictions from multiple low-rank approximations of the input image, enabling precise classification of attacks as either gradient-based or frequency-constrained. Uniquely, Sentinel includes a recovery module specifically designed for frequency-constrained attacks, employing adaptive Robust Principal Component Analysis-based denoising to suppress perturbations concentrated in smaller singular values while preserving essential image structure. This allows for effective image reconstruction, an area overlooked by existing methods. Evaluated across four diverse medical imaging datasets, Sentinel demonstrates consistently high detection accuracy, classification performance, and adversarial recovery without the need for model retraining or GPU support, making it a highly practical and scalable solution for integration into clinical AI systems. Additional explainability analyses confirm the reliability and interpretability of Sentinel's predictions, establishing it as a significant advancement in adversarial defense.

title: IDME: Interpretable Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction via Meta-Path Attribute Encoding
abstract: Drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction aims to identify positive or negative interactions between drugs and is critical for drug development, clinical decision-making, and patient safety. DDIs are commonly modeled as graphs, where drugs are nodes and interactions are edges. Although heterogeneous graph neural networks (GNNs) can integrate diverse entities and relationships, existing methods usually treat all meta-paths equally and overlook meta-path attributes, such as edge type and path length. This limits their ability to capture distinct relational contexts and weakens the interpretability of DDI predictions. To address this issue, we propose IDME, an interpretable DDI prediction framework based on meta-path attribute encoding. IDME learns conversion factors for different edge types and attenuation factors for meta-path lengths, and uses them to modulate the message propagation process of GNNs. The framework contains three modules: meta-path attribute encoding, meta-path attribute aggregation, and DDI prediction. The encoding module assigns attribute-aware factors to meta-paths, the aggregation module integrates semantic information from diverse meta-paths to generate refined drug embeddings, and the prediction module produces interpretable DDI predictions. Experiments on three datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of IDME. Moreover, the learned conversion and attenuation factors reveal the importance of specific edge types and the influence of path length, providing useful insights into the underlying mechanisms of DDIs.

title: Deriving a Deployment Threshold for Benefit and Harm in Clinical AI: Multi-Institutional Decision-Analytic Modeling Study
abstract: Background: Clinical AI operates in a health care environment heterogeneous in biology, clinical practice, and documentation, so its benefit-harm balance is deployment-specific: an intervention can help in one setting and harm in another when the determinant of response is not routinely observed. Objective: This study had 2 aims: to derive the deployment threshold at which an AI intervention whose effect changes sign becomes beneficial, using zero-phase component analysis whitening (a retraining-free correction to clinical retrieval embeddings) as a worked case, and to determine whether the evidence needed to apply that threshold exists in the published literature or must be measured locally. Methods: We specified a 3-arm decision-analytic model—no action, universal deployment, and screen-and-treat—for interventions with sign-changing effects and instantiated it on a retraining-free correction to clinical retrieval embeddings. Empirical effect groups were defined by measured response rather than nominal mechanistic tier. Screening accuracy was derived from between-condition variability and tested by local resampling. Transportability was evaluated on emergency-department notes and discharge summaries from 2 US academic centers. A structural sensitivity analysis allowed the downstream value of benefit and harm to differ. Results: Measured response defined 6 benefited and 7 harmed configurations at the base-case regularization. The universal-deployment threshold was p *=0.50; the exact and zero-cost forms differ by 2.8×10 –5 , so strategy cost had a negligible effect on it, and across 6 regularization settings, the threshold ranged from 0.32 to 0.70. Published descriptions did not identify the response-defined state: none of the 55 published systems had been evaluated under the intervention, so response prevalence remained unidentified without classification assumptions. Local screening reduced the minimum required prior probability from 0.210 with 1 scored condition to 0.071 with 6. The nominal mechanistic tier agreed with response in all 52 institutional section-level cells, but 1 benchmark-harmed configuration benefited in all 4 institutional conditions. In the joint fit-and-evaluation resampling protocol, specificity rose from 0.328 at 10 documents to 0.974 at 75 documents. Conclusions: The deployment threshold is analytically identifiable, but the state needed to apply; it cannot be recovered reliably from model identity or the published literature. Deployment validity is therefore local in the setting examined: local measurement is needed when the response-defining state cannot otherwise be established reliably before deployment, and an unsuitable measured state requires local action rather than plug-and-play transfer. The data do not identify any single adaptation method as universally necessary. Trial Registration:

title: Large Language Model–Assisted Semiautomated Data Harmonization Pipeline for the Multiple Chronic Disease Disparities Research Consortium: Framework Development and Comparative Validation Study
abstract: Background: The increasing availability of machine-readable research data has created a growing need for efficient large-scale data harmonization (DH). Although large language models (LLMs) show promise for reducing the time and labor required for DH, their effective integration into harmonization workflows remains an important methodological challenge. Objective: This study aims to develop and evaluate a semiautomated, human-in-the-loop (HITL) LLM-assisted DH workflow as a proof of concept across 8 projects within a research consortium focused on disparities in multiple chronic conditions. Methods: We developed an LLM-assisted DH workflow that combined preprocessing, semantic mapping, variable response mapping, synthetic data generation, data transformation, and iterative researcher review. Using Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT-4o) hosted in a secure academic environment, project-specific survey items were mapped to 114 Consortium Common Data Element (CDE) semantic groups. Semantic mapping accuracy was evaluated based on the Consortium’s consensus harmonization results. Complete and incomplete semantic mappings were distinguished according to construct overlap, and incomplete mappings requiring context-dependent human judgment were excluded for mapped item pairs and CDE semantic groups with and without HITL review. Results: Following preprocessing, 884 survey items were included in the DH workflow, of which 812 were mapped to a mean of 79 CDE semantic groups per project. Mean semantic mapping accuracy for item pairs was 95.9% (SD 5.7%) with HITL review and 86.7% (SD 8.6%) without HITL review. At the CDE semantic-group level, the corresponding accuracies were 98.9% (SD 1.7%) and 94.9% (SD 4.0%), respectively. Across projects, omission of valid semantic mappings occurred more frequently than incorrect semantic mappings, particularly for heterogeneous response structures and subjective constructs measured using different instruments. Pipeline components—including concept-based preprocessing, iterative prompt refinement, and targeted HITL review—improved mapping completeness and supported variable harmonization across heterogeneous datasets. Conclusions: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates that the effectiveness of LLM-assisted DH depends more on the design of a structured HITL workflow rather than on the LLM alone. Combining preprocessing, iterative verification, and targeted human oversight improved the efficiency and reliability of DH while preserving researcher judgment for complex mapping decisions.

title: Nonlinear Feature Modeling Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Electroencephalography for Depression Classification: Deep Learning Study
abstract: Background: Depression is a common mental disorder that seriously affects mental health and quality of life. Traditional depression diagnosis mainly relies on clinical interviews and subjective assessments, which may lead to variability in diagnostic outcomes. Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based computer-aided diagnosis has emerged as a promising, objective approach for depression recognition. However, effectively modeling the complex nonlinear characteristics of EEG signals remains a major challenge for existing deep learning methods. Objective: This study aimed to investigate the applicability of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) for EEG-based depression recognition and to evaluate the effectiveness of KAN-based nonlinear modeling frameworks on frequency-domain EEG features. Methods: KAN was introduced into EEG-based depression recognition to enhance nonlinear feature representation of brain electrical signals. Two representative KAN-based convolutional architectures, ConvKAN and its efficiency-optimized variant ConvKAN Efficient, were systematically investigated for EEG classification tasks. These architectures incorporated KANLinear layers together with dynamic grid updating, enhanced weight initialization, and regularization strategies to improve nonlinear modeling capability while maintaining computational efficiency. Extensive experiments were conducted on the EDRA dataset, and the proposed framework was compared with conventional convolutional neural network–based methods and traditional machine learning approaches. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and -score metrics. Results: Experimental results demonstrated that the KAN-based frameworks achieved superior EEG classification performance compared with conventional convolutional neural network–based methods and traditional machine learning approaches. Among the evaluated models, ConvKAN Efficient achieved the best overall performance, with accuracy, precision, recall, and -score all exceeding 94% on the EDRA dataset. The results indicate that KAN-based architectures can effectively capture the complex nonlinear characteristics of EEG signals while preserving high computational efficiency. Conclusions: This study systematically demonstrates the applicability of KAN-based nonlinear modeling frameworks to EEG-based depression recognition. The proposed framework provides a scalable and effective approach for EEG signal analysis and offers valuable technical support for both theoretical research and clinical applications in computer-aided depression recognition.

title: AI for Poststroke Epilepsy: Scoping Review of Imaging-Based Prediction Models and Implications for African Settings
abstract: Background: Poststroke seizures (PSS) and poststroke epilepsy (PSE) are important neurological complications associated with poorer functional recovery, increased mortality, and reduced quality of life after stroke. Neuroimaging plays a central role in identifying patients at increased risk, and recent advances in AI have enabled the development of imaging-based prediction models that may improve individualized risk stratification. However, the current evidence remains fragmented, and the extent to which these approaches are applicable to African health care settings is unclear. Objective: This scoping review aimed to chart the existing global evidence on the development of imaging-based prediction models that can help in predicting PSS and PSE, especially AI-based ones. The purpose was to look into the imaging techniques, computational algorithms, and validation methodologies used and the representation of African populations. Methods: This scoping review was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodological framework, and the results were presented based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) framework. Articles searched using databases such as PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar involved the application of computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), angiography imaging techniques, radiomic markers, or multimodal neuroimaging techniques in statistical and AI-based prediction models for seizure-related outcomes after stroke. Results: Twenty-three studies published between 2005 and 2026 met the eligibility criteria. The evidence demonstrated a clear methodological evolution from conventional imaging-based prediction models to radiomics, machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI, and multimodal approaches. MRI and CT were the predominant imaging modalities, with cortical involvement, lesion location, infarct volume, hemorrhagic transformation, and quantitative radiomic features emerging as the most frequently reported imaging predictors. Most AI models relied on internal validation, while relatively few underwent external validation. The evidence base was concentrated in East Asia, Europe, and North America, with no eligible imaging-based AI models having been developed or externally validated using African datasets. Conclusions: Imaging-based AI for predicting PSS and PSE has progressed rapidly, but important methodological and geographical gaps remain. Limited external validation, heterogeneous reporting, and the absence of African development and validation cohorts restrict confidence in the generalizability of existing models. Future research should prioritize the development of explainable imaging-based AI models using representative African neuroimaging datasets and their external validation in multicenter studies.

title: CRISPR-HAWK: haplotype- and variant-aware guide design toolkit for CRISPR-Cas
abstract: Abstract Motivation Current CRISPR guide RNA design tools rely on reference genomes, overlooking how genetic variation impacts editing outcomes. As genome editing advances toward clinical applications, incorporating population diversity becomes essential for ensuring therapeutic efficacy across diverse populations. Results We present CRISPR-HAWK, a framework integrating individual- and population-scale variants and haplotypes into gRNA design. Analyzing therapeutic targets across 79 648 genomes reveals that genetic variants substantially alter guide performance. For the clinically approved sickle cell disease therapeutic guide targeting BCL11A, we identify haplotypes that completely abolish predicted cutting activity. Across seven therapeutic loci, 82.5% of guides contain variants modifying on-target activity. Variants also create novel protospacer adjacent motif sites generating individual-specific guides invisible to reference-based design. These findings demonstrate that variant-aware selection is critical for equitable genome editing. Availability CRISPR-HAWK is available at https://github.com/pinellolab/CRISPR-HAWK and https://github.com/InfOmics/CRISPR-HAWK .

title: Seumetry: a versatile and comprehensive R toolkit to accelerate high-dimensional flow and mass cytometry data analysis
abstract: Abstract Motivation Recent progress in flow and mass cytometry technologies enables the simultaneous measurement of over 50 parameters for an individual cell. The resulting increase in data volume and complexity present challenges for conventional analysis methods, which are based on manual gating, are time-consuming and fail to capture unknown or minor cell populations. Advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) technologies have prompted the development of computational analysis tools designed to process and analyze high-dimensional biological data. Building on these advances, we here present Seumetry, a framework that combines flow and mass cytometry data-specific analysis methods with the capabilities of Seurat, a powerful tool for the analysis of scRNAseq data. Results Seumetry offers methods for advanced quality control, data visualizations, and differential population abundance and protein expression analysis. We tested Seumetry on an in-house generated complex dataset of immune cells from different layers of human intestines, demonstrating that Seumetry accurately identifies distinct immune cell populations. Furthermore, benchmarking against public datasets showed that Seumetry aligns with manual-gated results, further validating its use for high-dimensional flow and mass cytometry data. In summary, Seumetry provides a new scalable framework for the comprehensive analysis of high-dimensional cytometry data with seamless integration into commonly used scRNAseq analysis tools, enabling in-depth analysis methods to facilitate biological interpretations. Availability Seumetry code is available open source under an MIT license and the current version can be viewed and used via Github: https://github.com/imsb-uke/Seumetry ; and archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21216681 . Flow cytometry data generated for this manuscript is available via Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11935872 .

title: hpci improves reproducibility of computational biology research by integrating Continuous Integration with High Performance Computing clusters
abstract: Abstract Motivation The reproducibility crisis in bioinformatics and computational biology can be mitigated by using Continuous Integration (CI), a proven software engineering practice, to automate the testing of analysis pipelines and models. However, the adoption of CI in bioinformatics is limited as existing solutions are typically tightly linked to specific CI platforms, specific HPC job schedulers, or require actions from HPC administrators. Results We developed hpci, a platform-agnostic, open-source utility that integrates CI platforms (e.g. GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) with common HPC job schedulers (Slurm, PBS). hpci operates as a standard unprivileged user via SSH, and requires no cluster-side installation. It terminates on the CI runner using the exact same exit code generated by the HPC job, providing feedback to researchers and preventing downstream CI steps if there are errors. We demonstrate hpci’s utility across five diverse computational biology workflows on HPC, highlighting the value of automated testing and continuous analysis for verifying reproducibility in bioinformatics workflows. Availability hpci is implemented in Haskell and is available under the GPL-3.0 licence. Source code and binaries can be downloaded from https://github.com/Garvan-Data-Science-Platform/hpci .Source code is archived in Software Heritage via Zenodo ( https://zenodo.org/records/19587650 ).

title: PhyloZoo: a unified framework for phylogenetic network analysis in Python
abstract: Abstract Summary Reticulate evolutionary processes (events in which lineages merge, such as hybridization, recombination, and horizontal gene transfer) are widespread across nature but cannot be represented by phylogenetic trees alone. Phylogenetic networks have therefore become an important modelling tool, yet existing software is typically tied to specific inference paradigms and provides limited support for working with multiple network representations in a unified and programmable environment. PhyloZoo is an open-source Python framework that lowers the barrier to developing practical, easy-to-use software for phylogenetic network analysis. It provides data structures and algorithms covering the main representations used in the field, together with dedicated visualization tools and robust I/O for all major phylogenetic file formats. A particular emphasis lies on semi-directed phylogenetic networks, which explicitly represent root uncertainty and have so far received limited support in existing software. By offering a shared, scalable foundation for developing interoperable tools and a combinatorial layer that supports computational proofs and theoretical exploration, PhyloZoo enables reproducible workflows for applied, methodological, and theoretical studies of reticulate evolution. Availability and implementation PhyloZoo is implemented in Python and installable from PyPI, with source code, documentation, and examples available at https://github.com/nholtgrefe/phylozoo .

title: FA-MFMR: a multivariable functional Mendelian randomization method that accounts for correlated longitudinal exposures via factor augmentation
abstract: Abstract Motivation Mendelian randomization (MR) is widely used for causal inference using genetic data, yet most existing MR methods treat exposures as static and have limited capacity to analyze longitudinal measurements. In many biomedical studies, multiple exposures evolve over time, are strongly correlated, and share unobserved temporal structure. Ignoring these features can lead to unstable estimation and reduced power. Results We propose factor-augmented multivariable functional Mendelian randomization (FA-MFMR) for estimating time-varying causal effects of multiple longitudinal exposures. FA-MFMR integrates genetic instruments with functional representations of exposure trajectories and a low-dimensional factor structure to capture shared temporal patterns. By separating common temporal variation from exposure-specific components, it mitigates multicollinearity, improves estimation stability, and accommodates sparse causal structures in which some exposures have no effect throughout the observation period. Simulations demonstrate lower estimation error and more efficient uncertainty quantification than competing approaches, particularly for highly correlated and sparsely observed longitudinal exposures. Applied to longitudinal biomarkers in a Parkinson’s disease cohort, FA-MFMR characterizes age-dependent patterns in the estimated trajectory-level coefficient functions while highlighting uncertainty in localized effects. Availability and implementation The developed R package and code to reproduce all the results are available at https://github.com/YQHuFD/FA-MFMR .

title: ProDTI: prior-guided positive-unlabeled learning for robust drug–target interaction prediction
abstract: Abstract Motivation Accurate Drug–Target Interaction (DTI) prediction is critical for drug discovery. While deep learning advances this field, the fundamental lack of verified negative interactions inevitably causes biased risk estimation. Although formulating DTI prediction as a Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning problem is theoretically sound, directly applying PU learning to deep models suffers from early-stage optimization instability and decision boundary ambiguity. Results We propose Pro DTI, a prior-guided PU learning framework integrating domain knowledge into the PU objective. We construct a hybrid prior combining explicit biochemical similarities with implicit semantic representations from large-scale pre-trained models. This prior drives two synergistic mechanisms: soft-label distillation to stabilize the optimization trajectory, and hard-anchor regularization to explicitly penalize reliable negatives and sharpen decision boundaries. Evaluated on five benchmarks, Pro DTI consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, exhibiting superior robustness in challenging cold-start scenarios and providing a reliable tool for computational drug discovery. Availability and Implementation Source code and data are available at https://github.com/WangYu-AI4SCI/ProDTI .

title: Serval: a modular framework for decoding imaging based spatial transcriptomics data
abstract: Abstract Motivation Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics technologies have opened new avenues for studying cellular organization and gene expression within intact tissues. However, the accuracy of downstream analyses depends critically on the decoding step that reconstructs barcodes from fluorescence patterns and maps them to gene identities. Despite a growing number of decoding methods, systematic benchmarking has been limited. Results Here, we introduce Serval, a modular framework for developing and benchmarking decoding methods across diverse spatial transcriptomics platforms. Serval separates key decoding stages into independently configurable modules, enabling flexible integration of alternative algorithms. Using this framework, we develop CoSiD (Cosine Similarity Decoder), a novel method that improves transcript recovery by optimizing cosine similarity to known barcodes. We evaluate CoSiD and baseline methods on synthetic and real MERFISH datasets, showing that CoSiD achieves higher transcript recovery and superior correlation with expression references compared to existing methods. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Serval framework generalizes beyond MERFISH. By extending to the DART-FISH platform, we show that CoSiD improves transcript recovery, clustering stability and supports more direct annotation of complex biological structures such as the human primary motor cortex. These results establish that modular decoding frameworks facilitate robust, platform-agnostic benchmarking, ultimately supporting more accurate spatial transcriptomics analysis across diverse biological samples. Availability Serval and CoSiD are open source and publicly available at https://github.com/Roth-Lab/serval . Code for the simulation and analysis pipelines is available from the repositories described in the Data Availability section.

title: BioForge: a fast and safe macromolecular structure preparation library in Rust
abstract: Abstract Summary BioForge is the first macromolecular structure preparation library for Rust, complementing sequence-analysis libraries such as Rust-Bio with cleaning, geometry-based missing-atom repair, protonation, and solvation as a force-field-agnostic preprocessing stage. Across 22 structures (1439–3 819 839 atoms) on a single CPU core, BioForge scales linearly in wall time (fitted N0.89) versus super-linear N1.17 for PDBFixer and N1.25 for PDB2PQR, completing the 3.8M-atom 9MJN in 5.1 s at 1.1 GB peak (PDBFixer: error, 273 GB); PDB2PQR is limited to fewer than 100 000 atoms. BioForge also compiles to WebAssembly for browser deployment and supports direct embedding into simulation and parameterization pipelines via its application programming interface. Availability and implementation An MIT-licensed Rust library crate ( bio-forge ) and a WebAssembly package ( bio-forge-wasm ) extend the Rust bioinformatics ecosystem with structure preparation, both published on https://crates.io and NPM respectively; the same WebAssembly binary powers a client-side web application at https://bio-forge.app that runs entirely in the browser without a server or data upload. Source code and precompiled command-line binaries are freely available at https://github.com/TKanX/bio-forge ; an archival snapshot of the version used for all reported experiments is deposited at Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21627953 ).

title: RAFA: RNA all-atom structure reconstruction from sparse anchor coordinates
abstract: Abstract Summary We present RAFA, a C++ command-line tool for RNA all-atom structure reconstruction from sparse or partial coordinates. RAFA targets settings in which coarse-grained modelling, low-resolution fitting, or partial experimental interpretation provides RNA anchor atoms but not a complete atomic model. The method retrieves experimentally observed 3–5 nt all-atom RNA fragments, fits them to local anchors, combines overlapping fragment-derived coordinate estimates by weighted consensus, and routes sparse and rich inputs through distinct reconstruction paths. In an independent RNA3DB train/test evaluation, no library–test pair exceeded 80% global sequence identity. RAFA achieved lower all-atom root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) values than Arena in 73.3% of target–mode comparisons, with the largest gains in input modes with the fewest structural constraints. Availability and implementation RAFA is available at https://github.com/wangleiofficial/RAFA and archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20951205 .

title: STiLE: automated tissue microarray dearraying for spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Abstract Summary Tissue microarrays (TMAs) enable high-throughput spatial transcriptomic profiling of dozens of tissue cores on a single slide.
