Furthermore, the fact that model selection in causal inference involves multiple components (causal estimator, ML regressor, hyperparameters, metric), complicates the issue even further. In order to evaluate the importance of each component, we perform an extensive empirical study on their combination. Our experimental setup involves many commonly used causal estimators, regressors (‘base learners’ henceforth) and metrics applied to four well-known causal inference benchmark datasets. Our results show that hyperparameter tuning increased the probability of reaching state-of-the-art performance in average ($$65\% {\rightarrow } 81\%$$) and individualised ($$50\% {\rightarrow } 57\%$$) effect estimation with only commonly used estimators. We also show that the performance of standard metrics can be inconsistent across different scenarios. Our findings highlight the need for further research to establish whether metrics uniformly capable of state-of-the-art performance in causal model evaluation can be found.

title: Product Manifold Flow Matching for Mixed-Type Tabular Data Generation
abstract: Synthetic tabular data generation is increasingly important for privacy-preserving machine learning in healthcare, finance, and other regulated industries. Many current methods embed categorical variables into continuous spaces, which can blur their discrete structure and introduce interpolations between categorical states. Here, we propose flow matching on product manifolds, where each variable type resides on its natural geometric space: continuous variables in Euclidean space, categorical variables on probability simplexes with Fisher-Rao geometry, and ordinal variables on order-preserving arcs of unit circles. Our framework employs coordinate-wise vector field decomposition for manifold-specific processing and geometry-aware midpoint aggregation to capture inter-type dependencies with preserved geometric consistency. We evaluate the method on 12 benchmark datasets that range from small clinical records to educational datasets with over 101 million samples. Results show measurable improvements in generation quality, particularly on categorical-heavy and large-scale datasets. Geometric constraints also exhibit empirical resistance to memorization without explicit noise injection, as measured by distance to the closest record and membership inference metrics. The coordinate-wise structure enables efficient parallel computation that scales well to large datasets.

title: Addressing Methodological Challenges in Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: Time series anomaly detection focuses on detecting unexpected events in time series data. Traditional techniques for this task include SVMs, k -Nearest Neighbors and PCA, while more recent approaches frequently employ deep learning, e.g., using variational autoencoders and graph neural networks. In several studies, these more elaborate techniques are regularly found to outperform traditional approaches. We present an in-depth review of 18 influential papers on time series anomaly detection using deep learning and found recurring methodological issues which lead to questionable or inconclusive results; leakage, modified datasets, and unclear baselines. We illustrate the importance of these issues with a novel empirical investigation and demonstrate it is not trivial to replicate reported relative performance of classical and deep learning methods. We find that older methods are frequently shown to perform worse than our non optimized implementations. We fail to reject the assumption of similar performance between these older and state of the art deep learning approaches on standard benchmark datasets.

title: RLAX: A Reinforcement Learning-Based Framework for Explaining Anomalous Data
abstract: Singling out the most informative features able to discriminate between normal and anomalous data is a formidable problem dealing with the enormous search space represented by the power set of the whole feature set. These features indeed encode the explanation of the deviating behavior associated with selected observations and represent the hidden knowledge of interest for the analyst in many applicative contexts, namely cybersecurity, bioinformatics, and green by AI, to cite a few. In this work, we present RLAX, a reinforcement learning-based algorithm detecting explanations from collections of high-dimensional data sets. The algorithm receives in input the unlabelled data collection of normal instances, a small set of labelled inlier examples, and a small set of anomalies to be explained. Separation between normal samples and anomalies is measured by means of a distance-based outlier score. The designed learning strategy thus induces a ranking among features that allows isolating those maximizing separation accuracy. Beyond an add-only formulation, we investigate a subspace refinement strategy that augments the action space with remove and stop actions, enabling non-monotone refinement and adaptive early termination. Experimental results highlight that the size of the explanation returned consists of a small fraction of the whole feature set, and that the associated accuracy and subspace margin are of remarkable quality. Additional analyses of the refinement strategy further clarify its impact on exploration efficiency and explanation quality.

title: MMT: Achieving Exact Federated Unlearning with Improved Post-unlearning Performance
abstract: Federated learning allows multiple clients to collaboratively train a shared global model by sharing only model updates, such as gradients or parameters, to a central server without sharing their private data. Even though the clients do not share their private data, their shared model updates across multiple communication rounds indirectly influence the global model. This indirect influence poses significant challenges in many real-life applications, where it is necessary to completely remove a specific client’s influence (exact unlearning) from the global model. For example, exact unlearning may be required to comply with privacy regulations such as the GDPR’s Right to be Forgotten, or to remove the influence of malicious or poisoned clients in security-sensitive applications (e.g., jointly trained fraud detection models), where eliminating their influence is necessary to maintain the model’s performance. While retraining the global model with the remaining clients from scratch can achieve exact unlearning, it inevitably introduces significant deployment delays and leads to severe performance degradation due to random initialization, making it impractical for time-sensitive applications. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes two exact federated unlearning algorithms, Bi-Models Training ( bmt ) and Multi-Models Training ( mmt ), that ensure immediate exact unlearning by design while achieving better performance post-unlearning. bmt preserves isolated local model copies during training and uses them to provide a stronger initialization for the global FL model after unlearning. To capture the joint influence of multiple clients, mmt trains a carefully constructed set of sub-FL models on disjoint client subsets to avoid overlapping influence, and then aggregates the most influential unaffected models to reinitialize the global FL model. Our experiments on vision and language tasks demonstrate that bmt consistently outperforms existing exact unlearning baselines, while mmt achieves over $$2\times$$ improvement in post-unlearning performance, all while maintaining exact unlearning guarantees and compatibility with arbitrary federated learning protocols.

title: KARAMEL: Knowledge-Aware Ranking for Multimodal Entity Linking in the Arts via Heterogeneous Graphs
abstract: Discovering and disambiguating entities from multimodal and heterogeneous data is a key challenge in discovery science, where relevant knowledge is often implicit and distributed across modalities. We present KARAMEL, a framework for multimodal entity linking (MEL)—the task of aligning visual and textual mentions to entities in a knowledge base—in the cultural heritage domain. Unlike prior vision–language models that primarily rely on surface-level multimodal alignment, our approach incorporates sociohistorical and contextual knowledge through a knowledge-aware architecture that fuses a vision–language encoder with a heterogeneous graph neural network. This design enables contextual reasoning over complex relational structures and supports robust entity disambiguation under ambiguous or underspecified evidence. To benchmark multimodal discovery in this setting, we introduce $$\mathcal {W}$$ iki $$\mathcal {M}$$ u $$\mathcal{S}\mathcal{A}$$ ($$\mathcal {W}$$ikidata-based $$\mathcal {M}$$ultimodal $$\mathcal {S}$$emantic data for $$\mathcal {A}$$rt), a new dataset that links artworks to Wikidata entities via images, textual descriptions, and structured contextual knowledge. Experimental results on both $$\mathcal {W}$$ iki $$\mathcal {M}$$ u $$\mathcal{S}\mathcal{A}$$ and MELArt show that KARAMEL surpasses strong baselines, particularly on implicit or abstract mentions, while ablation studies highlight the critical role of domain-specific, structured context in learning expressive representations. These results suggest that KARAMEL has potential for other scientific applications where knowledge is critical for better entity linking. Both the dataset and the code are publicly available on Zenodo ( https://zenodo.org/records/23019880 ) and GitHub ( https://github.com/cilabuniba/karamel ).

title: A Survey on Loss-based Regularization for Model Generalization
abstract: Regularization is a central and fundamental research topic in machine learning. Despite the numerous methods developed in current fast growing literature, there is a lack of theoretical understanding and rigorous analysis of regularization. The first part of this paper is an answer to this need: we formulate regularization as a solution of ill-posed problems, examine fundamental principles of regularization, analyze the effectiveness of Tikhonov regularization in linear systems, and propose a consistency principle for the design of regularization methods in both linear and nonlinear systems. Based on these analyses, the second part of this paper is a survey of recent loss-based regularizers. We develop a comprehensive taxonomy and summarize prominent features of these regularizers. Finally, results of benchmark tests confirm the effectiveness of representative loss-based regularizers.

title: Grid-based Decision Tree Learning
abstract: Decision tree learning algorithms, such as Classification and Regression Trees (CART), are commonly founded on heuristics that greedily maximize purity gain. Despite their practical success, the theoretical properties of these algorithms, such as consistency, remain unclear. This paper uncovers a substantial obstacle in analyzing the consistency of decision tree learning algorithms, in which the worst-case purity gain can be zero and a gain value of zero usually results in a non-convergent training error. Building upon this observation, our previous work introduced GridCART, a grid-based decision tree that can yield positive purity gain and achieve consistency under Lipschitz smoothness and a product feature distribution. This article extends the grid-based construction to random forests and gradient boosting decision trees, and establishes consistency-rate upper bounds for Grid-based Random Forests (GridForest) and a square-loss specialization of the Grid-based Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GridGBDT). Experiments on 20 OpenML datasets show that the grid-based ensembles perform comparably to their conventional counterparts.

title: Knockoff-Guided Compressive Sensing: A Statistical Machine Learning Framework for Support-Assured Signal Recovery
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) is a technique used to recover signals from incomplete or compressed measurements, enabling efficient signal reconstruction. However, commonly used methods like $$\ell _1$$-based approaches (e.g., LASSO) do not directly control the rate of false discoveries when selecting the correct signal components, especially in the presence of correlations between measurements. To address this, we propose KnockoffCS , a novel framework that incorporates a knockoff-guided mechanism for support selection. This framework not only controls the false discovery rate (FDR)-a statistical measure to limit false positives-but also employs a separate estimation stage to improve signal recovery. Our theoretical analysis shows that by enforcing FDR control, KnockoffCS can reliably identify the correct components and reconstruct signals, even under conditions that are weaker than those typically required by $$\ell _1$$ methods, while maintaining high accuracy. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of KnockoffCS over existing baselines. In synthetic simulations, KnockoffCS significantly improves support recovery (up to $$3.9\times $$ improvement in F1 score) and reduces reconstruction errors. On real-world datasets, KnockoffCS achieves strong downstream predictive performance, surpassing existing CS methods in 71.4% of evaluated modelâ€“dataset combinations, ranking in the top two among CS methods (compared to the compressed baseline, gains are dataset/predictor-dependent). However, performance varies depending on the dataset and predictor, with certain datasets where compressed signal baselines remain competitive. These results highlight KnockoffCS as an effective and strong competitive alternative that integrates statistical guarantees into compressive sensing, offering both theoretical reliability and strong empirical results.

title: On Kernel Eigen-Alignments of KRR: Reconstruction and Generalization
abstract: This paper investigates the critical role of Eigenalignments between the kernel matrix and learning targets in achieving robust generalization in learning problems. We establish a direct connection between generalization performance in kernel methods and the estimation of Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues of matrices, offering a more intuitive understanding compared to prior work with minimal assumptions. We also show that, since the prediction task in KRR is essentially the weighted sum of Eigenvectors/singular vectors, by analyzing how much error can be caused by perturbations to the kernel matrix, we can then derive a bound on this generalization error using the estimation stability of matrix Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors. Compared with previous work, our analysis concentrates on finite-sample settings and on the generalization error arising from having a suboptimal finite training set. Our findings reveal that in kernel methods, as long as the kernel is of high rank, the near-zero reconstruction error can be trivially obtained, implying that the reconstruction error will have limited predictive power for generalization. Additionally, we establish a generalization bound from an Eigenvalues/Eigenvectors estimation perspective, showing that strong generalization requires increasing Eigenvector alignment, Eigenvalue magnitude, or gaps between consecutive Eigenvalues. Finally, we also demonstrate empirically our simplified risk estimator is able to track testing errors in trailing Eigendirections more closely than the existing literature.

title: FedHybrid-ViT: A Federated-Hybrid Framework for Generalizable Deepfake Detection on Heterogeneous Data
abstract: The rapid advancement of deep generative models has significantly increased the realism and accessibility of deepfake media, posing serious threats to digital integrity, public trust, and information security. Although recent deepfake detection methods report high accuracy on benchmark datasets, their performance often degrades under real-world conditions due to domain shift and data heterogeneity. Centralized models tend to overfit to dataset-specific artifacts and fail to generalize across diverse data sources, while federated learning (FL) approaches, although privacy-preserving, suffer from unstable convergence when trained on non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) client data. To address these challenges, we propose FedHybrid-ViT, a privacy-aware deepfake detection framework that integrates a dual-stream Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) within a federated learning setting. The CNN branch captures local high-frequency artifacts such as blending inconsistencies and compression traces, whereas the ViT branch models global semantic relationships across facial regions. The complementary features are fused to enable robust multi-scale representation learning. The framework is trained using a collaborative federated optimization protocol, allowing decentralized model updates without sharing raw data and thereby reducing the need for centralized raw data sharing. We evaluate the proposed approach on a heterogeneous multi-source dataset constructed from publicly available deepfake benchmarks under both independent and non-IID distribution settings. Experimental results demonstrate that FedHybrid-ViT consistently outperforms standalone CNN and ViT models as well as standard federated baselines. The proposed method achieves an AUC of 0.925 and maintains stable performance across highly heterogeneous conditions, indicating improved robustness under heterogeneous source distributions. These results highlight the effectiveness of combining hybrid architectures with federated learning for scalable and robust deepfake detection, offering a promising approach for distributed deepfake detection scenarios.

title: TACCO: Actor–Critic Contrastive Optimization for OOD Action Mitigation in Offline Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Offline Reinforcement Learning provides a viable solution for tasks where online interaction is costly or infeasible by leveraging pre-collected data for policy learning. However, in an offline setting, the policy improvement process is prone to value overestimation due to distribution shifts, which can lead to policy degradation. Existing methods primarily address this issue through policy constraints or conservative value regularization, but few explicitly model the problem actions from a representation learning perspective. This paper proposes TACCO (TD3+BC with Actor-Critic Contrastive Optimization), a contrastive offline reinforcement learning method based on the TD3+BC framework, designed to address the out-of-distribution (OOD) action problem in offline reinforcement learning. We define OOD actions as those that lack local data support in a given state, do not match the current state, or exhibit low reliability. Furthermore, for dense and sparse reward environments, we design two distinct contrastive learning policies: TACCO-A performs contrastive learning on the actor side between data-driven actions, random actions, and cross-state policy actions; TACCO-B filters reliable samples on the critic side based on high Q-values and low uncertainty, and applies contrastive constraints to both reliable and remaining samples simultaneously. In this paper, we compare TACCO with six state-of-the-art offline reinforcement learning algorithms on the Mujoco and Adroit environments within the D4RL benchmark. Experimental results demonstrate that TACCO achieves superior performance on most tasks, validating its effectiveness in mitigating OOD action interference and enhancing policy stability.

title: SURGE: Structural Perturbation Response Field Guided Residual Distillation for Graph Unlearning
abstract: We introduce SURGE, a graph unlearning framework that treats deletion requests as prediction-level structural perturbations. Graph unlearning requires removing requested nodes, edges, or features from a trained graph neural network (GNN) without full retraining while preserving utility on retained data. Existing approaches either disrupt graph structure through partitioning, approximate removal in parameter space, or rely on fixed neighborhoods that cannot express heterogeneous node sensitivity. SURGE addresses this limitation with a Sense–Repair–Distill pipeline: it estimates a continuous response field over all nodes, solves graph-regularized corrected logits without backpropagation, and transfers the corrected knowledge through response-adaptive distillation. Across seven standard benchmarks and multiple GNN backbones, SURGE achieves leading or competitive utility and forgetting effectiveness for node, edge, and feature unlearning. In a matched 18-cell evaluation across deletion types, datasets, backbones, and ten random seeds, SURGE attains the highest mean micro-F1 (0.8632) and retraining faithfulness (0.0243 test JSD) among SURGE, ETR, MEGU, and IDEA; an ogbn-arxiv ablation further supports scalability on a large graph.

title: Beyond Lipschitz: generalization and optimization analysis for adversarial training under Hölder-type conditions
abstract: Adversarial training improves model robustness but may exhibit robust overfitting. Previous theoretical analyses mostly emphasize Lipschitz continuity of the adversarial loss, while understanding under weaker smoothness conditions (often observed in practice) remains limited. This paper investigates this problem in adversarial training, focusing on the generalization and optimization analyses of adversarial losses under weaker smoothness. We introduce Hölder continuity for the adversarial loss and propose a new concept of approximate Hölder smoothness, extending classical analyses from Lipschitz assumptions to a more general regime. A stability analysis for adversarial training is then developed, forming the theoretical basis for analyzing generalization and optimization. Under these conditions, we establish upper bounds on the generalization error and optimization gap of stochastic gradient descent for both convex and non-convex adversarial losses, and analyze the induced excess risk. These findings apply to a broad class of non-Lipschitz but Hölder smooth losses in deep learning, and offer theoretical insights into how optimization and generalization interact in adversarial training, contributing to a systematic understanding of robust overfitting. Furthermore, we empirically validate our theoretical findings using a practical example, demonstrating that the framework accurately captures generalization behavior under adversarial training.

title: Large Language Model Guided Series Saliency Module for Accurate and Interpretable Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Time series data analysis is an essential task in numerous critical applications, such as air quality assessment and stock price prediction, where the goal is to extract underlying patterns and predict future values. Despite the recent strong performance of deep models in multivariate time series forecasting, their failure to utilize essential trend information may hinder their effectiveness in filtering out anomalous patterns such as sawtooth shapes and spikes, thereby negatively affecting both accuracy and interpretability. To address these challenges, we propose a Series Saliency (SS) module that effectively perceives key trend information during both training and interpretation processes while exploring the previously uncharted sample space. In the training process, we leverage a Large Language Model (LLM) to guide the SS module in adaptively incorporating trend information to improve generalization. While in the interpretation process, we update the SS module to identify trend information for prediction and leverage the LLM’s domain knowledge to provide intuitive natural language explanations. We conduct comprehensive experiments from qualitative and quantitative perspectives to demonstrate the SS module’s superiority and plug-in benefits. Our code is included in the supplementary materials for examination and will be published upon acceptance.

title: CausalCACTUS: A Causally Consistent and Context-Aware Framework for Counterfactual Explanations
abstract: Counterfactual explanations have been proposed to provide actionable insights for complex black-box classifiers by suggesting “what-if” explanations that alter undesirable prediction outcomes to desired ones. Recent advances have emphasized desirable properties such as causality, plausibility, and contextual alignment; however, existing methods often address these objectives in isolation. In particular, causal counterfactual approaches enforce structural dependencies among features, typically assuming access to a fully specified structural causal model, while context-aware counterfactual frameworks focus on improving alignment with user-defined contextual constraints. As a result, a gap remains between context-aware and causally grounded counterfactual generation, especially in latent-space representations, which can jointly address multiple objectives and improve validity across domains. In this work, we introduce CausalCACTUS, a causally consistent and context-aware counterfactual explanation framework that extends the CACTUS method by integrating automatically learned causal structure into latent-space counterfactual generation using a composite $$\beta $$-VAE model. CausalCACTUS incorporates a directed acyclic graph learned from data-driven causal discovery to impose causal feasibility constraints, together with a phase-based latent optimization strategy that improves convergence stability and counterfactual validity while preserving user-defined contextual constraints. Our experimental evaluation across five publicly available tabular datasets and multiple baseline models demonstrates that CausalCACTUS achieves improved context alignment and causal consistency metrics while maintaining competitive performance on standard counterfactual metrics, such as validity and proximity. Ablation studies and qualitative examples further illustrate that jointly enforcing context preservation and causal structure leads to more actionable, trustworthy counterfactual explanations that respect user-defined contexts and causal dependencies in real-world scenarios.

title: Evaluation of a ResNet34-U-Net workflow for automated semantic segmentation of steel microstructures in SEM images
abstract: Automated segmentation of metallographic images can support quantitative microstructural characterisation while reducing the manual effort associated with conventional image analysis. This study evaluated a ResNet34-U-Net workflow for five-class semantic segmentation of steel microstructures using the publicly available MetalDAM scanning electron microscopy (SEM) dataset. Forty-two expert-annotated source micrographs were partitioned into training (29), validation (6), and test (7) subsets before extraction of 378 non-overlapping 256 × 256-pixel patches (260, 55, and 63 patches, respectively), preventing source-image overlap between subsets. The model incorporated an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet34 encoder and was trained using multiclass Dice loss. Three independent training runs were performed to assess reproducibility. On the held-out test subset, the initial pretrained model achieved a five-class macro Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.5950, macro intersection over union (IoU) of 0.4972, and pixel accuracy of 0.8015. Across three independent runs, validation macro DSC was 0.6018 ± 0.0190 and macro IoU was 0.4965 ± 0.0252 (mean ± standard deviation). For a separately defined binary Matrix-versus-non-Matrix task, the model achieved a DSC of 0.8647, compared with 0.8233 for Otsu thresholding and 0.8232 for adaptive thresholding. Class-specific analysis identified substantial limitations in Precipitate and Martensite/Austenite segmentation. Connected-component analysis further demonstrated discrepancies between predicted and reference morphological measurements. Mean inference latency was 18.902 ms per 256 × 256-pixel patch on an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of integrating established deep learning architectures with quantitative metallographic image analysis while highlighting the importance of source-image-level evaluation, minority-class performance, and validation of downstream morphological descriptors. Further investigation using larger and independently acquired datasets is required before industrial application.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Comparative analysis of diabetes-related factors using machine learning on the CDC health indicator dataset: metabolic, lifestyle, socioeconomic and demographic domains
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic disease that continues to pose significant global health pressure, affecting a considerable proportion of the world’s population, with an estimated 537 million people affected worldwide in 2021, with an expected increase of 46% in the number of diabetic patients by 2045 [1]. Diabetes is strongly associated with lifestyle behaviors, metabolic conditions, and socioeconomic status. This paper presents a comprehensive machine learning analysis of the CDC Health Indicator Dataset ( n = 253,680), sourced from the 2015 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS). Following systematic data preprocessing with feature binning and multimodal exploratory data analysis, including interactive correlation matrices, radar charts, Sankey diagrams, animated feature distributions, and other graphical representations to examine data distributions, relationships, patterns, and feature importance. Four supervised classification models were trained and evaluated, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost. All four machine learning models achieved comparable overall accuracy ranging from 83.06% to 84.74%. As 84.3% of the participants belong from the non-diabetic class so the accuracy is driven almost entirely by the majority class due to which accuracy alone could be misleading. The Macro-averaged F1 (0.383–0.396) and balanced accuracy (0.384–0.387) shows the four models performing far closer together than accuracy alone suggests, and the per-class recall reveals a near-total inability to detect the pre-diabetic class (recall ≈ 0.00) regardless of the model choice. This result was confirmed under fivefold stratified cross-validation, in which Class 1 recall was exactly 0.0000 in every fold for three of the four models, and the results persisted across both the original BRFSS encoded data and the binned dataset. All four models were then retrained under balanced class weighting. Weighting raised the recall for the Class 1 (pre-Diabetic Class) recall from 0.0000 to between 0.293–0.310 for three of the four models, where the precision for the Class 1 remained between 0.021 and 0.031 and the overall accuracy decreased to approximately 58.26–73.08%. Cross Validated Class 1 PR-AUC ranged from 0.0243–0.0370 against a base rate of 0.018. These results indicate that class weighting can reduce majority-class bias and improve minority-class sensitivity, but it does not by itself provide reliable pre-diabetic discrimination from the available non-glycaemic survey predictors. Feature importance was found to depend on the representation used rather than being a fixed property of the data. Under the binned representation, general health status and high blood pressure ranked highest; under the original BRFSS coding, in which BMI is retained as a continuous variable, BMI was the strongest predictor by a wide margin. Predictor rankings are therefore reported separately for each representation. Income and education were associated with diabetes prevalence, but because the data are cross-sectional and self-reported, these associations are reported without causal interpretation.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Physics-guided neural network framework for predicting compressive strength of coconut fiber reinforced concrete
abstract: Machine-learning models for the compressive strength of coconut fiber reinforced concrete (CFRC) are usually fitted to minimise prediction error alone and evaluated on random splits of data pooled from many studies. This can hide physically inconsistent behaviour and overstate accuracy. This study proposes a physics-guided neural network (PGNN) that computes five physics-engineered features inside the network: a normalised ACI 209 hydration factor, an Abrams factor, a fiber reinforcing index, an RCA reduction factor and an aggregate packing factor. It also imposes four directional laws (for curing age, water-to-cement ratio, cement content and recycled aggregate replacement) as soft derivative penalties at collocation points that extend beyond the data. The model was trained on 586 source-verified records from 30 studies and evaluated with repeated random splits, leave-one-study-out (LOSO) validation, an ablation study, one-factor-at-a-time compliance tests and extrapolation tests. Under random splits, the PGNN reached R 2 = 0.914 ± 0.033 (RMSE 4.63 MPa), below unconstrained gradient boosting (R 2 = 0.957). Under LOSO, every machine-learning model lost most of its accuracy (R 2 ≤ 0.33; PGNN 0.19) and a four-coefficient physics-only model did no worse (R 2 = 0.40), showing that unrecorded between-study differences dominate prediction for a new study. The physics loss reduced the share of test mixes violating the four laws from 23–100% for unconstrained networks and tree ensembles to 1.3–4.3%, without any post-hoc calibration. When trained on ages up to 90 days, the PGNN predicted 180–546-day strengths with an RMSE of 3.08 MPa, compared with 22.0 MPa for an unconstrained network. For a reference mix, the predicted fiber optimum was 1.0–1.5% and was not imposed by the assumed saturation constant, whereas measured optima varied widely between studies. Physics guidance therefore improves physical consistency and extrapolation along the constrained directions, but it does not replace richer and better-harmonised data for predicting new studies.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Discretisation-induced stiffening and its impact on CNN-based delamination detection in composite structures
abstract: The structural application of composite materials has intensified in high-performance engineering sectors; however, interlaminar delamination remains one of the most critical damage mechanisms due to its low detectability and complex effects on dynamic response. This work investigates the influence of multiple internal delaminations on the vibration behavior of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) laminated plates and evaluates the feasibility of using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for damage identification from modal data. A ply-level finite element model was developed to generate 1,000 damage scenarios, spanning delaminated areas from $$0.004\%$$ to $$3.10\%$$, producing 40, 000 modal field images. As a theoretical innovation, this work establishes via the Courant-Fischer theorem that constraint-release delamination models cannot physically increase natural frequencies; any observed positive shifts strictly represent discretisation errors, thereby defining a numerical noise floor. Statistical analysis reveals that mean modal curvature and frequency shifts exhibit statistically indistinguishable correlations with damage severity ($$r = 0.50$$ and 0.46, respectively). Furthermore, CNN performance is rigorously benchmarked against novel analytical reference predictors derived from the sampling design. The networks achieved accuracies below 0.20 and $$R^2
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Artificial neural network-based prediction of gas turbine fuel consumption and exhaust temperature for fuel management support
abstract: Gas imbalance can increase the operational importance of fuel-use efficiency at gas compressor stations. This study develops a multi-layer feed-forward artificial neural network (ANN) to simultaneously predict fuel consumption and exhaust gas temperature of a MotorSich AI336-2–8 gas turbine using three operating inputs: ambient temperature, fuel temperature, and turbine rotational speed. The study record contains 290 recorded observations, with 235 used for model development and 55 held out for testing. Based on the values encoded in the original test data, the test-set performance is MAE = 10.16 kg/h, RMSE = 11.74 kg/h and R 2 = 0.9933 for fuel consumption, and MAE = 3.64 °C, RMSE = 4.45 °C and R 2 = 0.9880 for exhaust temperature. The maximum absolute percentage errors are 1.764% and 1.490%, respectively, when normalized by the measured value. Sensitivity analysis indicates that turbine speed is the most influential of the available inputs for fuel consumption, whereas fuel temperature has the greatest normalized sensitivity for exhaust temperature. The model should be interpreted as a prediction and decision-support tool within the operating envelope represented by the available data; no direct gas-allocation strategy or quantified national gas-balance improvement is demonstrated.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: LLM-driven design of physics-constrained constitutive models: Two agents are better than one
abstract: Developing constitutive models that capture how materials deform under load traditionally requires years of specialized expertise in continuum mechanics, machine learning, and scientific programming. Large language models (LLMs) have recently been shown to lower this barrier by generating constitutive models on demand, but existing single-agent pipelines lack systematic checks that the resulting models respect fundamental physical laws. To close this gap, we introduce the first multi-agent LLM-driven approach for constitutive model generation: a Creator agent proposes a model tailored to the data, while an Inspector agent critically audits each proposal against nine physical constraints and returns it for refinement whenever a violation is detected. We demonstrate this concept with constitutive artificial neural networks (CANNs) and benchmark it on brain tissue and rubber as isotropic materials, and on porcine skin tissue as a transversely isotropic material with a preferred fiber direction, using two different LLM backbones (Claude Opus 4.7 and Kimi K2.5). Whether a generated model satisfies the physical constraints is assessed numerically, by probing each constraint across a broad sample of deformation states, rotations, and perturbation directions. Adding the Inspector raises the share of exported models that pass all these checks from 90% to 95% for Opus and from 47% to 60% for Kimi. In addition, the generated models are on par with or even surpass expert-designed models in accuracy, extrapolate reliably beyond the training data, and generalize remarkably well to unseen loading paths. Separating generation from inspection thus turns LLM-driven constitutive modeling into a substantially more trustworthy process. The paradigm is deliberately technique-agnostic and scales automatically with advances in LLM capability, opening a promising path toward automated, physics-aware model discovery.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Energy-based characterization of sparse sensor interactions
abstract: Large-dimensional empirical data in science and engineering frequently have a low-rank structure and can be represented as a combination of just a few eigenmodes. Because of this structure, we can use just a few spatially localized sensor measurements to reconstruct the full state of a complex system. The quality of this reconstruction, especially in the presence of sensor noise, depends significantly on the spatial configuration of the sensors. Multiple algorithms based on gappy interpolation and QR factorization have been proposed to optimize sensor placement. Here, instead of an algorithm that outputs a single “optimal” sensor configuration, we take a statistical mechanics view to compute the full landscape of sensor interactions induced by the training data. The two key advances of this paper are the recasting of the sensor placement landscape in an Ising model form and a regularized reconstruction that significantly decreases reconstruction error for few sensors. In addition, we provide first uncertainty quantification of the sparse sensing reconstruction and open questions about the shape of reconstruction risk curve. Mapping out these data-induced sensor interactions allows combining them with external selection criteria as constraints in sensor placement optimization, and anticipating sensor replacement impacts on reconstruction quality.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Damage detection, localization, and sizing in composite structures using modal shape and multi-head convolutional neural network
abstract: Owing to their favorable weight-to-performance characteristics, composite sandwich panels are extensively employed across engineering sectors; however, internal defects often escape identification when relying on conventional, visually-driven inspection routines. This study proposes a data-driven framework combining modal shape, image processing, and a multi-head convolutional neural network (CNN) for automated damage identification, localization, and extent estimation. Damage is numerically modeled by introducing localized regions of reduced stiffness through the insertion of low-stiffness material in the core, skin, or interface layers, enabling realistic representation of structural degradation. The first five non-null vibration mode shapes are transformed into contour images and used as inputs to the proposed architecture. A multi-head CNN processes each vibration mode independently to enhance feature extraction and structural condition classification into four categories: undamaged, core damage, skin damage, and interface damage. Subsequently, a dedicated CNN predicts damage position and geometry based on two spatial coordinates and three shape parameters. Among the evaluated image processing techniques, the residual approach yielded the best performance, achieving F1-scores of 0.99 for core damage and 0.87 for both skin and interface damage. The framework also achieved high localization capability, with an average position error of approximately 4% and maximum relative errors below 5% of the plate dimensions; these localization and sizing results were obtained using the ground-truth damage class to route each sample to its corresponding regression network, and therefore do not reflect the potential propagation of classification errors through the complete classification-routing-regression pipeline. Compared with a previously developed baseline model, the proposed framework reduced the mean absolute error for most geometric parameters, with improvements exceeding 30% in several localization and sizing tasks. Despite challenges in angular orientation prediction, these results demonstrate the potential of the proposed methodology for structural health monitoring of composite sandwich structures.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Machine learning interatomic potential study of grain boundaries thermal conductance and tensile strength in hexagonal boron nitride
abstract: Chemical vapor deposition enables the scalable synthesis of large-area two-dimensional (2D) materials, but the resulting grain boundaries (GBs) can strongly influence their thermal and mechanical performance. In this work, we employ machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) to systematically investigate thermal transport and tensile response across representative 5|7-based grain boundaries in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN). The considered GBs span different defect densities and include both symmetric and asymmetric configurations containing B–B and N–N homonuclear bonds. The developed potential is first validated against first-principles calculations, showing excellent agreement for the phonon dispersion and tensile strength of pristine h-BN under thermal ground-state conditions. Non-equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations predict a room-temperature thermal conductivity of approximately 600 W/m·K for pristine h-BN, consistent with the range reported in previous experimental and theoretical studies. The grain boundary calculations reveal a clear increase in thermal conductance with decreasing defect density, indicating reduced phonon scattering as the spacing between neighboring defect pairs increases. In parallel, tensile simulations exhibit predominantly brittle failure, consistent with the strong covalent bonding characteristic of 2D h-BN. Interestingly, the mechanical response follows an opposite trend: grain boundaries with higher defect densities can exhibit distinctly higher tensile strengths. This counterintuitive strengthening is attributed to the more uniform arrangement of closely spaced defect pairs, which promotes a more homogeneous stress distribution and suppresses stress concentrations. As the defect density decreases and the separation between neighboring defect pairs increases, the tensile strength progressively approaches a saturation-like regime. These results demonstrate that grain boundary defect density can exert contrasting effects on thermal transport and mechanical strength, highlighting the critical role of GB topology in governing the thermal and mechanical properties of polycrystalline h-BN. The findings provide atomistic insights for investigating the thermal and mechanical properties of polycrystalline and defective 2D materials.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: 3PCL-Net: A machine-learning-based framework for accelerating contact-line reconstruction in computational simulations of three-phase flow
abstract: In three-phase flows, a contact line forms at the intersection of solid, liquid, and gas phases. Simulating such flows with the Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) method requires accurate geometric reconstruction of the interface near the contact line. Pathak and Raessi (J. Comput. Phys., 2016) developed a Piecewise-Linear Interface Calculation (PLIC) based geometric framework for three-phase flows. In this framework, the liquid–gas interface orientation is found by iteratively minimizing a volume-fraction-based error function using a Golden Section Search. This minimization runs at every three-phase cell and dominates the reconstruction cost. In this work, we develop 3PCL-Net (Three-Phase Contact-Line Neural Network), a machine-learning (ML) surrogate based on a multilayer perceptron, trained on $$O(10^{6})$$ configurations analytically generated from planar and spherical interface geometries at prescribed contact angles, and replace the iterative minimization with it. The network runs in two schemes: (1) Pure ML predicts the interface normal directly, and (2) Hybrid ML provides an initial guess that is then refined through iterative minimization. We tested 3PCL-Net by integrating it with an in-house solver. Pure ML reaches local speedups near $$20\times $$ and a global speedup near $$4.3\times $$ in three-phase-dominated cases. Hybrid ML matches the baseline VOF error and reaches a global speedup near $$1.4\times $$. The results suggest that 3PCL-Net can reduce the cost of contact-line reconstruction in three-phase flows while preserving the accuracy of the baseline geometric algorithm.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: A holomorphic Kolmogorov-Arnold network framework for solving elliptic problems on arbitrary 2D domains
abstract: Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks (PIHNNs) have recently emerged as efficient surrogate models for solving differential problems such as the linear elasticity model in solid mechanics. By embedding the underlying problem structure into the network, PIHNNs require training only to satisfy boundary conditions, often resulting in significantly improved accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). In this work, we improve and extend the application of PIHNNs to two-dimensional problems. First, we introduce a novel holomorphic network architecture based on the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation (PIHKAN), which achieves higher accuracy with reduced model complexity. Second, we develop mathematical extensions that broaden the applicability of PIHNNs to a wider class of elliptic partial differential equations, including the Helmholtz equation. Finally, we propose a new method based on Laurent series theory that enables the application of holomorphic networks to multiply-connected plane domains, thereby removing the previous limitation to simply-connected geometries.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: On-demand inverse design of metamaterials via denoising diffusion probabilistic models
abstract: The nonlinear and non-unique relationship between unit-cell topology and bandgap properties motivates the development of complementary data-driven approaches for metamaterial inverse design. This work presents a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM)-based framework for the on-demand generation of two-dimensional metamaterial unit cells conditioned on prescribed bandgap properties. We employ a conditional DDPM because its non-adversarial denoising objective enables stable training and stochastic generation of diverse candidate topologies, although it requires iterative sampling and does not provide the explicit low-dimensional latent representation available in variational autoencoders. The model learns a probabilistic mapping from Gaussian noise, conditioned on the prescribed bandgap width and mid-frequency, to binary unit-cell topologies. The results show that the proposed framework generates structurally diverse candidate topologies with low surrogate-predicted errors relative to the prescribed targets. The proposed approach provides a flexible framework for conditional one-to-many metamaterial inverse design and a basis for future extension to broader classes of periodic structures.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Decoding microstructure-property relationships in polycrystals: an explainable GNN surrogate for crystal plasticity
abstract: In this work, a surrogate modeling approach based on graph neural networks (GNNs) is presented to rapidly predict the homogenized stress-strain response of polycrystalline microstructure volume elements (MVEs). Each grain is represented as a node in a graph, with features such as crystallographic orientation, grain size, and aspect ratio, while grain boundaries are encoded as edges. This graph-based representation enables the GNN to capture both local and long-range interactions that govern the macroscopic mechanical response. A synthetic dataset of MVEs was generated using DREAM.3D, covering a wide range of microstructural variations in grain size distributions, morphological anisotropy, and four crystallographic texture classes. Full-field crystal plasticity (CP) simulations performed on these MVEs provided the ground-truth stress-strain data used to train and validate the GNN model. The results demonstrate high correlation between GNN predictions and CP simulations, with strong agreement across different loading conditions and an inference-time speedup of approximately 55,000$$\times $$ relative to full-field CP, achieved up to the reported accuracies and excluding the one-time training and data-generation overhead. The trained surrogate is then subjected to a comprehensive explainability analysis using integrated gradients, providing grain-level attribution maps that identify the microstructural features most influential to the predicted stress response. Population-level attribution statistics, together with cross-validation against GradientShap, trace the dominant attribution to the statistical representativity of each volume element, whose response dispersion scales inversely with the square root of its grain count. Overall, the proposed framework offers an accurate, efficient, and interpretable tool for microstructure-informed mechanical property prediction in heterogeneous polycrystalline materials.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: EVA-PINN: an emergency-aware physics-constrained neural surrogate for multiscale crowd evacuation
abstract: We present EVA-PINN, an emergency-aware physics-constrained neural surrogate for multiscale crowd evacuation. The contribution is not the generic combination of neural prediction and physical constraints, which is established in prior physics-infused crowd simulation, but a pedestrian-level allocation of ten data and physics objectives conditioned on emergency risk and geometry. The reference dynamics combine a social-force law, contact interactions, a reaction–diffusion field, and bounded individual activation. We evaluate the surrogate on controlled synthetic benchmarks and by zero-shot transfer to 100 Jülich and 39 MADRAS real-world sequences. A new matched weighting experiment compares fixed weights, an SA-PINN-style loss-adaptive baseline, and the proposed risk-conditioned weighting on 20 paired scenarios spanning four geometries and five density levels. Relative to SA-style weighting, EVA-PINN increases evacuated fraction by 0.111 (95% CI 0.085–0.141; Holm-adjusted $$p=1.7\times 10^{-5}$$), reduces $$T_{50}$$ by 11.72 s (95% CI 8.56–15.05 s reduction; adjusted $$p=0.00117$$), and reduces cumulative contact duration by 18,092 pair$$\cdot $$s (95% CI 9,504–27,089 pair$$\cdot $$s reduction; adjusted $$p=6.7\times 10^{-5}$$). EVA-PINN also reproduces density-dependent speed reduction, preserves evacuation-time sensitivity to the reaction–diffusion coefficient over the tested range, and achieves approximately 15$$\times $$ lower CPU rollout time than the reference simulator.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Stochastic material characterization of SWCNT-nanocomposites based on multiscale finite element and neural network coupling
abstract: Atomic vacancies introduce uncertainty into the response of single-walled-carbon nanotube (SWCNT)-reinforced polymer nanocomposites, making probabilistic characterization essential for design. This study presents a multiscale framework for evaluating the distributions of Young’s modulus and yield strength in SWCNT-reinforced polyphenylsulfone (PPSU) nanocomposites with SWCNT volume fraction and vacancy level. The novelty is combining representative-volume-element (RVE) modeling, Monte Carlo simulation (MCS), and artificial neural networks (ANNs) to describe defect-driven variability without imposing a probability distribution. Four configurations combined SWCNT volume fractions of 2.5% and 5.0% and vacancy levels of 5% and 10%. To provide a flexible statistical representation of the MCS results, the present work couples the multiscale RVE-MCS framework with an ANN-based non-parametric probability-distribution learner. The ANN does not replace the finite element simulations required to generate the datasets; instead, it provides rapid and accurate probabilistic distribution function (PDF) and cumulative distribution function (CDF) evaluation after training for each investigated material configuration. Increasing SWCNT content substantially increased both Young’s modulus and yield strength. Increasing the vacancy level from 5 to 10% reduced the mean values of both properties by approximately 36–37% and increased the coefficient of variation from about 3% to 6.6–7.4%. All simulated distributions are left-skewed, confirming the non-Gaussian nature of vacancy-driven mechanical variability and the necessity of non-parametric ANN-based characterization for reliable probabilistic nanocomposite design. The ANN reproduced the MCS cumulative distributions with mean squared errors between 8E − 6 and 1.6E − 5 and regression coefficients close to unity. These errors were several orders of magnitude lower than those of Weibull and Gaussian models, demonstrating improved representation of defect-sensitive mechanical-property distributions.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: ProCAMMix: Progressive class activation map guided mixing augmentation with semantic label correction for image classification
abstract: Mixing-based data augmentation methods have demonstrated significant improvements in the generalisation of deep convolutional neural networks for image classification. Although saliency-guided methods such as SnapMix have demonstrated that using training-model class activation maps (CAMs) with semantically weighted labels outperforms area-proportional baselines, two distinct limitations remain unaddressed across this family: the absence of temporal smoothing for per-batch CAM estimates, and the lack of a progressive schedule that adapts CAM influence to the evolving reliability of the network’s representations during training. We propose ProCAMMix , which addresses these two limitations simultaneously. ProCAMMix accumulates stable per-class attention representations through an exponential moving average (EMA) buffer, and introduces a progressive annealing schedule that interpolates from standard CutMix behaviour in early training epochs—when CAMs are noisy and background-biased—to fully CAM-guided mixing in later epochs—when CAMs are discriminative. Label assignment is further corrected by replacing area-proportional mixing ratios with CAM-mass-weighted ratios. Experiments on CIFAR-100 with ResNet-50, repeated over three independent random seeds, show that ProCAMMix achieves $$80.86 \pm 0.21$$% top-1 accuracy, surpassing CutMix by 0.60%, SaliencyMix by 0.38%, SnapMix by 0.22%, and Mixup by 1.40%. ProCAMMix also requires 37% less per-epoch training time than SaliencyMix, and 18% less than SnapMix. Ablation studies run under the full 200-epoch protocol confirm that the EMA buffer and the progressive schedule each contribute independently and positively to classification performance.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: E-PINNs: epistemic physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have demonstrated promise as a framework for solving forward and inverse problems involving partial differential equations. Despite recent progress in the field, it remains challenging to quantify uncertainty in these networks. While techniques such as Bayesian PINNs (B-PINNs) provide a principled approach to capturing epistemic uncertainty through Bayesian inference, they can be computationally expensive for large-scale applications. In this work, we propose Epistemic Physics-Informed Neural Networks (E-PINNs), a framework that uses a small network, the epinet , to efficiently quantify epistemic uncertainty in PINNs. The proposed approach works as an add-on to existing, pre-trained PINNs with a small computational overhead. We demonstrate the applicability of the proposed framework in various test cases and compare the results with B-PINNs using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) posterior estimation and dropout-equipped PINNs (Dropout-PINNs). In our experiments, E-PINNs achieve calibrated coverage with competitive sharpness at substantially lower cost. We demonstrate that when B-PINNs produce narrower bands, they under-cover in our tests. E-PINNs also show better calibration than Dropout-PINNs in these examples, indicating a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Continual learning for autoregressive PDE surrogates under evolving physical regimes
abstract: Deploying machine learning surrogates in scientific simulations faces multifaceted challenges, primary among which is the lack of Continual Learning (CL) capabilities—specifically, the inability to adapt to new physical regimes without significantly degrading performance on prior ones. This is particularly problematic for autoregressive surrogates of time-dependent Partial Differential Equations (PDEs), where small prediction errors can accumulate over long rollouts and new physical regimes overwrite previously learned dynamics. We formulate this adaptation as a CL problem, demonstrating that while standard Experience Replay (ER) is a robust baseline across Advection-Diffusion, Burgers’, and Navier-Stokes equations, storing full high-resolution rollouts can be memory-inefficient. To address this, we introduce Replay-TS , a temporal-slicing replay strategy that stores compact autoregressive windows sampled across past simulations. Through empirical analysis, we show that Replay-TS exploits the low-frequency spectral redundancy of physical systems to enable sparse supervision for rollout steps. By preserving the contiguous historical context and sparsely penalizing the autoregressive target steps, Replay-TS improves retention performance under a fixed memory budget by leveraging higher sample diversity. Replay-TS consistently outperforms standard ER methods across standard 1D and 2D streams, achieving over a 30% MSE reduction in a mixed-physics stream, while remaining architecture-agnostic.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Decoder-free operator autoencoder for reduced-order modeling of dynamical systems
abstract: This paper presents a Fourier-enhanced operator autoencoder (F-OAE) for decoder-free reconstruction and latent learning of dynamical systems. Conventional autoencoder-based reduced-order models compress high-dimensional fields into compact latent variables but recover the full physical fields via a nonlinear neural decoder, thereby introducing an additional reconstruction stage during prediction and deployment. In contrast, the proposed framework reformulates the reconstruction using the branch-trunk architecture. The branch network encodes each field snapshot or response sample into latent coefficients, while the trunk network learns shared spatial basis functions on a fixed coordinate grid. The full field is reconstructed through explicit linear superposition of the coefficients and learned basis functions. Fourier layers are introduced into the trunk network to improve the expressiveness of the learned basis functions for complex spatiotemporal fields. The proposed framework is evaluated through four representative dynamic case studies. The results show that F-OAE achieves accuracy comparable to or better than classical AE-based reduced-order models while providing a more efficient latent-to-field reconstruction path. In the cylinder wake case, F-OAE decreases the total inference time from 0.991 s to 0.559 s. In the physics-augmented Navier–Stokes benchmark, the training-epoch time is reduced from 54.10 ms to 24.00 ms compared with the AE baseline.
journal: Springer Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering

title: Complexities and capabilities of Scan4Safety in NHS hospitals: a qualitative study of a national demonstrator site
abstract: Objectives Data standards and barcoding technologies are implemented in hospitals to uniquely identify objects, people and locations; streamline the management of supplies and inventories; improve efficiency; reduce waste and improve patient safety and quality of care. This study examined the implementation of the Scan4Safety programme at one NHS demonstrator site to understand the hospital experience of adopting these standards, barcoding and related technologies. Methods Exploratory case study design, informed by information infrastructure theory, at one Scan4Safety demonstrator site. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with internal and external stakeholders (n=19), and 67 documents related to the Scan4Safety programme were identified. Interview transcripts and documents underwent thematic analysis. Results Key enablers for Scan4Safety included allocated funding, government role/regulation, executive buy-in/wide stakeholder involvement, patient focus, agile/adaptive approach and data linkage. Challenges were both internal and external, mainly pertaining to data quality, work-as-done and trade-offs. Mechanisms of anticipated positive outcomes and potential risks were also identified. Discussion Scan4Safety benefits are delivered through tracking and tracing capabilities, and automating data capture, alerts and data linkages. For traceability of devices, the benefits depend on the extent to which items are tracked in inventory and consistent barcode scanning at the point of care. Conclusions Linked standards for identification of patients, products, places and procedures, across supplies and hospital processes, constitute a wide-ranging information infrastructure with the potential for significant value to patients and the whole health system.
authors: ["Lichtner, V., Irnazarow, A., Bush, S., Dowding, D., Elphick, P., Franklin, B. D., Jani, Y. H., Songhurst, M."]

title: Enhancing the accuracy of a multivariable prediction model to identify medical patients suitable for same day emergency care services
abstract: Objectives To assess the performance of the Glasgow admission prediction score (GAPS) and ambulatory score (AmbS) for identifying emergency department (ED) attendances suitable for medical same day emergency care (SDEC) services and to derive and validate a novel tool for this purpose, the SDEC Triage Tool (SDEC-T). Methods A retrospective diagnostic study using routine healthcare data from three hospitals in a diverse urban setting (Birmingham, UK). All unplanned ED attendances by adults requiring internal medicine assessment were included. The primary outcome was suitability for SDEC, defined as discharged alive with a length of stay under 12 hours (LOS Results 152 877 attendances were included (median age: 58 years; 54.3% female; 68.4% White ethnicity); LOS Discussion The SDEC-T demonstrated improved discrimination using routinely available variables, balancing predictive performance with clinical practicality. Its design supports implementation across hospitals with varying digital maturity. Conclusions In a diverse patient cohort, the SDEC-T outperformed existing tools for identifying patients suitable for medical SDEC services.
authors: ["Atkin, C., Gallier, S., Hodson, J., Li, L., Evison, F., Reddy-Kolanu, V., Sapey, E."]

title: Online survey assessing US primary care physicians attitudes toward AI use in clinical administrative tasks
abstract: Objectives To examine primary care physicians’ attitudes regarding artificial intelligence (AI) use for administrative clinical tasks. Methods Web-based survey with US physicians in family medicine or internal medicine (N=420, response rate 5.13%). Two hypothetical AI tools for administrative clinical activities were described. We examined physicians’ attitudes towards AI tools, and their associations with practice years, exposure to AI, use case and stakeholder type were evaluated using generalised estimating equations. Results Participants were on average 49.6 years (SD=12.5) and 56.7% men (238/420). Physicians with fewer practice years were more likely to endorse the tools’ benefits (OR 1.70–1.96), the tools’ benefits outweighing risks (OR 1.79–2.06) and their openness to use (OR 1.63–1.83), and were less likely to endorse disclosure of AI use (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.36 to 0.998)). Physicians with AI exposure were more likely to agree the tools’ benefits outweighed their risks (OR 1.51 (95% CI 1.06 to 2.16)). Physicians were more likely to endorse the tools’ benefit to physicians (OR 4.94 (95% CI 4.16 to 5.86)) and physicians’ openness to using them (OR 3.53 (95% CI 2.97 to 4.20)) than they were to endorse their benefit to patients and patients’ openness. Physicians rated an AI tool for notes generation as more beneficial than one for billing assistance (OR 1.73 (95% CI 1.39 to 2.16)). Discussion Although the findings are preliminary, US primary care physicians’ attitudes toward AI for clinical administration varied by practice years, prior exposure to AI, use case and stakeholder type. Conclusion Our findings highlight opportunities to develop training and implementation strategies in service of advancing safe and effective integration of administrative AI tools in primary care.
authors: ["Kim, B., Ryan, K., Kasun, M., Roberts, L. W., Kim, J."]

title: Explainable AI for mortality prediction: a comparative study using the MIMIC-III dataset
abstract: Objectives Predicting mortality is vital for tailoring treatments, improving care and reducing costs. Machine learning (ML) has shown strong potential, often outperforming traditional severity-of-illness scoring systems in intensive care units (ICUs). However, the black-box nature of ML limits adoption. This study evaluates the accuracy of several ML algorithms on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III (MIMIC-III) dataset and applies explainable artificial intelligence to identify variables influencing ICU mortality. Methods A retrospective cohort of 600 MIMIC-III patient records was analysed. ML algorithms tested included support vector machine (SVM), K-nearest neighbour (KNN), decision trees (DT), gradient boosting (GB), random forests (RF), Naive Bayes (NB), logistic regression (LR) and extra trees (ET). Models were assessed with threefold cross-validation using F1 Score, sensitivity, specificity, confusion matrix and accuracy. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was applied to explain key factors influencing predictions. Results Among the eight algorithms evaluated, ET and GB achieved the highest accuracy (98.33% and 98.23%, respectively) with F1-scores above 96%. SVM also performed strongly (97.50% accuracy, F1=94.34%). RF and DT yielded accuracies of 95.00% and 94.17%, respectively. NB reached 96.67% accuracy with 100% recall, while KNN and LR showed lower discriminative performance (76.67% and 75.83% accuracy, respectively). SHAP, LIME and Shapley values consistently identified hypertension, tumours and endocrine and digestive disease as the leading predictors of mortality. Discussion Findings highlight ML’s potential to optimise ICU decision-making and support clinicians. However, reliance on retrospective data remains a limitation, and clinical validation is required. Conclusion ML algorithms are highly effective for mortality prediction, and explainability is key for trust and adoption. When combined, accuracy and interpretability enable ML to safely support informed ICU decisions and improve patient outcomes.
authors: ["Shafiabady, N., Akume, D., Haghighat, M., Ud Din, F., Sattarshetty, K., Karim, A., Zhou, J., Alsharaydeh, E."]

title: Smart scheduling of arthroplasty surgery with machine learning and optimisation improves operating room utilisation
abstract: Objectives Total hip and knee arthroplasty (THA and TKA, respectively) are effective procedures but are costly and resource intensive. As such, scheduling can have a significant impact on hospitals. The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficiency of a surgical schedule generated using machine learning (ML) and mathematical optimisation to current gold-standard scheduling practices. Methods All primary and revision TKA and THA cases between April 2012 and February 2022 from a single institution were included (n=15 267). Data was split by year into training/validation and test sets. Procedure-specific models were trained for predicting operative time. Integer linear programming optimisation of operating room (OR) utilisation using these ML predictions was compared with historic scheduling (using surgeon-surgery-specific rolling average values). Weekly simulated schedules were generated and compared based on OR underutilisation, overtime and cases completed. Results The neural network models performed the best for all four procedures (median MSE: 594.6). This was a 7.1% improvement in 15 min buffer accuracy compared with rolling average times. The ML-predicted and optimised schedule reduced OR underutilisation (p Discussion ML-predicted operative times and optimisation has the potential to reduce idle OR time and improve patient throughput. Conclusion Approaches to surgical scheduling leveraging data maximises utilisation of existing resources.
authors: ["Lex, J. R., Abbas, A., Toor, J. S., Khalil, E. B., Ravi, B., Whyne, C. M."]

title: Data-driven queueing modelling: a simulation case study of emergency department crowding
abstract: Objectives Emergency department crowding refers to a complex state of congestion associated with a set of performance indicators such as occupation levels, waiting times and specific scores. Among current methods to model it, an objective gap exists between forecasting machine learning methods, focusing on prediction precision and queueing and simulation methods, focusing on capturing correctly the effect of decision variables for evaluation and optimisation purposes. The objective of the present analysis is to implement and numerically validate a novel data-driven queueing methodology that can bridge this gap and to show its applicability in a simulation case study. Methods A statistical modelling of the queueing processes, particularly patient departure rates and probabilities, is developed to cross the gap defined above. Using the data from a major emergency department of eastern France, the resultant data-driven queueing network model is validated and applied through a synchronous simulation algorithm. Results The model obtained considers the complex effects of patient arrivals and doctor and nurse allocations while offering an unbiased and accurate measure of long-term crowding. Its application with the case study quantifies the impact of the opening of new Unscheduled Care Services on emergency department crowding. Discussion The new data-driven queueing methodology is able to model and quantify complex crowding effects at a detailed level in an emergency department. Conclusions This study shows an alternative approach successfully bridging the modelling gap by establishing a model that can effectively predict system crowding dynamics under the influence of multiple key variables.
authors: ["Wartelle, A., Mourad-Chehade, F., Yalaoui, F., Laplanche, D., Sanchez, S."]

title: User-centred prototyping solutions to solve adult critical care issues: a scoping review
abstract: Background How user-centred prototyping is carried out to solve adult critical care issues depends on the unique characteristics of this context. This review aimed to characterise prototyping in the context of critical care in terms of the types of prototypes developed, activities used to generate prototypes and settings in which prototypes were generated. Methods Four databases (PubMed, CINAHL, SCOPUS and IEEExplore) were searched for articles published from inception to 25 September 2025, in English, that involved prototyping to address issues in adult critical care. Two reviewers independently screened the search results to identify eligible articles and reviewed retained articles. Results 22 of 860 articles met the eligibility criteria. Role, look and feel, implementation and integration prototype types which combined two or more of these prototypes were identified. Prototypes addressing both role and look and feel were most common. 10 prototyping activities were reported, namely sketching, storyboarding, interactivity simulation, digitalising and adapting paper-based forms, rank ordering, building a functional device model, survey for item selection, card sorting, adapting a predeveloped high-tech prototype to a low-tech version, and revising existing workflow. Six of 22 articles reported multiple activities. Sketching was the most often used activity, and the in-person hospital setting was the most reported. Conclusions Overall, there was a lack of reporting on the details of the prototyping processes. Such details could help future researchers anticipate the unique challenges of prototyping to develop solutions to solve adult critical care issues, learn from prior successful experiences and better plan strategies to address these challenges.
authors: ["Cong, L., Walubita, T., Epstein, R. A., Johnson, J., Beestrum, M., Abahuje, E., Slocum, J. D., Holl, J. L., Ankenman, B., Stey, A. M., Berry, A."]

title: Chatbot interventions for improving mental health among people in Asia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
abstract: Objectives Chatbot-delivered treatments offer tremendous mental health benefits. This systematic review aimed at examining the effectiveness of using chatbots for improving mental health among people in Asia. Methods Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on standalone chatbot interventions targeting mental health conditions, ranging from mental well-being to clinically relevant mental health symptoms (eg, depression, anxiety, stress, affect, distress, insomnia and psychological well-being), were included. Four electronic databases (PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Medline) were searched until 11 December 2024. Results A total of eight RCTs (n=921) were included. Our meta-analysis results by random-effects models showed that chatbot interventions reduced the severity of depressive symptoms by 0.46 (95% CI –0.76 to –0.16, p=0.002, I 2 =73%). In the subgroup analyses, chatbot interventions were effective in reducing depression in clinical populations by 0.54 (95% CI –1.02 to –0.07, p=0.02, I 2 =73%), among Chinese participants by 0.55 (95% CI –0.92 to –0.17, p=0.004, I 2 =81%), and when being compared with traditional bibliotherapy (eg, paperback books or e-book) by 0.47 (95% CI –0.76 to –0.18, p=0.001, I 2 =26%). Meanwhile, chatbot interventions were shown to reduce levels of negative affect by 1.95 (95% CI –3.46 to –0.44, p=0.01, I 2 =0%) versus no treatment. However, no significant effects were found for other mental health outcomes, including anxiety, positive affect and stress. Other relevant mental health outcomes included insomnia, attention deficit symptoms, panic disorder, social phobia, problem gambling and methamphetamine use disorder. No adverse events were reported. Discussion and conclusion Chatbot-assisted therapy is a clinically beneficial and safe modality for treating depressive symptoms in the Asian context. PROSPERO registration number CRD42024546316.
authors: ["Leung, W. K. C., Lam, S. C., Chan, B. C. L., Chow, J. N. L., Wong, Y. Y. Y., Ng, F., Yip, C. C. K., Chan, A. C. K."]

title: Barriers associated with the implementation, adoption, scale-up and sustainability of mHealth in Sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review guided by the NASSS Framework
abstract: Objectives The objectives of this study were to highlight and evaluate the factors affecting the non-adoption, abandonment of and challenges to scale-up, spread and sustainability of mHealth in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and to assess the appropriateness of the Non-adoption, Abandonment, Scale-up, Spread, and Sustainability (NASSS) Framework in the SSA context. Methods A systematic search of published research was conducted using PubMed and Embase research databases from 2012 to 2025. Peer-reviewed studies from SSA countries, evaluating mHealth interventions, were included in this study.
