abstract: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), including abuse, neglect, and household dysfunction, are prevalent and represent a major risk factor for psychological distress in adulthood. Although control-related constructs such as self-efficacy, mastery, and perceived control have been widely examined in this context, the role of locus of control (LoC) remains less well understood. The present study investigated the associations between ACEs, LoC, and psychological distress, and examined whether LoC mediates or moderates the relationship between ACE exposure and psychological distress. Data were drawn from a representative survey of the German general population [N = 2,463; age range 16–96 years; female 1,237 female (50.2%)]. ACEs were assessed using the Adverse Childhood Experiences Questionnaire, psychological distress was measured with the Patient Health Questionnaire–4, and LoC was assessed with the Internal–External Locus of Control Short Scale–4. Structural equation modeling with robust diagonally weighted least squares estimation was applied. Higher ACE exposure significantly predicted greater psychological distress and a more external LoC orientation. Mediation analyses indicated that LoC accounted for approximately half of the association between ACE exposure and psychological distress. In contrast, moderation analyses did not reveal a significant interaction effect between ACE exposure and LoC in predicting psychological distress. These findings highlight control beliefs as an important psychological factor, linking early adversity to adult psychological distress and suggest that interventions targeting perceived control may help mitigate long-term mental health consequences of childhood adversity.
authors: ["I. Behrens", "B. Schmalbach", "E. Brähler", "V. Clemens", "K. Petrowski", "J. M. Fegert"]

title: Overcrowding, conflicts over dwelling space, and mental health: a longitudinal causal mediation analysis in Chile’s social housing context
abstract: Background Access to adequate housing is a current challenge in an increasingly urban worldwide context. Housing is fundamental to mental health; yet causal evidence remains limited due to the complexity of housing exposure in longitudinal studies. We evaluated whether conflicts over space mediate the relationship between household overcrowding and mental health among Chilean social housing residents, with attention to gender differences. Methods We conducted a three-wave longitudinal study with 6-month intervals (2018–2022) in two peri-urban social housing neighborhoods in central Chile. We measured household overcrowding (> 2 people per sleeping room) at baseline, conflicts over space at wave 2, and general mental health using General Health Questionnaire-12 (GHQ-12) dimensions at wave 3 among 660 participants (569 women and 91 men). Because of the small sample size in the men group, the mediation analysis is only for 477 women. We employed causal mediation analysis using quasi-Bayesian methods (1000 iterations) and adjusting for confounders (gender, age, education, household composition, study site, and housing renovation). Secondly, we use structural equation modeling (SEM) to test serial and parallel mediation and to model measurement error and covariance between GHQ-12 dimensions. Results Overcrowding prevalence was 21–25% in women and 10–14% in men. Causal mediation analysis showed that overcrowding has no direct effect on mental health. However, conflicts over space mediated the relationship between overcrowding and dysphoria symptoms (β = 0.20; CI: 0.05, 0.43) in women. SEM shows a significant direct effect of overcrowding on conflicts over space (β = 1.80, p = .001), but no significant indirect effect (β = 0.037, p = .068), nor for the other GHQ-12 dimensions. Conclusions We found no total effect, but an indirect effect of overcrowding on women’s dysphoria through increased conflicts over space. Social housing policies should address dwelling size alongside household social dynamics regarding space.

title: Weather extremes and diarrheal disease: findings from a multi-city study in the Asia Pacific Region
abstract: Background Changes in weather patterns including increasing extreme weather events tied to ongoing climate change is impacting burden of diarrheal disease, yet there is a paucity of data regarding how this risk varies across large urban areas within the high-risk Asia Pacific Region (APR). We investigated the association between weather extremes (temperature, precipitation) and risk of diarrheal disease burden in large metropolitan areas of APR. Method We obtained diarrheal disease records from 17 cities located across the APR, including cities in Nepal, Taiwan, Vietnam, India, Singapore, and Indonesia. We used a distributed lag non-linear model to investigate the association between exposure to weather extremes (high: 95th percentile and low: 5th percentile of temperature and precipitation) and diarrheal disease burden. City-specific risk estimates were subsequently pooled using multivariate random-effects meta-analysis. Results A total of 10,358,987 diarrheal disease cases were included. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in temperature- and precipitation-related associations across cities. At the pooled level, neither extreme low nor extreme high temperature was significantly associated with diarrheal disease, with RRs of 1.02 (95% CI: 0.88–1.19) and 1.09 (95% CI: 0.96–1.24), respectively; pooled associations with extreme precipitation were also not statistically significant. However, extreme high temperature was associated with increased risk in Ahmedabad (RR: 2.32; 95% CI: 1.43–3.74), while extreme low temperature was associated with increased risk in Kaohsiung (RR: 1.83; 95% CI: 1.39–2.41). Latitude-specific analyses suggested stronger associations with extreme low temperature at higher latitudes and somewhat stronger associations with extreme high temperature at lower latitudes. Conclusion Our data point to significant spatial heterogeneity in diarrheal disease burden associated with exposure to extreme temperatures and precipitation. Public health adaptation strategies designed to help communities adapt to health threats of climate change need to account for such heterogeneity.

title: When the frontier is drawn by the poorest countries: comparison-set sensitivity in health system efficiency rankings
abstract: Background Cross-country league tables of health system efficiency rank countries and are used to argue that one institutional form outperforms another. A country’s score depends on the comparator set. We ask how much of a ranking that choice produces, and what survives when it is made explicit and second-stage inference uses methods suited to bounded DEA scores. Methods Input-oriented data envelopment analysis (DEA) was applied to a 2019 cross-section of 70 countries with complete data on four health inputs and one output (life expectancy at birth). Countries were scored against a pooled frontier, an income-group frontier, and a DEA meta-frontier with a technology gap ratio. Bias-corrected scores and confidence intervals came from a non-parametric bootstrap that resampled the decision-making units (B = 1000 replications). Leave-one-out and order-m estimates tested whether the pooled frontier was anchored by one or two observations. Second-stage inference used the Papke-Wooldridge fractional response model and a parametric truncated regression in the Simar-Wilson framework (B = 1000) on three dependent variables (pooled VRS, within-group CRS, meta-frontier TGR), n = 58. Results Two of 70 countries defined the pooled CRS frontier (Gambia, Papua New Guinea). China scored 0.158 against pooled CRS (34th of 70) and 0.997 against pooled VRS (25th of 70; 23 of 70 countries sit on the VRS frontier with score = 1.000, so China is close to the VRS frontier). Within its upper-middle-income group it scored 0.491 (14th of 17), with a technology gap ratio of 0.322. Removing both frontier countries together moved China’s CRS score to 0.169 (rank 33 of 68) while leaving the country ordering nearly intact (Spearman rho = 0.993). The out-of-pocket share was not associated with efficiency on any of the three primary dependent variables (all p > 0.30). System-type coefficients did not reverse sign under VRS, and their 95% confidence intervals included zero on the TGR dependent variable; marginal VRS associations in one control set did not survive the other control set. The United States market-based coefficient was negative in direction but imprecise in the bounded-outcome model. Common support was poor (mean GDP per capita US$4813 vs. US$58842 across fragmented and national-health-service groups). Conclusions Comparison-set sensitivity is the main result. The out-of-pocket association and system-type effects reported in earlier pooled-CRS work do not survive methodologically appropriate re-estimation; they reflect that a pooled CRS frontier spanning all income groups is defined by the lowest-spending countries. China’s financing projections are exploratory.

title: Exploring factors contributing to inappropriate use of antibiotics for common childhood illnesses among parents in Nepal: a qualitative study
abstract: Background Inappropriate antibiotic use contributes to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and is particularly concerning in children, who frequently experience common infections. Evidence on how parents use antibiotics for common childhood illnesses in Nepal is limited. This study explored factors contributing the inappropriate antibiotic use by parents in managing common childhood illnesses in Nepal. Methods This qualitative study was embedded within a mixed-methods study conducted between December 2022 and September 2023. Twenty-six parents of children admitted to the inpatient departments for common childhood illnesses - fever, acute respiratory infections, and diarrhea were purposively selected following a quantitative survey. In-depth interviews were conducted in Nepali until saturation was achieved, audio-recorded, transcribed and translated into English. Data were analysed using codebook thematic analysis with deductive and inductive coding. Results The study identified four major themes with varying understandings of antibiotic use and resistance among the parents. Antibiotics were perceived as strong and effective medicines, particularly when other medicines did not improve child’s illness. Parents exhibited a strong inclination towards using antibiotics frequently without medical consultation, reusing previously prescribed medicines, retaining leftover antibiotics and discontinuing treatment following perceived recovery. Pharmacies were preferred for their accessibility, lower costs and perceived effectiveness of medicines, while financial constraints influenced completion of antibiotic treatment. Geographic barriers further shaped health-care seeking among participants from rural settings, including buying antibiotics from grocery stores. Interactions with healthcare providers and previous treatment experiences also informed subsequent antibiotic-use practices. Conclusion Inappropriate antibiotic use was shaped by parents’ understandings and beliefs about antibiotics their prior experiences of antibiotic usage and healthcare-seeking contexts. These findings underscore the need for improving reliable antibiotic information, strengthening between healthcare providers-parents communication, strengthening confidence in formal healthcare services and addressing non-prescription access to antibiotics.

title: From symptoms to diagnosis: investigation of care-seeking behaviors and pre-diagnostic costs for tuberculosis in Iran
abstract: Background In Iran, despite free tuberculosis (TB) diagnostic tests and treatments, patients face significant pre-diagnosis costs, impeding the End TB Strategy. This study explores care-seeking patterns and estimates direct and indirect expenses incurred by TB patients before diagnosis. Methods The study included newly diagnosed pulmonary TB cases in adults (≥ 18 years) in Tehran, recorded in the National Tuberculosis Patient Registration System from July 2022 to July 2023. Data were collected via telephone interviews using a WHO-based questionnaire by TB coordinators from three medical universities (Tehran, Shahid Beheshti, Iran). Costs in Iranian Rials (IRR) were converted to USD (1 USD = 282,435 IRR, January 2023) and international dollars (Int) using the 2022–2023 Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) rate (76,195IRR/Int). A generalized linear model with gamma distribution identified cost predictors. Results The study included 166 of 212 eligible TB patients (mean age: 61 years, SD = 19.82; 57.2% male, 73.4% literate, 59.6% married, 91.6% in manual/skilled labor, 30.7% from eastern Tehran). Patients delayed care-seeking by a median of 14 days (IQR: 6–40); 5.4% tried self-treatment, Iranian/Islamic medicine, 52.4% visited private providers, and 42.2% used public facilities. Diagnosis took a median of 57 days (IQR: 25–121), fastest by general practitioners/specialists (31 days) and slowest by private hospitals/clinics (63 days). Median pre-diagnostic costs were 148,660,000 IRR (IQR: 52,615,000–329,805,000), equivalent to US$526 or Int$1,951 PPP-adjusted, comprising 48.8% medical, 10.2% non-medical, and 41% indirect costs. Higher costs were associated with private hospital diagnoses (61% increase, p = 0.006), multiple hospitalizations (3.56-fold, p = 0.006), and older patients with comorbidities (35–65 years: 5.04-fold, p = 0.001; >65 years: 4.94-fold, p = 0.001). Conclusion This study highlights the significant delays and financial burden that patients face before being diagnosed with TB. These costs are primarily attributed to TB diagnoses in private hospitals and clinics, multiple hospital admissions, and older age with comorbidities. Strengthening the referral system, building trust in public healthcare, raising awareness of TB symptoms, and ensuring free diagnosis and treatment in public health centers are crucial steps in addressing these challenges.

title: The precarity trap: Modelling longitudinal trajectories of precarious youth employment and associations with mental health in the Australian HILDA Survey
abstract: Background Early employment experiences are an important determinant of health and wellbeing in later adulthood. However, research on the mental health impacts of precarious employment has largely focused on older working-age adults, with limited attention paid to the consequences of employment precarity in young people under the age of 25. This study aimed to identify longitudinal trajectories of precarious employment during emerging adulthood (18–24 years) and examine associations with short- and long-term mental health outcomes. Methods Group-based trajectory modelling and adjusted linear/logistic regressions were applied to panel data from the nationally representative Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) Survey. The analytic sample ( n = 498; person-year observations = 5,856) included participants employed between ages 18–24, with mental health measured at 25 and 35 years using the Mental Health Inventory-Five Item (MHI-5). Informed by a lived experience youth advisory group, employment precarity was measured with subjective survey items capturing perceived job security and job control. Results Two distinct trajectories of precarious employment were identified: persistent high precarity and low and decreasing precarity . Overall, persistent high precarity was associated with poorer mental health at age 25, particularly for females. By age 35, distinct sex differences emerged. For the job security dimension, males in persistent high precarity trajectories exhibited significantly poorer mental health compared to females. Conversely, females had significantly poorer mental health at 35 for persistent low job control. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that early and chronic employment precarity is associated with poorer short- and long-term mental health and suggest sex-specific pathways of vulnerability to different aspects of precarity. Policymakers and employers can help to safeguard the current and future mental health of young Australians by promoting secure and supportive working conditions.

title: Who is not benefitting from contemporary antiretroviral therapy? Correlates of virological non suppression among people with HIV accessing care in a Boston community health center
abstract: Background Despite significant resources invested to control and ultimately eradicate HIV, a subset of people living with HIV (PLWH) have not fully benefitted from treatment advances, even in resource-rich settings. This study aimed to better understand the factors impeding HIV viral suppression in high resource settings with nearly universal access to health insurance and affirmative and culturally tailored care for sexual and gender minority (SGM) PLWH. Methods We used electronic medical record data from 2,843 PLWH at a federally qualified community health center in Boston, Massachusetts focused on SGM clients and PLWH to conduct bivariate comparisons and multivariable regression models assessing sociodemographic, clinical, and mental health characteristics associated with virological suppression. Within the bivariate comparisons, we used the Wilcoxson Rank-Sum Test and chi-square tests. Results The majority (96.2%) were virally suppressed at their last assessment. Those who were unsuppressed were younger ( p p p =.03), be Black or multi-racial ( p =.002) and have a psychotic disorder ( p =.008) but were less likely to have an alcohol use disorder ( p =.02). In multivariable logistic models, risk of alcohol use disorder and having a recorded psychotic disorder documented were associated with higher odds of virally unsuppression (aOR = 0.4, 95% CI = 0.2–0.8 and aOR = 5.8, 95% CI = 2.5–13.8; respectively). Neither the GAD-7, PHQ-9, nor the DAST were associated with viral suppression in similar models. Conclusions Over 40 years into the HIV epidemic, in high resource settings with SGM expertise, PLWH in poverty, who are Black and multi-racial, and those with serious mental illness still need additional interventions to achieve viral suppression. To eradicate HIV in high resource settings, investment in efforts to eliminate poverty and racial inequities and increase access to quality mental healthcare are needed.

title: Development and internal validation of a routine metabolic screening model for current hyperuricemia among gas station workers in Guangxi, China: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Serum uric acid (SUA) measurement is the direct basis for identifying current hyperuricemia (HUA). We developed a non-SUA screening model for situations in which routine occupational health information is already available but a contemporaneous SUA result is temporarily unavailable, delayed, or requires separate testing. Methods This cross-sectional study included 894 workers from 11 gas stations and related operational sites in Nanning, Guangxi, China. Current HUA was defined as same-examination SUA > 420 µmol/L in both sexes. Twelve prespecified non-SUA candidate variables were considered; total cholesterol was excluded because of high redundancy and multicollinearity with LDL-C, leaving 11 candidates for least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) screening. Internal validation used 100 repetitions of site-grouped five-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using out-of-fold (OOF) predictions, discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, candidate screening thresholds, and bootstrap optimism correction. Results Among 894 participants, 169 (18.9%) had current HUA. Sex, waist circumference, triglycerides (TG), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and fasting blood glucose (FBG) met the prespecified selection-stability threshold and comprised the final model. The mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) across repeated site-grouped cross-validation was 0.858 (SD 0.004), and the pooled OOF AUC was 0.866 (95% CI, 0.838–0.893). The pooled OOF Brier score was 0.108, the calibration intercept was − 0.064 (95% CI, -0.322 to 0.192), and the calibration slope was 0.920 (95% CI, 0.791–1.077). At a 10% candidate probability threshold, sensitivity was 92.9%, specificity was 64.6%, and the negative predictive value was 97.5%. Conclusions The five-variable model estimates the probability of current HUA and may support prioritization of confirmatory SUA testing when a contemporaneous SUA result is unavailable. It does not replace direct SUA measurement or predict future incident HUA. Independent external validation is required before broader implementation.

title: Disparities in type 2 diabetes incidence trends during the COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden: a register-based population study
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly affected health care provision for chronic diseases, including type 2 diabetes. However, its effects on type 2 diabetes incidence remain poorly understood, particularly how they differ between population groups, which has not yet been examined in a Swedish context. We aimed to investigate trends in type 2 diabetes incidence in Sweden from 2016 to 2022, and to explore whether potential changes in type 2 diabetes incidence associated with the COVID-19 pandemic varied by sex, age, or migration status. Methods Quarterly incidence rates of new-onset type 2 diabetes were calculated from individual-level register data for a dynamic population consisting of all adults (age ≥ 18 years) in Sweden during 2016–2019 (pre-pandemic) and 2020–2022 (pandemic). Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for each pandemic year were modelled in multivariable Poisson regression analysis using the pre-pandemic years as reference, adjusted for age, sex, migration status, season, and long-term annual trend. Stratified and interaction analyses were performed based on age, sex, and migration status. Results Overall, the incidence of type 2 diabetes showed an increasing underlying linear trend of 3.6% (IRR 1.036, 95% CI 1.028, 1.045) between 2016 and 2022. During the pandemic (2020–2022), the overall type 2 diabetes incidence decreased by 6% relative to the underlying linear trend (IRR 0.94, 95% CI 0.91, 0.97). The decrease was strongest in 2020 (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.87, 0.94) compared to 2021 (IRR 1.03, 95% CI 0.99, 1.06) and 2022 (IRR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91, 0.99). The decline in type 2 diabetes incidence in 2020 was most pronounced among individuals 65 years and older and in the native-born Swedish population. Conclusions During the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden, a decline in incidence of type 2 diabetes was observed that varied in magnitude by sex, age, and migration status. This finding may reflect differential but transient changes in health-seeking behaviour during the initial phases of the pandemic. Our results underscore the challenges of maintaining continuous health care for non-communicable diseases during a major health crisis in society, highlighting the need to ensure equitable access for vulnerable groups such as older persons.

title: Understanding vulnerability to reproductive, maternal, neonatal and child health outcomes in Senegal using a population segmentation
abstract: Background Senegal has made improvements in maternal and child health over the last decades, but disparities in outcomes persist. There is a limited understanding of how vulnerability to poor maternal, reproductive, neonatal and child health outcomes in the country is distributed. As such, this study aims to understand what distinct population segments can be identified among women in Senegal based on multidimensional social, cultural, behavioural, economic, environmental and health-related characteristics and how maternal, reproductive and child health outcomes differ across these segments. Methods This study uses a cross-sectional descriptive segmentation study design based on the pooled data from the 2018 and 2019 Senegal Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) that included 7816 women who had been in a union and given birth to a child in the prior 5 years which was the study population. The segmentation was done iteratively, with the initial list of variables developed and matched with the DHS together with the Ministry of Health and maternal and child health experts. After assessing the associations between outcomes and variables of interest, principal component analysis was used to reduce the number of variables and latent class analysis to create segments based on the fit of the model. Results We found 9 segments that were differentiated by urban or rural location and varying vulnerability to poor reproductive, maternal, neonatal and child health outcomes. The segmentation findings show deep health disparities among women in Senegal, with substantial heterogeneity in health behaviours, service utilisation, and structural determinants across population groups. Conclusions The segment-level analysis of Senegalese women reveals entrenched inequalities in health service access and maternal and child health outcomes. Achieving meaningful progress will require a shift from national-average targets to equity-oriented, data-driven, segment-specific strategies combining health system strengthening, sociocultural interventions, and broader socioeconomic development.

title: Iranian parents’ needs and willingness to use serious games for child sexual abuse prevention: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Child sexual abuse (CSA) prevention requires culturally sensitive and developmentally appropriate educational strategies. Parents play a crucial role in children’s sexuality education (SE); however, limited information exists about their perceptions of innovative educational approaches, such as serious games (SGs). This study aimed to assess Iranian parents’ perceived needs and attitudes regarding SE for CSA prevention, and their willingness to use SGs as a supportive educational tool. Methods This cross-sectional study was conducted among 219 Iranian parents (79% mothers) with at least one child under 18 years, recruited via an online survey distributed across Iranian provinces. A researcher-developed questionnaire, based on expert input and the UNESCO sexuality education framework, assessed parents’ perceived needs, attitudes, and willingness to use SGs. Content validity was evaluated by nine experts (CVR = 0.94, via Lawshe’s method; CVI = 0.99, via the I-CVI/S-CVI/Ave procedure). Test–retest reliability, assessed among 20 parents over a one-week interval, demonstrated excellent stability (Spearman’s ρ = 0.90; ICC [1, 3] = 0.83). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and nonparametric tests, including chi-square, Kruskal–Wallis H, Mann–Whitney U, and Spearman correlation, performed in Python. Results A total of 219 Iranian parents (79% mothers) participated in the study. Almost all parents (99.5%) recognized the importance of sexuality education for children’s safety, and 94.5% reported a need for supportive educational tools, although 74.9% had never used digital games for this purpose. Educational level was significantly associated with perceived need for educational tools (χ² [16] = 31.556, p = 0.012, Cramér’s V = 0.190); in a sensitivity analysis with collapsed categories, the association was also significant (χ² [4] = 14.725, p = 0.005, Cramér’s V = 0.183). Parents with higher educational attainment also showed greater willingness to use SGs (H [5] = 43.688, p p r = 0.264), and perceived need correlated positively with willingness to use SGs (ρ = 0.358, p Conclusions Iranian parents reported a strong perceived need for SE and conditional willingness to use SGs, particularly when content is culturally appropriate, age-specific, and expert-validated. As this study did not develop or test a SG, these findings indicate parental willingness rather than demonstrated acceptability, feasibility, or effectiveness; these outcomes should be evaluated in future intervention studies.

title: Is the health system working for people? Comparison of adolescent and adult perspectives from the people´s voice survey in Germany
abstract: Background People-centred health system performance assessments rely largely on adults, with limited inclusion of adolescents despite their distinct health needs and rights to participate in decisions concerning their health. The People’s Voice Survey is a multi-country, adult-population-representative survey of health system perceptions, but it includes adolescents in the German survey. Germany’s health system offers financial protection and commits to adolescent participation, yet little is known about adolescents’ views of its performance. We aimed to identify adolescent-specific experiences and perspectives by comparing adolescents’ and adults’ experiences and perceptions of health system performance. Methods Population-representative data were collected through an online panel between December 2024 and January 2025. Respondents could choose to take the survey in either German or English. Because adolescents were intentionally oversampled to enable age-group comparisons, we conducted a weighted cross-sectional analysis comparing adolescents (15–19 years) with adults (≥ 20 years) using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Variables included self-reported health status, confidence and autonomy in managing health, experiences during care delivery, and perceptions of the health system. Weighted descriptive analyses and chi-square tests were performed. Results The total sample included 2,698 participants: 257 adolescents and 2,441 adults. Compared with adults, adolescents reported better physical but poorer mental health, lower confidence and autonomy in making their own health decisions and communicating concerns to healthcare providers. Compared with adults, adolescents more frequently perceived medical mistakes and receiving care without feeling sufficiently informed, and reported higher levels of unfair or discriminatory treatment. Adults were more critical of the changes to the health system in the past two years and of the system's overall performance. Despite adolescents’ poorer experiences, they had a more positive outlook on the health system's performance. Conclusions Our findings underscore the need to support adolescents' autonomy in making their own health-related decisions and participating in healthcare through age-appropriate communication and opportunities for independent consultations. They also highlight the importance of directly including adolescents in health system performance monitoring, as relying primarily on adult populations may overlook adolescents' unique healthcare experiences and unmet needs.

title: Vaccine literacy among healthcare workers in a metropolis of China
abstract: Background Suboptimal vaccine uptake remains a public health concern in China. This study aimed to assess vaccine literacy and its associated factors among healthcare workers (HCWs) in an urban district of Shanghai, China. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among HCWs in Shanghai during August–September 2025 using an online questionnaire. The questionnaire collected information on demographic characteristics and five dimensions of vaccine literacy: knowledge, ability, decision-making, specific vaccine, and recommendation literacy. Overall and dimension-specific vaccine literacy scores were calculated. Correlation analysis, multivariable linear regression, and cluster analysis were used to examine relationships among dimensions, identify factors associated with overall vaccine literacy, and characterize vaccine literacy profiles among HCWs, respectively. Results A total of 911 HCWs were included in the analysis. The mean standardized overall vaccine literacy score was 75.22 ± 11.72. Among the five dimensions, knowledge literacy scored highest, followed by ability literacy ( P P n = 550) and a lower-literacy cluster ( n = 361), with the lower-literacy cluster scoring significantly lower across all five dimensions (all P Conclusions The overall vaccine literacy among HCWs was favorable, while scores varied across different dimensions. Overall vaccine literacy was associated with age, position category, monthly income, and child caregiver status. Vaccine literacy appears to be a multidimensional construct with interrelated components. Interventions may prioritize HCWs with lower vaccine literacy and focus on decision-making and specific vaccine literacy. Potential strategies include targeted training in vaccine decision-making and risk communication, standardized information and decision-support tools, clear recommendation responsibilities, and rapid referral, appointment, and vaccination feedback.

title: Where are rabies cases lost along the surveillance pathway? A comparative evaluation of participatory and passive rabies surveillance in urban Lilongwe, Malawi
abstract: Background Rabies remains under-ascertained in many endemic settings, from limited effective surveillance and timely public health interventions, particularly in low-resource countries. Participatory surveillance has the potential to improve case detection, but evidence of its effect on surveillance attrition, case ascertainment, and public health decision-making remains limited. We evaluated a participatory rabies surveillance programme implemented in urban Lilongwe, Malawi, during a six-month pilot (January–June 2020). Methods Programme records from the pilot were retrospectively analysed. Surveillance progression was tracked from reporting through traceability assessment, investigation, and final case classification. Case retention, case ascertainment, and diagnostic yield were compared between participatory and passive surveillance pathways. Historical rabies diagnostic records from corresponding January–June periods during 2015–2019 served as a comparator. Results Of 610 suspected rabies reports, 393 (64.4%) were lost before traceability could be established. Of the 217 traceable reports, a further 67 (30.9%) did not progress from traceability assessment to investigation and final classification. Overall, only 150 reports (24.6%) completed the surveillance pathway. Participatory surveillance retained all reports through classification compared with 104 of 564 (18.4%) passive reports ( p p = 0.001). Participatory surveillance identified 13 of 20 (65.0%) confirmed or probable rabies cases, including all nine laboratory-confirmed cases detected during the study period. Compared with historical routine surveillance, participatory surveillance was associated with a 2.4-fold increase in laboratory-confirmed rabies detection and a 4.8-fold increase in overall case ascertainment. Among investigated bite exposures, 136 of 141 (96.5%) initiated post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), although only 16 (11.8%) were linked to confirmed or probable rabies exposures. Conclusion Rabies cases were lost predominantly between initial reporting and traceability assessment, with further attrition before investigation and final classification. Participatory surveillance reduced surveillance losses, improved case ascertainment, and generated more timely animal health evidence to support One Health public health decision-making, including more appropriate PEP use.

title: Insights from the young people who serve on youth advisory councils in Africa: a mixed-methods study
abstract: Background Youth Advisory Councils (YAC) are increasingly recognized as key mechanisms to promote meaningful youth engagement. Despite the rapidly growing adolescent population in Africa, existing research on youth engagement largely focuses on barriers to youth engagement in non-African contexts. This mixed-methods study expands understanding of youth engagement by examining who participates in YACs in Africa, how YAC members in Africa define meaningful youth engagement, and what factors facilitate their participation. Methods This cross-sectional study draws on quantitative surveys ( n = 154) and qualitative interviews ( n = 14) with current or past YAC members living in Africa (aged 18–30 years old). Quantitative data were summarized using descriptive statistics and interviews were analyzed thematically. Findings from both sources were triangulated to identify key patterns. Results Participants resided across 15 countries, and the majority were current YAC members (94.2%). Despite diverse experiences within their roles on advisory councils, YAC members shared a common conceptualization of meaningful youth engagement, including co-creating and valuing youth voices. Further, YAC members voiced that co-creating and valuing youth voices is attainable through two key factors: integrating youth perspectives into organizational frameworks and providing key support. However, many participants’ lived experiences as youth advisors fell short of true meaningful youth engagement. Conclusions Our findings underscore the importance of youth-led engagement in Africa and organizational support to foster meaningful youth engagement, particularly in light of the continent’s rapidly expanding youth demographic. Engaging and amplifying the voices of adolescents when developing policies and advocating for solutions is essential for both youth development and social and economic outcomes.

title: Dietary patterns and adult mental health: a systematic review of observational studies
abstract: Background Diet is a factor related to individuals' lifestyle that has been widely studied in relation to its association with common mental disorders (depression and anxiety). However, the relationship between dietary patterns and these mental health conditions has not been systematically reviewed. The purpose of the present study was to systematically review and synthesize published research on associations between common mental disorders and dietary patterns in adults. Methods The present systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Six electronic databases were searched through 2024, without restrictions regarding the initial year of publication and the selected articles were imported into Rayyan Web® software. Two reviewers independently selected and extracted data, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools. The results were presented in tables, text, and forest plots. The results were presented in tables, text, and forest plots. Results A total of 26 studies were included: 20 examined depression, 5 examined anxiety, and one assessed both conditions. The number of participants ranged from 135 to 14,541. The results of this review suggest an inverse association between healthy dietary patterns and common mental disorders (especially for depression, which had the largest number of articles available in the literature ( n = 20). Evidence regarding anxiety was limited and inconsistent due to the small number of available studies. The association with unhealthy dietary patterns is still unclear, due to the high heterogeneity of the results found in the studies. Mixed and mixed-alcoholic patterns were also not consistently associated with the common mental disorders analyzed. Conclusion Healthy dietary patterns may be associated, particularly, with a lower frequency of depression. Thus, although the results reinforce the importance of diet as a key component of mental health promotion strategies, more robust future studies are needed to better understand these associations.

title: Sleep health and stroke risk: complementary analyses of CHARLS and the UK Biobank, including genetic susceptibility in the UK Biobank
abstract: Background Previous prospective studies have linked sleep patterns and genetic susceptibility with cardiovascular disease and stroke risk. However, less is known about how specific sleep dimensions, potential cardiometabolic pathways, and stroke-specific genetic susceptibility complement composite sleep-pattern analyses across distinct populations. We therefore examined these questions using two population-based cohorts from China and the United Kingdom. Methods This prospective analysis included 11,574 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) and 485,014 participants from the UK Biobank. In CHARLS, nighttime sleep duration, daytime napping, and restless sleep were examined in relation to incident stroke, with hypertension and heart disease evaluated separately as potential mediators. In the UK Biobank, a five-component sleep score was constructed from sleep duration, chronotype, insomnia, snoring, and daytime sleepiness; sleep patterns were classified as healthy (scores 0–1), moderate (2–3), or poor (4–5), and polygenic risk score (PRS) was categorized into low, intermediate, and high genetic risk according to tertiles. CHARLS participants were followed through the 2013, 2015, and 2018 survey waves, providing up to approximately 7 years of follow-up. During follow-up, 707 incident stroke events occurred in CHARLS and 8,929 incident ischemic stroke events occurred in the UK Biobank Cox analysis. Cox proportional hazards models and mediation analyses were performed. Results In CHARLS, nighttime sleep duration and daytime napping were not significantly associated with incident stroke after multivariable adjustment, whereas restless sleep most or all of the time was associated with higher stroke risk compared with rare or no restless sleep (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.00–1.48). Mediation analyses suggested potential indirect contributions through hypertension (19.5% mediated, 95% CI 4.0%–49.0%) and heart disease (17.0% mediated, 95% CI 6.0%–42.0%). In the UK Biobank, each 1-point increase in sleep score was associated with higher ischemic stroke risk (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.05–1.09). Compared with a healthy sleep pattern, moderate and poor sleep patterns were associated with HRs of 1.10 (95% CI 1.05–1.14) and 1.29 (95% CI 1.16–1.44), respectively. In the joint analysis, compared with low genetic risk plus healthy sleep, high genetic risk combined with moderate or poor sleep was associated with HRs of 2.11 (95% CI 1.83–2.43) and 2.09 (95% CI 1.54–2.84), respectively. Conclusions Across two population-based cohorts, stroke risk appeared to vary according to both sleep health and genetic background. These findings suggest that multidimensional sleep assessment, particularly when considered alongside cardiometabolic conditions and inherited risk, may help refine population-level stroke prevention strategies.

title: Outcomes of severe acute malnutrition management in therapeutic feeding centres: a retrospective records study in Yemen (2025)
abstract: Introduction Severe acute malnutrition (SAM) remains a major public health concern in countries affected by humanitarian crises, particularly in conflict settings. Therapeutic Feeding Centres (TFCs) play a crucial role in the management of children with complicated SAM. This study assessed treatment outcomes and key performance indicators — including recovery, mortality, and default rates — across TFCs in Yemen in order to identify potential areas for programme improvement. Method A retrospective secondary analysis was conducted using anonymized routine programme data from TFCs in the ten governorates under the internationally recognised Government of Yemen. Aggregate performance indicators were first analysed across all governorates. Aden was selected as it is the capital and the most populous included governorate; a descriptive comparison of its two TFCs was subsequently performed. RESULTS: Mean recovery (97.10%), mortality (0.67%) and default (2.23%) rates across the governorates were generally within the Sphere recommended standards. However, the aggregate data for Aden governorate were the lowest (92.27%, 1.25%, 6.48%). Within Aden, the PHC-based TFC (recovery rate = 98.25%, mortality rate = 0.22%, default rate = 1.53%) showed better programme indicators than the hospital-based TFC (recovery rate = 86.07%, mortality rate = 2.70%, default rate = 11.23%). The PHC-based facility also demonstrated a more even distribution of admissions throughout the year. However, as this comparison was limited to two facilities, the observed differences may also reflect unmeasured contextual and organisational factors. CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest that the organization and context of TFC service delivery may be associated with differences in programme performance in humanitarian settings. Results should be interpreted with caution because of the limited sample and observational design. Larger multicentre studies are needed to determine whether specific service delivery models are associated with improved treatment outcomes and to inform national nutrition policies in conflict-affected settings.

title: Prevalence of active trachoma among children aged 1–9 years in Ethiopia: umbrella review
abstract: Background Trachoma ranks as the third leading cause of avoidable blindness, behind cataracts and glaucoma. While numerous studies have estimated its prevalence and identified potential risk factors, the reported findings remain inconsistent. This umbrella review synthesizes existing systematic reviews and meta-analyses to provide a consolidated, comprehensive overview of active trachoma prevalence and its associated factors to inform targeted public health interventions. Methods The databases searched include Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed Central, CINAHL, EMBASE, and Google Scholar for relevant systematic reviews and meta-analyses. This study synthesized data from five systematic reviews and Meta analyses published from beginning through November 27, 2025. Five authors independently extracted data for analysis in STATA 17.0. The Joanna Briggs Institute rating technique for prevalence data was used to evaluate the methodological quality. In accordance with standard Cochrane and PRISMA guidance, publication bias was not formally evaluated using funnel plots or egger’s test, as a total number of included systematic reviews was less than 10 ( n Results Out of 876 articles retrieved, five met the inclusion criteria, representing a total sample of 745,994 children. As broad summary of the currently available evidence rather than an absolute national figure, the overall pooled national prevalence of active trachoma among children aged 1–9 years was 22.28% (95% CI: 19.51, 25.06). Non-latrine utilization [AOR = 3.79; 95% CI: 2.29, 5.29] and lack of soap usage for face washing [AOR = 2.92; 95% CI: 1.43, 4.40] were significantly associated with an increased risk of active trachoma. Conclusion Active trachoma remains a major public health concern among children aged 1–9 years in Ethiopia, with pooled estimates exceeding WHO elimination targets. Synthesized evidence demonstrated significant statistical associations between active trachoma and key individual and environmental factors, including non-utilization of latrines and face washing without soap. To accelerate progress towards elimination targets, comprehensive interventions should focus on expanding sanitation infrastructure and promoting facial hygiene within the multi-component WHO SAFE framework.

title: Nationwide epidemiology of laboratory-confirmed Vibrio and Shewanella infections in Denmark, 2019–2025
abstract: Background Vibrio and Shewanella infections are climate-sensitive marine bacterial infections of increasing public health relevance in northern Europe, particularly in areas with brackish or low-salinity waters. Previous nationwide Danish data described infection patterns through 2018, but registry-linked severity outcomes and a standardised episode-based baseline for routine surveillance have not been described. We characterised laboratory-confirmed infections in Denmark during 2019–2025 and established an epidemiological baseline for national surveillance. Methods We conducted a nationwide registry-linked study using the Danish Microbiology Database linked to demographic, geographical, hospitalisation and mortality registries. Infection episodes were constructed using a six-month algorithm applied separately by species, and one representative specimen category was selected per episode using a predefined hierarchy. We described species, specimen categories, seasonality, travel history, geographical distribution, hospitalisation and all-cause mortality within 30 days. Results We identified 1,181 infection episodes, including 680 Vibrio and 501 Shewanella episodes. Episodes were concentrated in June-September, particularly for V. vulnificus (31/32; 97%), V. parahaemolyticus (184/217; 85%), S. algae (234/298; 79%) and V. alginolyticus (171/241; 71%). Wound or soft-tissue specimens were most common (564/1,181; 48%). V. vulnificus had the highest proportion of blood/invasive or deep-tissue specimens (18/32; 56%) and hospitalisation (22/32; 69%). Overall, 183 episodes (15%) involved hospitalisation and 13 (1%) were followed by death within 30 days. Cumulative incidence was highest in several coastal and island municipalities. Conclusion Registry linkage provided severity indicators beyond microbiological infection patterns and identified V. vulnificus as the species most frequently associated with invasive or deep-tissue specimens and hospitalisation. Shewanella accounted for a substantial proportion of episodes, supporting its inclusion alongside Vibrio in routine surveillance. The standardised episode-based approach provides a national baseline for MiBa-based surveillance implemented from 2026, informs preparedness, and may inform surveillance of marine bacterial infections in other northern European coastal settings.

title: Cardiometabolic risk following dolutegravir-based antiretroviral therapy in Sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis of diabetes mellitus and hypertension
abstract: Background Dolutegravir (DTG)-based antiretroviral therapy (ART) is the preferred regimen across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), but concerns have emerged about its cardiometabolic effects. We evaluated the burden of diabetes mellitus (DM) and hypertension (HTN) among adults receiving DTG-based ART in SSA and the comparative risk of incident HTN versus non-DTG regimens. Methods Following PRISMA 2020, we searched eight bibliographic databases, Google Scholar and grey literature from 1 January 2018 to 30 May 2026. DerSimonian–Laird random-effects models pooled prevalence and comparative estimates; risk ratios (RRs) and hazard ratios (HRs) were combined as a pragmatic approximation. Sensitivity analyses explored diagnostic thresholds and study characteristics, and certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE. Results Twenty-nine studies were included. The pooled prevalence of DM/hyperglycaemia (including prediabetes; five studies, N = 1,841) was 23.9% (95% CI 10.7–40.2%; I 2 = 98.3%), with reported estimates ranging from 7.7% (diabetes by strict American Diabetes Association criteria) to 55.9% (random blood sugar-based hyperglycaemia); excluding the random blood sugar-based study gave 17.1% (95% CI 11.4–23.7%), suggesting that diagnostic-threshold heterogeneity contributes substantially to this variation. HTN prevalence (three studies; N = 1,289) was 19.7% (95% CI 13.1–27.2%). In four studies with poolable published estimates, DTG was associated with a higher risk of incident HTN than non-DTG regimens (pooled RR/HR 1.23, 95% CI 1.13–1.34; I 2 = 0.0%), including after exclusion of the largest study (1.34, 95% CI 1.13–1.59). A large multi-country cohort (AFRICOS; approximately 3,250 participants) that reported no positive association could not be pooled because its adjusted estimate was available only in conference material. Incident DM (0.29–9.8 per 100 person-years) was synthesised narratively. Conclusion The burden of hyperglycaemia/DM and HTN among adults receiving DTG-based ART in SSA is substantial, although DM/hyperglycaemia estimates vary widely with diagnostic definitions, and single-arm estimates do not show that DTG caused this disease. The pooled RR/HR of 1.23 reflects only the published, quantitatively poolable studies and may overestimate the true association, because the AFRICOS cohort could not be included. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. These findings support risk-based cardiometabolic monitoring within HIV care and standardised diagnostic definitions in future studies. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Post-2020 trajectory of adult necrotizing fasciitis-associated mortality in the United States, 2003–2024: a national death-certificate study
abstract: Background Necrotizing fasciitis is an uncommon but life-threatening bacterial soft-tissue infection. Prior U.S. mortality analyses reported findings through 2013 and 2020, leaving the subsequent national trajectory uncharacterized. Methods We analyzed final CDC WONDER/NCHS Multiple Cause of Death data for U.S. adults aged 25 years or older during 2003–2024, identifying deaths with ICD-10 M72.6 anywhere on the death certificate. Annual age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 used year-specific population denominators and the 2000 U.S. standard population. Exploratory interrupted time-series models estimated level and slope differences beginning in 2020, with sensitivity analyses for baseline shape and serial correlation. Results Adult necrotizing fasciitis-associated deaths numbered 1,506 in 2019, 2,056 in 2022, and 1,995 in 2024. AAMRs per 100,000 were 0.583, 0.795 (the highest observed annual rate), and 0.740, respectively. The primary segmented model estimated a 2020 level difference of 0.223 per 100,000 (95% CI, 0.142 to 0.304), with a slope difference of -0.002 per 100,000 per year (95% CI, -0.021 to 0.017). Positive level estimates persisted across sensitivity models, but the estimated 2024 difference from the projected pretrend depended on baseline specification. Secondary 2024-to-2019 and 2024-to-2022 rate ratios were 1.27 (95% CI, 1.18 to 1.36) and 0.93 (95% CI, 0.87 to 0.99), respectively. Conclusions Adult mortality in 2024 was lower than in 2022 but remained higher than in 2019. Exploratory models supported a higher fitted level beginning in 2020, with a model-dependent longer-term trajectory. These findings do not establish pandemic causation or a 2022 turning point.

title: Timing of appropriate antibiotic therapy and 30-day all-cause mortality in vancomycin-resistant and vancomycin-susceptible Enterococcus faecium bloodstream infections: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Enterococcus faecium (EF) bloodstream infections (BSIs) are associated with high mortality and limited treatment options. Diagnostic delays between the detection of Gram-positive cocci and the availability of antimicrobial susceptibility results often complicate the timely initiation of targeted therapy (TT). We aimed to investigate the association between the timing of appropriate antibiotic therapy and clinical outcomes in patients with EF BSIs. Methods This retrospective cohort study included adult patients with monomicrobial EF BSIs admitted to medical wards, surgical departments, or intensive care units at Kaohsiung Chang Gung Memorial Hospital, Taiwan, between January 2011 and June 2023. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Isolates were stratified according to vancomycin susceptibility as vancomycin-resistant EF (VREF) or vancomycin-susceptible EF (VSEF). Antibiotic therapy was categorized as appropriate empiric therapy (AET) or inappropriate empiric therapy (IET), followed by TT initiated within or beyond 3 days after BSI diagnosis. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression were performed to evaluate the association between antibiotic timing and clinical outcomes. Results A total of 336 patients with EF BSIs were included, comprising 196 (58.3%) VREF and 140 (41.7%) VSEF. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis identified higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.16; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01–1.34; p = 0.03) and AET (aHR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.09–0.94; p = 0.04) as independent factors associated with 30-day all-cause mortality. In Kaplan–Meier survival analysis, delayed TT (> 3 days) was associated with higher mortality in patients with VREF BSIs but not in those with VSEF BSIs. Conclusions Higher SOFA scores and IET were associated with higher 30-day all-cause mortality in patients with EF BSIs. The association between delayed targeted therapy (TT > 3 days) and mortality differed according to vancomycin susceptibility. Timely initiation of effective therapy remains an important clinical consideration in this high-risk population

title: Detection profiles and co-detection patterns of respiratory pathogens in hospitalized patients with acute respiratory infections after the COVID-19 pandemic in Nantong, China
abstract: Background Respiratory-pathogen circulation may have changed after relaxation of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) control measures. We characterized the pathogen spectrum, clinical-site distribution, age-specific patterns, co-detection patterns, and seasonality among hospitalized patients with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) in Nantong, China. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 5,808 patients hospitalized with ARTIs at the Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University between December 2023 and December 2025. Respiratory specimens collected at admission were tested for 16 pathogens using multiplex real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Pathogen detection was compared by infection site, age group, and season. False discovery rate correction, multivariable logistic regression, and Cochran-Armitage trend tests were applied as appropriate. Results At least one pathogen was detected in 3,129 of 5,808 patients (53.87%). Single and mixed detections occurred in 2,103 (36.21%) and 1,026 (17.67%) patients, respectively. Klebsiella pneumoniae , Staphylococcus aureus , and Haemophilus influenzae were the most frequently detected bacterial targets. After false discovery rate correction, Mycoplasma pneumoniae , adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, H. influenzae , parainfluenza virus type III, and influenza B virus were more frequently detected in lower than upper respiratory tract infections (all q M. pneumoniae and H. influenzae remained associated with lower respiratory tract infections. M. pneumoniae detection peaked among children aged 6–17 years (30.92%, 81/262; P-trend S. aureus with K. pneumoniae . Influenza A virus showed a marked winter peak (21.31% vs. 1.20–2.54% in other seasons; q Conclusion Hospitalized patients in eastern China showed frequent bacterial-target detection, age-related heterogeneity, and distinct seasonal patterns. The school-age peak in M. pneumoniae and the winter peak in influenza A virus support age- and season-informed surveillance. Because molecular detection cannot distinguish active infection from colonization, bacterial findings should be interpreted alongside clinical, culture, and biomarker data.

title: Association between antibiotic treatment duration and mortality in sepsis patients: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background The optimal duration of antibiotic therapy in sepsis remains uncertain. Observational studies of treatment duration are vulnerable to immortal time bias because patients must survive long enough to be classified into longer-duration groups. This study investigated the association between antibiotic duration and mortality in sepsis using a landmark analytic approach to address this bias. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using MIMIC-IV v3.1, including adults admitted to intensive care units at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center between 2008 and 2019 who met Sepsis-3 criteria during their first septic episode and received at least 5 days of antibiotics. Patients were grouped by total active antibiotic duration: 7–10 days, 10–14 days, and >14 days. Propensity score matching and inverse probability of treatment weighting were used to balance baseline characteristics. Cox proportional hazards models estimated 28-day, 90-day, and 1-year mortality. The primary analysis used a 14-day landmark, with additional landmark analyses at 5, 7, and 10 days. Results After 1:1:1 matching, 2,448 patients were included. In analyses before landmark correction, >14 days of antibiotics was associated with lower 28-day mortality. However, as the landmark advanced from 5 to 14 days, this association progressively attenuated and disappeared at the 14-day landmark (HR:1.02 with propensity score matching and 1.12 with inverse probability weighting). At 90 days and 1 year, >14 days was associated with higher mortality in weighted analyses, although this finding may reflect confounding by indication. No prespecified subgroup showed a survival benefit from prolonged therapy. Conclusions In this MIMIC-IV cohort of patients with sepsis, antibiotic therapy beyond 14 days was not associated with improved survival after landmark correction for immortal time bias. These findings do not support routine prolongation of antibiotics beyond guideline-recommended durations.

title: Global burden of CAZ-AVI resistance among carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) remains a significant public health threat, which is associated with an estimated 11,800 deaths globally in 2019. Although ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) has demonstrated high clinical efficacy and bacterial clearance in treating CRPA infections, reports of resistance are emerging. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to estimate the global burden of CAZ-AVI resistance among CRPA clinical isolates. Methods This review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Observational studies reporting CAZ-AVI resistance in CRPA clinical isolates were included and were searched in PubMed, EMBASE, SCOPUS, Web of Science databases, and Google Scholar. STATA version 17 software was used for the data analysis. Pooled prevalences were calculated using a random-effects model, and the heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran’s Q chi-square (I²) statistics. Publication bias was assessed using a funnel plot with Egger’s and Begg’s tests, and sources of heterogeneity were explored by subgroup analysis and meta-regression. Results Of 36 studies (13,231 CRPA isolates; published 2016–2025) in the systematic review, 33 independent reports remained after removing three reports nested within larger datasets, and 31 reports (12,091 isolates; 3,469 resistant) with at least one resistant isolate contributed to the pooled estimate. The pooled prevalence of CAZ-AVI resistance was 32.93% (95% CI: 27.50–38.37; I² = 97.95%, p p = 0.041). Conclusions CAZ-AVI resistance was substantial among CRPA isolates (about one in three isolates) and varied markedly between regions. However, the extreme heterogeneity, the low certainty of the evidence, and the uneven geographical representation warrant cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates. Strengthened, standardized surveillance, particularly in under-represented regions, and antimicrobial stewardship are needed to preserve the efficacy of CAZ-AVI. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: From spatial clusters to annual rainfall: assessing the relationship between rainfall and annual cholera case counts in Uganda
abstract: Background Cholera remains a global public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where inadequate water, sanitation, and hygiene persist. The transmission of cholera can be influenced by environmental factors, such as rainfall, water availability and sanitation conditions, and contamination sources. Building on a spatial cluster analysis that previously reported cholera hotspot districts in Uganda, this study assessed the relationship between mean annual rainfall and annual cholera case counts in previously identified cholera hotspot districts with high occurrence of such clustering between 2012 and 2022. Methods This study employed a retrospective ecological design to examine the relationship between annual rainfall and annual cholera case counts in previously identified cholera hotspot districts in Uganda using district-level data from 2012 to 2022. Cholera surveillance data were obtained from the Ministry of Health, while rainfall data were derived from the Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Stations (CHIRPS) dataset. Daily rainfall estimates were processed in Google Earth Engine and aggregated to district-level annual rainfall totals. Exploratory analyses included descriptive statistics, scatterplots, and assessments of overdispersion and zero inflation. The relationship between annual rainfall and cholera case counts was evaluated using Generalized estimating equation (GEE) negative binomial regression as the primary analytic approach in Stata version 18. The district-level analyses were conducted as exploratory assessments to examine heterogeneity in rainfall–cholera relationships across hotspot districts. Results Significant spatial and temporal variation in annual rainfall was observed across hotspot districts. Cholera case counts ranged from 0 to 577 cases, with 46 of 154 district-year observations (29.9%) recording no cases. District-level analyses suggested heterogeneity in rainfall-cholera relationships across hotspot districts. In the primary GEE model analysis, annual rainfall showed a positive association with annual cholera case counts, with a 100 mm increase in rainfall corresponding to an estimated 13.2% increase in annual cholera case counts (CR = 1.132, 95% CI: 1.024–1.251). However, sensitivity analyses yielded directionally similar but less precise estimates and did not consistently demonstrate statistical significance, suggesting that this finding should be interpreted with appropriate caution. Conclusion This study assessed the association between annual district-level rainfall totals and annual cholera case counts within previously identified cholera hotspot districts in Uganda. The primary GEE model identified a positive association between annual rainfall and annual cholera case counts, while exploratory district-level analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity across hotspot districts. Future studies should incorporate population-adjusted incidence measures, seasonal rainfall indicators, and additional environmental, WASH, demographic, and health-system variables.

title: Using HVR2-G in molecular epidemiology surveillance of HRSV: a supplement for the application of WGS
abstract: Background Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) is among the major pathogens causing acute lower respiratory tract infections in infants, young children and older adults. The second hypervariable region near the C-terminus of the G gene (HVR2-G) is the target for genotyping that has been used in molecular epidemiology surveillance for nearly 28 years, and a large amount of virological data has been accumulated. Whole-genome sequence (WGS) has been suggested for use in classifying lineages because it has provided the highest resolution since 2020. As such, evaluating the applicability of the HVR2-G sequencing window for lineage classification and integrating previous HVR2-G genotypes with the new WGS-defined lineage nomenclature are needed. Methods The HVR2-G region was extracted from WGS sequences from GenBank and the lineage nomenclature data were downloaded from Nextstrain. Phylogenetic and nucleotide pairwise distance (p-distance) analyses of HVR2-G sequences were conducted using IQ-TREE 2.3.6 and MEGA11.0, respectively. Results Phylogenetic analyses revealed that the primary lineages defined by WGS-defined lineage nomenclature could be classified using the HVR2-G region with a bootstrap over 70%; the nested lineages could not be distinguished. Nineteen and 37 previous HVR2-G genotypes of HRSVA and B were reduced to 4 (A.1, A.2, A.3 and A.D) and 5 (B.1, B.2, B.3, B.4 and B.D) lineages with P-distance thresholds greater than 0.102 and 0.0591, respectively. Conclusion This study verified that the HVR2-G sequencing window provides reliable assignment of major HRSV lineages and enables integration with historical surveillance datasets. It has the potential to serve as a complement to the application of WGS for molecular virological surveillance of HRSV in China and globally, especially in resource-limited areas.

title: Bacterial pathogens in chronic and recurrent tonsillitis: surface vs. core tonsillar microbiota assessed by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry
abstract: Background The aetiology of chronic tonsillitis (CT) remains incompletely characterised, and surface tonsillar swab culture may not accurately reflect the microbiota of deeper tonsillar tissue. We aimed to identify bacterial pathogens in CT by three-site intraoperative sampling, compare surface and core microbiological findings, evaluate the diagnostic utility of antistreptolysin O (ASO) and anti-DNase B titres, and characterise antibiotic susceptibility profiles. Methods A prospective observational study enrolled 110 CT patients undergoing tonsillectomy. Samples were collected from the tonsillar surface and core under aerobic conditions, and from the core under anaerobic conditions. Organisms were identified by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry. Paired comparisons (surface vs. core) were performed using McNemar’s test with Bonferroni correction. Antibiotic susceptibility was interpreted according to EUCAST 2025 breakpoints. Results Among 106 cultured bacterial species, 14 were classified as potentially pathogenic; at least one pathogen was confirmed in 108 patients (98.2%). Staphylococcus aureus was the most frequently isolated organism (60.0%), followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae (58.2%) and Streptococcus anginosus (44.5%); Streptococcus pyogenes was detected in only 9.1% of patients. Combined-core prevalence was significantly higher than surface prevalence for S. aureus , S. pneumoniae , S. anginosus , and H. influenzae (all p S. aureus , 33.3% of S. anginosus , and 20.0% of S. pneumoniae isolates. Neither ASO nor anti-DNase B predicted fulfilment of the Paradise criteria on logistic regression; anti-DNase B positivity was associated with S. pyogenes recovery from the tonsillar surface. Conclusions Surface swab culture substantially underestimates the bacteriological complexity of CT. Core sampling with anaerobic culture conditions provides a more complete microbiological assessment. The observed macrolide resistance supports susceptibility-guided use of erythromycin, particularly when it is considered as an alternative in patients with beta-lactam allergy. ASO and anti-DNase B should be interpreted in the context of clinical suspicion for recent streptococcal infection rather than as universal CT markers.

title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of human metapneumovirus pneumonia: focus on patients aged 80 years and older
abstract: Introduction Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a significant viral pathogen associated with acute lower respiratory tract infections, particularly in elderly people. However, data on the clinical characteristics and outcomes of hMPV pneumonia among elderly people remain sparse. Methods We retrospectively reviewed data from 106 adult patients with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed hMPV infection and radiologically confirmed pneumonia diagnosed at Ewha Womans University Seoul Hospital between September 2022 and March 2025. Baseline characteristics, treatment, and clinical outcomes were analyzed by age group ( Results The 106 patients had a median age of 71 years, and 37.8% of them were male. Hypertension (43.4%), malignancy (24.5%), and diabetes mellitus (24.5%) were the most common comorbidities. The patients were categorized into two age groups: n = 79, 74.5%) and ≥ 80 years ( n = 27, 25.5%). Patients aged ≥ 80 years had a significantly higher prevalence of hypertension (63.0% vs. 36.7%, p = 0.017), dementia (22.2% vs. 5.1%, p = 0.016), multilobar involvement (92.6% vs. 74.7%, p = 0.048), and pleural effusion (22.2% vs. 3.8%, p = 0.008). Additional microorganisms were detected in 32.1% of patients, with bacterial organisms alone (24.5%) being more common than viral organisms alone (5.7%); Haemophilus influenzae and Klebsiella pneumoniae were the most frequently detected bacteria. The overall hospitalization rate was 82.1% and was significantly higher among patients aged ≥ 80 years (96.3% vs. 77.2%, p = 0.038). ICU admission rates were numerically higher in patients aged ≥ 80 years (25.9% vs. 10.1%), although the difference was not statistically significant ( p = 0.150). In multivariable analysis among hospitalized patients, greater initial oxygen requirement was associated with longer hospitalization. Conclusion Adults aged ≥ 80 years with hMPV pneumonia had higher hospitalization rates and more severe clinical and radiologic features in age-group comparisons. These findings highlight the substantial clinical burden of hMPV pneumonia in older adults and the importance of careful assessment of disease severity at presentation.

title: Antiretroviral therapy and reduced hazard of mortality in HIV/AIDS patients: a 32-year cohort study from Iran
abstract: Background This study represents the first 32-year population-based cohort study in Mazandaran province to comprehensively analyze the survival of people living with HIV and identify factors associated with long-term outcomes. By quantifying the association of antiretroviral therapy with survival and providing real-world evidence on the magnitude of this association, this study addresses a critical gap in the regional literature. Methods A historical cohort study was conducted on all HIV/AIDS patients registered in Mazandaran province between 1991 and 2023 ( n = 507). A census sampling method was employed using data from all registered patients with complete records. Demographic, clinical, and behavioral data were collected. Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. All statistical analyses were conducted using STATA version 17. Results Of 507 patients, 72.78% were male, with a mean age of 34.86 years. High prevalence of addiction (63.87%) and unsafe sexual practices (64.11%) were observed. During follow-up, 37.28% died, 5.13% were lost to follow-up, and 57.59% were censored. In the multivariable Cox model, lack of ART showed the strongest association with mortality (HR = 3.72; 95% CI: 2.52–5.48; p p = 0.04). Mean survival time was 16.24 years (95% CI: 15.14–17.34) in patients receiving ART versus 8.72 years (95% CI: 7.14–10.31) in untreated patients. Conclusions Based on our findings, lack of ART showed the strongest association with poorer long-term survival in HIV/AIDS patients in this cohort; however, this association should be interpreted as observational, because ART receipt was collinear with treatment era and immortal-time bias may have inflated the apparent benefit. A history of addiction was independently associated with an increased hazard of death by more than twofold. Therefore, we recommend targeted interventions for people who inject drugs, alongside expanding ART access and strengthening adherence support, as these strategies target the main factors identified in this 32-year cohort.

title: Parotid abscess due to brucellosis: a case report
abstract: Background Brucellosis is a systemic disease that can damage one or multiple organs. It can present with different clinical characteristics and nonspecific symptoms. Although local abscess formation secondary to brucellosis has been reported in various organs including spleen and liver, parotid abscess due to brucellosis is a rare event. Case presentation The patient was a 65 years-old male who was engaged in sheep breeding in Gansu province, the northwestern part of China. He had a 2-year history of lower back pain, a 6-month history of the right knee pain and a 20-day history of pain, swelling, and redness in the right side of his neck. The Brucella spp. was found in the culture of the abscess drainage fluid. He was considered to be parotid abscess and spondylitis due to brucellosis. Antibiotics combined with local drainage achieved clinical improvement in this patient, and formal surgical incision or parotidectomy was avoided. Conclusions Parotid abscess is a rare complication of brucellosis. This case offers clinical experience for the diagnosis and management of this brucellosis-associated complication.

title: Early virologic and immunologic outcomes of albuvirtide-based regimens in treatment-naïve adults with advanced HIV disease and ultra-high viral loads: a multicenter retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Advanced HIV-1 infection with ultra-high viral loads (> 500,000 copies/mL) represents a high-risk clinical presentation characterized by extreme viremia and profound immunosuppression. This clinical setting requires prompt initiation of effective antiretroviral therapy to achieve early control of plasma viremia. We evaluated the early virologic and immunologic outcomes and safety of albuvirtide (ABT)-based regimens in this high-risk cohort. Methods We conducted a multicenter, retrospective study analyzing real-world data from 25 clinical centers in China. The cohort comprised treatment-naïve adults with baseline HIV-1 RNA > 500,000 copies/mL and CD4 + T-cell counts Results Among 358 eligible patients who initiated ABT-based therapy, 287 had an evaluable Week-12 virologic outcome, of whom 132 (46.0%) were classified as CDC stage C3. The median baseline viral load was 1,060,000 (IQR: 696,000–2,205,000) copies/mL and the median CD4 + T-cell count was 48 (IQR: 25–100) cells/µL. At Week 12, 40.4% (116/287) achieved HIV-1 RNA + T-cell counts increased over 12 weeks. Among the 287 participants included in the 12-week safety analysis, 45 (15.7%) had at least one recorded Grade 1 or 2 laboratory abnormality. No Grade 3 laboratory abnormalities, serious adverse events, adverse event-related treatment discontinuations or regimen switches, or deaths were recorded. Conclusion Among treatment-naïve adults with ultra-high HIV-1 viral loads and advanced immunosuppression, ABT-based regimens were associated with early reductions in HIV-1 RNA and increases in CD4 + T-cell counts over 12 weeks. These observational findings warrant further evaluation in prospective comparative studies. Clinical trial number Not applicable. Graphical Abstract

title: Periodontitis modulates PS-dependent non-canonical entry pathways associated with SARS-CoV-2 susceptibility
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 infection extends beyond the respiratory tract, with the oral cavity emerging as a critical site of viral activity shaped by epithelial receptor expression, microbial interactions, and inflammatory status. Periodontal disease (PD), a chronic dysbiotic condition, co-occurs with alterations linked to SARS-CoV-2 susceptibility markers through inflammation-driven upregulation of non-canonical viral entry pathways. In this study, we aimed to determine whether periodontitis-associated inflammatory changes are accompanied by activation of the PS/TIM pathway and whether this pathway correlates with molecular patterns that SARS-CoV-2 can potentially engage for cellular entry.
