title: Advancing Automated Reporting in Manufacturing With Dual-Channel GCN and CNN Architectures
abstract: The automation of reporting in the manufacturing sector, enabled by advanced sensing technologies and sophisticated software, offers considerable promise for enhancing operational efficiency and profitability. Despite substantial economic benefits, fully realizing automated reporting remains hindered by critical challenges in human action recognition. These obstacles include visual occlusions in dynamic environments, heavy reliance on large-scale labeled video datasets, requirements for real-time activity identification, and the complexity of recognizing sequential and interdependent tasks typical in manufacturing settings. This article introduces a novel CNN-based framework specifically designed to overcome these challenges, thereby enhancing automated reporting capabilities in manufacturing. Our proposed method incorporates innovative geometric convolution layers, significantly improving the accuracy of motion identification and posture estimation under challenging conditions. To reduce dependence on extensive labeled datasets, we integrate a self-supervised learning strategy, leveraging unlabeled video data effectively. Moreover, we propose a robust dual-channel graph convolutional network that concurrently addresses multitask action recognition and prediction, effectively capturing complex sequential activities. Collectively, these contributions equip manufacturers with the tools necessary for precise, real-time monitoring of worker actions, enabling optimized operations, enhanced worker safety, and ultimately, improved profitability.

title: Finite-Time Adaptive Robust Disturbance Observer and Filter-Based Controller for Human–Robot Interaction in Rehabilitation Robots
abstract: Rehabilitation robots operate under continuous physical human–robot interaction (pHRI). However, many rehabilitation robots lack sensors for directly measuring interaction forces. Therefore, their control strategies must account for interaction dynamics, especially when such forces are unknown or cannot be measured directly. To address this limitation, this article proposes a finite-time adaptive robust disturbance observer integrated with an adaptive finite-time filter-based control strategy for the real-time control of sensorless rehabilitation robots during pHRI. The observer estimates pHRI online using the concept of generalized momentum, while the filter-based controller avoids computationally demanding inertia-matrix inversion and eliminates the need for joint acceleration measurements, thereby reducing sensitivity to noisy signals. Lyapunov-based analysis is used to establish the stability of the integrated observer–controller closed-loop system and to guarantee bounded finite-time convergence of the tracking, parameter-estimation, and observer errors. Numerical simulations in MATLAB/Simulink on a 2-DOF lower-limb exoskeleton model validate the proposed strategy and demonstrate improved trajectory tracking and pHRI estimation compared with competing controllers. Experimental validation is then conducted on a custom-made seated lower-limb rehabilitation robot with ten subjects. The results confirm improved tracking performance and reliable pHRI estimation, highlighting the observer's role in enabling sensorless pHRI-aware control and its potential to improve rehabilitation outcomes.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Adaptive-Enhanced Constraint Management for Switched Systems via Self-Adjusting Feedback Triggering Mechanism
abstract: Human-in-the-loop switched systems often suffer from unmeasurable states and strict safety constraints, which may lead to unacceptable workload or even catastrophic errors for human operators. This article proposes an adaptive-enhanced constraint-management strategy for such human-machine shared-control platforms. The main results and contributions are as follows. first, a self-adjusting event-triggered mechanism is introduced to reduce the update frequency of the autopilot, alleviating the operator’s cognitive burden while ensuring communication efficiency; Second, an adaptive state observer is designed to reconstruct unmeasurable states in real time, providing accurate state information for feedback control; Third, by incorporating a tan-type barrier Lyapunov function, we theoretically guarantee that all state variables strictly remain within predefined human-safe ranges throughout system operation; fourth, fuzzy-logic systems are employed to approximate unknown nonlinearities arising from pilot-autopilot interactions, with established approximation error bounds; Finally, under the average dwell-time switching law, we rigorously prove that the closed-loop human–machine system achieves uniformly ultimately bounded stability while excluding Zeno behavior. Numerical simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, demonstrating improved tracking accuracy and reduced control update frequency compared with traditional periodic control schemes.

title: Gentamicin and antibiotic use in Norwegian hospitals: a study from 35 point-prevalence surveys, 2015 to 2023
abstract: BACKGROUND Inappropriate and excessive use of broad-spectrum antibiotics drives antimicrobial resistance. Gentamicin, an Access antibiotic in the WHO AWaRe framework with low resistance potential, has long been recommended in Norway for empirical treatment of serious infections. However, real-world data on aminoglycoside use remain limited. AIM We aimed to describe gentamicin and overall antibiotic use in Norway, including COVID-19 pandemic-related changes, and report the extent of gentamicin use across selected indications. METHODS Data were obtained from patients ≥ 20 years from 35 national point-prevalence surveys (2015–2023) across 68 Norwegian hospitals. RESULTS Among 241,546 hospitalised patients, 66,586 received antibiotics (yearly prevalence 26.9–28.1%), with the highest proportions in the 70–79 (26.4%) and ≥ 80 (23.4%) years age groups. Aminoglycosides, mainly gentamicin, ranked ninth among all antibiotic prescriptions. From 2021, third-generation cephalosporins (13–14%) surpassed β-lactamase–sensitive penicillins (12–13%). Gentamicin use increased from 4.1% in 2015 to 5.8% in 2023, mainly in combination with ampicillin, benzylpenicillin, or ampicillin plus metronidazole. Main indications were urinary tract, lower respiratory tract and intraabdominal infections, and sepsis. An increasing pre-COVID-19 pandemic trend in gentamicin use (β 1 : 0.105; p 3 : − 0.112; p = 0.013). CONCLUSION Gentamicin use among hospitalised patients in Norway remains low but appears higher than in other European countries. Increases in gentamicin use pre-COVID-19 pandemic were no longer observed after COVID-19, supporting the need for surveillance and antibiotic stewardship to minimise unnecessary use of broad-spectrum antibiotics.

title: Minimised SARS-CoV-2 transmission during Tokyo 2020 Olympic and Paralympic Games: insights from enhanced integrated surveillance, Japan, July to September 2021
abstract: BACKGROUND Amid the COVID-19 pandemic, stringent public health measures were taken during the Tokyo 2020 Olympic and Paralympic Games (Tokyo 2020). AIM We describe SARS-CoV-2 transmission among Games participants and in-person contributors (GPIPC)s. METHODS Tokyo 2020-related SARS-CoV-2 infection cases were individuals linked to the event, testing positive for the virus between 1 July−19 September 2021, reported to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government. Attack rates among athletes and team officials were determined. Enhanced case-based surveillance integrating genomic sequencing data supported viral spread investigations among various GPIPC groups. RESULTS A total 804 cases (median age: 35 years, interquartile range (IQR): 27–45; 194 female/610 male) were reported. Among athletes and team officials, attack rates were 0.6% (65/11,400) in Olympic Games and 0.6% (30/4,800) in Paralympic Games. These 95 infections concerned mainly overseas travellers (n = 92), 85 of whom were diagnosed within 14 days of arrival in Japan. Among the 804 cases, whole-genome sequencing data were obtained for 304 (median age: 38 years, IQR: 29–47; 67 female/237 male) with sufficient viral load (as indicated by RT-PCR Cq ≤ 32), including 79% (75/95) of athletes and team officials cases, 74% (131/176) of Games’ organisers and media cases, and ˂ 20% (98/533) of remaining cases. Delta variants dominated (94%; 285/304), with domestic (AY.29 lineage) Delta strains prominent among Delta-variant-affected resident cases (96%; 104/108) and Games’ organisers and media cases diagnosed ≥ 15 days after entering Japan (97%; 63/65). Overseas Delta strains mostly affected travellers within 14 days of entry, particularly athletes and team officials (97%; 66/68) and Games’ organisers and media (29/34). CONCLUSION Multilayered-risk-reduction measures likely minimised SARS-CoV-2 transmission to athletes.

title: Andes virus reaches Europe: a narrative review on clinical challenges, diagnostic gaps and public health preparedness, 2026
abstract: BACKGROUND Up to 2 July 2026, a total of 13 cases of Andes virus (ANDV) including three deaths were reported in connection to an outbreak on the cruise ship m/v Hondius , which departed from Argentina in April and subsequently travelled to Europe to evacuate the passengers. This event prompted all European health authorities to take action to limit the spread of the virus. AIM To synthesise current knowledge on ANDV, with particular attention on laboratory diagnosis and capability gaps. METHODS A literature search on ANDV was conducted, with a focus on human infection, transmission, outbreak investigations, countermeasures and diagnostics. To provide context for the ship-linked outbreak, updates from official public health sources, including the World Health Organization and European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control were used. Moreover, activities by European Union Public Health Reference Laboratories for Emerging, Rodent-borne and Zoonotic Viral Pathogens (EURL-PH-ERZV) were briefly presented. RESULTS Andes virus is unique among hantaviruses because of sustained person-to-person transmission. Diagnosis relies on integration of clinical and epidemiological information with molecular detection of viral RNA or serological evidence. At the time of the outbreak, European diagnostic preparedness was generally well established, but important gaps remained prompting rapid support from the EURL-PH-ERZV. CONCLUSIONS The recent event demonstrated how a geographically restricted zoonotic infection can pose public health challenges beyond endemic areas. This highlights the need for strong collaboration between clinical services, public health authorities and reference laboratories to strengthen surveillance, early detection, risk assessment and diagnostic preparedness for emerging pathogens.

title: Repeated detection of West Nile virus in Aedes caspius during an unusually early transmission season in humans in northern Italy, 2026
abstract: In Lombardy, northern Italy, 2026, the first neuroinvasive West Nile virus (WNV) human case was reported on 7 July. Concurrently, high abundances of Aedes caspius and low numbers of Culex pipiens occurred at several surveillance sites. Testing seven archived Ae. caspius pools collected in July revealed WNV lineage 2 in six pools from three independent sites. A virus sequence from Ae. caspius shared > 99.94% nt identity with contemporaneous human-derived sequences. Further investigating possible Ae. caspius vector competence, particularly for WNV lineage 2, is warranted.

title: Fatal encephalitis caused by Shamonda virus Europe 1 (SHAV-EU1) in a patient with a severely weakened immune system, France, 2026
abstract: New Shamonda virus clades (SHAV-EU1 and SHAV-EU2) emerged in Europe in summer 2026, primarily affecting cattle. We report the first human infection with SHAV-EU1: a French patient with a severely weakened immune system developed fatal encephalitis in September 2026, 1 month after their allogeneic stem cell transplantation. Metatranscriptomics detected SHAV-EU1 in cerebrospinal fluid, confirmed by RT-PCR. Biopsies from central nervous system showed high viral loads. Investigations revealed SHAV-EU1 in serum, respiratory and stool samples at least for 2 months before encephalitis onset.

title: Understanding vaccination against human papillomavirus (HPV): knowledge and perceptions among parents or guardians and healthcare workers, Germany, 2023
abstract: BACKGROUND Vaccination against human papillomavirus (HPV) is effective against certain types of cancer. Despite longstanding vaccination recommendation, HPV vaccination has the lowest coverage among all recommended vaccines for children and adolescents in Germany, with notable differences between sexes. AIM We aimed to investigate attitudes towards vaccination against HPV and HPV-related knowledge among parents or guardians and healthcare workers (HCW) in Germany, alongside vaccination intentions and determinants in parents/guardians and vaccination counselling in HCWs. METHODS In autumn 2023, we conducted telephone interviews with 1,508 parents/guardians of children and adolescents aged 9–14 years and 503 HCWs from paediatric practices. We used weighting and analysed the responses with t test and ANOVA. RESULTS Overall, 34.5% children of the interviewed parents/guardians were already vaccinated against HPV, while 24.8% of parents/guardians reported a high intention, 5.6% opposed to vaccination and 35.2% were considered vaccine hesitant. Parents/guardians and HCWs considered vaccination of females more important than of males (p CONCLUSION These findings highlight the need for tailored vaccination communication, alongside timely, active physician recommendations and appropriate education to support HPV vaccination decisions.

title: High levels of domestic transmission and drug resistance –analysis of national surveillance data for shigellosis, the Netherlands, 2018 to 2024
abstract: BACKGROUND Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among Shigella species is increasing, which is concerning. Strengthening surveillance is key to obtaining accurate, timely and actionable data on shigellosis. AIM We aimed to describe Dutch national shigellosis surveillance data from 2018 to 2024, spanning the implementation of national genomic surveillance in 2022. METHODS We described notified shigellosis cases and used logistic regression models to analyse associations between shigellosis and age, sex, year of infection, province, MSM (men who have sex with men) association, travel status, severity of disease and Shigella species. RESULTS In 2018–2024, 3,020 shigellosis cases were notified. Incidence of shigellosis decreased during the COVID-19 pandemic years 2020–2021 but returned to pre-pandemic incidence in 2023 and 2024. Most cases were males (n = 1,887; 62.5%). Of the 1,731 cases with available data, 732 (42.3%) reported recent contact with MSM, representing 24.2% of all shigellosis cases. The proportion of extensive drug resistant (XDR) isolates increased from 2018 (1/58) to 2023 (24/109; 22.0%) (p CONCLUSION Implementation of genomic surveillance facilitated detection of clusters, provided more timely data on AMR and allowed for more detailed analyses of risk factors for Shigella transmission. Continued intervention efforts promoting hygiene and raising awareness on shigellosis and AMR are important to curb the increase of XDR shigellosis.

title: A multi-country outbreak of Salmonella Blockley associated with tomato consumption, July to October 2024
abstract: Between July and October 2024, 216 cases with genetically related Salmonella Blockley sequence type 52 were identified in France (n = 56), Germany (n = 30), the United Kingdom (UK) (n = 129) and the United States (US) (n = 1). Case interviews in the UK identified tomatoes as a possible vehicle of infection. A rapid case–control study with 29 cases and 87 controls was conducted to investigate this hypothesis, using pre-existing control data. Multivariable, Firth penalised logistic regression was used to explore associations between illness, food exposures and retailers. Consumption of tomatoes and shopping at Retailer A (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 10.75; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.52–103.16) was associated with being a case. Salmonella spp. was not detected in any of the 312 tomato samples tested by a standard culture method, but a low concentration of Salmonella DNA was detected in two enriched broths by PCR. These detections could not be confirmed by culture. Evidence derived from epidemiological, microbiological and food chain investigations in the UK identified imported tomatoes from Morocco as the most likely vehicle of infection.

title: Changes in age composition and epidemiology of candidaemia, Iceland, 2012 to 2023
abstract: BACKGROUND Candidaemia places a substantial burden on healthcare systems. Long-term, population-based studies of candidaemia rates with appropriate adjustments for changes in age composition are lacking. AIM We aimed to determine trends in candidaemia incidence rates, species distribution, antifungal susceptibility, and concurrent antifungal use in Iceland between 2012 and 2023, as well as long-term (2000–2023) trends in age-standardised incidence rates (ASRs). METHODS We analysed patient data with blood cultures positive for Candida species, or yeasts previously assigned to the genus Candida . We calculated ASRs, standardised to the 2023 Icelandic population, and performed susceptibility testing on all available isolates. RESULTS Overall, we identified 207 candidaemia episodes in 193 patients. The average ASR was 5.2 cases per 100,000 population. The ASR increased significantly from 2012 to 2023 (incidence rate ratio (IRR) = 1.07; p = 0.001), mainly driven by increased rates among males (IRR = 1.10; p = 0.001). From 2000 to 2023, the ASR remained stable (average 5.8/100,000; IRR = 1.00). The ASR was higher among males, both during 2012–2023 (p = 0.014) and long-term (2000–2023, p = 0.001). Age-specific incidence rate was highest among > 80-year-old males (44.0/100,000). Candida albicans was the most frequent species (41.0%), followed by Nakaseomyces glabratus (27.2%) and Candida tropicalis (11.1%). Fluconazole susceptibility remained high ( C. albicans 99%, C. tropicalis 75%, Candida parapsilosis 100%), and echinocandin resistance was rare (1.9%). CONCLUSION Despite an apparent increase from 2012 to 2023, candidaemia incidence in Iceland has remained stable in a long-term (24-year) perspective, when appropriate adjustments are made for the ageing population. Concurrently, the epidemiology has shifted towards non- albicans Candida infections.

title: Assessing the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on routine childhood vaccination uptake, the Netherlands, 2016 to 2025
abstract: BACKGROUND The Netherlands has experienced a decline in routine childhood vaccination uptake during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, with emerging evidence of reduced parental vaccine confidence. AIM To evaluate the immediate and long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on first-dose diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis-poliomyelitis (DTaP-IPV) vaccination uptake. METHODS We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study including all children born in the Netherlands in 2016–2024. First-dose DTaP-IPV vaccination status by age 6 months was obtained from the national immunisation register. National trends in vaccination uptake across pre-pandemic, pandemic and post-pandemic periods were assessed using interrupted time series analyses (ITS). To further assess the independent effects of the pandemic, matched-sibling analysis compared vaccination uptake within families before, during and after the pandemic. RESULTS ITS showed significant immediate decreases in vaccination uptake both at the start and end of the pandemic, accompanied by a continuing downward trend during the pandemic (OR: 0.984; 95% CI: 0.981–0.986) that further declined after its end (OR: 0.995; 95% CI: 0.993–0.998). In the matched-sibling analysis, children eligible during and after the pandemic had lower odds of being vaccinated (pandemic: OR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.55–0.80; post-pandemic: OR: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.17–0.25) compared with their pre-pandemic siblings. Also, later birth order was associated with lower odds compared with first-born siblings (second-born: OR: 0.42; 95% CI: 0.37–0.48). CONCLUSIONS Both analyses indicate a negative impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on childhood vaccination uptake, which may reflect lingering pandemic effects and/or new post-pandemic factors, highlighting the need for further research into the drivers of vaccination uptake changes in the post-pandemic era.

title: Benign overfitting beyond prediction: the ordinary least-squares interpolator
abstract: Summary Recent advances in deep learning have highlighted the phenomenon of benign overfitting in overparameterized statistical models, sparking significant interest in understanding its foundations. Owing to its simplicity and practical relevance, the ordinary least-squares interpolator has become a key object of study for gaining theoretical insight into this phenomenon. While the properties of ordinary least squares are well understood in classical underparameterized settings, its behaviour in the overparameterized regime, unlike that of ridge regression or the lasso, remains comparatively less explored. We contribute to this growing literature by deriving new algebraic and statistical results for the minimum $ \ell_{2} $-norm ordinary least-squares interpolator. In contrast to much of the existing work, which focuses on prediction risk, we centre our analysis on parameter estimation and inference, which are fundamental to many statistics and causal inference applications. Specifically, we establish overparameterized analogues of (i) the leave-$ k $-out formulas, (ii) the omitted-variable bias formula and (iii) the Frisch–Waugh–Lovell theorem. Under the Gauss–Markov model, we further extend the Gauss–Markov theorem and analyse variance estimation under homoscedasticity in the overparameterized setting. Collectively,these results provide a systematic framework for studying parameter estimation and inference in overparameterized linear models, offering a novel perspective on benign overfitting beyond its implications for prediction.

title: Post-reduction inference for confidence sets of models
abstract: Summary Sparsity in a regression context makes the model itself an object of interest, pointing to a confidence set of models as the appropriate presentation of the evidence. A difficulty in areas such as genomics, where the number of candidate variables is vast, arises from the need for preliminary reduction before the assessment of models. The present paper considers a resolution using inferential separations fundamental to the Fisherian approach to conditional inference, namely, the sufficiency/co-sufficiency separation and the ancillary/co-ancillary separation. Tests of model adequacy based on such separations do not involve specifying a direction of departure from any postulated model, avoiding calibration issues that would arise in directed tests from using the same data for reduction and for model assessment. In idealized cases with no nuisance parameters, the separations extract the relevant information without loss or redundancy. The extent to which estimation of nuisance parameters affects this idealization is illustrated in detail for the normal-theory linear regression model, extending immediately to a lognormal accelerated-life model for time-to-event outcomes. As part of the analysis, we introduce a modified version of the refitted cross-validation estimator of Fan et al. (2012), whose distribution theory is tractable in the appropriate conditional sense. The paper concludes, among other things, that in settings where reduction on a reduced sample is unproblematic, sample splitting has high efficiency relative to our conditional analysis, echoing Cox (1975); otherwise, it gives miscalibrated confidence sets.

title: Asymmetric penalties underlie proper loss functions in probabilistic forecasting
abstract: Abstract Accurately forecasting the probability distribution of phenomena of interest is a classic and increasingly widespread goal in statistics and decision theory. In comparison to point forecasts, probabilistic forecasts aim to provide a more complete and informative characterization of the target variable. This endeavour is only fruitful, however, if a forecast is ‘close’ to the distribution it attempts to predict. The role of a loss function, also known as a scoring rule, is to make this precise by providing a quantitative measure of proximity between a forecast distribution and the target random variable. Numerous loss functions have been proposed in the literature, with a strong focus on proper losses, that is, losses whose expectations are minimized when the forecast distribution is the same as the target. In this paper, we show that a broad class of proper loss functions penalize asymmetrically , in the sense that underestimating a given parameter of the target distribution can incur a larger loss than overestimating it, or vice versa. Our theory covers many popular losses, such as the logarithmic, continuous ranked probability, quadratic and spherical losses, as well as the energy and threshold-weighted generalizations of continuous ranked probability loss. To complement our theory, we present experiments with real epidemiological, meteorological and retail forecast datasets. Furthermore, as an implication of the loss asymmetries revealed by our work, we show that hedging is possible under distribution shift.

title: The home physical activity environment as a potential mediator of the association between parental physical activity and preschoolers’ physical fitness: a cross-sectional study in urban China
abstract: IntroductionFamily-level associations with preschool children’s physical fitness remain incompletely understood.ObjectiveThis study examined cross-sectional associations among parental physical activity, the home physical activity environment (HPAE), and preschool children’s fitness, including a potential indirect association through the HPAE.MethodsWe recruited 568 parent–child dyads from 23 kindergartens in Nanchang, China, using multistage stratified random sampling. Parental activity was assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form, the HPAE using a purpose-developed 18-item scale, and children’s fitness using an adapted Chinese National Physical Fitness Measurement framework. Mediation analysis used 5,000 bootstrap resamples. The primary model controlled for parental education and family income. A sensitivity model additionally controlled for children’s outdoor activity, organized sport participation, and screen time.ResultsIn the primary model, parental activity was positively associated with children’s fitness (path c, β = 0.167) and the HPAE (path a, β = 0.349), which was also associated with fitness (path b, β = 0.234; all p < 0.001). The indirect association was statistically significant (a × b = 0.081, 95% CI [0.055, 0.109]), and the direct association remained significant (path c′, β = 0.085, p = 0.006). The 48.9% mediated proportion applies only to the primary model. After additional adjustment for children’s outdoor activity, organized sport participation, and screen time, the estimated indirect association was close to zero and was not statistically significant (a × b = −0.002, 95% CI [−0.013, 0.007]).ConclusionThe primary model showed a pattern of associations consistent with a potential pathway through the HPAE, but the indirect association was not robust to adjustment for child activity variables. These cross-sectional findings do not establish a mediation mechanism. Longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to clarify temporal ordering and evaluate potential intervention targets.

title: How and why women’s life histories and homelessness services generate heterogeneous recovery outcomes in Barcelona: a co-created realist evaluation protocol
abstract: IntroductionHomelessness is rising in Spain, particularly in Barcelona, where women are the fastest-growing subgroup, accounting for approximately 30% of service places. Yet services have historically been designed by default for men. Women’s pathways into homelessness are shaped by individual, social, and structural determinants which increase trauma exposure and make this population highly heterogeneous. While evidence highlights the need for gender- and trauma-informed services adapted to different subgroups, there remains limited systematic understanding of how women’s life experiences influence their engagement with and outcomes from homelessness services. This study aims to understand how and why women’s life experiences and determinants interact with homelessness service and intervention elements to activate or inhibit mechanisms (e.g., personal strengths) leading to different recovery outcomes (e.g., identity), thereby informing recommendations on how services can better support person-centered recovery of women.MethodsThis study protocol describes a realist evaluation that will combine a realist review with realist interviews, using co-creation methodologies involving homelessness service users and providers, through Community Advisory Committees, in Barcelona. An initial programme theory will be co-designed in parallel with literature screening and appraisal. Data will be analyzed to extract context–mechanism–outcome configurations explaining how women’s experiences and determinants generate different outcomes when interacting with service/intervention components. Co-refined programme theories will subsequently be tested through interviews and focus groups, with data analyzed retroductively and co-interpreted using different theoretical lenses and approaches such as the Social Determinants of Health, Trauma Theory, Trauma-Informed Care and the Power Threat Meaning Framework.DiscussionThe study integrates realist evaluation with co-creation methodologies, enabling the development of evidence-based, context-sensitive middle-range programme theories while prioritizing the voices of both professionals and people with lived experience in the knowledge-building process, aiming for epistemic justice. Co-created causal, feminist and trauma-informed explanatory theories linking women’s experiences, mechanisms of change and intervention outcomes in Barcelona are intended to serve as a foundation for the co-production of actionable service guidelines for homelessness, as well as policy recommendations. Findings will be disseminated to both the academic and general public and will include the participation of co-researcher stakeholders for this purpose.

title: Kansas City Brain Builders: associations between a multisectoral community language nutrition intervention and change in practices and growth in child language over two years
abstract: Background and objectivesHealth literacy in adulthood plays a major role in an individual’s ability to use health information to benefit their health. Social determinants in early childhood initiate the development of health literacy through newborn brain development and oral language acquisition. Both of these processes are promoted by stimulation from everyday interactions with parents/caregivers at home and in the community. Unequal access to language-learning opportunities during early childhood represents a modifiable developmental and social determinant of later educational and health outcomes. There are inequities in these time-sensitive interactions—specifically language-learning opportunities—across families in the population, which are social determinants of early literacy, achievement in school, and later-life education, health, and economic and social well-being across the life span. This gap is most pronounced among children who grow up in poverty in the United States and internationally. The healthcare system in the United States effectively reaches to nearly all infants; however, language-learning opportunities are not a focus during well-child visits. The term “Language Nutrition” (LN) was coined in prior research to refer to these developmentally rich interactions known to support brain and language growth in children younger than preschool age. We developed Kansas City Brain Builders (KCBB) to address this inequity by promoting LN broadly among families and children in a community so that all children have a more equitable home language environment. The purpose of this study is to report longitudinal empirical findings on families and children related to the implementation of KCBB, a public health approach to community change, over 2 years.MethodsThe evaluation involved two parallel longitudinal studies: the Community study and the Family study. The Community study assessed the implementation of a KCBB multisectoral community partnership to promote LN-friendly changes in local programs, practices, and policies. The Family study involved longitudinal assessments of a sample of 83 English- and Spanish-speaking families with children younger than 36 months of age, evaluating the KCBB impacts on parental behaviors and child growth in language skills.ResultsKCBB led to a high level of documented program implementation and substantial LN promotion throughout the community. Repeated parent assessments indicated that participants had received LN messages from multiple community sectors over time, increased their knowledge of the importance of LN, and used LN through storybook reading, verbal responsiveness, and teaching behaviors during interactions with their children. Growth in children’s early language skills was significantly associated with the amount of LN they received.Discussion/ConclusionKCBB is one of the few multisectoral interventions designed to promote community-wide change targeting LN. It is a manualized intervention that can be replicated by other communities. This study employed three levels of measurement such that change could be evaluated in a theoretical framework of influence from community engagement to parental behavior and growth in child language skills. Findings provide preliminary evidence that a multisectoral community approach can achieve broad reach and is associated with changes in caregiver practices and child language growth. Larger, controlled, and replicated studies are needed to establish causal effects and determine whether such approaches reduce disparities in language-learning opportunities.
authors: ["Charles R. Greenwood", "Gabriela Guerrero", "Alana G. Schnitz", "Sandra Cintora", "Christine Giancola", "Judith J. Carta"]

title: Safeguarding implementation elements in a national school mental health intervention: implementers’ perspectives
abstract: ObjectiveThe purpose of this study was to identify and describe implementation determinants that are sensitive when undertaking a school mental health intervention and that require particular attention during implementation.MethodsA multisite qualitative study was conducted using a deductive analytical approach. Thirty team members implementing a national preventive school mental health program were interviewed. The interviews were analyzed using content analysis based on pre-established categories from the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR).ResultsThe findings highlight several implementation conditions requiring particular attention, including resources and time; training, feedback and monitoring; structural alignment across organizational levels; school over-intervention; and the recognition of adaptations as plausible elements within an intervention.DiscussionThis research provides empirical insights regarding the implementation factors of SMH programs within authentic school settings. Furthermore, the qualitative depth achieved through interviews with both implementers and coordinators allows a multi-level understanding of the factors influencing long-term sustainability and the intervention’s ecological validity.
authors: ["Loreto Leiva", "Gloria Zavala-Villalón", "Fernanda Sánchez-Vilaró"]

title: A journey mapping study of internship stress among undergraduate nursing interns
abstract: AimTo explore the dynamic process of stress experienced by undergraduate nursing interns during clinical internships and to construct a journey map of internship stress in order to identify stage-specific stressors, emotional experiences, and pain points.MethodsUsing purposive sampling, 19 undergraduate nursing interns were recruited from five tertiary hospitals in Sichuan Province between May 2025 and March 2026. Data were collected at different stages of the internship through semi-structured interviews. Thematic analysis was employed for coding, and journey mapping was applied to integrate and visually represent the trajectory of stress over time.ResultsInternship-related stress among undergraduate nursing interns evolved across four periods: Preparation Period; Shock Period; Adaptation Period; Differentiation Period. A total of 36 themes were identified across three overarching dimensions—tasks, emotional experiences, and pain points—systematically illustrating the trajectory of stress evolution.ConclusionStress among undergraduate nursing interns demonstrates a stage-based and dynamic trajectory, with distinct pain points and corresponding support needs at each stage. These findings provide empirical evidence for nursing educators and clinical managers to develop stage-specific, targeted interventions and to optimize internship support systems.
authors: ["Yuhang Cheng", "Rong Zeng", "Yi Li", "Yan Huang", "Huilan Wang", "Yuzi Zhao", "Wenxiu Jiang", "Qian Yang"]

title: BMI distribution and sex- and grade-specific trends in primary school health surveillance records in Xi’an, China, 2014–2024: a repeated cross-sectional study
abstract: BackgroundConventional childhood obesity surveillance relies mainly on mean body mass index (BMI) and overweight/obesity prevalence, which may mask unequal changes across the BMI distribution and population subgroups. Whether long-term BMI increases are concentrated in the upper tail and how high-BMI prevalence trends differ jointly by sex and school grade remain insufficiently characterized in consecutive school surveillance data.MethodsWe analyzed 7,187,779 records from students aged 6.0–12.99 years across 1,394 school codes and 13 districts in Xi’an, China, during 2014–2024 using a repeated cross-sectional design. High BMI comprised overweight or obesity under national sex- and grade-specific cutoffs. Primary analyses used logistic regression to estimate high-BMI prevalence and quantile regression to estimate covariate-adjusted changes in conditional BMI quantiles at the 50th, 75th, 90th, and 95th percentiles (P50, P75, P90, P95). Models adjusted for age in months, sex, grade, and district, with school-clustered inference. Secondary analyses assessed sex-by-grade differences in prevalence change; exploratory analyses examined P5, P10, and P25.ResultsBetween 2014 and 2024, observed high-BMI prevalence increased from 17.01 to 21.11%. Adjusted prevalence peaked at 22.75% in 2020; its 2014–2024 increase was 3.35 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.69–4.01). Covariate-adjusted changes in conditional BMI quantiles were 0.134 kg/m2 at P50 and 0.735 kg/m2 at P95; the P95 − P50 difference in 2014–2024 change was 0.601 kg/m2 (95% CI 0.468–0.734; p < 0.001). Exploratory estimates were 0.097 kg/m2 at P5 (pointwise 95% CI 0.027–0.167), 0.047 at P10 (−0.008–0.103), and 0.048 at P25 (−0.002–0.097). The increase in adjusted high-BMI prevalence was 1.65 percentage points greater among boys than girls (95% CI 1.17–2.14); the difference within Grades 4–6 was 2.59 percentage points (95% CI 1.95–3.23).ConclusionAmong participating-school surveillance records, adjusted high-BMI prevalence increased between 2014 and 2024, with greater increases among boys than girls overall and within Grades 4–6. BMI increases were greater at the upper conditional quantiles than at the median. Joint reporting of high-BMI prevalence, upper-tail BMI changes, and sex- and grade-specific estimates may provide a more complete picture of BMI trends.
authors: ["Chengwei Xu", "Han Hao", "Bing Shi"]

title: The association between illness perception and family functioning with good death expectations in community-dwelling older adults with chronic diseases
abstract: ObjectiveTo examine the association between good death expectations and family functioning in community-dwelling older adults with chronic diseases, and the association with illness perception.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study (Nov 2025–Mar 2026) of 300 community-dwelling older adults (≥60 years, ≥1 chronic disease) from three districts of a city in China, validated tools measured key variables. Mediation analysis used PROCESS bootstrapping (5,000 samples) with sociodemographic adjustment.ResultsFamily functioning positively correlated with good death expectations (r = 0.561, p < 0.01) and negatively with illness perception (r = −0.482, p < 0.01). Illness perception negatively correlated with good death expectations (r = −0.506, p < 0.01). Illness perception showed a significant indirect effect in the relationship [indirect effect = 0.1317; 95% CI (0.0804,0.1912)], accounting for 26.12% of the total effect.ConclusionFamily functioning was associated with good death expectations and illness perception showed a significant indirect association. Future research is needed to determine whether interventions targeting these factors could improve end-of-life expectations.
authors: ["Yixuan Liang", "Yingchun Wang"]

title: Real-time occupational radiation dosimetry in anesthesiology personnel during fluoroscopy-guided interventions: a single-center descriptive and exploratory study
abstract: Anesthesia personnel participating in fluoroscopy-guided interventions are routinely exposed to ionizing radiation; however, their occupational radiation burden remains insufficiently characterized. This single-center descriptive and exploratory study investigated occupational ionizing radiation exposure among anesthesiology personnel using real-time personal dosimetry. A total of 134 procedures across multiple interventional specialties were evaluated using the HERADO radiation management platform and ALMAR active personal dosimeters. Mean over-apron personal dose equivalent Hp(10) ranged from 0.010 ± 0.009 mSv to 0.025 ± 0.011 mSv per procedure. Descriptive differences in occupational exposure were observed across procedural categories; however, these differences should not be attributed independently to procedural category because relevant technical, geometric, shielding, and workflow factors were not fully quantified. The findings demonstrate the value of real-time personal dosimetry for procedure-level characterization of occupational exposure and may inform radiation-protection strategies in fluoroscopy-guided clinical practice.
authors: ["T. M. Axakali", "M. A. Kouri", "P. Georgakis", "E. Bournaki", "V. Tanou", "E. Kounadi", "C. Michail", "N. Kalyvas", "I. Valais", "G. Fountos"]

title: Effects of collective volleyball cooperative tactical training on social anxiety and peer interaction ability in school-aged children: a controlled intervention study
abstract: BackgroundSchool-aged children that experience social anxiety and have difficulty with interactions among peers can create significant challenges to their development in terms of both psychology and behavior. A team sport such as volleyball provides a common setting that naturally includes all aspects of social interaction (communication, cooperation, role coordination, etc.) and shared goals which is essential to improve the child’s confidence in interacting socially and abilities to interact socially with peers.ObjectiveThis research is an examination of the effect that a 12-week collective volleyball cooperative tactical training program will have on social anxiety and peer interaction in children (8–12).MethodsA sample of 80 healthy school-age children was obtained via two methods of campus based, voluntary and/or open recruitment. These children were then randomly assigned to either an experimental intervention group (n = 40) or an active control group receiving standard physical education (n = 40). For 12 consecutive weeks, participants in the experimental group engaged in a type of volleyball cooperative tactical team training that occurred on 3 days each week at 1 h per day. During this time the participants in the control group engaged in standard physical education classes of matched frequency and duration. Social anxiety was measured by use of the Social Anxiety Scale for Children (SASC); SASC measures include total social anxiety, fear of negative evaluation and social avoidance/distress. Participant peer interaction was evaluated using a study-specific 25-item peer-interaction questionnaire covering interaction initiative, peer acceptance, interaction coordination, interaction openness, and conflict resolution ability. Data collection occurred prior to, as well as subsequent to, the intervention. Statistical analyses were conducted utilizing SPSS version 26.0 software. A 2 × 2 mixed-design ANOVA was conducted to examine Group × Time interaction effects, with group (intervention vs. control) as the between-subjects factor and time (pre-intervention vs. post-intervention) as the within-subject factor. Effect sizes were reported using partial eta squared (η2p), and post hoc comparisons were performed when significant interactions were identified.ResultsGroup × Time Interaction Effects from a mixed-design ANOVA were found to be statistically significant for both of the outcomes (social anxiety and peer interaction) of this study. Children participating in an intervention that included an instructional program using the Collective Volleyball Cooperative Tactical Training Model showed significantly greater improvement than did those in the Control Condition in reducing their level of social anxiety as well as improving their peer interaction abilities over the course of the 12-weeks. Although we found a statistically-significant improvement in both children’s social anxiety, and their peer interaction skills through a 12-week program, there is no data available for us to understand if those positive results will continue into the future because we did not assess children at later points in time. Thus, future researchers are encouraged to consider extended assessment periods as part of their study designs to determine how long such interventions have an impact. Secondly, as a feasibility study in a controlled environment showed promise for implementation of cooperative tactical volleyball programs, there may be barriers to successful implementation in regular school settings such as lack of facilities, class size and teacher workload. Future research is needed to examine how cooperative tactical volleyball programs can be adapted to encompass large groups of students and incorporated into routine physical education curriculum. Furthermore, although the intervention showed feasibility under controlled conditions, implementation in regular school settings may face practical challenges, including limited facilities, larger class sizes, and teacher workload. Future studies should examine how cooperative volleyball tactical training can be adapted for broader school-based implementation.ConclusionCollective Volleyball Cooperative Tactical Training is an effective method for reducing social anxiety and improving the ability of school aged children to interact with peers. The program offers a viable, school-based model for integrating sport skills acquisition (training) and psychosocial growth through physical activity.
authors: ["Qiaoxian Zhang", "Yuli Zhou"]

title: Association of early feeding patterns with physical growth and neurodevelopment in term high-risk infants: a retrospective study
abstract: Background and objectivesThe relationship between early feeding patterns and growth and neurodevelopment in term high-risk infants remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the associations between feeding patterns during the first 6 months of life and physical growth and neurodevelopment in term high-risk infants.Subjects and methodsA total of 108 term high-risk infants were retrospectively included and classified according to feeding patterns during the first 6 months of life into an exclusive breastfeeding group (n = 32), a mixed feeding group (n = 45), and a formula feeding group (n = 31). Data on weight, length, and head circumference at 6, 8, and 12 months were collected. Weight-for-age Z score (WAZ), length-for-age Z score (LAZ), and head circumference-for-age Z score (HCZ) were calculated using WHO Anthro software. Neurodevelopment at 8 and 12 months was assessed using the Developmental Screening Test (DST) for children aged 0–6 years in China. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze the associations between feeding patterns and physical growth trajectories, with adjustment for sex, birth weight, fetal/neonatal risk factors, and maternal risk factors.ResultsIn unadjusted analyses, the exclusive breastfeeding group had higher WAZ and LAZ at 6 months, higher WAZ and HCZ at 8 months, and higher WAZ at 12 months than the formula feeding group (all p 0.05).ConclusionEarly feeding patterns were associated with growth trajectories in term high-risk infants, and breastfeeding may have been associated with more favorable physical growth in early life. No clear differences in neurodevelopmental outcomes were observed among feeding patterns; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size available for neurodevelopmental assessment.
authors: ["Cheng-Cheng Zhang", "Xiao-Jing Xu", "Yan Li", "Ying-Yan Wang"]

title: My daughter knows over 21 people that have died from drug overdose or suicide: cross-sector rural provider perspectives on adverse childhood experiences
abstract: BackgroundCumulative exposure to adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) is associated with an increased risk of substance use, overdose, and suicide. Rural children are more likely to experience most ACEs. There is limited literature contextualizing rural individuals’ experiences with ACEs. Public Health 3.0 calls for multisector partner engagement to generate collective impact. The purpose of this study was to evaluate rural providers’ perspectives on challenges and recommendations for ACEs mitigation in their community from a cross-sector context.Participants and settingParticipants were 74 providers enrolled in an online ACEs training. Participants lived and/or worked in five rural Missouri counties with high drug overdose death rates.MethodsThis was a conventional content analysis of written responses to structured discussion prompts from three training modules. Analysis included familiarization, inductive identification of major codes, and refinement of codes, followed by independent coding by two authors until consensus, and reporting major patterns. Artificial intelligence supported preliminary code development. An adapted Sequential Intercept Model (SIM) framework organized challenges and recommendations by setting.ResultsResults included personal stories about how ACEs impacted their communities through overdose, suicide, homelessness, unemployment, and adverse health effects. Settings included schools, government, healthcare, daycares, criminal justice, Extension, fire departments, libraries, and nonprofits. Participants recommended expanding the ACEs definition to include satanic abuse, bullying, incest, war, genocide, military family stressors, and death of a loved one. Intervention recommendations included whole-family interventions, community-wide training, trauma-informed training, expanded access to treatment, classes in prison/jails, and fostering positive childhood experiences.ConclusionCommunity voice is necessary to contextualize setting-specific insights that inform development of upstream interventions appropriate for and tailored to the community. Participants identified both strategies that could be incorporated into everyday practice—including empathy, listening, providing judgment-free and safe spaces, providing food for children experiencing hunger, encouraging positive childhood experiences, mentoring, and connecting individuals with resources for food, shelter, clothing, and mental health—and broader structural changes that may require policy-level action. The adapted SIM organizes these concepts.
authors: ["Ashley E. Douglas", "Julie M. Kapp"]

title: Tobacco and nicotine products in Switzerland: a national analysis of market notifications
abstract: Since the mid-2000s, the tobacco and nicotine products market has undergone rapid diversification. Since 2024, the Federal Act on Tobacco Products modernized the Swiss product notification system through the mandatory use of the electronic platform Tabacinfo.ch. This study aims to describe the scope, evolution and characteristics of tobacco and nicotine products notified on the Swiss market as of 2026. The number of notified products increased from 2,460 in 2000 to 9,857 in January 2026. Electronic cigarettes represent 51% of all notifications (n = 5,032), followed by smoking tobacco products (40%; n = 3,956), other products (6%; n = 590), nicotine products for oral use (2%; n = 200) and heated tobacco products (1%; n = 79). Cigars are the most frequently notified product (n = 3,102). Cigarette notifications remained limited, reflecting a market concentrated around major tobacco companies and supermarket brands. Flavor descriptors among electronic cigarettes, nicotine pouches and snus are dominated by cooling-, mint- and fruit-related terms. Several descriptors that may be particularly appealing to young people were identified (e.g. lemonade, cola and candy). Most nicotine-containing electronic cigarettes are concentrated between 17 and 20 mg/mL, whereas nicotine pouch concentrations vary widely from 1.5 to 30 mg per pouch. Switzerland remains a distinctive case in Europe, with comparatively weak regulations that may facilitate the availability and attractiveness of a wide range of addictive nicotine products. These results document products on the market and may inform policymaking. Strengthening tobacco control measures, particularly regarding flavors, nicotine concentration and product-specific exemptions, would reduce exposure to harmful products and limit their appeal, especially among young people.
authors: ["Jérémy Cros", "Karin Zürcher", "Luc Lebon"]

title: Decomposition of gender disparities in abnormal sleep duration among Chinese older adults: evidence from a national survey
abstract: BackgroundSleep duration is an important component of healthy aging, yet gender differences in short and long sleep among older adults remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine gender differences in sleep duration among Chinese older adults and quantify the contributions of socioeconomic, behavioral, functional, and health-related factors to these differences.MethodsData were obtained from 9,590 adults aged ≥65 years who participated in the 2018 wave of the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. Sleep duration was self-reported and categorized as short ( 8 h). Multinomial logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with short and long sleep, with weighted analyses and Poisson regression performed as sensitivity analyses. Separate Fairlie decomposition analyses were conducted for short and long sleep to quantify the contributions of observed characteristics to gender differences.ResultsOverall, 44.95% of participants had abnormal sleep duration, with a higher prevalence among women than men (46.87% vs. 42.66%, p < 0.001). Compared with men, women had a higher relative risk of short sleep (RRR = 1.399, 95% CI: 1.204–1.625) but a lower relative risk of long sleep (RRR = 0.856, 95% CI: 0.754–0.972). The association with short sleep remained significant in the weighted analysis (RRR = 1.530, 95% CI: 1.210–1.935), whereas the gender difference in long sleep was attenuated (RRR = 0.821, 95% CI: 0.661–1.021). For short sleep, observed characteristics explained 21.65% of the gender disparity. Education (22.75%), depressive symptoms (11.07%), IADL limitation (6.02%), and self-assessed health (4.82%) contributed positively to the disparity, whereas smoking status (−22.57%), drinking status (−12.45%), and exercise (−4.87%) partially offset it. The gender difference in long sleep was negligible, with substantial offsetting contributions across factors.ConclusionGender differences in sleep duration among Chinese older adults were primarily concentrated in short sleep, with women experiencing a higher risk. Socioeconomic, behavioral, psychological, and functional characteristics contributed to this disparity, although most of the short-sleep difference remained unexplained. Gender-sensitive interventions addressing educational disadvantage, depressive symptoms, functional limitations, and health behaviors may help reduce inequalities in sleep duration among older adults.
authors: ["Na Zhang", "Mengqian Wu", "Kaijun Han", "Manlan He", "Lu Chen"]

title: Unequal recovery of health facility visits in hospitals and township health centres after COVID-19 disruption in Henan Province, China, 2014–2024: a time-series study
abstract: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic disrupted health service utilisation worldwide. Its long-term effect remains uncertain, especially after the major adjustment of China’s COVID-19 control policies at the end of 2022. Evidence is also limited on whether recovery differed between hospitals and township health centres (THCs). The research aimed to evaluate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and its ending on health facility visits in hospitals and THCs in Henan Province from 2014 to 2024.MethodsMonthly aggregate data on total health facility visits in hospitals and THCs in Henan Province from January, 2014, to December, 2024, were obtained from the health statistics system. The observation period was divided into the pre-pandemic period (2014–2019), the pandemic period (2020–2022), and the post-pandemic period (2023–2024). A Quasi-Poisson regression model was trained with data from 2014 to 2018. The residual series from the Quasi-Poisson model was then modelled using an LSTM neural network. Data from 2019 were used as the validation set to compare the predictive performance of the Quasi-Poisson model and the Quasi-Poisson-LSTM hybrid model. The final model was used to generate counterfactual predictions for 2020–2024, and relative differences between observed and predicted values were calculated with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).Key resultsIn 2024, hospitals and THCs in Henan Province recorded 423 million health facility visits. During 2014–2019, the EAPC in per-person visits was 5.0% (95% CI 3.8–6.1) overall, with a faster increase in hospitals (6.5%, 5.8–7.3) than in THCs (2.2%, −0.5 to 5.0). Over 2014–2024, the EAPC increased to 4.4% (3.0–5.8) in THCs, whereas it decreased to 4.8% (3.8–5.9) in hospitals. The Quasi-Poisson-LSTM model had lower prediction error than the Quasi-Poisson model alone for total visits (RMSE 42.7081 vs. 51.7871; MAE 34.2020 vs. 39.8669). Counterfactual predictions showed that total visits were 14.7% (95% CI 13.2–16.2%) lower than expected in 2020, 4.8% (2.8–7.0%) lower in 2021, and 6.8% (4.3–9.3%) lower in 2022. In 2023 and 2024, total visits returned to near-expected levels, with non-significant relative differences of −1.4% (−4.4% to 1.7%) and 2.3% (−1.2% to 6.0%), respectively. However, facility-specific patterns diverged. In 2024, hospital visits remained 6.0% (3.9–9.5%) below expected levels, whereas THCs visits were 39.7% (20.8–45.0) above expected levels.ConclusionThe COVID-19 pandemic had divergent effects on health facility visits in hospitals and THCs in Henan Province. Although total visit volume had returned to the expected level in the post-pandemic era, hospital-based visits remained persistently below expected levels, while THCs showed substantial excess use. These findings suggest that care-seeking patterns might have shifted structurally in the post-pandemic era.
authors: ["Xin Tan", "Yu Hua", "Yanwei Ma", "Yulin Shi"]

title: Trends and disparities in depression-related mortality among older adults in the United States, 1999–2020
abstract: BackgroundNational trends in mortality with depression recorded as the underlying cause among older adults remain insufficiently characterized. We examined recorded mortality and demographic and geographic disparities among U.S. adults aged ≥65 years during 1999–2020.MethodsCDC WONDER Underlying Cause of Death data were used to identify deaths with ICD-10 F32 or F33 as the underlying cause. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population and age-specific rates were calculated. Joinpoint regression assessed temporal trends, ARIMA generated exploratory projections through 2030, and Frontier analysis provided descriptive state-level benchmarking. Sensitivity analyses examined any mention of F32/F33 in multiple-cause-of-death records and trends after excluding 2020.ResultsThe primary analysis identified 11,858 deaths, with an overall AAMR of 1.29 per 100,000. Higher recorded rates were observed among women, non-Hispanic and White older adults, nonmetropolitan residents, and residents of the Midwest. Overall AAMR declined (AAPC, −3.26%; p < 0.001), most sharply during 2003–2007; the 2018–2020 increase was not statistically significant. A long-term decline remained after excluding 2020. The broader multiple-cause definition identified 236,831 deaths, 19.97 times the primary count, and showed a different late-period pattern. ARIMA projected declining rates. Frontier analysis showed substantial state-level heterogeneity.ConclusionMortality with depression recorded as the underlying cause declined, but the broader any-mention definition yielded different trends. Continued surveillance, equitable recognition and documentation, and culturally responsive geriatric mental health care remain important.
authors: ["Tong Feng", "Pengcheng Zheng", "Qingyuan Li", "Ding Han", "Ran Duan"]

title: Accelerometer-derived moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity: sex differences in health benefits and health equivalence between the sexes: a prospective cohort study
abstract: BackgroundCurrent physical activity guidelines are sex-neutral despite well-recognized physiological sex differences. Previous studies have reported sex differences in associations between moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity (MVPA) and several health outcomes. However, sex differences in these associations and the health equivalence of MVPA between the sexes remain incompletely understood across a broad range of outcomes. Sex differences in associations between moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity (MVPA) and numerous health outcomes, and the health equivalence of MVPA between the sexes, remain unexplored. We aimed to identify sex differences in associations of MVPA with mortality and incident diseases, and to quantify the health equivalence of MVPA between the sexes.MethodsSex-specific associations of MVPA with all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and cancer mortality, and with incident diseases were examined using Cox and Fine-Gray models. Sex differences were tested using likelihood ratio tests comparing models with and without sex-by-MVPA interaction terms. The health equivalence of MVPA between the sexes was quantified for the selected outcomes.ResultsAmong 86,196 individuals (43.1% male), 5,195 deaths occurred over a median 7.93-year follow-up. For mortality, sex differences were identified in the associations of MVPA with all-cause, CVD, and cancer mortality, with median male-to-female MVPA duration ratios of 0.90, 1.37, and 0.71, respectively. For disease incidence, no sex differences remained significant after correction for multiple testing. Among incident diseases with nominally significant sex differences, MVPA was significantly associated with 12 in women only and 4 in both sexes. Exploratory health equivalence analyses yielded median male-to-female MVPA duration ratios of 2.02, 2.59, 1.87, and 1.73 for coronary atherosclerosis, other unspecified chronic ischemic heart disease, chronic airway obstruction, and gastroesophageal reflux disease, respectively.ConclusionFor mortality, significant sex differences were identified in the associations of MVPA with all-cause, CVD, and cancer mortality. For disease incidence, no significant sex differences were identified after correction for multiple testing. The health-equivalence estimates, based on model-predicted weekly MVPA durations, should be interpreted cautiously as exploratory findings and require independent validation.
