title: Semantic Governance Stops at the Model: What Laboratory-Aware AI Checklists Leave to Post-Deployment Oversight
When Human Oversight Cannot Keep Pace: A Task-level Oversight-margin Framework for Cardiovascular Artificial Intelligence
Evaluating Case Selection for Human Oversight in Clinical AI
Leveraging High-Frequency Postoperative ICU Arterial Blood Pressure Data from Electronic Health Records for Research: A Brief Report
abstract: Postoperative blood pressure fluctuations after cardiac surgery are highly clinically relevant, yet analyzing high-frequency arterial pressure data remains challenging. In this study, we introduce a novel methodology for processing minute-by-minute postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) arterial pressure data. The pipeline implements a series of systematic data-cleaning steps to resolve artifacts and ensure physiological plausibility, and deploys a multi-stage imputation framework to address missing intervals. Our approach constructs longitudinal blood pressure profiles that quantify the time spent within predefined blood pressure ranges, minimizing assumptions and enhancing data utility for research. We detail a rigorous and reusable workflow for data extraction, cleaning, and imputation, which may address limitations of previous methods and offer a framework to build a robust exposure metric for future research utilizing postoperative arterial pressure data.

title: Decision-Use Qualification of Digital Therapeutic Alliance for Version Selection in Generative Mental-Health AI
Real-World Deployment and Operational Evaluation of an On-Premise Thermal IoMT System in an Intensive Care Unit
abstract: Thermal imaging provides a non-contact approach for continuous environmental monitoring in intensive care units, although most existing studies remain limited to controlled or experimental settings with limited real-world validation. This study aimed to design, deploy, and operationally evaluate a scalable, low-cost, on-premise thermal Internet of Medical Things system in a real intensive care unit. A distributed network of seven thermal acquisition nodes, scalable to thirteen beds, was implemented using embedded devices and radiometric infrared cameras. Thermal images were transmitted through the hospital Wi-Fi network to a local server for storage, indexing, and near real-time visualization. System performance was evaluated using operational metrics including end-to-end latency, throughput, availability, and connectivity incidents. During a 10-day structured evaluation, the system generated 5,763,312 thermal images (approximately 1.47 TB), achieving an aggregate acquisition rate of 6.67 images per second. After architectural optimization, mean latency decreased from 26,344 ms to 126 ms (99.52% reduction), with a median of 117 ms and a 95th percentile of 207 ms. Effective system availability reached 95.29%, with most incidents associated with transient wireless connectivity interruptions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of deploying a distributed thermal IoMT system in a real intensive care unit under hospital information technology governance, offering a preliminary reference model for on-premise, nonintrusive thermal sensing infrastructures in critical care, pending validation across additional institutional and hardware settings.

title: Association of Chest Compression Depth, Rate, and Spring Resistance with “Quality CardioPulmonary Resuscitation” (QCPR) Scores in a Manikin Model
abstract: Training in high-quality chest compressions (CCs) is essential for effective resuscitation; however, it remains unclear how accurately real-time feedback systems, such as Laerdal Medical’s (Stavanger, Norway) Quality CardioPulmonary Resuscitation (QCPR) scoring system, reflect guideline-compliant CC quality. We aimed to investigate how CC depth, rate, and spring resistance affect QCPR scores. We conducted an experimental study using a Resusci Anne QCPR manikin (Laerdal Medical, Stavanger, Norway) equipped with interchangeable 30-, 50-, and 60-kg chest springs and a Corpuls mechanical CC device (GS Elektromedizinische Geräte G. Stemple GmbH, Kaufering, Germany). For each spring resistance, continuous CCs were delivered in two-minute intervals at predefined combinations of CC depth (2.0–6.0 cm) and rate (80–120 compressions per minute). CC quality was quantified using the QCPR score (0%–100%). Across all spring resistances, QCPR scores rose modestly at 3.0–3.5 cm and increased further at 4.0–4.5 cm, where the greatest score variation across preset CC rates and spring resistances was observed. At ≥ 5.0 cm, QCPR scores were consistently high (57%–100%). Overall, CC depth was the primary determinant of the QCPR score, with the highest scores observed at ≥ 5.0 cm. Additionally, we observed QCPR score differences of up to 18% for identical preset CC depth and rate settings with different springs. High QCPR scores were often achieved outside guideline ranges, emphasizing the need to interpret QCPR scores alongside absolute CC parameters and use guideline-compliant metrics as the standard for training and research.

title: Preserving Nursing Observations in Ambient AI Documentation on Psychiatric Wards
Beyond Regulatory Approval: Lifecycle Assurance for Clinical Artificial Intelligence
Forecast-Driven Dynamic Physician Staffing in a Pediatric Emergency Department: A Prospective Quasi-Experimental Pilot Study
abstract: Emergency department crowding is a persistent threat to acute care quality, yet predictive models for ED demand have rarely been translated into prospective operational staffing interventions. Here we report a prospective single-center quasi-experimental pilot study evaluating forecast-driven dynamic physician scheduling in the pediatric ED of Hacettepe University Ihsan Dogramaci Children’s Hospital (December 2024 to May 2025). Using a deep learning demand forecasting model (TiDE-RIN) combined with linear programming, we determined daily physician counts (range 3 to 6) for evening shifts (16:00 to 24:00) during days 1 to 15 of each month; days 16 to end of month maintained the institution’s standard fixed four-physician schedule. Among after-hours visits with valid disposition timestamps ( n = 9,626), mean post-evaluation length of stay (PE-LOS) was 175.9 min in the intervention arm and 184.0 min in the control arm (unadjusted difference 8.2 min; propensity-score-matched 7.9 min, median 10.0; stabilised inverse-probability weighting 8.5 min). Because staffing was allocated by calendar day, inference was clustered on the 182 study days: the two-way fixed-effects arm contrast was a reduction of 8.9 min (95% CI − 22.5 to + 4.8; p = 0.20) and the fully covariate-adjusted contrast 11.0 min (95% CI − 24.4 to + 2.5; p = 0.11). All design-consistent specifications placed the reduction between 4 and 11 min, none excluded no effect under day-level clustering, and the pilot was not powered for a difference of this size. Diagnostic testing was modestly lower (any-test rate 0.51 versus 0.54; p = 0.009). Effects were concentrated among lower-acuity patients and during the early-evening demand peak, and the optimised schedule allocated physicians demand-responsively (mean 4.31 versus 4.00 per shift) with no signal of compromised short-term patient safety, although per-physician workload effects did not reach significance in this pilot. Spillover analysis confirmed no progressive improvement in the concurrent control period. In this prospective pilot, coupling deep learning demand forecasting with optimisation-based physician scheduling was associated with a consistent but modest reduction in PE-LOS whose confidence interval included no effect, supporting feasibility and motivating multi-centre evaluation, and directly addressing the translational gap between predictive model development and real-world clinical implementation.

title: Climate and health capacity building for climate-resilient health systems: a case study of the ASPHER-GCCHE European course
abstract: Abstract Climate change poses growing risks to population health and health system functioning across Europe. Building climate-resilient and low-carbon health systems requires a workforce equipped with appropriate competencies. However, structured climate and health education remains unevenly implemented. This study evaluated the 2025 ASPHER–GCCHE European Climate Resilient Health Systems Course, a large-scale, competency-based online training programme designed to strengthen climate-health capacity among health professionals. We conducted a longitudinal evaluation of a 10-week, open-access, fully virtual course delivered in English between January and April 2025. Participants completed pre- and post-course surveys assessing self-reported confidence across six climate-resilience competency domains using a 10-point Likert scale. Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests assessed pre–post changes overall and by geographical region. A total of 4432 individuals from 164 countries registered for the course. Among 1029 participants (1029) from 119 countries, 446 participants were from the WHO European Region, met attendance and assessment criteria and were included in the analysis. Statistically significant improvements were observed across all six competency domains ( P 001), with mean confidence increases ranging from 45% to 59%. Self-reported confidence gains were consistent across European subregions, indicating comparable learning effects despite differing policy and institutional contexts. Nearly half of all registrants were from low- and middle-income countries, highlighting the reach of the open-access model. This evaluation demonstrates that competency-based online education was associated with improved self-reported confidence in climate-resilient health-system competencies. Integrating similar training into formal education and professional development pathways may support implementation of climate-resilient and low-carbon health system policies across Europe and beyond.

title: Is adherence to the 24-hour movement guidelines related to a lower risk of cardiovascular events? A prospective cohort study including 13 897 participants from the SUN project
abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading global cause of death, and preventive interventions are likely to be the most effective strategies. The 24-hour movement guidelines emphasize an integrated score, including physical activity (PA), sedentary time, and sleep. The combined effect of adhering to all three 24-hour movement guidelines on CVD events remains unclear. In a prospective assessment of 13 897 Spanish university graduates from the Seguimiento Universidad de Navarra cohort, the relationship between a comprehensive exposure (adherence to all three 24-hour movement guidelines) and CVD incidence was investigated. Participants completed baseline questionnaires from 1999, with biennial follow-up. Exposure was assessed using the Canadian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines: ≥ 150 minutes/week of moderate-to-vigorous PA, ≤ 8 hours/day sitting, and 7–9 hours/night sleep (or 7–8 hours for ≥ 65 years). A composite score (0–3 points) was calculated for the exposure. The primary endpoint was incident CVD (nonfatal myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death). Nearly half (46.68%) of participants met all three guidelines, while only 0.96% met none. Over a mean follow-up of 14.48 years, 148 cardiovascular event (CVE) occurred. Fully adjusted models revealed a significantly reduced CVE risk for participants meeting two [hazard ratio (HR) = 0.37; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.14–0.99], or three (HR = 0.36; 95% CI: 0.14–0.95) guidelines compared to meeting none. Adherence to at least two of the 24-hour movement guidelines appears to be associated with a lower risk of CVEs. These findings suggest that a comprehensive approach to daily movement behaviors may play a beneficial role in CVD prevention. Public health strategies could consider promoting these integrated guidelines as part of broader efforts to improve cardiovascular health.

title: Hepatitis B screening among asylum seekers: a retrospective cohort study in Modena, Northern Italy
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis B virus remains a major health challenge among migrants from high-endemic regions arriving in low-endemic countries like Italy. However, more evidence on both infection burden and immunity gaps among asylum seekers is needed to inform prevention policies. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 739 asylum seekers screened for Hepatitis B virus (HBV) in Modena, Northern Italy, between 2019 and 2023. Serological testing included quantitative determination of HBsAg, HBcAb, and HBsAb, allowing identification of active infection, natural immunity, vaccine-induced immunity, and susceptibility. Demographic characteristics, geographic origin, and migration routes were analyzed in relation to HBV status. title: Shaping public health policy in personalized prevention: the multidimensional PROPHET framework
abstract: Abstract There is currently no widely accepted framework to guide decision-making for preventive approaches using genetic and genomic technologies. In the context of the PROPHET project, we developed a multidimensional framework integrating Health Technology Assessment and Health Impact Assessment, complemented by a monitoring phase to assess the impact of policies implementing personalized prevention interventions. This integrated approach links technical, clinical, and societal dimensions, supporting prevention strategies that are effective, equitable and sustainable. The PROPHET framework supports policy makers in the equitable and efficient implementation of personalized prevention policies at scale.

title: Institutions, people, knowledge: rebuilding the capacities of global health diplomacy
Ceuta 2026: the case for guaranteed health surge capacity at Europe’s external borders
abstract: On 30–31 July 2026, tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta in under 48 hours: the largest single migratory surge recorded at a European external border. Spain’s government confirmed 72 000 arrivals in a statement of 10 August, an episode that left 82 dead, mainly by drowning, according to official Spanish records, and a further 67 estimated on the Moroccan side by the Spanish NGO Caminando Fronteras, per figures endorsed by Human Rights Watch as of 21 August [ 1 ]. Some 5000 people who had crossed in late July remained in Ceuta by 13 August, per the interior ministry, a figure local organizations put as high as 10 000 [ 1 ]. According to the health minister, in her appearance before the Spanish Parliament on 27 August, health services recorded 1146 attendances on 30 July alone and between 250 and 350 a day thereafter, with some 75 more emergency presentations daily than a year earlier and a peak of 35 migrant inpatients on 13 August, in a system serving 84 000 residents [ 2 ]. Ceuta illustrates a recurring pattern: sudden mass arrivals overwhelm local health and reception systems, harming migrants and host communities alike, before any coordinated European public health response can be mobilized.

title: Neonatal hypoglycemia nursing decision support system: mixed-methods development and evaluation using interrupted time series
abstract: Background Neonatal hypoglycemia risks irreversible neurological damage, necessitating timely intervention. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a Neonatal Hypoglycemia Nursing Decision Support System (NHNDSS) to enhance clinical decision-making and management of neonatal hypoglycemia. Methods This quasi-experimental study employed an interrupted time series (ITS) design using segmented regression analysis to assess both immediate and long-term impacts of the NHNDSS. Data were collected weekly across 20 time points during both the pre-implementation (June to October 2024, n = 1828) and post-implementation (December 2024 to April 2025, n = 1716) periods. Segmented regression was used to estimate changes in outcome level and trends following system deployment. Key outcomes included hypoglycemia incidence, recurrence, NICU transfers, hospital stay, breastfeeding guidance adherence, and missed glucose monitoring. Additionally, qualitative interviews were conducted with nurses post-implementation to explore their experiences with system usability and integration into clinical workflows. Results Among 3544 neonates screened, hypoglycemia incidence decreased from 30.14% (551/1828) to 24.94% (428/1716) post-implementation. Initial hypoglycemia incidence significantly declined ( β 3 = -0.014, P β 3 = -0.517, P = 0.003). The average length of hospital stay initially increased but significantly decreased over time ( β 3 = -0.144, P β 3 = -0.308, P β 3 = -0.149, P = 0.439) and breastfeeding guidance impact ( β 3 = 0.440, P = 0.279) were limited. Nurses acknowledged NHNDSS while suggesting improvements in interoperability and technical functionality. Conclusions NHNDSS supports evidence-based decision-making, improving neonatal hypoglycemia management and gaining clinical acceptance among nurses.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Federated learning approach to optimize coronary revascularization decisions with privacy-preserving data integration from multiple hospitals
abstract: Background Coronary revascularization has a crucial role in the treatment of acute coronary syndrome and significantly affects patient mortality. We aimed to develop a federated learning model to predict the receipt of coronary revascularization within 1 week after an emergency room visit among patients who obtained ECG and cardiac biomarker testing (troponin and CK-MB), while preserving privacy using multicenter data. We conducted a retrospective analysis using de-identified data from three hospitals in South Korea (Korea University Anam Hospital, Ansan Hospital, and Guro Hospital). Methods This study included patients who underwent electrocardiography, troponin, and CK-MB tests, and excluded those who were discharged, deceased, transferred, or had trauma. The data were divided into training (January 2017 to July 2020) and test (August 2020 to July 2021) sets for model development and evaluation. We developed models using local, centralized, and federated learning approaches. To enhance privacy, we added Gaussian noise (SD = 0.01) to each site’s parameters before server aggregation. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, the area under the precision-recall curve, precision, recall, and accuracy. Clinical usefulness was evaluated using Cohen’s kappa, and the model predictions were compared with physicians’ decisions regarding coronary angiography. Results This study included 26,906 cases from Anam, 27,194 cases from Ansan, and 21,397 cases from Guro, with revascularization rates ranging from 2.6% to 3.4%. Both the federated learning and centralized learning models outperformed the local learning model, achieving an AUROC of 0.95 and an AUPRC of 0.64. Furthermore, the federated learning model demonstrated robust performance even with added noise and showed moderate-to-substantial agreement with physicians’ decisions to perform coronary angiography. Conclusions Federated learning using multi-center emergency room improved discrimination for predicting receipt of coronary revascularization among patients undergoing ECG and cardiac biomarker testing, while avoiding direct data sharing. This approach may enable scalable decision support that reduces unnecessary coronary angiography while maintaining identification of patients likely to require intervention.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Real-world implementation of an EMR-integrated mobile patient self-report system for injured patients in the emergency department: a retrospective observational study
abstract: Background Communication errors and information loss during history-taking are common in the emergency department (ED). Although digital patient self-report systems may mitigate these problems, prior studies often required hospital-owned devices or app installation, limiting scalability. We evaluated the real-world implementation of an electronic medical record (EMR)-integrated mobile web-based patient self-report system for injured patients delivered through a widely used messaging platform. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective study of injury-related ED visits at a tertiary academic hospital in Seoul, South Korea. From June 7 to December 31, 2023, eligible patients received a structured injury history questionnaire link via a mobile messaging platform during ED waiting time, and responses were automatically imported into the EMR. The primary outcome was questionnaire completion among message recipients; associated factors were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Documentation completeness of registry-mandated injury fields and agreement of patient-entered responses with the medical record were additionally assessed. Results Of 3,966 injury-related ED visits, 3,684 were eligible, 3,029 (82.2%) received the questionnaire message, and 962 (31.8%) of message recipients completed it. In adjusted analyses among message recipients, younger age groups had higher completion than patients aged ≥ 75 years, and completion was also higher with longer waiting times. Completion was higher among patients with lower-acuity visits, during daytime and evening visits than nighttime visits, and among patients arriving by other vehicle or other ambulance than by 119 ambulance. Sex was not associated with completion. Additionally, documentation completeness was higher among patients who completed the questionnaire, and patient-reported responses showed high agreement with documentation (95.2% for general injuries and 91.7% for traffic injuries). Conclusions An EMR-integrated mobile web-based patient self-report system was implemented in a real-world ED setting, and questionnaire completion was associated with greater documentation completeness, while patient-reported responses showed high agreement with documentation. These findings identify patient- and workflow-related considerations that may inform the future implementation and optimization of mobile self-report systems in the ED. Trial registration number Not applicable.

title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting short-term mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury
abstract: Background Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is a life-threatening complication in critically ill patients, with a high 28-day mortality rate. Current prognostic tools lack accuracy, especially in early/mild SA-AKI, highlighting an urgent need for more effective prediction models. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 1,823 adult SA-AKI patients from a single intensive care unit (ICU). A baseline-based model was developed using 40 features encompassing demographics, comorbidities, vital signs, laboratory indices, and organ support status. Five machine learning algorithms were trained and evaluated on an independent test set. The optimal model was compared against eight clinical indices. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and interpretability was achieved using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results The XGBoost model demonstrated superior discriminative performance for predicting 28-day mortality, achieving an AUC of 0.881 (95% CI: 0.840–0.916) in the test cohort, significantly outperforming all traditional clinical indices. The model maintained robust predictive accuracy across key clinical subgroups, particularly in patients with milder disease. SHAP analysis identified lactic acid, FiO 2 , Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) as the most influential predictors. Conclusions The developed XGBoost model provides a highly accurate and interpretable tool for early prediction of 28-day mortality in SA-AKI patients, outperforming conventional scores. Its strong performance in identifying high-risk patients in milder cases could facilitate timely interventions and improve resource allocation. Clinical trial number Not applicable.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Development of a multimodel predictive framework for gangrenous cholecystitis with SHAP-based interpretability
abstract: Background Gangrenous Cholecystitis (GC) is a critical pathological type of acute cholecystitis that tends to induce gallbladder wall necrosis or perforation, thereby leading to localized or diffuse peritonitis and is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Due to its nonspecific clinical symptoms and strong heterogeneous manifestations, timely and accurate identification of GC preoperatively remains a clinical challenge. To address this unmet clinical need, we developed an interpretable machine learning (ML) model using routinely available preoperative variables to facilitate the early prediction of GC and support clinical decision-making. Methods This was a retrospective cohort study, including 487 patients with acute cholecystitis who underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy in our hospital between February 2020 and July 2023. After initial univariate analysis and logistic regression, nine ML models were constructed, including logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), XGBoost, LightGBM, support vector machine (SVM), artificial neural network (ANN), k-nearest neighbor (KNN), linear discriminant analysis (LDA), and a Stacking ensemble model. LASSO regression was used to select key preoperative predictors. Model performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, F1-score, sensitivity, specificity, decision curve analysis (DCA), and calibration curves. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was performed to enhance model interpretability. Results LASSO regression identified five key preoperative predictors: preoperative C-reactive protein (pre-CRP), gallbladder diameter, pericholecystic exudation, albumin (ALB), and basophil percentage (BA). Among all constructed models, XGBoost and RF exhibited superior predictive performance, with AUC values of 0.90 and 0.89, respectively. Both models demonstrated robust discrimination, good calibration, and significant net clinical benefit across the entire range of decision thresholds. SHAP analysis revealed that pre-CRP and gallbladder diameter were the most influential predictors of GC, while BA and ALB showed inverse or sample-dependent associations with GC occurrence. Conclusions We developed an interpretable, non-invasive, and high-performance ML framework for preoperative GC prediction using routine clinical variables. This framework provides a valuable clinical tool to assist surgeons in decision-making and early risk stratification of patients with suspected GC, potentially improving patient outcomes by enabling timely intervention.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Interpretable machine-learning models for Guillain-Barré syndrome subtype assignment using acute-phase nerve conduction study: a multicenter study
abstract: Background Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) comprises clinically and electrophysiologically heterogeneous subtypes whose assignment may vary according to nerve conduction study (NCS) timing, serological availability, and examiner expertise. Interpretable machine-learning models may help standardize subtype assignment from acute-phase NCS data, with and without serology. Methods In a multicenter cohort of 99 patients across nine Korean hospitals (73 internal, 26 external), NCS parameters harmonized across acquisition systems and stimulation protocols were used to train gradient-boosting models (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) to classify three mechanism-oriented operational subtypes (axonal-predominant, demyelinating, and Miller Fisher spectrum) under with-serology and without-serology conditions, with the without-serology model as the primary analysis. Discrimination was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (PRC) over repeated internal splits, with the external set serving as an independent validation set. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to examine whether model attributions were consistent with conventional electrophysiological patterns. Results In the primary without-serology analysis, macro-averaged AUC was 0.87 internally and 0.80 on external validation, increasing to 0.92 and 0.90 with serology. SHAP attributions identified subtype-relevant NCS features and supported model face validity, although performance estimates were limited by the small external sample. Conclusions Interpretable machine-learning models showed preliminary ability to reproduce expert-assigned GBS subtype assignments from acute-phase NCS. Feature attributions were consistent with expected electrophysiological patterns, supporting model face validity. Larger prospective cohorts with independent adjudication and outcome linkage are needed before these models can be used for clinical decision-making or mechanistic inference.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Artificial intelligence and IoT-enabled approaches for COPD detection and monitoring: a systematic literature review
abstract: Background Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Conventional approaches to COPD diagnosis and management rely on periodic clinical assessments, limiting opportunities for early detection and continuous patient monitoring. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies have enabled intelligent, data-driven healthcare solutions for COPD detection and management. This systematic literature review synthesizes current evidence on AI- and IoT-enabled approaches for COPD detection and management, and it identifies existing research gaps and implementation challenges. Methods This review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A comprehensive systematic literature review was performed across PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar for studies published between January 2015 and May 2026. Following duplicate removal and a two-stage screening process using predefined eligibility criteria, 32 peer-reviewed studies were included. The selected studies were synthesized under four COPD detection and management domains: early detection, exacerbation prediction, remote monitoring, and self-monitoring. Results The reviewed studies demonstrate that AI and IoT technologies can improve COPD detection and management through intelligent analysis of physiological and environmental data collected from wearable devices, smart sensors, and digital health platforms. Traditional machine learning algorithms and deep learning models showed promising performance for COPD detection and exacerbation prediction, while IoT-enabled systems supported continuous patient monitoring and self-monitoring. However, most studies focused on individual COPD management domains and were limited by small, single-center datasets and inadequate external validation. Conclusions AI-IoT integration has considerable potential to transform COPD management by enabling continuous, personalized, and data-driven healthcare. Nevertheless, future research should prioritize the development of integrated, cost-effective systems that combine early detection, exacerbation prediction, remote monitoring, and self-monitoring within a unified framework, supported by large-scale multicenter validation to facilitate real-world clinical adoption. Trial registration Registration number CRD420261448597 Date 14 Jul 2026.

title: Cross-national transportability and local adaptation of a parsimonious 30-day mortality prediction model for ICU patients with bloodstream infection: from MIMIC-IV to a Chinese tertiary hospital
abstract: Background Timely risk stratification of ICU patients with bloodstream infection (BSI) is essential for guiding clinical decisions. Prediction models developed in Western populations may not generalize to other regions because healthcare systems, case mix, and clinical practice differ. We evaluated the cross-national transportability of a parsimonious ICU mortality model and tested local logistic recalibration in a Chinese external cohort. Methods We developed a 30-day mortality model using MIMIC-IV ( n = 1,501) with Elastic Net regularization and multivariable logistic regression. The simplified model included five routinely available predictors: age, 24-hour Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), serum potassium, and fungal BSI. We externally validated the model in an independent cohort of 285 ICU patients with BSI from a tertiary teaching hospital in China. Results In internal validation, the simplified model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.776, compared with 0.796 for the full model. In the Chinese cohort, discrimination remained acceptable (AUC 0.764), but calibration was poor, with systematic underestimation of 30-day mortality (calibration-in-the-large > 0). Local logistic recalibration improved calibration, bringing the calibration-in-the-large and slope closer to target values and reducing the Brier score to 0.182. Conclusions The US-derived parsimonious model retained acceptable discrimination in this Chinese ICU cohort but showed important calibration drift. Local logistic recalibration may offer a practical, low-resource approach to support local adaptation. Because recalibration was estimated and evaluated in the same cohort, the improvement may be optimistic and requires validation in independent healthcare systems.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Improving thyroid cancer diagnosis through stacked explainable machine learning integrating ultrasound and Raman cytological features
abstract: Background Indeterminate thyroid cytology remains a diagnostic challenge. We investigated whether ultrasound-derived clinical features and Raman spectra acquired from fine-needle aspiration samples could be integrated within an explainable multimodal machine learning framework. Methods The analytical cohort comprised 203 patients from a single center who underwent thyroid surgery, including 64 follicular adenomas (FA) and 139 malignant lesions according to postoperative histology. The malignant class comprised 117 papillary thyroid carcinomas (PTC), 21 follicular-variant papillary thyroid carcinomas (FV-PTC), and one mixed FA+PTC lesion. The fixed primary architecture combined a clinical Logistic Regression classifier and a raw-Raman Extra Trees classifier through a Logistic Regression meta-learner. Internal validation used stratified fivefold cross-validation repeated 20 times, with all data-dependent preprocessing, stacking, and operating-threshold selection restricted to the corresponding training data. Results The stacked model achieved a mean repeated out-of-fold AUC of 0.856 (95% case-level bootstrap CI 0.796–0.909; resampling SD 0.011). In an exploratory held-out analysis of 93 TIR3A/TIR3B cases, the corresponding AUC was 0.859 (95% CI 0.783–0.922; resampling SD 0.019). SHAP analyses identified model-dependent clinical and Raman associations that were stable at the clinical-feature and Raman-region levels across resampled outer folds. Conclusions The multimodal model showed promising internal discrimination in a single-center, surgery-selected cohort. Prospective multicenter validation of a locked model and a prespecified clinical decision strategy is required before assessing clinical utility or any effect on surgical management.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Real-time sepsis risk stratification on cloud data warehouses: a fuzzy inference system on MIMIC-IV
abstract: Intensive care monitoring generates continuous streams of physiological measurements that demand real-time interpretation, yet traditional batch analytics cannot capture the temporal dynamics critical for early clinical intervention. We present an end-to-end, event-based framework that influences managed cloud infrastructure (Google BigQuery) and standard SQL to construct a unified, temporally aware clinical event from the MIMIC-IV v3.1 database. In addition to conventional threshold-based warnings, we implement a Mamdani fuzzy inference system that represents clinical reasoning using three input variables (qSOFA score, hours since suspected infection, and infection confidence) and thirteen linguistic rules. The fuzzy model produces well-calibrated risk scores (Brier = 0.090) on 38,888 ICU events from 17,783 hospital admissions, with 79.7% of rule-based alerts classified as high fuzzy risk and the remaining 20.3% assigned moderate risk based on temporal context. The system shows consistency with existing clinical guidelines while providing graded, interpretable outputs. This architecture proves that real-time, event-based analytics can be supported by managed cloud warehouses without specialized stream processors, and that fuzzy reasoning offers scalable, interpretable risk stratification that binary thresholds cannot achieve.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Web-based contraception decision support tool and women’s decisional conflict: a cluster randomised trial in Spain
abstract: Background The choice of a contraceptive method is a complex decision in which decisional conflict can occur, which can lead to poor adherence and unplanned pregnancies. The objective was to assess whether a web-based Decision Support Tool (DST) reduced decisional conflict compared with usual contraceptive counselling. Methods A parallel, controlled cluster randomised clinical trial was carried out in 43 clinical contraceptive counselling units in Spain between 2019 and 2021. Seventy-one professionals were randomly assigned to intervention group or control group and recruited a sample of 895 women. Participants in the intervention group (IG, n = 478) received professional counselling supported by the DST, after brief training in its use, while those in the control group (CG, n = 417) received the same professional counselling without the tool (usual care). Decisional conflict, a prespecified secondary outcome of the trial, was measured with O’Connor’s 16-item Decisional Conflict Scale. Results Decisional conflict was low in both groups; only 1.9% of participants in the intervention group and 1.7% in the control group had DCS scores above 37.5. After accounting for the clustering effect by professional and adjusting for baseline covariates, no statistically significant differences in total decisional conflict were observed between the groups (adjusted mean difference: 2.2 points; 95% CI: −1.9 to 6.3; p = 0.297), nor in any of the subscales (all p ≥ 0.13). Variability between professionals was considerable (ICC = 0.37 for the total score; between 0.24 and 0.34 for the subscales), and the results remained unchanged in a three-level sensitivity analysis. Conclusions In this cluster-randomised trial, we found no evidence that the decision support tool (DST) reduced decisional conflict among women receiving contraceptive counselling; after accounting for the clustering effect by provider, decisional conflict did not differ significantly between groups and was generally low. A substantial portion of the residual variability in decisional conflict was attributable to the providers offering the counselling rather than to the tool itself. Therefore, the DST may be more useful as a complement to professional counselling than as a substitute for it. Trial registration ISRCTN58279944. Registered 15 April 2019 (prospectively registered).
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: CARDINAL: physiology-guided directional structure and prototype learning for small-sample echocardiographic assessment
abstract: Background Echocardiographic assessment of diastolic dysfunction from small clinical cohorts is susceptible to overfitting, unstable feature attribution, and poorly calibrated confidence estimates, limiting the clinical translation of machine learning models. This study aimed to develop and evaluate CARDINAL, a physiology-guided framework combining a dataset-specific structural prior, directional graph regularization, prototype-aligned representation learning, and Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty estimation, and to assess whether it improves discrimination, calibration, and uncertainty-guided referral relative to established tabular learning models under a leakage-controlled protocol. Methods We present CARDINAL, a physiology-guided framework that integrates four components: (i) a dataset-specific structural prior that encodes known physiological relations among clinical variables; (ii) directional graph refinement under sparsity and acyclicity penalties, serving as a regularizer and interpretability scaffold rather than as an identified causal model; (iii) prototype-aligned representation learning to enforce intra-class compactness under limited data; and (iv) Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty estimation ($$T=30$$, dropout rate 0.20) for calibrated confidence and selective referral of borderline cases. The study cohort comprised 118 cases classified by a composite reference index as normal ($$n=37$$), mild ($$n=42$$), or severe ($$n=39$$). Evaluation followed a leakage-controlled protocol with a fixed stratified 70/15/15 split producing an 82-case training pool, an 18-case validation set, and an 18-case locked test set evaluated once after all modeling choices were finalized. Results On the locked test set, CARDINAL achieved a binary abnormal-versus-normal ROC-AUC of 0.969, AUPRC of 0.990, accuracy of 0.944, sensitivity of 0.923, specificity of 1.000, Brier score of 0.066, ECE of 0.095, and NLL of 0.223. Patient-level DeLong and McNemar tests were non-significant on this single split ($$n=18$$), reflecting limited statistical power rather than equivalence. Across 20 matched repeated runs, CARDINAL showed consistent stability with Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon $$p = 3.05\times10^{-5}$$ versus TabPFN-tuned. Three-class confusion analysis indicated reasonable grade-level discrimination, with misclassifications occurring predominantly between adjacent grades. Ablation analysis suggested that each framework component—directional graph regularization, prototype alignment, and uncertainty calibration—contributed to overall performance. Three public datasets (UCI Heart Disease, Heart Failure Clinical Records, and MIMIC-IV) served as tabular robustness benchmarks; CARDINAL showed consistently modest numerical advantages across all four datasets. Conclusions These results suggest that physiological structure, prototype learning, and uncertainty quantification can be integrated within a leakage-controlled evaluation framework. Feature importance analysis indicated that $${E/e}^\prime$$ and LAVI—label-adjacent variables in the reference index—were the predominant contributors to model predictions, consistent with established cardiology guidelines. A complementary analysis excluding these label-adjacent variables preserved CARDINAL’s relative advantage (ROC-AUC 0.873 versus 0.846 for TabPFN-tuned). Uncertainty estimates may assist in identifying borderline cases for selective human review. These findings motivate prospective multi-center validation to evaluate clinical utility, transportability, and the impact of uncertainty-guided review on patient care.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based prediction model for 3-year major adverse cardiovascular events in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting: a multicenter study
abstract: Background Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) represent a residual risk following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and adversely affect long-term prognosis. Accurate risk prediction is critical for postoperative risk stratification and secondary prevention. We aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model for early postoperative estimation of 3-year MACE risk after CABG. Methods This multicenter retrospective study enrolled 3,930 adults undergoing CABG between January 2019 and December 2022 at eight cardiac centers in Jiangsu Province, China. We collected 232 preoperative, intraoperative, and early postoperative variables. Data from 3,018 patients at Nanjing First Hospital were divided into training and internal validation sets; data from 912 patients at seven other centers formed the external validation set. Features were selected using minimum redundancy maximum relevance (mRMR) followed by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Ten machine learning models were developed and compared. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to interpret the final model. Results The 3-year MACE incidence was 16.41% (645/3,930). Seventeen predictors were selected. The Extremely Randomized Trees (ET) model, selected based on internal validation performance, achieved AUROCs of 0.90 (95% CI: 0.87–0.93) in the internal validation set and 0.82 (95% CI: 0.78–0.86) in the external validation set, with an external AUC-PR of 0.59. At the prespecified probability threshold of 0.50, external accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score were 0.87, 0.54, 0.94, and 0.59, respectively. External Brier score, calibration intercept, and slope were 0.100, −0.20, and 0.80, respectively. Postoperative left ventricular ejection fraction was the most important predictor, followed by preoperative neutrophil percentage and preoperative New York Heart Association (NYHA) class. Conclusions The ET model provided externally validated estimates of 3-year MACE risk after CABG. The model is intended for early postoperative risk stratification once required postoperative inputs are available, although threshold-specific sensitivity was limited. SHAP analysis described predictor contributions, and a web-based calculator was developed for further evaluation. Prospective evaluation and threshold validation are required before clinical implementation.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Application of machine learning prediction models for in-hospital mortality in diabetic sepsis patients: a study based on the MIMIC IV database
abstract: Background Sepsis complicated by diabetes mellitus represents a significant clinical challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Accurate prognostication of in-hospital mortality in this complex patient population is crucial for optimizing clinical decision making, resource allocation, and patient management strategies. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study utilizing data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database. The study focused on adult ICU patients with concurrent diagnoses of sepsis and diabetes mellitus. Six machine learning algorithms were evaluated for their predictive performance: Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), XGBoost and LightGBM. Additionally, we assessed the prognostic capability of the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score. Model discrimination was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). To enhance model interpretability, we employed SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values to elucidate the relative importance of predictor variables. Results The study cohort comprised 7716 patients, with 1357 (17.6%) experiencing in-hospital mortality. Among the machine learning models evaluated, GBDT exhibited superior predictive performance achieving an AUC of 0.792 (95% CI: 0.769–0.814). This performance surpassed that of other machine learning algorithms and the conventional SOFA score. SHAP analysis provided valuable insights into the hierarchical importance of various clinical and demographic features contributing to the GBDT model’s predictions. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning approaches in accurately predicting in-hospital mortality among ICU patients with sepsis and diabetes mellitus. These advanced analytical techniques outperform traditional scoring systems such as SOFA. The integration of SHAP values enhances model interpretability, potentially facilitating the adoption of these predictive tools in clinical practice. Further multi-center validation studies and prospective trials are warranted to confirm the generalizability of these results and to explore the clinical impact of implementing such models in diverse healthcare settings.

title: Design and evaluation of a smartphone-based self-care application for patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting
abstract: Background In recent years, the use of mobile applications for medical care education purposes has gained considerable attention. However, in Iran, there is no effective application specifically designed for post-open-heart surgery care to educate patients on self-care following cardiac surgery. Therefore, the present study was conducted with the aim of designing and evaluating a smartphone-based self-care application for patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Methods This applied research focused on technology development was carried out in four phases during 2024–2025. The first phase involved identifying the educational needs of patients undergoing CABG through a review of relevant literature and articles. The second phase entailed collecting the necessary self-care content from credible sources, resulting in the development of 41 educational topics presented in text and video formats, which were subsequently validated by experts. In the third phase, the application was designed and approved by specialists. In the fourth phase, the application was evaluated by 35 patients who had undergone cardiac surgery using the standardized Questionnaire for User Interaction Satisfaction (QUIS). Data analysis was performed using SPSS software version 21, employing descriptive statistical methods to assess the application. Results Among the 35 participants, 60.0% were male, 57.1% were aged 51–60 years, and 51.4% had a high school diploma or lower educational attainment. Regarding usability, 91.4% of patients rated the application as good, 5.7% as moderate, and 2.9% as poor. The mean overall evaluation score for the application was 7.9 ± 1.032 (range: 0–9). The highest mean scores were observed for user learnability (8.2 ± 0.84) and overall application capabilities (8.6 ± 0.54). Conclusion The developed smartphone-based self-care application demonstrated favorable usability and user satisfaction among patients undergoing CABG. These findings suggest that the application may serve as a complementary digital tool to support post-discharge self-care. However, clinical effectiveness was not evaluated in the present study, and further studies are required to determine its effects on self-care behaviors and clinical outcomes.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Unveiling diagnostic variability: clinical performance and pitfalls of two commercial AI tools for intracranial haemorrhage detection
abstract: Background and Objectives Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies have become increasingly prominent in emergency neuroimaging, yet most clinical studies have evaluated only single diagnostic models. Comparative evidence on the performance trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity in AI-based detection of intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) is limited. The objective of this study is to compare the diagnostic accuracy of two FDA-cleared AI models for detecting ICH on non-contrast brain computed tomography (NCBCT) and to explore the trade-offs between high sensitivity and high specificity algorithms. Methods In this single-centre, retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, consecutive adult patients undergoing NCBCT in the emergency department between 1 September 2024 and 28 February 2025 were included ( n = 3,884). Each CT was analysed by two FDA-cleared AI algorithms—NeuroSuite CT ICH Assessment System (EFAI-ICH) and Rapid ICH (RAPIDAI-ICH)—using 5 mm axial reconstructions. Model outputs were benchmarked against the final neuroradiologist report, with all false-positive and false-negative findings adjudicated. Performance metrics included sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), with subgroup analysis by ICH subtype. Results Out of 3,884 CT, 421(10.8%) exhibited ICH, comprising 183 intraparenchymal, 56 intraventricular, 201 subarachnoid, 183 subdural, and 18 epidural subtypes. EFAI-ICH yielded 377 true-positives and 44 false-negatives (sensitivity 89.5%), whereas RAPIDAI-ICH yielded 308 true-positives and 113 false-negatives (sensitivity 73.2%). Specificity favoured RAPIDAI-ICH (97.1% vs 91.5%). Overall accuracy was higher for RAPIDAI-ICH compared to EFAI-ICH (94.5% vs 91.3%). EFAI-ICH demonstrated superior NPV (98.6%), while RAPIDAI-ICH achieved superior PPV (75.7%). Discussion Both AI platforms demonstrated robust diagnostic capabilities for emergency ICH detection, with complementary strengths. EFAI-ICH minimizes missed bleeds but at the cost of more false alarms; RAPIDAI-ICH excels at ruling out haemorrhage but risks under-calling subtle bleeds. Recognizing these performance variations is crucial for optimal AI integration into neuroradiological practice and ultimately enhancing patient care outcomes. Graphical Abstract

title: A clinically conditional deep learning model for predicting histological subtypes of pituitary neuroendocrine tumors from hematoxylin-eosin whole-slide images
abstract: Background Histological subtype classification of pituitary neuroendocrine tumors is important for prognostic assessment and therapeutic decision-making. However, current subtype classification relies heavily on extensive immunohistochemistry, which can be time-consuming, costly, and tissue-consuming. We aimed to develop a clinically conditional deep learning model that integrates routinely available clinical features with hematoxylin-eosin-stained whole-slide images to predict five subtypes of pituitary neuroendocrine tumors. Methods To address the histomorphologic characteristics of pituitary neuroendocrine tumors, we designed an automatic pathology-informed patch selection strategy focusing on diagnostically relevant tumor regions, and applied a masking strategy to simulate missing clinical features. Model performance was evaluated using ensemble inference from five cross-validated models on an internal test set and a temporal and external validation set. Models were assessed by accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, with 95% confidence intervals. Paired DeLong and McNemar tests were used to compare models, with P Results On the internal hold-out test set, the clinically conditional model achieved an overall accuracy of 91.8% and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.934, outperforming the unimodal WSIs model (accuracy, 87.3%; AUC, 0.905; P P Conclusions These preliminary findings suggest that integrating clinical feature with histopathology may better simulate the comprehensive reasoning process of pathologists in routine diagnoses. This exploratory approach could potentially serve as a supplementary decision-support tool to facilitate ancillary test prioritization, optimize diagnostic workflow, and improve resource allocation, particularly in resource-constrained settings.
journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

title: Uncertainty-aware prediction of 48-month eGFR decline in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a secondary analysis of ACCORD
abstract: Background Long-horizon kidney trajectory models in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) commonly report point estimates or event risks, leaving uncertainty around predicted eGFR change less clear. We developed and internally evaluated a baseline clinical model with conformal intervals for annualized 48-month eGFR change. Methods We analyzed 6,853 adults with T2DM and high cardiovascular risk from the multicenter Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD) trial with baseline and 48-month eGFR and at least three measurements. We compared penalized linear, random forest, histogram gradient boosting, and XGBoost models with mean-outcome and clinical linear benchmarks. The primary model included baseline eGFR, demographics, cardiometabolic measures, medications, and history. Five-fold training-set cross-validation selected the model, while separate calibration and test sets evaluated point accuracy and calibration, rapid-decline discrimination, and split and locally adaptive 90% interval coverage and width. Results In 1,371 test participants, random forest mean absolute error was 3.370 mL/min/1.73 m² per year (95% CI 3.221 to 3.527) and R² was 0.359 (95% CI 0.233 to 0.466). Locally adaptive intervals achieved coverage of 0.909 (95% CI 0.894 to 0.923) and mean width of 14.706 mL/min/1.73 m² per year. Rapid decline ( ≤ − 5 mL/min/1.73 m² per year) occurred in 467 (34.1%), with AUC of 0.732 (95% CI 0.708 to 0.758). Unadjusted Q5 had higher error and rapid-decline prevalence than Q1. After width quintiles were assigned within 20 baseline-eGFR strata, Q5 had higher HbA1c (8.6% vs. 8.2%), triglycerides (253.3 vs. 177.5 mg/dL), and female proportion (49.6% vs. 30.7%) than Q1 despite similar baseline eGFR. Conclusions Conformal intervals achieved near-nominal marginal coverage but remained broad. Conditioned width differences across HbA1c, triglycerides, and sex revealed variation in modeled uncertainty beyond baseline eGFR. These findings make forecast uncertainty explicit and provide a foundation for external, decision-focused evaluation. Clinical trial number Not applicable.
