title: An XFEM-based moving refinement patch method for crack propagation
abstract: Accurate simulation of crack propagation by the extended finite element method (XFEM) is often limited by the high computational cost associated with global mesh refinement, or the need for predefined crack path. This paper presents an efficient alternative, namely an XFEM-based moving refinement patch method (MRPM). The main contribution is a penalty-based coupling scheme that connects a locally refined mesh patch with a coarse global mesh. With this formulation, the refinement patch can dynamically follow the propagating crack tip without re-meshing or prescribing the crack path in advance. In this way, the proposed method combines the accuracy of local mesh refinement with the computational efficiency of coarse-mesh discretization. The performance of the proposed method is assessed through several benchmark problems, including crack propagation in a beam under four-point bending and crack coalescence in a plate containing two separated cracks. The results show that MRPM can accurately capture both local fracture evolution and global structural response, while significantly reducing the computational cost compared with the classical XFEM.

title: Hybrid LRA constitutive model-driven FEM: small sample machine learning framework for evaluating four-point bending property of the laser deposition repaired TA15 short beam in aerospace
abstract: For the problems of scarce data, high cost and low efficiency in four-point bending property evaluation of the Laser Deposition Repaired TA15 short beam in aerospace, a Hybrid Constitutive Model Driven FEM - Small Sample Machine Learning framework is established to solve small sample scale issue in this study. Five Machine Learning model- ANN, SVR, GPR, RF and LSBoost were trained and compared by combining a novel K-Means Clustering-based data augmentation strategy (KMCE). the KMCE (Tangent core function) - GPR demonstrating superior accuracy and stability, achieving the lowest error (

title: Automated lattice embedding and transitioning with application to multi-lattice topology optimization
abstract: Structures composed of spatially-varying architected materials have great potential for targeted mechanical and/or multifunctional behavior, but lack of structural integrity at the interfaces between different architecture geometries can degrade the expected performance. While smooth transitions between functionally-defined architected materials can be designed easily using mathematical interpolation, a robust transitioning scheme is less apparent for architectures without a simple mathematical description. Here we focus on periodic, strut-based lattices exhibiting cubic symmetry of their nodes and propose an algorithm that automates the design of smoothly-varying transitions between any finite set of these lattices embedded in a macroscale structure. The algorithm takes in lattice existence and relative density fields indicating which lattice and associated relative density exists at each point in the macroscale structure, and an ordered set of $$m$$ key lattices to be embedded. We define a transitional skeleton (i.e., nodes and connectivity) that encapsulates all $$m$$ key lattices via a continuous morphing between different nodal configurations, and use it to spatially transition between the different lattice geometries. Material is added after manipulating the skeletons according to the given relative density distribution. We explain details of the algorithm in 2D using a multi-lattice design obtained from topology optimization and show the flexibility and robustness of the algorithm by generating a lattice-embedded rendering of The Starry Night by Vincent Van Gogh. In 3D, we explore the effect of the transition radius and demonstrate manufacturability of the spatially-varying lattice-embedded structures by 3D printing a multi-lattice canopy obtained from topology optimization.

title: Deep generative graphs for synthesizing microstructure of topology-preserved polymer-bonded explosives
abstract: We introduce a generative artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm trained to generate realistic three-dimensional microstructures of polymer-bonded explosives (PBX). We idealize PBX as a two-phase composite with anisotropic crystals as inclusions in a polymer matrix. To improve memory efficiency, we introduce a two-stage hierarchical algorithm in which a deep generative graph model captures the grain topology in the PBX, while a latent diffusion model generates the 3D geometry of individual grains. This approach enables us to idealize each grain as a simply connected body embedded in three-dimensional space. This divide-and-conquer strategy enables us to bypass the challenging task of generating manifolds of complex topology and to avoid wasted computations when applying convolutions to grids dominated by constant values. To generate PBX microstructures with realistic grain topology, we sample sub-domains of segmented micro-computed tomography (CT) images of a mock PBX with Idoxuridine (IDOX) grains to form a dataset. Each sub-domain is represented by a node-weighted graph with the position, size, and shape descriptors stored as node features. The topological dataset is then used to train a graph recurrent neural network (GraphRNN) that learns to add nodes and edges sequentially to form a weighted graph describing the IDOX granular network, consisting of nodes with features connected by edges. With the global topology prescribed, the individual grains are generated by a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model that takes node features as inputs and produces grains that match the prescribed node features. Numerical examples assess the similarity between the actual and synthetic microstructures.

title: Understanding surrogate modeling for reliability analysis: optimization versus active learning with a probability-aware SPLA metric
abstract: Surrogate modeling is widely used to reduce the computational cost of Monte Carlo simulation (MCS)-based reliability analysis involving expensive performance functions. However, the relative effectiveness of different surrogate construction strategies in reliability applications remains insufficiently understood. This study compares two major paradigms for surrogate modeling: optimization-based and active learning-based strategies, referred to as oMMs and iMMs. Three representative techniques—artificial neural networks, Gaussian process regression, and support vector regression—are implemented within these frameworks. To assess surrogate performance from a reliability perspective, a probability-aware sign-penalized limit-state accuracy (SPLA) index is proposed. The index emphasizes prediction accuracy near the limit-state surface and penalizes sign misclassification that directly affects failure probability estimation. Four structural and geotechnical examples are investigated. The results show that high global surrogate accuracy achieved by oMMs does not guarantee reliable failure probability estimates and often requires substantially higher computational cost. In contrast, iMMs consistently provide more accurate and stable reliability predictions by adaptively enriching training data near the limit-state surface, as reflected by higher SPLA values. Furthermore, SPLA is employed to guide the selection of reliable models in bootstrap-based bagging ensembles, enhancing the robustness of surrogate predictions while maintaining high reliability estimation accuracy.

title: Efficient finite element quadrature on immersed voxel data
abstract: High-resolution computed tomography (CT) scans provide voxel-wise information on geometry and material properties. Direct numerical simulations on CT data in which each voxel is considered a finite element can yield billions of unknowns, a resolution that is often excessive. Coarsening the finite element mesh reduces the number of unknowns, but accurate quadrature then becomes a challenge. Composed integration by distributing Gauss-Legendre points on each voxel is computationally expensive due to the resulting large number of integration points. The standard remedy is to pre-integrate the stiffness contribution of each voxel in reference coordinates. However, this approach does not directly extend to local enrichment of the finite element space. For example, under hierarchical octree-based refinement the basis functions vary from element to element. For such cases, we develop an efficient voxel quadrature scheme based on a modified moment-fitting approach. The method computes a custom integration rule for each element which absorbs voxel information directly into the integration weights. This enables exact integration of the stiffness matrix of finite elements with any polynomial degree while limiting the number of quadrature points during assembly. In contrast to pre-integration, our approach decouples the material resolution from the finite element basis and is even faster for coarse finite element resolutions, while remaining far cheaper than composed Gauss-Legendre quadrature. We demonstrate voxel-based moment fitting on three examples: a scaling analysis for heterogeneous voxel data, a voxelized L-shaped domain with adaptivity driven by a residual-based error estimator, and a locally refined phase-field fracture simulation.

title: Voronoi diagram-based volume decomposition and overhang control in topology optimization for multi-axis additive manufacturing
abstract: The paper proposes a partition-based topology optimization approach for multi-axis additive manufacturing (AM), aiming to fully leverage its advantages in dynamic build orientation adjustment and region-specific manufacturing. To address the challenge of decomposing the evolving structural layouts, an implicit decomposition method based on Voronoi diagrams is introduced, which employs a Softmax function combined with Heaviside projection. This approach yields a non-overlapping decomposition whose partitions and interfaces together cover the design domain, and hence provides stable partitioning for arbitrary geometries. Complex volume decomposition is achieved by controlling a small number of seed points within the Voronoi diagram. To prevent unrealistic diffuse interfaces between partitions, a Kreisselmeier–Steinhauser(KS) aggregation-based distance constraint is imposed on the seed points. By integrating the volume decomposition with the spatial gradient of the structural density field, global overhang constraints are formulated for individual partitions. We then optimize the topological layout, partitions and their associated build orientations simultaneously to obtain self-supported design in density-based topology optimization. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, several 2D and 3D numerical examples are studied. The influence of partitioning parameters, including the initial build orientations in partitions and the number of partitions, on the optimized design is investigated. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method yields reasonable partitioned designs, with the overhang surfaces in the partitions effectively controlled.

title: A serial multi-layer latent mapping-based multi-fidelity framework for time-dependent reliability analysis under mixed random–fuzzy uncertainty
abstract: To address the problem of time-dependent reliability analysis for high-cost engineering structures under mixed random–fuzzy uncertainty, a novel multi-fidelity framework is proposed by integrating a serial multi-layer latent mapping model (SMLM) with hyper-rectangular constrained subset simulation (HCSS). The proposed method employs SMLM to provide a unified characterization of the correlation structure among data of different fidelity levels, thereby enhancing the response approximation capability for mixed inputs involving random continuous variables and fuzzy state variables. Meanwhile, HCSS generates critical candidate samples layer by layer within constrained hyper-rectangular regions, enabling sequential surrogate updates in the vicinity of the failure boundary and thus improving the efficiency and accuracy of interval estimation for time-dependent failure probabilities. Numerical examples and the engineering case of a wing box structure demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively fuse multi-fidelity information and maintain high accuracy and stability in boundary estimation while significantly reducing the number of high-fidelity model evaluations.

title: FEM-Bench: a structured scientific reasoning benchmark for evaluating code-generating LLMs
abstract: As LLMs advance their reasoning capabilities about the physical world, the absence of rigorous benchmarks for evaluating their ability to generate scientifically valid physical models has become a critical gap. Computational mechanics, the discipline that develops and applies mathematical models and numerical methods to predict the behavior of physical systems under forces, deformation, and constraints, provides an ideal foundation for structured scientific reasoning based evaluation. Problems follow a clear mathematical structure, enforce strict physical and numerical constraints, and support objective verification. The discipline also requires constructing explicit models of physical systems and reasoning about geometry, spatial relationships, and material behavior, which connects directly to emerging goals in AI related to physical reasoning and world modeling. We introduce FEM-Bench, a computational mechanics benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of LLMs to generate correct finite element method (FEM) code. FEM-Bench 2025 contains a suite of introductory but nontrivial tasks aligned with material from a first graduate course on computational mechanics. These tasks capture essential numerical and physical modeling challenges while representing only a small fraction of the complexity present in the discipline. Despite their simplicity, state-of-the-art LLMs do not reliably solve all of them. In a five attempt run, the best performing model at function writing, Gemini 3 Pro, completed 30/33 tasks at least one out of five times, and 26/33 tasks five out of five times. The best performing model at unit test writing, GPT-5, had an Average Joint Success Rate of 73.8%. Other popular models showed a broad range of performance on the benchmark. FEM-Bench establishes a structured foundation for evaluating AI-generated scientific code, and future iterations will incorporate increasingly sophisticated tasks to track progress as models evolve.

title: A parametric physics-informed deep learning approach for 6th-order bending analysis of MSGT microbeams
abstract: This study investigates the size-dependent static bending behavior of Euler-Bernoulli microbeams with the modified strain gradient theory (MSGT). To address the numerical stiffness and computational bottleneck caused by the sixth-order governing differential equations, a novel Parametric Physics-Informed Neural Network (P-PINN) framework is established. The original higher-order equation is mathematically decoupled into a trio of dependent systems of second-order differential equations, which enhances the gradient flow and convergence stability. Unlike traditional networks limited to fixed parameters, the P-PINN incorporates the dimensionless internal length scale ratio as a continuous input, functioning as a surrogate model for the predetermined parametric manifold without retraining. A dynamic Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) based adaptive loss weighting algorithm and a two-stage (Adam and L-BFGS) optimization strategy are employed to enforce complex higher-order boundary conditions. The framework is validated against analytical solutions across simply supported and two variations of clamped-free boundary conditions. The results demonstrate predictive accuracy with Mean Squared Errors strictly bounded between $$\:{10}^{-7}$$ and $$\:{10}^{-11}$$, verifying the framework’s potential to be an alternative solution method.

title: FLOWS: a model to simulate water and solutes fluxes in agricultural and environmental systems: 2. Modules for specific applications in water and nutrient management
abstract: This paper is the second of two companion studies. The first paper focused on describing the model FLOWS, theory and the model benchmarking. This paper addresses FLOWS modules on specific applications: irrigation, temperature, organic carbon processes and nutrient transformation and transport in the soil. It also includes applications of FLOWS model in real scenarios. In the irrigation module, FLOWS allows for different scenarios: (1) no irrigation, i.e., only rainfall; (2) irrigation introduced by the user as a top-boundary, temporally variable, input flux; (3) irrigation computed as the daily potential evapotranspiration demand; and (4) irrigation computed by the model. In the latter, FLOWS optimizes irrigation fluxes and schedule according to a criterion based on the average pressure head along a user-specified depth, e.g., the root zone. Since soil temperature influences several soil processes, FLOWS simulates the temperature distribution in depth and time by using a solution to heat flow equations proposed by van Wijk and De Vries. FLOWS simulates fertilizer applications as organic matter (manure and crop residues) or mineral fertilizers. It can either simulate organic matter decomposition with coupled carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus transformations governed by C:N and C:P ratios or simulate nitrogen transport alone using an empirical mineralization approach independent on organic matter dynamics. Two applications of the model are presented in this paper: (1) analysing the role of spatial variability in soil and vegetation for large-scale irrigation optimization, and (2) monitoring and modelling water and nutrient fluxes from irrigated fields to the surface drainage network. In the first application, FLOWS proved reliable for optimizing irrigation at large scales by accounting for the spatial variability of soil and vegetation properties and by enabling the analysis of the uncertainty associated with progressively overlooking this variability. In the second application, FLOWS was coupled with another physically based model (KWV) founded on kinematic wave theory. FLOWS was used to accurately simulate water, nitrate, and phosphorus fluxes to runoff, which were then routed through the KWV model to produce runoff hydrographs and nutrient concentrations at different sections of the drainage network and at the field outlet.

title: A mesh-based neural energy solver for linear and nonlinear plane elasticity problems
abstract: This study presents a mesh-based neural energy solver (MNES) for linear and nonlinear elasticity on fixed finite-element discretizations. MNES is formulated as a neural reparameterization of a discrete finite-element energy problem, in which only the nodal displacement vector is parameterized by a coordinate-based neural network, while the finite-element mesh, interpolation, boundary conditions, and element energies remain fixed. The loss function is defined as the total potential energy of the discretized system, assembled element-wise from strain energy and external work, with element energies evaluated using the predicted nodal displacements and the prescribed finite-element interpolation. Unlike residual-based physics-informed neural networks and continuous-field deep energy methods, the loss function is constructed directly from the discretized finite-element energy without requiring spatial differentiation of the neural network outputs with respect to the input coordinates. Several benchmark problems in both linear and nonlinear elasticity are investigated to assess the proposed formulation. The results demonstrate that MNES accurately reproduces the corresponding finite-element energy solutions and highlight the potential of neural reparameterization as an alternative formulation for solving discretized finite-element variational problems.

title: Free-form geometric modeling of ship hulls using generative adversarial networks
abstract: This paper presents a system-agnostic framework for ship hull generation that integrates Free-Form Deformation (FFD) with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The proposed FFD-GAN maps a low-dimensional latent vector to FFD control-point displacements, which deform a reference mesh through the FFD mechanism to produce feasible hull geometries. A key contribution is the development of a generative model independent of specific CAD systems, achieved through a mapping procedure that converts diverse geometric descriptions into a unified FFD representation, enabling training on hull data from multiple parameterization sources. Hydrodynamic performance is assessed using the Holtrop & Mennen empirical model, allowing rapid evaluation within a low-fidelity design framework. The generalization capability of FFD-GAN is examined under constraints beyond the training domain, where generated hulls retain geometric feasibility. Overall, the framework provides a compact and flexible approach to ship hull generation, effectively linking deep learning with geometric modeling for naval architecture applications.

title: Mechanical analysis of functionally graded materials with complex singularities by singularity-informed deep finite element method
abstract: Functionally graded materials (FGMs) containing interacting cracks and holes exhibit strong local singularities and steep displacement gradients, which pose significant challenges to conventional numerical analysis. This study proposes a Singularity-Informed Deep Finite Element Method (SIDFEM) for the elastic analysis of FGM plates with a central elliptical hole and asymmetric collinear cracks. Built on the Deep Finite Element Method (DFEM), the proposed method reconstructs the approximation space by embedding crack-tip distance information, near-tip square-root asymptotics, crack-surface topology, and hole-boundary enrichment, so that the neural approximation is better aligned with the local singular structure of the mechanical field. The displacement solution is obtained through discrete potential-energy minimization with FEM-style quadrature and a two-stage Adam/Limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (L-BFGS) optimization strategy. Compared with Abaqus reference solutions, the benchmark case yields a relative $$L_2$$ error of 0.026 for the displacement vector and a maximum absolute error of 0.015. In addition, compared with standard DFEM, SIDFEM reduces the relative $$L_2$$ errors of $$u_x$$, $$u_y$$, and the displacement vector by more than $$92\%$$. Further studies on ablation, geometric degeneration, defect rotation, load reversal, and generalized J -integral evaluation demonstrate the robustness and mechanical applicability of the proposed framework for fracture analysis of nonhomogeneous materials.

title: A parallel adaptive skip-mesh method for efficient simulation of microstructural evolutions in additive manufacturing
abstract: To resolve the high computational cost challenge in microstructural evolution simulations in additive manufacturing, a novel parallel adaptive skip-mesh (ASM) phase-field method is proposed. The adaptive skip-mesh criterion is established based on the automatic division of the computational domain into stable and active regions through the real-time monitoring of phase-field variable changes. In the stable regions, an adaptive skip interval strategy is employed to bypass the computation of non-essential nodes. High-resolution meshes are maintained near the grain boundaries, and a safety-check mechanism, including stability coefficient and consistency validation, is implemented to ensure computational accuracy. The average width of columnar grains in the simulation is found to deviate by less than 15% compared to the experimental results. In terms of computational efficiency, reductions of 68.05% in cell number and 56.03% in node number are achieved by the phase-field model based on the ASM method. The output storage requirement is reduced by 66.67%. The computation time is reduced by 66.15% with OpenMP alone, from 29.1 h to 9.85 h. While the combined OpenMP-ASM strategy achieves an overall reduction of approximately 79.04%, from 29.1 h to 6.1 h. The ASM-based PFM reproduces the microstructural evolution characteristics observed in the reported LMD cases, including the formation of Z-shaped columnar grains induced by bidirectional scanning. Computation time can be reduced by up to 28.3% with the appropriate initial skip interval.

title: Me-fPINNs: multi-model ensemble fractional physics-informed neural networks for solving fractional integro-differential equations
abstract: Fractional integro-differential equations (FIDEs) play a pivotal role in modeling nonlocal and memory-dependent phenomena across scientific and engineering domains. While fractional physics-informed neural networks (fPINNs) offer a mesh-free alternative to conventional numerical methods, their reliance on single-network architectures often leads to limited accuracy, structural bias, and poor generalization under sparse data or high-dimensional settings. To address these limitations, this work proposes a Multi-Model Ensemble Fractional Physics-Informed Neural Network (Me-fPINNs), a novel soft computing framework that integrates five heterogeneous base models constructed from seven neural networks with diverse architectures, activation functions, and loss formulations. A key innovation lies in an operator-decoupled subnetwork design, which separately approximates fractional derivative and integral operators before adaptively fusing them through a nonlinear ensemble network. Extensive numerical experiments on one-dimensional linear/nonlinear, three-dimensional, and coupled fractional systems, as well as inverse problems, demonstrate that Me-fPINNs consistently outperform conventional fPINNs in accuracy stability, and robustness. As a mesh-free deep learning scheme, Me-fPINNs provide a promising solution for complex fractional modeling tasks in real-world applications.

title: MilsPD: a lightweight multiphysics-integrated peridynamics solver
abstract: This paper presents MilsPD, a highly efficient multiphysics-integrated peridynamics (PD) solver designed for fracture mechanics applications. It addresses a key computational challenge in the field: the expensive simulation of large-scale multiphysics problems involving evolving fractures and fluid–solid interactions. Central to its performance is a set of fused multiphysics algorithms that update both coupled thermo-mechanical and thermo-hydrodynamic governing equations in optimized passes over material points. Using massive parallelism, our GPU implementation achieves speedups exceeding 1200$$\times $$ relative to the leading CPU-based codes. We demonstrate the practical utility and superior performance of MilsPD by simulating the large-scale quenching process and formation of columnar joints, a task that remains computationally infeasible for the existing CPU-based multiphysics PD approach. MilsPD thus provides a robust new framework that significantly enhances the capability for high-fidelity failure analysis on previously intractable problems.

title: Machine learning-based design of optimal explicit Runge–Kutta schemes for compressible flow equations
abstract: This study presents a novel artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted framework for developing adaptive optimized explicit Runge–Kutta (OERK) schemes for compressible flow simulations. Unlike existing optimized Runge–Kutta methods developed for either convection or diffusion-dominated regimes, the proposed approach incorporates the local Peclet number directly into the optimization process, enabling adaptive time integration across a broad range of flow conditions. Convex optimization is used to construct optimal stability polynomials for different Peclet numbers and temporal orders of accuracy. The resulting optimized coefficients are then used to train an ANN that predicts locally optimal Runge–Kutta coefficients without repeated optimization during simulations. The proposed methodology is validated using linear and nonlinear ordinary differential equations, one-dimensional convection–diffusion equation, laminar flow over a circular cylinder and turbulent flow around a NACA 0012 airfoil. Numerical results demonstrate that the ANN-predicted schemes preserve the desired order of accuracy while reproducing the optimized stability characteristics. For flow over cylinder case, computational cost reductions of 54–69% relative to classical Runge–Kutta schemes and 17–22% relative to previously optimized methods are achieved. For simulation of turbulent flow over airfoil, CPU-time reductions of 28–41% and 29–35% are obtained, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining convex optimization and machine learning to develop stable, accurate, and computationally efficient adaptive time-integration schemes.

title: Transition-aware learning for surrogate modeling of expensive engineering response surfaces
abstract: Active learning methods for Gaussian-process regression typically focus on reducing global uncertainty or balancing exploration with exploitation. In many scientific and engineering applications, however, the main difficulty in surrogate modeling lies in localized transition regions where the response changes rapidly. These regions often govern threshold detection, regime identification, and local sensitivity, yet standard acquisition rules, such as maximum predictive variance and upper confidence bound, may not allocate samples efficiently in regions where such structural changes occur. This paper introduces Transition-Aware Learning (TAL), a novel Gaussian-process active-learning strategy designed specifically for transition-rich response surfaces. TAL combines predictive uncertainty with transition-sensitive posterior indicators derived from the evolving surrogate, including gradient- and curvature-related quantities in one dimension and their natural extensions in two dimensions. In this way, the method preferentially samples locations where epistemic uncertainty and local structural change coincide, directing evaluations toward the most informative transition zones while remaining fully sequential and computationally comparable to standard Gaussian-process baselines. TAL is evaluated against random sampling, maximum predictive variance, and Gaussian-process upper confidence bound on a benchmark suite of six one-dimensional synthetic engineering-style response surfaces and two two-dimensional extension cases. The one-dimensional suite spans transition-rich behaviors, including stall-like drops, smooth regime switches, saturation knees, piecewise shoulders, multiple transitions, and oscillation-gated responses. At the same time, the two-dimensional cases test whether the same sampling principle remains effective when the dominant feature is a transition contour rather than a point. A sensitivity study is additionally used to assess robustness to the relative weighting of the uncertainty, gradient, and curvature terms, and an experimental NACA 0012 lift dataset provides an engineering demonstration of active reconstruction near aerodynamic stall. Performance is assessed using both global and transition-focused metrics, including root-mean-square error, transition-location error, transition-band error, and transition-mask intersection-over-union. Across the one-dimensional benchmark suite, TAL achieves the lowest average final transition-location error and the lowest average final root-mean-square error while remaining computationally comparable to the strongest baselines. The weight-sensitivity study shows that these results are robust to moderate changes in the acquisition weights rather than depending strongly on the nominal weighting. In the two-dimensional extension cases, TAL remains competitive in both global and local transition-region accuracy. It consistently outperforms the upper confidence bound, although its advantage over maximum predictive variance is less uniform than in one dimension. On the experimental NACA 0012 data, TAL achieves the lowest aggregate final reconstruction error while maintaining competitive stall-angle localization, providing evidence that the transition-aware sampling principle extends beyond the synthetic benchmark suite. These results show that transition-aware acquisition provides a practical and effective alternative to standard active-learning rules when accurate resolution of structural change is a primary modeling objective.

title: Evaluation of location tracking methods to understand human-wildlife contact and pathogen spillover risks
abstract: Background Most emerging infectious diseases originate in wildlife populations. As demonstrated by recent epidemics and pandemics, pathogen spillover from zoonotic reservoirs can have devastating public health impacts. Contact between humans and wildlife reservoirs determines spillover risk, but these interactions remain poorly understood. Despite advancements in geolocation technology and its widespread integration into devices available to consumers and researchers, there are significant challenges to collecting fine-scale human movement data in remote areas to assess contact with wildlife. We aimed to evaluate available methods for collecting these data. We applied the findings to identify an optimal method for a case study on pathogen spillover from bats in rural communities of Macenta Prefecture, Republic of Guinea. Methods Among existing methods for collecting location data from humans, we identified two methods as candidates for our case study: (1) a mobile device with the GPSLogger application and (2) a custom-designed wristwatch with geolocation technology. The spatial accuracy, battery life, and user experience of these methods were assessed under field conditions. This preliminary testing was conducted in remote, forested regions of Macenta, Guinea and Malaysian Borneo, which are areas with repeated zoonotic spillover events. Results Overall, both methods enabled collection of fine-scale spatial data on human movement and proximity to wildlife habitats in remote, forested regions. From initial trials, the custom-designed wristwatch had greater accuracy, had longer battery life, and was reported by participants to be more comfortable to carry than the mobile devices. We demonstrated the utility of these methods for quantifying individual heterogeneities in space use and identifying areas and populations with high risk for human-wildlife contact. Conclusion This proof-of-concept study provides evidence of the value of custom-designed location tracking watches, through their application in epidemiologic research in rural Guinea. However, mobile devices may be more accessible and suitable in contexts with high mobile phone usage and service coverage. Further research is needed to integrate these movement data with ecological and demographic data to understand how environment and human behaviour shape the dynamics of disease emergence.

title: Integrating explainable machine learning and multi-scale spatial modelling to reveal spatiotemporal dynamics and drivers of aerosol optical depth in a complex-terrain city: a case study of Chengdu Plain region, 2001–2024
abstract: Investigating the drivers of aerosol optical depth (AOD) in basin cities can improve our understanding of atmospheric processes and their responses to complex terrain and environmental changes. However, the nonlinear relationships between AOD and its potential drivers, as well as their spatial variation across different scales, remain poorly understood. The Theil–Sen trend estimator and nonparametric Mann–Kendall test were used to estimate and assess temporal trends in AOD. XGBoost-SHAP was used to identify nonlinear AOD–driver relationships and quantify the relative importance of individual predictors, while multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) was used to assess their spatial heterogeneity and characteristic spatial scales. AOD showed a distinct rise–decline pattern over the study period. The annual mean AOD decreased to 0.409 during 2015–2020, a 42.1% reduction from the pre-2015 level. Seasonally, AOD was highest in winter (0.844 ± 0.180), followed by spring (0.765 ± 0.152), while summer (0.702 ± 0.178) and autumn (0.700 ± 0.158) showed similar levels. Spatially, higher AOD values were concentrated mainly across the central and eastern plains, whereas lower values occurred over the western Longmen Mountains. XGBoost achieved an R 2 of 0.85 ± 0.03 in leave-one-year-out cross-validation and 0.91 on the independent 2024 test set. Elevation, relative humidity, and precipitation were the three most influential predictors, with normalized mean absolute SHAP contributions of 46.94%, 19.37%, and 13.54%, respectively, together accounting for 79.85% of the total. MGWR indicated distinct spatial scales among the drivers, with bandwidths of 44–47 km for topographic and meteorological variables, 38–41 km for socioeconomic and vegetation-related variables, and approximately 36 km for road-distance effects. A temporal comparison showed that the relative contribution of anthropogenic factors decreased from 73.6% in 2001–2013 to 48.2% in 2014–2024, indicating a change in the statistical structure of AOD drivers. Population distribution across AOD levels was uneven, with approximately 40% of residents living in areas where AOD exceeded 0.45 and nearly 20% in areas exceeding 0.55. These results show that AOD variability was associated with regional topographic and meteorological conditions as well as spatially varying anthropogenic factors, with their relative importance differing across time and spatial scales.

title: Identification of high notification clusters of congenital heart disease in Colombia (2016–2020): a spatial epidemiology and machine learning approach
abstract: Introduction Congenital heart diseases (CHD) are the most common congenital anomalies and a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in neonates and children. In Colombia, geographic variation in their notification reflects not only the true distribution of the disease, but also differences in access to prenatal and postnatal diagnosis and the performance of the healthcare system. Understanding these spatial patterns and their determinants is crucial for identifying potential inequities in detection and reporting. Methods A retrospective ecological study (2016–2020) was conducted at the municipal level. CHD cases reported to SIVIGILA were used, with live births from DANE as the denominator. Geographic, sociodemographic, and healthcare access indicators were obtained from SISPRO and Terridata. Spatial analysis (SaTScan) was used to identify clusters of high CHD notification, and the XGBoost algorithm was applied to model cluster membership. The contribution of associated factors was assessed using SHAP values. Results Between 2016 and 2020, 2.4 notified CHD cases per 1,000 live births were reported in Colombia. Five high-notification clusters were identified, predominantly in the Andean region and in areas with high population density. The XGBoost model predicted cluster membership with an AUC-ROC of 0.89. Altitude, economic and urban dimensions, population density, access to improved water sources, and prenatal care coverage were the most predictive factors. Conclusions The identified clusters reflect non-random spatial patterns in CHD notification in Colombia, associated with socio-geographic contextual characteristics that suggest a paradox: greater effectiveness of diagnostic, referral, and reporting systems, rather than a higher underlying occurrence of disease, may be contributing to the observed notification patterns and masking the true burden of CHD.

title: Openfootprint-HH-sampling: a reproducible building-based sampling framework for spatially explicit household surveys in data-scarce urban environments
abstract: Background Reliable household sampling frames are frequently unavailable in rapidly growing secondary cities of sub-Saharan Africa, complicating spatially explicit household surveys. Although satellite-assisted methods have improved field logistics, few approaches combine automated frame construction from open geospatial data with systematic validation of how realized samples adhere to the intended spatial design. Methods We developed OpenFootprint-HH-Sampling, a parameterized QGIS workflow that transforms Google Open Building Footprints into spatially explicit sampling frames. Implemented in Ziniaré and Kombissiri, Burkina Faso, the approach combined proportional stratified random sampling by administrative sector with GPS-based mobile navigation. Sampling performance was evaluated through sector-level allocation, exclusive nearest-neighbor matching, nearest-neighbor distance analysis, and Ripley’s L functions. Direct differences between theoretical and realized L(r) functions were quantified using ΔL(r), MAD, MAE, RMSE, correlation coefficients, and R² values. A total of 723 household interviews were completed during August-October 2024. Results Median displacement between theoretical and realized interview locations was 89.4 m in Ziniaré and 90.3 m in Kombissiri, with larger deviations in some peripheral sectors. Nearest-neighbor analysis showed preserved local spatial structure in 5 of 10. Ripley-based comparisons indicated that both theoretical and realized samples retained clustered spatial configuration, while ΔL(r)-based metrics revealed stronger preservation at the city level than at the sector level. At the city level, theoretical and realized L(r) functions showed very high shape similarity, with R² values of 0.980 in Ziniaré and 0.988 in Kombissiri. Conclusions Open building footprint data can support reproducible, spatially explicit household sampling where conventional address systems or complete household registers are unavailable. The results demonstrate operational feasibility and substantial fidelity of the realized sample to the intended spatial design, particularly at the city scale, rather than demographic representativeness of the underlying household population. The workflow may be adapted for health, nutrition, disease surveillance, and demographic surveys, provided that context-specific field verification and household-level inclusion checks are incorporated where population inference is required.

title: A GIS-based framework for standardized environmental characterization in One-Health surveillance: a case study of highly pathogenic avian influenza monitoring in Italian wetlands
abstract: Background The Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) panzootic caused by H5 viruses of clade 2.3.4.4b is constantly re-shaping disease ecology in terms of spatio-temporal spread and host spectrum. Because of this, there is an increasing need to complement traditional surveillance methods with approaches that consider environmental factors into epidemiological interpretation. Although environmental surveillance is increasingly recognized within a One Health framework, environmental descriptors are not always consistently structured, underscoring the importance of adopting standardized approaches for their collection and management. Method A GIS-based framework was developed to standardize environmental characterization of HPAI surveillance sites. Environmental data were collected at nine wetlands in north-eastern Italy, using ESRI field map tool, synchronised through ArcGIS online. Data were validated with field-base ground truthing, stored in a spatial relational database and aggregated into harmonised site-specific descriptors, suitable for epidemiological modelling and analyses. Results This study introduces a GIS-based framework designed to standardize how environmental features are recorded at sampling sites for HPAI surveillance. The workflow turns different types of field observations into organized geographical datasets that can be analysed. When used at wetland surveillance sites in north-eastern Italy, this framework produced consistent environmental data and standardized records for each site. Conclusions The workflow combines mobile GIS tools (ESRI Field Maps), ArcGIS Online/Pro, and a PostGIS database to create standardized outputs for epidemiological analysis. This setup creates a reliable connection between field ecology, spatial data infrastructures, and disease risk analysis.

title: Spatial-temporal clustering and high-risk area identification of dengue in Thailand: a 20-year national analysis using space-time scan statistics
abstract: Dengue remains a major public health challenge in Thailand, with substantial geographic variation. This study analyzed national dengue surveillance data (2005–2024; 1,640,368 cases) across five consecutive 4-year intervals to identify spatial clustering patterns, detect space-time clusters, and characterize the evolution of high-risk areas. Province-level pooled incidence rates were assessed using Global Moran’s I, Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), and SaTScan space-time scan statistics with discrete Poisson models. Global Moran’s I showed significant positive spatial autocorrelation in four periods (I = 0.211–0.473, p p = 0.190), indicating spatial fragmentation. LISA revealed a progressive decline in High-High cluster provinces from 11 to 2 and a geographic shift from Central-Eastern to Northern Thailand. SaTScan detected 13 statistically significant clusters; the most likely cluster occurred in Northern Thailand (2013–2016, relative risk = 2.33, p

title: A GIS-based multi-objective optimization strategy for urban automated external defibrillator deployment
abstract: Background Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a critical urban health challenge due to persistently low survival rates and uneven access to automated external defibrillators (AEDs). Existing deployment strategies often rely on heuristic decisions, limiting their ability to address spatial disparities in emergency response. This study aims to develop a spatially informed, data-driven framework to optimize AED placement and improve urban emergency response capacity. Methods Using Qinhuai District in Nanjing as a case study, we applied Geodetector to identify the spatial determinants of OHCA risk. High-risk population density and its interaction with resident density emerged as dominant factors, informing the construction of a high-resolution AED Demand Index for candidate site selection. We then formulated a multi-objective optimization model to balance service coverage, perceived accessibility, and cost-effectiveness. The model was solved using an enhanced NSGA-II algorithm incorporating tabu search and 2-opt mutation. Results The optimized layouts demonstrated substantial improvements over existing AED configurations. The maximum service distance decreased by 55.3%, and overall satisfaction reached a near-optimal level of 0.997. The enhanced algorithm also achieved notable computational gains compared with standard approaches. Conclusions The proposed GIS-based optimization framework provides a scalable and evidence-based tool for improving AED deployment in dense urban environments. By integrating spatial risk detection with multi-objective optimization, this approach supports urban planners in reducing spatial inequities and strengthening emergency response systems.

title: Ecological context modifies estimated effects of residential greenspace on mental illness mortality: a case study of Washington State, USA
abstract: Background Residential greenspace has been associated with lower mortality in large population-based studies, yet most analyses assume that identical levels of greenness have comparable health effects across ecologically diverse landscapes. We investigated whether the association between residential greenspace and mental illness mortality varies across ecological subregions when greenspace is defined using within-region exposure thresholds. Methods Death certificate records from Washington State in 2018 were used to construct an analytical cohort of 31,245 decedents, including 233 deaths attributed to mental illness (ICD-10 codes F20–F69 and F99). Residential greenspace exposure was measured as the five-year mean Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) within a 15-minute pedestrian walkshed around each residence. Binary treatment indicators were defined using the 50th, 60th, 70th, 80th, and 90th percentiles of the NDVI distribution within each ecological subregion. Average treatment effects were estimated using covariate-balancing propensity score matching followed by logistic regression. Results Statewide treatment effect estimates varied across NDVI thresholds without a consistent protective association. In contrast, subregion-specific analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity in both the direction and magnitude of estimated effects across ecological settings. Region-specific NDVI thresholds produced more stable and interpretable estimates than statewide absolute NDVI cutoffs, indicating that associations between residential greenspace and mental illness mortality depend on local ecological context. Conclusions The association between residential greenspace and mental illness mortality differed across ecological subregions, suggesting that the health relevance of a given NDVI value is context dependent. These findings highlight ecological stratification as an important consideration in environmental health research and support the use of context-specific exposure definitions when evaluating the health effects of residential greenspace. Larger longitudinal studies with improved exposure assessment are needed to clarify these relationships.

title: Short-term recovery of outdoor exercise after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Beijing: a GPS-based study of urban environmental differences
abstract: Background Large infection waves can disrupt health-related physical activity even when outdoor spaces remain accessible. However, little is known about how outdoor activity recovers across different urban environments immediately after public health restrictions are lifted. This study examined short-term changes in outdoor exercise in Beijing after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions, with particular attention to temporal phases, spatial heterogeneity and differences among urban environmental settings. Methods We analysed 196,524 anonymised walking, running and cycling trajectories recorded by the Keep app from 13 December 2022 to 31 March 2023. Activity in January 2022 was used as a reference period. Daily trajectory counts were modelled as time series to identify recovery phases. Spatial clustering, hotspot statistics and trajectory-based counts were used to compare changes across urban green spaces, active transportation corridors and localised sports facilities, and between central and suburban areas. Results Outdoor exercise did not show a simple linear recovery. Four short-term phases were identified: initial stability, brief disruption, rapid rebound and later stabilisation. The main decline occurred after the infection peak, indicating a delayed behavioural response rather than an immediate reduction when restrictions were lifted. Recovery varied markedly by urban setting. After accounting for differences in spatial extent, urban green spaces showed the most stable activity intensity across phases. Active transportation corridors exhibited the largest relative increase during the rapid recovery phase, particularly in central urban areas, whereas localised sports facilities showed a later increase in activity intensity. These patterns describe differences in observed trajectory activity across exercise-space typologies rather than behavioural preferences of population groups. Spatial differences were also evident, central and suburban areas exhibited different recovery patterns in observed exercise trajectories, with variation in the timing and magnitude of activity changes. Conclusions Outdoor exercise recovery after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions was phased, delayed and spatially uneven. Analysis of spatially normalized activity intensity and trajectory changes revealed differentiated recovery patterns across exercise-space typologies: urban green spaces showed the greatest stability, active transportation corridors showed the strongest increase during early recovery, and localised sports facilities showed higher activity intensity during later recovery. These findings highlight that different exercise-space typologies exhibited distinct recovery patterns after a major public health shock.

title: Exploring nonlinear associations between environmental and social media variables and active leisure travel
abstract: Background In the context of healthy urban development, active leisure travel modes such as cycling, jogging, and walking promote physical health and reduce health risks. Current research has predominantly focused on the associations between environmental variables and active leisure travel, while limited attention has been given to public perceptions and online interaction characteristics captured through social media. This study expands the existing environmental variable framework by incorporating social media variables. It aims to investigate the nonlinear associations between multidimensional variables and different types of active leisure travel. Methodology This study utilized 5,451 active leisure travel trajectory records to develop cycling, jogging, and walking indices, which were used as dependent variables. The Chinese-RoBERTa-wwm-ext model was utilized to analyze social media data, producing emotional scores and interaction heat variables. Environmental and social media variables were integrated, and the XGBoost model combined with the SHAP interpretation approach was employed to examine their nonlinear associations with active leisure travel. Results The three active leisure travel modes exhibit notable spatiotemporal heterogeneity, characterized by considerable variations in key explanatory variables and contribution patterns. For cycling, interaction heat, average temperature, and NDVI were the variables with relatively higher contributions; for jogging, population density and spatial accessibility showed greater importance; and for walking, average temperature, interaction heat, and emotional scores exhibited relatively higher contributions. Conclusion All variables demonstrate distinct nonlinear associations and threshold patterns with active leisure travel, with their significance and explanatory capacity varying across different travel modes. Furthermore, social media characteristics make significant contributions. The results enhance our comprehension of active leisure travel and offer a novel viewpoint for research on urban leisure travel.

title: Smoothing-based approaches for detecting age-specific spatial clusters in small-area mortality data: a simulation evaluation
abstract: Background With the increasing availability of high-resolution rate data such as age-specific mortality and disease incidence rates, it has become feasible to perform cluster detection stratified by age group. However, the accurate identification of spatial clusters in small populations remains challenging due to population sparsity and low event rates. To address this challenge, this study proposes a smoothing-based analytical framework to improve cluster detection performance in SaTScan under sparse and unstable conditions. Methods Three smoothing approaches, the Whittaker–Henderson (WH), Partial Standardized Mortality Ratio (PSMR), and Besag–York–Mollié (BYM2) methods, were evaluated through simulation studies across varying population sizes and age groups. Results The results indicate that all methods substantially improve the detection power of SaTScan compared to unsmoothed data, while WH achieves a better balance between statistical power and false detection rates. When applied to Taiwan’s 2021 female cancer mortality data, the WH method identified a significant hotspot among women aged 70 to 74 in southern Taiwan, primarily associated with elevated lung and liver cancer mortality. Conclusions The findings suggest that WH smoothing provides a practical and statistically reliable solution for stabilizing mortality estimates and identifying meaningful spatial clusters in small-population contexts. This framework offers valuable methodological and applied insights for spatial epidemiology and small-area health surveillance.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns of kidney transplantation, chronic kidney disease, and traumatic brain injury mortality in Brazil
abstract: Introduction Kidney transplantation, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and traumatic brain injury (TBI) mortality exhibit substantial regional variation in Brazil, yet their spatiotemporal relationships remain poorly understood. Objective To analyze spatiotemporal patterns and geographic associations among kidney transplantation rates, TBI-related mortality, and CKD burden in Brazil using the Space Time Cube (STC) approach. Methods This ecological, retrospective, and longitudinal study analyzed secondary data from DATASUS between 2010 and 2021 across Brazilian health regions. Data included TBI-related mortality, kidney transplantation rates, and CKD-related hospitalizations and hemodialysis procedures used as proxy indicators of advanced CKD burden. Spatial analyses were performed in ArcGIS Pro using the STC tool, and emerging hotspots were identified using the Getis–Ord Gi* statistics. Results Marked regional disparities were observed across Brazil. TBI-related mortality clusters were concentrated in the Northeast, particulary in Alagoas, Paraíba, and Sergipe, whereas kidney transplantation hotspots predominated in the South and Southeast, especially in Paraná and Rio Grande do Sul, followed by the Southeast. Indicators of CKD burden showed a more heterogeneous spatial distribution, with higher concentrations in the Southeast. Notably, regions with higher TBI-related mortality did not necessarily correspond to those with higher transplantation rates, suggesting important geographic inequalities in transplantation access and healthcare infrastructure. Conclusion These findings highlight the importance of regionally targeted policies to strengthen emergency care networks, organ donation systems, and transplant infrastructure, helping reduce geographic inequalities and improve equitable access to kidney transplantation across Brazil.

title: Assessing cardiovascular disease vulnerability in India: a spatially disaggregated index-based framework
abstract: In this study, we develop a district-level vulnerability index for cardiovascular diseases in India, addressing the persistent public health challenges posed by socioeconomic, environmental, and infrastructural disparities. Drawing on 26 indicators across seven domains, viz., socioeconomic, physiological, behavioural, healthcare, dietary, and environmental (both indoor and outdoor), we sourced data from the National Family Health Survey-5, Rural Health Statistics 2021-22, and satellite datasets. After preprocessing, curating, and integrating these datasets to a uniform scale, we applied a one-common-factor model to derive weights for each indicator for calculating domain scores. These domain scores were then computed and aggregated into an overall vulnerability score, assigning equal weight to each domain. Further to understand the spatial patterns, we employed Global Moran’s I and Anselin’s Local Moran’s I statistics. The results highlight noticeable vulnerability in eastern and northeastern districts, including Kolkata, Haora, Kamrup Metropolitan, and Paschim Barddhaman, primarily due to degraded air quality, inadequate healthcare access, and suboptimal dietary practices. In contrast, districts in hilly and western regions, such as Bageshwar, Barmer, Rudraprayag, Chamba, Agar Malwa, and Pali, demonstrate lower vulnerability, supported by favourable air quality indices, nutritious diets, and physically active lifestyles influenced by rugged terrain. Global Moran’s I yielded a value of 0.636 (Z = 27.17, pseudo p-value = 0.001), indicating strong spatial autocorrelation, while local analysis revealed high-high clusters in the east and low-low clusters in western and hilly areas. It is important to note that this index captures potential future vulnerability based on current structural, environmental, and behavioural risk conditions, rather than reflecting actual current disease burden. This index provides a valuable framework for pinpointing and addressing CVD vulnerabilities at the local level, underscoring the imperative for tailored public health strategies and interventions by policymakers and researchers.

title: Spatial co-clustering of facility-recorded malaria and sickle cell disease admissions across health facility catchments in Uganda: a Bayesian shared-component disease mapping analysis
abstract: Background Malaria and sickle cell disease (SCD) remain major causes of morbidity and mortality in Uganda, yet their joint spatial organization across routine service geographies has rarely been examined. We assessed whether facility-recorded malaria and SCD admissions shared residual spatial structure across modeled health-facility catchments. Methods We conducted a national ecological study using higher-level health-facility catchments as spatial units. Monthly facility-level inpatient malaria and SCD admissions reported in Uganda’s DHIS2 from January 2020 to December 2024 were aggregated over 5 years to stabilize sparse catchment-level counts. Catchments were delineated using a two-step floating catchment area approach based on nearest higher-level facility assignment and a 60-minute travel-time threshold. We summarized crude cumulative admission rates per 10,000 modeled catchment population. We then fitted Bayesian shared-component disease-mapping models, including baseline, extended, and covariate-adjusted specifications. Expected counts were derived from total catchment population as a pragmatic standardization baseline. Results Mean crude malaria admission burden was 293.6 per 10,000 catchment population, mean crude SCD admission burden was 27.9 per 10,000, and mean descriptive composite admission burden was 321.5 per 10,000. The extended model fit better than the baseline model (DIC 3326.33 vs. 3400.12; WAIC 4964.56 vs. 5908.24). In the extended model, the shared spatial precision was low (posterior mean 0.010, 95% CrI 0.007 to 0.012), consistent with substantial shared residual spatial heterogeneity across the two recorded admission outcomes, whereas disease-specific spatial precision parameters were very large and highly uncertain, suggesting limited stable evidence for additional disease-specific spatial structure. Positive shared spatial effects were concentrated most consistently across health-facility catchments in northern and eastern Uganda. The SCD copy-loading parameter was close to zero (mean − 0.084, 95% CrI − 0.232 to 0.066). In covariate-adjusted analyses, model fit improved further (the lowest DIC in the fully adjusted model, 3023.63) with the same residual shared signal persisting. Conclusions Facility-recorded malaria and SCD admissions exhibited residual spatial co-patterning across some service geographies, where integrated approaches to surveillance and service strengthening may be evaluated, while recognizing that the shared component may also reflect common referral, diagnostic, and reporting processes.

title: Evaluation of a spatial microsimulation framework for small-area estimation of population health outcomes using the behavioral risk factor surveillance system
abstract: Background Health decision-making relies on population health data, yet ground-truth data are often unavailable. Therefore, small area estimation (SAE) techniques are used to model health outcomes at fine geographic scales. While multilevel regression modeling is commonly applied, spatial microsimulation has emerged as a state-of-the-art approach, but its application in health-related SAE remains narrow and its broader potential for producing reliable, multi-outcome estimates is underexplored. Methods We introduce the Spatial Health and Population Estimator (SHAPE), a spatial microsimulation framework that applies hierarchical iterative proportional fitting (IPF) to estimate two health risk behaviors and eleven health outcomes across multiple settings and scales. SHAPE was evaluated using county-level Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) direct estimates and county- and census tract–level model-based estimates from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Population Level Analysis and Community Estimates (CDC PLACES) for New York (2021) and Florida (2019). Results SHAPE’s evaluation results varied by location, spatial scale, and health behavior or outcome. Generally, the framework showed moderate consistency with direct estimates (r̄ ≈ 0.54), similar to CDC PLACES (r̄ ≈ 0.66). SHAPE demonstrated stronger alignment with CDC PLACES at both county (r̄ ≈ 0.81) and census tract (r̄ ≈ 0.74) levels. Conclusions SHAPE offers a flexible, sustainable tool for public health SAE that generates synthetic populations with preserved joint distributions of individual characteristics, enabling detailed analysis of health disparities and supporting downstream modeling applications, like agent-based simulations.

title: Influence of spatial connectivity on the spread of Mpox in Maï-Ndombe province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2025
abstract: Background Human mobility is a major determinant of the spatial spread of emerging infectious diseases. In Maï-Ndombe province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, dependence on waterways as the primary transport network, combined with a degraded road infrastructure and marked environmental constraints, creates profound heterogeneity in spatial connectivity between health zones. In this context, the spread of Mpox shows an irregular spatial distribution whose structural mechanisms remain poorly understood, partly due to the scarcity of mobility data and the fragility of surveillance systems. Objective To quantify the intra-provincial spatial connectivity of Maï-Ndombe by simultaneously integrating road and river networks, and to assess its influence on the spread of Mpox between 2022 and 2025. Methods A spatial connectivity analysis based on an enhanced gravity model integrating demographic attractiveness and a distance-cost factor accounting for slope and land use via the Fuzzy-AHP method was combined with a spatialized metapopulation SEIR model. Inter-zone flows, centrality, and accessibility were quantified. The performance of SEIR models with and without connectivity was compared using RMSE, MAE, and precision gain per zone. Results Flows are strongly concentrated around pivotal zones (Bokoro, Nioki, Mushie), while peripheral areas (Mimia, Oshwe, Kiri) remain structurally isolated, with accessibility provided primarily by river corridors (Gini index = 0.65; CV = 1.52). The integration of connectivity degrades the overall model fit (ΔRMSE = -0.468), reflecting the predominance of local transmission at the provincial scale. However, this aggregate degradation conceals marked spatial heterogeneity: connectivity significantly improves predictions in highly connected zones (Bokoro: +59.8%; Mushie: +33.3%; Nioki: +17.3%), while degrading them in poorly connected zones (Kiri: -46.1%; Mimia: -27.4%; Oshwe: -22.4%). Conclusion Spatial connectivity does not strengthen the overall prediction of incidence, but structures the spatial redistribution of epidemic risk. The aggregate model degradation reflects both the limitations of the surveillance system and structural constraints of the gravity model, particularly the use of static populations as denominators and the absence of temporal exposure duration at destination zones. These results highlight the importance of targeting surveillance interventions in high-centrality areas, while developing metapopulation approaches that integrate the temporal dimension of mobility to improve preparedness for future Mpox outbreaks in tropical forest environments.

title: Unraveling hybrid diffusion structures in epidemics: a bayesian spatiotemporal modeling framework
abstract: Infectious disease epidemics in complex urban environments often exhibit hybrid diffusion dynamics that combine localized expansion with sporadic long-distance relocation. Traditional spatial statistical models, such as Conditional Autoregressive (CAR) models, typically rely on fixed, adjacency-based spatial weight matrices, creating risks of structural misspecification when transmission pathways deviate from geographic proximity. To address this limitation, this study develops a Bayesian spatiotemporal modeling framework that treats the spatial weight matrix W as an estimable quantity rather than a fixed input, employing an adaptive CAR prior to infer latent diffusion networks directly from routine surveillance data. This reframing allows the model to distinguish expansion-type from relocation-type connectivity links without requiring pre-specified mobility data. The framework is first evaluated through simulation experiments, demonstrating strong capacity to identify the structural distinction between expansion-type and relocation-type diffusion links (Pearson’s correlation > 0.8). We then apply the model to the 2015 dengue outbreak in Tainan, Taiwan. The inferred diffusion network reveals a distinct hybrid topology: the urban core is sustained by a mixture of contiguous expansion links (30%) and within-cluster relocation links (46%), whereas peripheral districts are predominantly seeded by external relocation links (67%) originating from the core. Community detection further delineates spatial clusters that reflect underlying socio-spatial interactions rather than administrative boundaries. By reframing the adaptive CAR prior as a network inference mechanism, this study provides a flexible and data-driven approach for uncovering complex diffusion pathways and guiding targeted surveillance strategies in settings where detailed mobility data are unavailable.

title: The Burak diagrams: a family of 3D diagrams for evaluation of climatological and hydrological simulations
abstract: This study introduces the Burak Diagrams by incorporating an orthogonal bias axis into the Taylor Diagram (Taylor 2001), thereby enabling multiple performance metrics to be represented as analytically derived 3D surfaces. Three Burak Diagrams are developed: BD-Clim for climatological simulations, BD-HydNSE for hydrological simulations incorporating the Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency $$(NSE)$$, and BD-HydKGE for hydrological simulations incorporating the Kling–Gupta Efficiency $$(KGE)$$. All three diagrams share a common theoretical foundation based on the geometric decomposition of the root-mean-square difference ($$RMSD $$ or $$E$$) proposed by Taylor (2001). BD-Clim extends the Taylor Diagram by incorporating bias ($$\overline{E }$$) as a third axis while preserving the original representation of correlation ($$R$$), variability, and centered root-mean-square difference ($$E^{\prime}$$), with $$E$$ (or $$RMSD$$) represented as analytic surfaces. Similarly, BD-HydNSE and BD-HydKGE incorporate percent bias ($$PBias$$) as a third axis while preserving the original Taylor Diagram representation, with $$NSE$$ and $$KGE$$ represented as analytic surfaces for evaluating hydrological model performance. Interactive visualization tools for all three diagrams are developed in the R programming environment and are available on CRAN as the “ burakDiagrams ” package. Together, the proposed diagrams support the simultaneous interpretation of complementary performance metrics, improve insight into model behaviour, and facilitate more comprehensive intercomparison of climatological and hydrological simulations. By representing $$RMSD$$, $$NSE$$, and $$KGE$$ as surfaces, the diagrams visually reveal how these metrics vary in response to changes in their underlying component metrics.
journal: Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment

title: Direct parameterization of paired rainfall-runoff events for peak discharge estimation: an event-based framework for flood risk assessment
abstract: Accurate estimation of event-scale peak discharge is essential for flood risk assessment and infrastructure design, yet conventional hydrologic modelling approaches often require extensive calibration procedures and computationally demanding optimization. This study presents a parsimonious event-based framework for estimating hourly runoff hydrographs and peak discharges through direct parameter estimation from physically consistent rainfall-runoff event pairs. The framework integrates precipitation event identification, streamflow baseflow separation, and event pairing with a process-based hydrologic model combining the Natural Resources Conservation Service Curve Number method for precipitation loss estimation and the Natural Resources Conservation Service Unit Hydrograph method for direct runoff transformation. Model parameters, including catchment lag time, peak rate factor, and seasonal Curve NumberPrecipitation relationships, are estimated directly from observed rainfall-runoff events, eliminating the need for inverse numerical optimization against an explicit likelihood or objective function. The framework is evaluated across seven catchments with varying drainage areas within the Housatonic River Basin, using a leave-one-out cross-validation approach. Results demonstrate consistent performance across catchments, with negligible bias and similar residual error characteristics between parameter estimation and evaluation datasets, indicating robust performance for unseen events. Compared with a geometric mean estimator, the proposed framework reduces the standard deviation of the logarithmic residuals by roughly 40 to 60 percent, providing a computationally efficient and physically interpretable tool for large-scale event-based peak discharge estimation.
journal: Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment

title: Delineation of hazardous regions in the unit hypercube: A copula-based approximation for the identification of low-frequency compound occurrences
abstract: The probabilistic characterization of compound extreme events, defined as those arising from the joint action of several (generally dependent) drivers, is a central problem in engineering hydrology and water resources. The copula-based scenarios customarily used in the literature (i.e., OR, AND, Kendall, and survival Kendall) summarize multivariate risk by tracing a single boundary in the unit hypercube and assigning to it a target probability, or equivalently a return period. Except for the rectangular OR and AND cases, the prescribed probability attaches to the bounding layer rather than to the hazardous region itself, which is then determined only implicitly. Moreover, the marginal exceedance rates of the drivers are fixed by the level of the critical layer and cannot be set independently. Here we introduce a copula-based approximation that characterizes the hazardous region directly as a full-dimensional set to which the target exceedance frequency is attached. The boundary of this set consists of linear segments meeting at a vertex at the point of maximum curvature of an equiprobability surface of the copula. Crucially, the per-variable exceedance rates are predefined by the user, so that application-specific marginal rates are reconciled with the joint target within a single region, allowing asymmetric compound occurrences (e.g., high discharge under moderate coastal water level, or the reverse) to be accommodated naturally. We develop the formulation in the frequency domain for both exchangeable and non-exchangeable copulas, provide a direct extension to higher dimensions, and demonstrate it on the symmetric and asymmetric versions of the Clayton and Gumbel copulas, taken as representative models of lower- and upper-tail dependence. The resulting construction is simple to implement and particularly suited to early-warning systems, in which a hazardous combination of drivers must be recognized as it develops.
journal: Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment

title: Ensemble quantile-based deep learning framework for streamflow and flood prediction in Australian catchments
abstract: In recent years, climate extremes such as floods have created significant environmental and economic hazards for Australia. Deep learning methods have been promising for predicting extreme climate events; however, large flooding events present a critical challenge due to factors such as model calibration and missing data. We present an ensemble quantile-based deep learning framework that addresses large-scale streamflow forecasts using quantile regression for uncertainty projections in prediction. We evaluate selected univariate and multivariate deep learning models and catchment strategies. We implement a multistep time-series prediction model using the CAMELS dataset for selected catchments across Australia. The ensemble model employs a set of quantile deep learning models for streamflow determined by historical streamflow data. We utilise the streamflow prediction and obtain flood probability using flood frequency analysis and compare it with historical flooding events for selected catchments. Our results demonstrate notable efficacy and uncertainties in streamflow forecasts with varied catchment properties. Our flood probability estimates show good accuracy in capturing the historical floods from the selected catchments. This underscores the potential for our deep learning framework to revolutionise flood forecasting across diverse regions and be implemented as an early warning system.
journal: Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment

title: Comparative assessment of classical, physically informed, machine learning, and hybrid rating curve models for streamflow estimation
abstract: The stage-discharge rating curve is an important tool for streamflow estimation, especially in poorly gauged basins where direct streamflow measurements are often unavailable. This study presents an integrated comparative evaluation of seven rating curve models using calibration and independent testing performance, flow-stratified predictive accuracy, extrapolation under very high flows, and uncertainty behaviour of estimated flows at a gauging station in the Shilabati River basin, eastern India. The rating curve models include classical power-law, polynomial, classical segmented power-law, Bayesian segmented rating curve (BaRatin), generalised power-law model (GPLM), vertically-segmented power-law, and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). Although all models achieve good calibration and testing performance and comparable accuracy at low and moderate flow values, major differences are observed when models’ performance is assessed at high flows, extrapolation conditions and uncertainty quantification. In this investigated site, classical models show comparatively weaker extrapolation performance, while GPLM, GPR, and vertically segmented power-law models tend to underestimate extreme discharges during extrapolation and reveal less balanced uncertainty characteristics.
